940.headline: Mario opens the first contest with an easy win
940.narrative: The first contest match was treated as a predetermined Mario win, with the real question being how dominant he would look. The writeup also stresses the unusual joke-vote and early-contest atmosphere surrounding the result.

941.headline: Morrigan surprises Spyro and starts early Board 8 traditions
941.narrative: Morrigan's win surprised a board that mostly knew Spyro better and expected him to prevail. The match became memorable for spawning early Board 8 traditions such as "wait until the kiddies wake up" and TJF.

942.headline: Aya upsets Terry and sends the board into a frenzy
942.narrative: Aya's win over Terry caused the contest's first major board frenzy after many regulars had expected Terry to cruise. The writeup says the result helped popularize TJF and fed the emerging Square-versus-the-world mentality.

943.headline: Donkey Kong wins but raises early strength concerns
943.narrative: Donkey Kong won an obvious mismatch, but the writeup focuses on how unimpressive the performance looked for a top seed against an obscure opponent. It immediately raised doubts about his ability to challenge Mario.

944.headline: Alucard surprises Tails and begins building a contest reputation
944.narrative: Alucard's victory surprised most of Board 8 even though the broader bracket predictions were nearly split. Tails cut into the percentage at times, but the writeup says Alucard controlled the match throughout and turned an apparent fluke into the start of a real contest reputation.

945.headline: Duke Nukem handles Iori in a routine opener
945.narrative: Duke Nukem handled an obscure Iori as expected and looked set for a favorable second-round path. The writeup treats the match as routine and mainly uses it to frame Duke as the favorite against Alucard.

946.headline: Pikachu beats PaRappa despite heavy board hostility
946.narrative: Pikachu won without being in serious danger, but most of Board 8 spent the match rooting for PaRappa. The writeup presents the poll as an early showcase of strong anti-Pokémon sentiment on the site.

947.headline: Cloud crushes Fox and ignites the Square-Nintendo rivalry
947.narrative: A heavily hyped first Square-versus-Nintendo matchup turned into an easy Cloud win. The writeup remembers the match less for suspense than for igniting the long-running Square-Nintendo rivalry and intensifying anticipation for Mario versus Cloud.

948.headline: Lara wins but immediately looks badly overseeded
948.narrative: Lara won comfortably, but the writeup treats the showing as poor for a top seed facing an obscure opponent. It argues that her first match already exposed serious overseeding and declining support.

949.headline: Ryo looks strong against an overmatched Guybrush
949.narrative: Ryo looked surprisingly strong against Guybrush and briefly earned some respect from the early contest results. In retrospect, the writeup attributes that appearance of strength largely to very weak opposition.

950.headline: Crono overwhelms Simon and announces himself as a threat
950.narrative: Some Board 8 users thought Simon's Castlevania name gave him a real chance, while Crono was still underestimated by people unfamiliar with Chrono Trigger. Crono's dominant performance instead established him as a serious threat.

951.headline: Dante handles Q*Bert and builds hype for Crono
951.narrative: Dante dispatched Q*Bert in a match whose main significance was setting up the next round. The writeup says the result added to heavy anticipation for what Board 8 expected to be a competitive Crono-Dante matchup.

952.headline: Aeris beats Kasumi and looks badly underseeded
952.narrative: Aeris beat Kasumi without much drama, reinforcing the view that her low seed badly understated her strength. The writeup sees the surrounding part of the bracket as hers to control before an expected meeting with Solid Snake.

953.headline: Tina shocks Gordon and starts the GFNW legend
953.narrative: Tina's unexpected win began the long-running "Gordon Freeman Never Wins" joke. The writeup emphasizes how embarrassing the loss seemed for Gordon, noting that even a link from a Half-Life site failed to rescue him.

954.headline: Knuckles posts the contest's first overwhelming blowout
954.narrative: Knuckles produced the contest's first truly overwhelming blowout and briefly inspired talk of a much deeper run. The writeup mainly treats the result as an early demonstration of his potential against very weak opposition.

955.headline: Snake handles Squall at the height of his popularity
955.narrative: Solid Snake entered as one of the contest's biggest favorites and easily handled a well-supported Squall. The writeup attributes Squall's poor showing to his weak standing at the time and explicitly describes the result as non-SFF.

956.headline: Pac-Man wins but looks weak for a top seed
956.narrative: Pac-Man won comfortably, but the writeup saw the performance as weak for a top seed against an obscure opponent. Like Lara before him, he immediately looked less formidable than his seeding suggested.

957.headline: Kyo upsets Abe in another early seeding surprise
957.narrative: Kyo produced another seeding upset for the early contest after other King of Fighters characters had struggled badly. The writeup interprets the result more as evidence of Abe's weakness than of Kyo's strength.

958.headline: Scorpion handles Kazuya in a forgettable fighting-game matchup
958.narrative: Scorpion beat Kazuya as expected in the contest's first matchup between two fighting-game characters. The writeup considers the result straightforward and mostly uses it to question how character popularity translated from their series.

959.headline: Max Payne cruises while looking ready for a deeper run
959.narrative: Max Payne dominated an obscure opponent and looked strong enough for a deep run by early-contest standards. The writeup also notes that the poll was the contest's lowest-scoring match to that point.

960.headline: Bomberman routs Kane after a disastrous match picture
960.narrative: Bomberman won easily, with the writeup placing unusual emphasis on Kane's disastrous match picture. It treats the result as an example of a recognizable game not automatically producing a strong contest character.
960.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kane's disastrous television-set match picture hurt him badly and made Bomberman's victory look obvious before voting developed.

961.headline: Jill holds off underseeded board favorite Kirby
961.narrative: Kirby was a major board favorite and widely viewed as badly underseeded, but Jill took an early lead and held it throughout. The final result looked close, yet the writeup stresses that Kirby never mounted a serious comeback.

962.headline: Strider edges Raziel in a quiet but controlled match
962.narrative: Strider and Raziel produced the closest result of the contest to that point, but the writeup says Strider remained in control throughout. The unusually quiet poll also gave Strider a long-lived record for a very low-scoring match winner.

963.headline: Link's first match reveals an early contest powerhouse
963.narrative: Link's first contest match was remembered as an early warning of how dominant he could become. The writeup says the performance made the rest of his division look incapable of stopping his path toward the late rounds.

964.headline: Sonic follows Link with another dominant opening performance
964.narrative: Sonic followed Link's dominant showing with another overwhelming win over obvious fodder. The writeup says there was little reason at the time to doubt that Sonic belonged with the contest's elite characters.

965.headline: Tidus survives Claire but inspires little confidence
965.narrative: Tidus survived a match the writeup saw as having real upset potential because of his unpopularity and Claire's stronger-than-expected position. His Square affiliation was enough to carry him through, but the performance gave little confidence before facing Sonic.

966.headline: Samus handles Ken and looks ready for Ryu
966.narrative: Samus beat Ken in a routine match that mainly served as a measuring stick for an expected meeting with Ryu. The writeup says her performance made her look well prepared for that matchup.

967.headline: Ryu crushes the heavily hyped joke entrant CATS
967.narrative: Ryu demolished CATS after the joke entrant had drawn considerable board hype. The writeup treats the result as proof that CATS's support was largely humorous rather than evidence of real contest strength.

968.headline: Mega Man's historic blowout turns him into a contender
968.narrative: Mega Man produced an unprecedented blowout that immediately elevated him from a respected entrant to one of the contest's major threats. Attention quickly shifted to whether he could reproduce that dominance against Sephiroth.

969.headline: Serious Sam wins a match treated largely as filler
969.narrative: Serious Sam won a low-interest match that the writeup viewed mostly as filler between Mega Man and Sephiroth appearances. Neither entrant was considered likely to matter beyond this round.

970.headline: Underseeded Sephiroth cruises and builds Mega Man hype
970.narrative: Sephiroth easily dispatched Gabe Logan while reinforcing the view that his seed badly understated his strength. The result intensified anticipation for his eventual showdown with Mega Man.

971.headline: Crash wins but confirms doubts about his high seed
971.narrative: Crash won comfortably, but the writeup saw his performance against Ulala as further evidence that his high seed reflected name recognition more than actual contest strength. Sephiroth already looked far beyond his reach.

972.headline: Mario wins again but leaves doubts before Cloud
972.narrative: Mario defeated Morrigan without serious trouble, yet the writeup viewed it as a second straight underwhelming performance compared with the contest's other elite characters. Cloud's next result therefore took on added importance for their expected meeting.

973.headline: Donkey Kong completes the contest's first major comeback
973.narrative: Aya stunned Donkey Kong with an early lead before he recovered and completed the contest's first major comeback. The writeup remembers the match for establishing both Donkey Kong's inconsistency and the early legend of Nintendo's morning vote.

974.headline: Alucard's surprise run continues through Duke Nukem
974.narrative: Alucard followed his surprise win over Tails by beating Duke even more convincingly, turning an obscure entrant into an unexpected divisional semifinalist. The writeup also notes that weak opposition had helped make the run possible.

975.headline: Cloud crushes Pikachu as early vote tracking takes shape
975.narrative: Cloud overwhelmed Pikachu and looked substantially stronger than Mario had through the same stage of the bracket. The match also became notable for Solarshadow's early vote-tracking work, a precursor to later poll-update culture.

976.headline: Lara advances while looking increasingly overseeded
976.narrative: Lara beat Ryo in an uneventful match, but once again failed to look like a true top seed against weak opposition. The writeup treats the result as another warning that stronger East Division entrants were likely to expose her.

977.headline: Crono turns a hyped Dante match into a rout
977.narrative: Crono turned a heavily anticipated close match with Dante into an easy victory. The writeup says the result revealed how misleading their superficially similar first-round performances had been and made Crono a serious threat to Lara.

978.headline: Aeris takes advantage of an unexpectedly easy path
978.narrative: Aeris received an unexpectedly easy path after Tina eliminated Gordon Freeman and took full advantage of it. The writeup views her low seed as misleading and her trip to the divisional semifinals as well deserved.

979.headline: Snake dismisses Knuckles hype and strengthens his contender case
979.narrative: Minor Knuckles upset hype disappeared almost immediately as Solid Snake controlled the match from the start. The writeup treats the result as confirmation that Snake belonged among the contest's serious contenders.

980.headline: Pac-Man advances despite mounting evidence of overseeding
980.narrative: Pac-Man won another match that was never seriously in doubt, but the writeup saw his performance as further proof that he was badly overseeded. His weak half of the division still appeared likely to protect him from consequences.

981.headline: Scorpion shocks Max Payne in a decisive upset
981.narrative: Scorpion demolished heavily favored Max Payne after most of the board misread their first-round blowouts. The writeup treats the result as both a major surprise and evidence that mainstream popularity did not translate cleanly to GameFAQs.

982.headline: Jill handles Bomberman and cements her contest place
982.narrative: Jill handled Bomberman without much suspense after already surviving the more dangerous Kirby matchup. The writeup says her two wins helped cement her as a recurring contest presence.

983.headline: Link cruises through another overmatched South Division opponent
983.narrative: Link crushed Strider in a match the writeup considered completely predetermined. The main takeaway was that Link looked like one of the strongest title favorites while facing little meaningful resistance in his division.

984.headline: Sonic dispatches Tidus and remains an elite contender
984.narrative: Sonic beat Tidus more comfortably than some upset-minded observers expected and remained an elite contender. The writeup attributes Tidus's ability to avoid a worse defeat largely to his Square affiliation despite his personal unpopularity.

985.headline: Samus brushes aside the Ryu upset case
985.narrative: Ryu was a fashionable upset pick before the contest, but Samus controlled their match from the start. The result confirmed that her earlier win over Ken was not misleading and sent her toward an expected meeting with Sonic.

986.headline: Mega Man's second rout sends Sephiroth hype into overdrive
986.narrative: Mega Man followed his first-round destruction with another extraordinary blowout, this time against an entrant who had already won a match. The writeup remembers this as the point when he became the contest's breakout star and a credible threat to Sephiroth.

987.headline: Sephiroth crushes Crash and completes the Mega Man setup
987.narrative: Sephiroth easily eliminated the much higher-seeded Crash and left no doubt that their seeds had badly misstated their relative strength. The writeup treats the match mainly as the final setup for the anticipated Mega Man showdown.

988.headline: Mario crushes Donkey Kong as SFF theory begins emerging
988.narrative: Mario finally produced the dominant performance people had been waiting for, restoring confidence before his expected match with Cloud. The result also became an early case used to develop Board 8's SFF theory.
988.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario's unusually dominant result against the closely linked Donkey Kong helped introduce what Board 8 would later universally call Same Fanbase Factor, though it was still treated as a fledgling theory at the time.

989.headline: Alucard's last stand makes Mario-Cloud uncertain again
989.narrative: Cloud ended Alucard's surprise run, but did not dominate as thoroughly as his earlier matches suggested he might. The writeup says that performance, combined with Mario's previous showing, restored genuine uncertainty before Mario versus Cloud.

990.headline: Crono destroys Lara and turns his run into contention
990.narrative: Crono demolished top-seeded Lara after her earlier matches had already exposed warning signs. The writeup treats Lara as a seeding fraud and Crono's performance as proof that his unexpected run had become a legitimate championship threat.

991.headline: Snake ends Aeris's underseeded run and awaits Crono
991.narrative: Solid Snake ended Aeris's underseeded run in an expected victory. The writeup focuses less on the match itself than on how Snake's showing might translate against the much stronger Crono.

992.headline: Scorpion shocks Pac-Man in the contest's original signature upset
992.narrative: Scorpion's decisive win over Pac-Man shocked most observers and exposed how weak the entire half-division had been. The writeup remembers the fallout, including outside attention from Penny Arcade, as the moment the first contest truly became a larger event.

993.headline: Link overwhelms Jill and continues his easy path
993.narrative: Link overwhelmed Jill in another match the writeup considered a formality. His weak division had effectively handed him a direct route toward the Final Four while he continued to look like the tournament favorite.

994.headline: Samus completes a stunning comeback amid rallying and controversy
994.narrative: Samus erased what had looked like a decisive late Sonic lead and won after an extraordinary closing surge. The match triggered a massive backlash, outside vote recruitment on both sides, cheating suspicions, and lasting changes to how contest results were followed.
994.anomaly_note: The writeup says Samus and Sonic supporters spammed for votes across the internet, chat rooms, buddy lists, and gaming chats. It also says many users suspected cheating behind Samus's extraordinary late comeback despite CJayC stating that no cheating was detected.

995.headline: Sephiroth rallies past Mega Man in an overlooked classic
995.narrative: Mega Man built a surprising early lead on Sephiroth before Sephiroth reversed the match and pulled away late. The writeup considers it one of the contest's best fights, but one overshadowed by the famous matches immediately before and after it.

996.headline: Mario edges Cloud in a historic and deeply controversial comeback
996.narrative: Cloud controlled much of the match before Mario mounted a comeback aided by unusually favorable circumstances and outside attention. The close finish, enormous board reaction, rallying, and unresolved cheating allegations made the match the writeup's choice for the greatest contest match ever.
996.anomaly_note: The writeup credits Mario's comeback partly to a Planet GameCube link and widespread vote solicitation, explicitly treating those efforts as rallying. It also describes alleged proxy voting and supposed vote-stuffing admissions, while emphasizing that the cheating claims were never proven.

997.headline: Crono upsets Snake and carries his Cinderella run onward
997.narrative: Crono's earlier warning signs became impossible to ignore when he controlled a heavily favored Solid Snake. The writeup treats the victory as the culmination of an unlikely run that had grown stronger with every round.

998.headline: Link crushes Scorpion and looks nearly unstoppable
998.narrative: Link destroyed Scorpion in a divisional final that the writeup saw as proof of the South's weakness. His continued dominance left Sephiroth as the only remaining opponent viewed as a plausible obstacle before the championship.

999.headline: Sephiroth recovers from Samus's fast start and advances
999.narrative: Samus surprised Sephiroth with a strong opening lead, but Sephiroth recovered quickly and controlled the rest of the match. Even in defeat, the writeup says Samus validated her earlier Sonic win while Sephiroth raised concerns about how he would fare against Link.

1000.headline: Mario survives Crono after vote-stuffing derails a dramatic comeback
1000.narrative: Crono nearly completed another remarkable comeback against Mario before CJayC intervened over fraudulent voting. The controversy ended Crono's Cinderella run but began the long-running Mario-Crono rivalry remembered by Board 8.
1000.anomaly_note: The writeup says Crono's comeback included blatant vote-stuffing and that CJayC removed fraudulent votes. It also discusses later statements suggesting the amount of fraudulent voting may have been larger than the number removed during the match.

1001.headline: Link overwhelms Sephiroth and effectively claims the contest
1001.narrative: Link dominated Sephiroth from the beginning, confirming fears raised by Sephiroth's earlier struggle with Samus. The writeup treats this as the match in which Link effectively secured the championship before the final was played.

1002.headline: Link beats Mario to win the first contest
1002.narrative: Link comfortably defeated Mario in a final the writeup considers anticlimactic. The result established Link as GameFAQs's strongest Nintendo character and closed a first contest successful enough to guarantee more tournaments.

1305.headline: Link opens 2003 with another overwhelming statement
1305.narrative: Link opened the 2003 contest with another enormous blowout and immediately reaffirmed his status as the entrant to beat. The writeup notes that some same-company overlap may have contributed, but not enough to diminish the statement.
1305.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link's overwhelming result may have included a small amount of SFF because AiAi was another Nintendo character, while stressing that the magnitude of the win was impressive regardless.

1306.headline: Fox routs Pikachu in an early textbook SFF result
1306.narrative: Fox routed Pikachu in a debated matchup that the writeup retrospectively considers an obvious SFF situation. The victory also ended Fox's poor first-contest seeding story by finally giving him a match win.
1306.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes Fox's decisive win over fellow Nintendo entrant Pikachu as an SFF result and argues that anti-Pokémon voting made Pikachu's position even worse.

1307.headline: Ganondorf survives Tidus as update-topic culture takes off
1307.narrative: Ganondorf survived a surprisingly strong Tidus comeback after Board 8 had largely treated the matchup as a lock. The match became especially important for popularizing dedicated update topics and exposing the gap between hardcore board expectations and the broader bracket field.

1308.headline: Magus wins comfortably but falls short of immense hype
1308.narrative: Magus won comfortably but failed to match the enormous expectations created by his pre-contest hype. The writeup says supporters blamed his low seed and kept treating him as a potential challenger to Link despite the underwhelming showing.

1309.headline: Squall surprises Jill supporters with a comfortable win
1309.narrative: Squall beat Jill far more comfortably than much of Board 8 expected after his disappointing 2002 showing. The writeup treats the result as clear evidence that his strength had changed substantially between contests.

1310.headline: Luigi wins big but cools his enormous pre-contest hype
1310.narrative: Luigi opened at an elite-looking level against Ratchet, then steadily declined as the match progressed. The writeup says the result cooled the extreme pre-contest hype around Luigi even though few considered his next match dangerous.

1311.headline: KOS-MOS upsets Crash as his contest relevance fades
1311.narrative: KOS-MOS decisively beat the favored Crash, confirming that his old platforming fame no longer guaranteed contest support. The writeup says the blowout made KOS-MOS look stronger than she really was while symbolizing Crash's decline.

1312.headline: Samus wins easily but misses the expected Nintendo blowout
1312.narrative: Samus easily beat Isaac, yet the writeup considered the margin disappointing because people expected a much harsher same-company blowout. Isaac's resistance became an enduring puzzle while Samus-over-Link speculation continued anyway.

1313.headline: CATS briefly leads Cloud and creates the CATS Army legend
1313.narrative: CATS briefly led Cloud at the opening, creating a memorable Board 8 spectacle before Cloud predictably destroyed him. The writeup treats the moment as the birth of the CATS Army and an early milestone in Cloud's long-running difficulty with the board vote.

1314.headline: Auron debuts by comfortably dispatching a favored Tails
1314.narrative: Auron comfortably beat Tails despite substantial board sentiment that favored the Sonic character. The writeup remembers the match as Auron's strong contest debut and an early indication that Tidus's unpopularity did not extend to him.

1315.headline: Bowser crushes popular upset pick Ness in his debut
1315.narrative: Bowser demolished a Ness who had been a popular upset pick, immediately overturning much of the pre-match speculation around the four-pack. The writeup remembers the scale of the blowout as one of the contest's early surprises.

1316.headline: Yoshi wins his debut but cools unrealistic expectations
1316.narrative: Yoshi beat Conker comfortably in his first contest match, but not by enough to satisfy the enormous expectations surrounding him. The writeup says the result largely ended fanciful Yoshi-over-Cloud talk while still leaving most people too confident about his chances against Bowser.

1317.headline: Aeris beats Sora in a retrospectively recognized SFF match
1317.narrative: Aeris handled Sora as expected and continued the pattern of outperforming her low seed. The writeup later came to view Sora's poor showing as an SFF result that understated his actual contest strength.
1317.anomaly_note: The writeup retrospectively identifies Aeris versus Sora as an SFF match, arguing that Sora's connection to Aeris through Kingdom Hearts made him look weaker than he would against an unrelated opponent.

1318.headline: Master Chief survives Felix amid heavy anti-Xbox sentiment
1318.narrative: Master Chief narrowly avoided an upset against Felix in a match the writeup says exposed intense anti-Xbox and anti-Halo sentiment. The result badly damaged Chief's pre-contest reputation despite the win.

1319.headline: Zero exposes Scorpion's 2002 run as misleading
1319.narrative: Zero decisively beat a Scorpion who had been heavily favored because of his surprising 2002 run. The writeup treats the result as the end of Scorpion's brief time as a serious contest threat and the start of Zero's strong career.

1320.headline: Sonic handles badly underseeded Ken despite a slow start
1320.narrative: Sonic beat a badly underseeded Ken without serious trouble, though his slow start created some concern among people hoping he could challenge Cloud. The writeup ultimately viewed the performance as acceptable given Ken's strength.

1321.headline: Mario opens the South with a routine SFF blowout
1321.narrative: Mario opened the heavily anticipated South Division by crushing Olimar. The writeup treats the result as a routine SFF blowout that revealed little about how Mario would fare against the division's elite opposition.
1321.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Mario's victory over fellow Nintendo entrant Olimar a mundane SFF beating and says SFF was in full swing during the match.

1322.headline: Shadow demolishes heavily favored Wario in a major surprise
1322.narrative: Shadow demolished a heavily favored Wario in one of the board's largest first-round surprises. The writeup says Wario's poor match picture made supporters nervous beforehand, but treats Shadow's strength and Wario's failure as the main story.

1323.headline: Kefka survives Pac-Man after the infamous Lettuce Kefka picture
1323.narrative: Kefka survived Pac-Man after an infamous match picture badly damaged confidence in the heavily hyped newcomer. Pac-Man mounted a long comeback attempt before Kefka recovered late, while the image became a lasting Board 8 running joke.
1323.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kefka's infamous 'lettuce' match picture hurt him badly, turning what had been treated as a comfortable win into a close, contested match against Pac-Man.

1324.headline: Crono cruises past Nook in an uneventful formality
1324.narrative: Crono cruised past Tom Nook in a match the writeup treats as little more than a formality before the expected Mario rematch. It then spends substantial time on Nook's more memorable connection to an unrelated Board 8 user contest.

1325.headline: Alucard handles Bomberman and moves toward the real fourpack test
1325.narrative: Alucard comfortably beat Bomberman while remaining less trusted than his previous contest results warranted. The writeup treats the victory as another steady step toward the much more debated Alucard-Kirby matchup.

1326.headline: Kirby stops Ramza but leaves doubts before Alucard
1326.narrative: Kirby beat a heavily hyped Ramza, but the writeup considered Ramza's resistance surprisingly strong for a cult newcomer. The result ended the Ramza upset talk while raising doubts about Kirby before facing Alucard.

1327.headline: Max Payne wins as the GFNW legend takes hold
1327.narrative: Max Payne beat Gordon Freeman in a match that looked close on paper but was never seriously in doubt. The writeup remembers it chiefly as the point where the long-running 'Gordon Freeman Never Wins' joke truly took hold.

1328.headline: Sephiroth crushes Raziel as the Oracle Challenge is born
1328.narrative: Sephiroth crushed Raziel exactly as expected and remained one of the division's dominant favorites. The writeup's lasting historical note is that a perfect percentage prediction around this match helped inspire the Oracle Challenge.

1329.headline: Snake routs Raiden in a severe same-series SFF match
1329.narrative: Snake routed Raiden in an expected same-series mismatch. The writeup emphasizes that the result was a severe SFF beating, though Raiden retained enough support to avoid the historically extreme percentage some expected.
1329.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Raiden was heavily SFFed by fellow Metal Gear character Solid Snake, while noting that Raiden still performed better than many expected.

1330.headline: Knuckles breaks a deadlock with Yuna through the day vote
1330.narrative: Knuckles won one of the most evenly debated first-round matches after spending much of the night in a near-stalemate with Yuna. His powerful day vote then turned the close contest into a comfortable finish.

1331.headline: Ryu crushes Duke and quietly warns the Dante backers
1331.narrative: Ryu demolished Duke Nukem far more convincingly than many expected. The writeup treats the performance as an overlooked warning that the supposedly obvious Dante-Ryu result in the next round was far from settled.

1332.headline: Dante answers Ryu's strong opener with his own rout
1332.narrative: Dante answered Ryu's impressive opener with a dominant win over Ryo Hazuki. The result restored confidence in Dante before their second-round meeting, even though the writeup retrospectively says he had been overrated.

1333.headline: Donkey Kong beats Vyse without settling the Vercetti debate
1333.narrative: Donkey Kong beat Vyse as expected but did not produce the overwhelming showing supporters wanted before a possible match with Tommy Vercetti. The writeup therefore left the once-unthinkable DK upset case alive without strongly endorsing it.

1334.headline: Vercetti beats Kite but sees his contender hype collapse
1334.narrative: Vercetti beat Kite but performed far below the level expected from a character once hyped to challenge Mega Man and Snake. The writeup says the result exposed his pre-contest reputation and made Donkey Kong a credible threat.

1335.headline: Zelda dispatches Lara as her former star power fades
1335.narrative: Zelda decisively beat a Lara Croft whose reputation had already fallen sharply from her former top-seed status. The writeup frames the loss as another sign of Lara's rapid decline while Zelda benefited from intense contemporary Zelda enthusiasm.

1336.headline: Mega Man crushes Resetti yet somehow disappoints expectations
1336.narrative: Mega Man annihilated Mr. Resetti, yet the writeup remembers the performance as a strange disappointment because expectations after 2002 were even more extreme. The match closed a first round full of upsets and inflated newcomer hype.

1337.headline: Link overwhelms Fox despite another heavy Nintendo SFF matchup
1337.narrative: Link opened the second round by overwhelming Fox and reinforcing his status as the contest favorite. The writeup acknowledges heavy Nintendo SFF but says the performance still looked dominant enough to keep repeat-title expectations intact.
1337.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly treats Link's rout of fellow Nintendo entrant Fox as an SFF result, while arguing that the size of the win remained impressive despite the overlap.

1338.headline: Magus barely survives Ganondorf after a day-long comeback battle
1338.narrative: Magus survived a dramatic Ganondorf comeback after his early lead nearly vanished during the morning vote. The razor-thin win punctured the enormous Magus-versus-Link hype even as it produced one of the contest's most memorable close matches.

1339.headline: Squall shocks Luigi and triggers a historic board meltdown
1339.narrative: Squall stunned the overwhelmingly favored Luigi and immediately turned a normal match into one of Board 8's largest explosions. The upset generated extraordinary cheating accusations and permanently changed both characters' contest reputations.
1339.anomaly_note: The writeup says Squall's upset of Luigi triggered cheating accusations on a scale rivaling any match in contest history, alongside mass account suicides, trolling, and other board chaos.

1340.headline: Samus ends KOS-MOS hype with a decisive win
1340.narrative: Samus decisively ended the brief KOS-MOS hype created by her first-round upset of Crash. The writeup saw the win as a partial recovery from Samus's disappointing opener and as evidence that Squall was unlikely to upset her next.

1341.headline: Cloud dismisses Auron in a straightforward Square SFF beating
1341.narrative: Cloud comfortably dismissed Auron in a match some had hoped could produce a same-company upset. Instead, the writeup says conventional SFF took over and strengthened the case that Cloud sat near the top of Square's hierarchy.
1341.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes Cloud's victory over fellow Final Fantasy entrant Auron as an SFF beating that overwhelmed any hoped-for reverse-SFF upset effect.

1342.headline: Bowser overturns Yoshi expectations with an SFF victory
1342.narrative: Bowser quickly erased Yoshi's brief opening lead and won a matchup most of the board had expected Yoshi to take. The writeup treats the result as both an upset of prevailing assumptions and a clear SFF performance.
1342.anomaly_note: The writeup says Bowser caught Yoshi and then laid an SFF beatdown on him, overturning expectations built from an earlier favorite-Mario-character poll.

1343.headline: Aeris comfortably ends Master Chief's overhyped first contest
1343.narrative: Aeris comfortably beat a Master Chief whose narrow escape against Felix had already destroyed most upset expectations. Chief showed some resistance after a terrible start, but the writeup treats the match mainly as another strong Aeris fourpack win.

1344.headline: Sonic survives Zero but loses his remaining aura of dominance
1344.narrative: Sonic beat Zero but looked dramatically weaker than expected as Zero steadily cut into what began as a comfortable advantage. The writeup calls it a Pyrrhic victory that effectively ended serious Sonic-over-Cloud hopes.

1345.headline: Mario beats Shadow but suddenly looks vulnerable to Crono
1345.narrative: Mario beat Shadow but performed so poorly that the result immediately fueled Crono upset talk. The writeup speculates that a reverse-SFF effect may explain Shadow's unusually strong showing, but treats the mechanism as uncertain.

1346.headline: Crono crushes Kefka as Square SFF becomes a major debate
1346.narrative: Crono obliterated a Kefka whose first-round struggle had already ended most upset expectations. The unusually severe result sparked arguments about Square SFF and set up the heavily anticipated Mario-Crono rematch.
1346.anomaly_note: The writeup retrospectively treats Crono's blowout of Kefka as an SFF match, while noting that Square SFF was still disputed and poorly understood at the time.

1347.headline: Alucard beats Kirby and wins another surprising fourpack
1347.narrative: Alucard won a heavily debated match with Kirby after an almost even opening. Though the final result looked close, the writeup says Alucard established control almost immediately and captured his fourpack for a second straight year.

1348.headline: Sephiroth crushes Max Payne and completes the South's elite trio
1348.narrative: Sephiroth demolished Max Payne in a match the writeup considered almost entirely predetermined. Its main significance was completing the path toward the long-awaited Mario-Crono-Sephiroth endgame in the South.

1349.headline: Snake repeats his Knuckles win in the first Character Battle rematch
1349.narrative: Snake comfortably beat Knuckles in the first rematch in Character Battle history, producing little suspense because the same matchup had already ended decisively the year before. The writeup treats Knuckles as another stepping stone toward Snake's eventual Mega Man test.

1350.headline: Ryu upsets Dante in an unexpectedly quiet result
1350.narrative: Ryu upset a Dante whom both the board and bracket field had largely treated as the obvious winner. The writeup remembers it as a surprisingly quiet upset because Ryu stayed in control and the board generated little outrage.

1351.headline: Vercetti survives Donkey Kong after a classic seesaw battle
1351.narrative: Vercetti and Donkey Kong traded the lead repeatedly in one of the era's best seesaw matches before Vercetti finally pulled away with the evening vote. The near-upset completed Vercetti's fall from supposed contender to obvious overhype.

1352.headline: Mega Man beats Zelda but finally looks merely mortal
1352.narrative: Mega Man beat Zelda without the usual overwhelming dominance associated with his early contest career. The writeup considered the result mildly disappointing while allowing that Zelda's strength may simply have been underestimated.

1353.headline: Link ends Magus hype despite an unexpectedly respectable showing
1353.narrative: Link ended the once-enormous Magus upset hype with a comfortable win, though Magus still performed better than expected. The writeup leaves the reason for that overperformance unresolved, mentioning both board hype and possible sprite-picture effects without settling on either.

1354.headline: Samus beats Squall as his breakout run gains legitimacy
1354.narrative: Samus beat Squall as expected, but Squall's strong showing confirmed that his earlier Luigi upset was not a fluke. The writeup notes complaints about Samus's sprite picture but does not treat the image as a demonstrated cause of the result.

1355.headline: Cloud crushes Bowser and sharply raises his title stock
1355.narrative: Cloud destroyed a Bowser whom much of the board had strongly supported, making the scale of the win especially striking. The writeup discusses a severe picture mismatch but stops short of attributing the result primarily to it.

1356.headline: Sonic survives Aeris but looks doomed against Cloud
1356.narrative: Sonic narrowly held off Aeris in another performance that confirmed how far he had slipped from his pre-2002 reputation. Aeris's strong resistance made an upcoming Sonic win over Cloud look extremely unlikely.

1357.headline: Mario survives Crono in a chaotic and controversial rematch
1357.narrative: Mario and Crono produced an enormous rematch in which Crono appeared to have the win secured before Mario erased a late lead and survived a controversially extended poll. Rallying, cheating allegations, and the disputed timing made it one of Board 8's most controversial matches.
1357.anomaly_note: The writeup describes supporters on both sides frantically rallying for votes during the late collapse of Crono's lead. It also records extensive cheating accusations around Mario's comeback, while noting that CJayC said his check found no cheating in the decisive extra period.

1358.headline: Sephiroth handles Alucard while attention remains on Mario-Crono
1358.narrative: Sephiroth dispatched Alucard in a match largely ignored because it followed the Mario-Crono controversy. The writeup mainly uses the result to strengthen Sephiroth's case before facing Mario in the divisional final.

1359.headline: Snake handles Ryu despite fears over his sprite picture
1359.narrative: Snake comfortably beat Ryu despite pre-match concern that his poor sprite image could hurt him. The writeup says the feared picture effect did not materialize here, though the performance did little to improve Snake's chances against Mega Man.

1360.headline: Mega Man crushes Vercetti and buries his old contender hype
1360.narrative: Mega Man demolished Vercetti and completed the collapse of the pre-contest hype that once had Vercetti winning the division. The writeup treats the match as an easy tune-up before Mega Man's real test against Snake.

1361.headline: Link beats Samus as Nintendo SFF ends the upset hope
1361.narrative: Link beat Samus in a long-awaited matchup that stayed competitive only briefly before Nintendo SFF took over. The writeup considers the result another sign of Link's dominance while arguing that Samus looked weaker than she really was.
1361.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says SFF took hold after Samus kept the opening close and later argues that Link SFFed her heavily enough to distort her apparent contest strength.

1362.headline: Cloud destroys Sonic and ignites serious Cloud-over-Link talk
1362.narrative: Cloud turned a briefly hopeful Sonic challenge into a devastating rout, confirming Sonic's decline and dramatically raising expectations for Cloud against Link. The writeup treats this as the point where Cloud's 2003 strength became impossible to dismiss.

1363.headline: Sephiroth demolishes Mario and crystallizes the Kingdom Hearts Factor
1363.narrative: Sephiroth unexpectedly demolished Mario in what had been expected to resemble the previous year's Mario-Cloud classic. The result became the writeup's clearest evidence yet for a broad Kingdom Hearts-era boost to several Square characters.

1364.headline: Mega Man handles Snake and earns his Sephiroth rematch
1364.narrative: Mega Man beat Snake in a steady match that produced little drama but finally sent him back to Sephiroth for a rematch of their near-upset from 2002. The writeup treats the coming Final Four as far more interesting than the match itself.

1365.headline: Cloud topples Link in the contest's defining upset
1365.narrative: Cloud shocked the contest by beating the seemingly invincible Link after taking control almost immediately and resisting the expected Zelda day-vote comeback. Heavy rallying, cheating allegations, and a disputed picture imbalance became part of the explanation for one of the contest's defining upsets.
1365.anomaly_note: The writeup says both sides engaged in heavy rallying and records widespread cheating accusations, while treating those accusations as roughly symmetric blame rather than proven fraud. It also says Link's Wind Waker image versus Cloud's Kingdom Hearts image may have cost Link a small but meaningful amount of support.

1366.headline: Sephiroth routs Mega Man and strengthens the Kingdom Hearts case
1366.narrative: Sephiroth dominated Mega Man in a rematch that had been nearly even one year earlier. The writeup treats the dramatic swing as some of the strongest evidence for the Kingdom Hearts Factor before the all-FF7 championship match.

1367.headline: Cloud beats Sephiroth to complete his championship run
1367.narrative: Cloud recovered from Sephiroth's early lead and won a final that the writeup says was less competitive than the ending suggested. It frames the result as the culmination of Cloud's strengthened post-Kingdom Hearts standing and likely same-fanbase suppression of Sephiroth.
1367.anomaly_note: The writeup says SFF likely had the most to do with Cloud beating fellow Final Fantasy VII character Sephiroth, and treats their later rematch as confirmation that Sephiroth was suppressed here.

1601.headline: Mario 3 opens the game contest with an easy rout
1601.narrative: Super Mario Bros. 3 opened the game contest with the expected rout. The writeup focuses more on the unexpectedly weak turnout and the sponsored poll above the contest than on the one-sided match itself.

1602.headline: Metroid overwhelms Pac-Man and fuels early series hype
1602.narrative: Metroid turned a mildly hyped matchup into a comfortable win and strengthened early talk that the series might contend with Zelda. The writeup attributes Pac-Man's weakness mainly to the site's younger audience, with his match picture also working against him.
1602.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pac-Man's match picture was not doing him any favors, explicitly presenting the image as another disadvantage for him against Metroid.

1603.headline: Contra exposes Phantasy Star's inflated seed with ease
1603.narrative: Contra comfortably beat an overseeded Phantasy Star in a matchup that had attracted substantial pre-match debate. The writeup treats the result as evidence that the nomination system inflated weaker-system seeds and that franchise recognition did little for Phantasy Star itself.

1604.headline: Final Fantasy crushes Pitfall and builds divisional credibility
1604.narrative: Final Fantasy crushed Pitfall in a match that was never competitive. The writeup mainly uses the result to strengthen the case that the original Final Fantasy could become a serious obstacle for Super Mario Bros. 3 later in the division.

1605.headline: Donkey Kong barely survives Duck Hunt's huge comeback
1605.narrative: Donkey Kong built what looked like a safe lead before Duck Hunt spent most of the day mounting a relentless comeback. The writeup says Donkey Kong escaped largely because time and bracket support ran out on Duck Hunt, making the match an early contest classic.

1606.headline: Zelda destroys Adventure and sparks dominance talk
1606.narrative: The Legend of Zelda annihilated the obscure Adventure and set multiple futility marks in the process. The performance immediately intensified talk that Zelda games might dominate the contest.

1607.headline: Pong dismisses River City Ransom after misleading board hype
1607.narrative: Pong easily beat River City Ransom after late board hype had tried to turn the cult favorite into a serious upset pick. The writeup treats the result as a lesson in the limits of vocal cult support against universal name recognition.

1608.headline: Tetris beats Galaga but leaves room for doubt
1608.narrative: Tetris beat Galaga as expected, but the writeup considered its performance unimpressive for much of the poll. That softness briefly encouraged speculation that Pong might have a real chance in the next round.

1609.headline: Chrono Trigger wins while its daytime weakness draws concern
1609.narrative: Chrono Trigger handled Secret of Mana but lost substantial momentum during the daytime, creating concern about how it would fare against stronger opponents. The writeup identifies that recurring voting pattern as a defining feature of Chrono Trigger's contest run.

1610.headline: Mario RPG wins a toss-up and triggers lasting board outrage
1610.narrative: Super Mario RPG recovered from an early Street Fighter II push and won a genuine toss-up. The lasting story in the writeup is the unusually persistent board outrage afterward, which turned the loss into a long-running community joke.

1611.headline: Sonic 2 routs Shining Force and fuels Mario matchup hype
1611.narrative: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 dispatched Shining Force in a predetermined mismatch. Its strong showing nevertheless encouraged Sonic supporters to argue that a classic Mario-Sonic showdown in the next round could be competitive.

1612.headline: Mario World crushes The Simpsons before its Sonic showdown
1612.narrative: Super Mario World crushed The Simpsons and reassured anyone who thought Mario's contest standing had weakened. The writeup sees the performance as a stronger warning for Sonic than many contemporary observers recognized.

1613.headline: Link to the Past extends Zelda's dominant opening run
1613.narrative: A Link to the Past obliterated Gunstar Heroes and added another emphatic result to Zelda's opening run. The writeup says the performance made the series look nearly unbeatable while also highlighting how strangely low the game's seed had been.

1614.headline: Super Metroid wins but weakens its case against Zelda
1614.narrative: Super Metroid won comfortably but failed to match the standard A Link to the Past had just set against weak opposition. The writeup treats that gap as an early sign that Super Metroid's hoped-for challenge to Zelda was already doomed.

1615.headline: Doom ends EarthBound hype and busts many brackets
1615.narrative: Doom beat the higher-seeded EarthBound after a heavily debated matchup that the writeup says was less competitive than the hype suggested. It presents the result as a bracket buster driven by mainstream recognition overcoming a dedicated cult fanbase.

1616.headline: Final Fantasy VI handles Mortal Kombat and gains credibility
1616.narrative: Final Fantasy VI comfortably defeated Mortal Kombat and began to look stronger than many observers had expected. The writeup treats the result as the first hint that the game belonged in the division's top tier rather than behind the presumed favorites.

1617.headline: Final Fantasy VII begins its title bid with domination
1617.narrative: Final Fantasy VII demolished Suikoden II in a routine opening match and looked every bit like a championship favorite. The writeup views the surrounding division largely as a waiting room for the expected showdown with Ocarina of Time.

1618.headline: Xenogears beats Pokémon after a troubled poll restart
1618.narrative: Xenogears beat Pokémon Gold and Silver after the original poll had to be restarted because of a voting bug. The writeup considers anti-Pokémon sentiment an important part of the loss while also crediting Xenogears' Square RPG appeal.

1619.headline: Final Fantasy Tactics wins while DDR earns unexpected respect
1619.narrative: Final Fantasy Tactics comfortably beat Dance Dance Revolution, though its opponent showed more support than many expected. The writeup says that resistance initially made Tactics look vulnerable before later matches revised the interpretation.

1620.headline: Metal Gear Solid handles Resident Evil before a tougher test
1620.narrative: Metal Gear Solid comfortably dispatched Resident Evil and reinforced its status as one of the strongest non-Nintendo, non-Square properties on the site. The result set up what looked on paper like a very even meeting with Final Fantasy Tactics.

1621.headline: Symphony survives Perfect Dark but weakens its GoldenEye case
1621.narrative: Symphony of the Night beat Perfect Dark after a matchup surrounded by elaborate pre-match strength theories. A long poll freeze interrupted the action, and Perfect Dark's late resistance left the writeup convinced that Castlevania had little chance against GoldenEye next.

1622.headline: GoldenEye routs Panzer Dragoon and settles the strength debate
1622.narrative: GoldenEye easily beat Panzer Dragoon Saga and validated the view that it was much stronger than Perfect Dark in this contest setting. The writeup treats the match mainly as confirmation that Symphony of the Night faced an overwhelming next-round obstacle.

1623.headline: Mario 64 cruises while its harsh bracket draw looms
1623.narrative: Super Mario 64 destroyed the obscure NiGHTS as expected. The writeup's main point is that Mario 64 was badly underseeded and deserved a much better fate than an immediate collision with Ocarina of Time.

1624.headline: Ocarina crushes Fallout while the FFVII comparison intensifies
1624.narrative: Ocarina of Time crushed Fallout 2 and extended Zelda's dominant start. The writeup nevertheless argues that comparison with Final Fantasy VII's opener already favored the Square game in their anticipated divisional showdown.

1625.headline: StarCraft topples Halo after an internet-wide voting war
1625.narrative: StarCraft overturned Halo in one of the contest's defining first-round battles after both fanbases drew outside support into the poll. The writeup treats the result as proof that Halo was badly overseeded, StarCraft badly underseeded, and the StarCraft fanbase capable of changing the entire division.
1625.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes mass Battle.net spamming, Xbox Live and Bungie involvement, and outside forces being brought in from across the internet to vote for both sides, with StarCraft ultimately benefiting most.

1626.headline: Kingdom Hearts survives SoulCalibur but loses its contender aura
1626.narrative: Kingdom Hearts barely recovered from SoulCalibur after entering the contest with much greater expectations. The match also coincided with a major site-layout change, and the writeup treats the narrow escape as evidence that Kingdom Hearts was the contest's biggest disappointment.

1627.headline: Wind Waker wins cleanly and emerges as divisional favorite
1627.narrative: The Wind Waker comfortably beat Skies of Arcadia and posted the clearest opening result in an otherwise chaotic division. The writeup still considered the performance modest by Zelda standards, but enough to make Wind Waker the provisional divisional favorite.

1628.headline: Metroid Prime beats Half-Life despite a respectable early fight
1628.narrative: Metroid Prime beat Half-Life after the PC game kept the opening portion more competitive than Gordon Freeman's contest reputation suggested. The writeup treats the result as another chapter in the GFNW joke while giving Half-Life credit for showing real strength.

1629.headline: Tactics Advance wins a quiet match and inspires little confidence
1629.narrative: Final Fantasy Tactics Advance beat Fire Emblem in a match the writeup remembers mainly for very weak interest and turnout. The victory did little to inspire confidence, with the result framed as proof that Tactics Advance would fold against the first serious threat.

1630.headline: Final Fantasy X wins but loses ground in divisional projections
1630.narrative: Final Fantasy X comfortably beat Shenmue but failed to look as strong as expected for a divisional favorite. The writeup says the result shifted the perceived edge toward The Wind Waker while leaving the division unsettled.

1631.headline: Vice City beats KOTOR in an unusually extended poll
1631.narrative: Vice City beat Knights of the Old Republic during an extended poll disrupted by site changes and downtime. The writeup says the win created serious second-round hype, while the unusual poll conditions made its true strength difficult to judge.

1632.headline: Melee survives MGS2 and inspires an enduring board phrase
1632.narrative: Super Smash Bros. Melee beat Metal Gear Solid 2 but looked much shakier than its seed suggested. The writeup credits Metal Gear Solid 2 with being underestimated and remembers the match for inspiring the joking phrase "Ulti-Style Blowout."

1633.headline: Mario 3 crushes Metroid and reasserts divisional control
1633.narrative: Super Mario Bros. 3 demolished Metroid and reclaimed the apparent favorite's position in the old-school division. The writeup treats the result as a straightforward show of strength before the eventual clash with Zelda.

1634.headline: Final Fantasy handles Contra and keeps Mario pressure alive
1634.narrative: Final Fantasy handled Contra convincingly and continued to look stronger than its place in the bracket suggested. The writeup emphasizes how much faith bracketmakers placed in the Final Fantasy name and builds anticipation for its meeting with Mario 3.

1635.headline: Zelda demolishes Donkey Kong and deepens series dominance
1635.narrative: The Legend of Zelda flattened Donkey Kong and extended the series' unbeaten, dominant start. The writeup portrays Donkey Kong as an especially unreliable Nintendo property and says the result made an all-Zelda late bracket feel increasingly plausible.

1636.headline: Tetris beats Pong as the match picture steals attention
1636.narrative: Tetris comfortably beat Pong in an otherwise forgettable match. The writeup remembers the poll primarily for the widely loved paddle-versus-block match picture and for another weak turnout in a division already viewed as filler before the heavyweights met.

1637.headline: Chrono Trigger advances while its daytime slide continues
1637.narrative: Chrono Trigger beat Super Mario RPG but again lost substantial strength during the day. The writeup says the recurring pattern kept alive doubts about Chrono Trigger's ability to survive stronger opponents later in the division.

1638.headline: Mario World crushes Sonic and becomes a Chrono threat
1638.narrative: Super Mario World crushed Sonic the Hedgehog 2 in a matchup many had expected to become the classic Mario-Sonic duel. The writeup treats the decisive result as proof that Mario World was a genuine threat to Chrono Trigger.

1639.headline: Link to the Past crushes Super Metroid and alarms rivals
1639.narrative: A Link to the Past demolished Super Metroid and delivered another startlingly strong Zelda result. The writeup says the margin transformed widespread Zelda confidence into genuine concern that the series might overwhelm the entire contest.

1640.headline: Final Fantasy VI beats Doom and joins the divisional race
1640.narrative: Final Fantasy VI handled Doom as expected, but the important story was how closely its apparent strength now matched Chrono Trigger and A Link to the Past. The writeup says the division had become a genuine multi-game race rather than the expected two-game collision.

1641.headline: Final Fantasy VII crushes Xenogears on its expected path
1641.narrative: Final Fantasy VII overwhelmed Xenogears in another routine step toward the expected Ocarina of Time showdown. The writeup treats the only real drama as measuring how convincingly the tournament favorite could dispatch familiar Square opposition.

1642.headline: Metal Gear Solid survives Tactics amid a disputed finish
1642.narrative: Metal Gear Solid and Final Fantasy Tactics traded tiny leads throughout an exceptionally tight match before Metal Gear Solid escaped at the end. The writeup considers the finish controversial because a large site advertisement and a suspicious late vote jump left the author unwilling to treat the result as fully credible.
1642.anomaly_note: The writeup calls Metal Gear Solid's late push suspicious, questions the credibility of the final result, and says the unexplained last-minute vote jump should have been investigated, while acknowledging there was no proof of cheating.

1643.headline: GoldenEye beats Castlevania and settles the overhyped triangle
1643.narrative: GoldenEye comfortably beat Symphony of the Night and ended the elaborate pre-match debate over that portion of the bracket. The writeup says Castlevania's earlier struggle with Perfect Dark had already revealed the mismatch and confirms GoldenEye as the clearly stronger property.

1644.headline: Ocarina crushes Mario 64 in an SFF-heavy showdown
1644.narrative: Ocarina of Time crushed the highly regarded Super Mario 64 and added another emphatic result to Zelda's unbeaten run. The writeup treats the same-fanbase matchup as evidence that Ocarina might be closer to Final Fantasy VII than earlier results had suggested.
1644.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes Ocarina of Time versus fellow Nintendo icon Super Mario 64 as a match riddled with SFF when comparing it with Final Fantasy VII's same-round result.

1645.headline: StarCraft beats Kingdom Hearts and validates its Cinderella run
1645.narrative: StarCraft beat Kingdom Hearts from start to finish and proved that its Halo victory had not been a fluke. The writeup casts Kingdom Hearts as the contest's biggest disappointment and StarCraft as a fanbase that could no longer be dismissed as a novelty upset.

1646.headline: Wind Waker beats Metroid Prime in a weak-turnout SFF match
1646.narrative: The Wind Waker beat Metroid Prime after the two Nintendo games stayed relatively close until the morning vote created separation. The writeup views the SFF matchup and weak turnout as further signs that Wind Waker was the vulnerable member of Zelda's otherwise dominant contest run.
1646.anomaly_note: The writeup groups Wind Waker versus fellow Nintendo title Metroid Prime with the contest's other SFF matches while discussing its unusually weak turnout.

1647.headline: Final Fantasy X advances but again fails to convince
1647.narrative: Final Fantasy X beat Tactics Advance as expected but again failed to deliver the dominant performance its supporters wanted. The writeup says the result deepened the sense that Division 128 had no trustworthy favorite.

1648.headline: Melee survives Vice City as the division stays unsettled
1648.narrative: Super Smash Bros. Melee pulled away from Vice City after an early deadlock and survived another difficult matchup. The writeup gives Vice City credit but says the weak turnout and Melee's repeated struggles left the division without an obvious favorite.

1649.headline: Mario 3 survives Final Fantasy but looks vulnerable
1649.narrative: Super Mario Bros. 3 beat Final Fantasy but looked much less dominant than expected for the division's presumed favorite. The writeup argues that strong loyalty to the Final Fantasy name explains much of the resistance while leaving Mario's prospects against Zelda less secure.

1650.headline: Zelda routs Tetris and strengthens its divisional favorite status
1650.narrative: Zelda dismissed Tetris and looked like the clear favorite to take its division. The writeup treats the result as another step in Zelda's dominant opening run, with Mario 3 offering the only real counterargument.

1651.headline: Chrono Trigger dismisses Mario World and restores contender status
1651.narrative: Chrono Trigger turned a heavily debated matchup into a comfortable win and restored confidence after earlier daytime weakness. The writeup says Super Mario World had looked like a plausible upset pick, but Chrono Trigger established itself as a true divisional favorite.

1652.headline: Link to the Past survives Final Fantasy VI's early challenge
1652.narrative: Final Fantasy VI's sustained early lead punctured Zelda's aura of invincibility before A Link to the Past recovered and pulled away. The writeup also remembers the notoriously poor official artwork as an impetus for later user-created match pictures.

1653.headline: Final Fantasy VII crushes Metal Gear Solid and seizes favorite status
1653.narrative: Final Fantasy VII crushed Metal Gear Solid and, in the writeup's view, became the unmistakable favorite for the entire contest. The performance was framed as a direct challenge to Ocarina of Time to show comparable strength the next day.

1654.headline: Ocarina wins easily but fails to answer Final Fantasy VII
1654.narrative: Ocarina of Time handled GoldenEye easily, but the writeup judged the showing insufficient to answer Final Fantasy VII's previous performance. The match is remembered mainly as the final setup for the division's anticipated showdown.

1655.headline: Starcraft rallies past Wind Waker and extends its miracle run
1655.narrative: Starcraft shocked The Wind Waker with another late comeback, extending its improbable run and ending Zelda's unbeaten start. The writeup credits Battle.net rallying for making the difference and treats the result as Starcraft's arrival as a legitimate contest force.
1655.anomaly_note: The writeup attributes Starcraft's decisive late comeback to organized Battle.net promotion and heavy Saturday-night traffic. It explicitly rejects cheating as the explanation for this particular match.

1656.headline: Melee edges Final Fantasy X and overturns old expectations
1656.narrative: Melee overturned the old assumption that Final Fantasy X would beat it comfortably. After an early lead, a comeback, and long stretches of near-even voting, Melee held off the late Square vote and advanced to face Starcraft.

1657.headline: Mario 3 beats Zelda and ends its early aura
1657.narrative: Super Mario Bros. 3 won a highly anticipated divisional final with surprising ease and further ended Zelda's early aura of invincibility. The writeup treats the matchup as a clear case where shared Nintendo support favored Mario.
1657.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says SFF finally worked against a Zelda title, with Super Mario Bros. 3 benefiting in the all-Nintendo matchup against the original Zelda.

1658.headline: Chrono Trigger survives an all-time duel with Link to the Past
1658.narrative: Chrono Trigger and A Link to the Past stayed virtually dead even for hours, repeatedly answering each other's small pushes. The writeup calls it one of the contest's greatest wire-to-wire matches before Chrono Trigger finally separated itself late.

1659.headline: Final Fantasy VII handles Ocarina in the anticipated showdown
1659.narrative: Final Fantasy VII beat Ocarina of Time without the drama expected from the contest's supposed true final. The writeup treats the result as confirmation of Final Fantasy VII's superiority in this field and as another sign of Zelda's sudden collapse.

1660.headline: Melee ends Starcraft's run amid rallying and cheating controversy
1660.narrative: Melee ended Starcraft's Cinderella run in a chaotic divisional final dominated by outside promotion, flame wars, and a detected cheating surge. The writeup remembers the match as both a strong Melee win and a damaging controversy around Starcraft's run.
1660.anomaly_note: The writeup says Starcraft was promoted through Battle.net and multiple Starcraft sites, while a separate sudden proxy-vote surge was identified as cheating. The controversy cast doubt over the legitimacy of parts of Starcraft's run even though Melee still won.

1661.headline: Chrono Trigger wins an anticlimactic Mario 3 semifinal
1661.narrative: The hoped-for third Mario-versus-Crono-style classic never materialized. Chrono Trigger took control after the opening exchange and stayed ahead, producing an anticlimactic semifinal despite the rivalry surrounding it.

1662.headline: Final Fantasy VII brushes aside Melee on its finals path
1662.narrative: Final Fantasy VII dispatched Melee in a semifinal the writeup considered essentially predetermined. Melee's failure to make the match competitive reinforced the contemporary belief that it could not challenge an elite game.

1663.headline: Final Fantasy VII defeats Chrono Trigger for the championship
1663.narrative: Chrono Trigger briefly resisted, but Final Fantasy VII ultimately controlled the championship match as expected. The writeup spends more time reflecting on the contest itself than on a final it considered straightforward.

1718.headline: Link crushes CATS and opens the Link-Cloud comparison
1718.narrative: Link obliterated joke entrant CATS after an early poll glitch obscured the opening votes. The writeup's main interest is that CATS gave Link and Cloud a common opponent, immediately fueling comparisons between the two championship favorites.

1719.headline: Ganondorf beats Alucard in a matchup of underseeded characters
1719.narrative: Ganondorf beat Alucard in a respectable matchup between two characters the writeup considered badly underseeded. Much of the discussion centers on the bracket apparently being arranged to produce Link versus Ganondorf in the next round.

1720.headline: Yoshi routs Ryo as his contest decline continues
1720.narrative: Yoshi routed Ryo Hazuki in a result the writeup sees mainly as further evidence of Ryo's decline into contest fodder. It argues that a character losing this badly to a mid-level Nintendo entrant no longer merits repeated appearances.

1721.headline: Luigi beats Pac-Man but raises concerns before Yoshi
1721.narrative: Luigi beat Pac-Man in a routine match but looked weaker than the writeup expected, raising concern before his heavily debated meeting with Yoshi. Pac-Man, meanwhile, is portrayed as a fading former top seed still capable of respectable support.

1722.headline: Magus crushes Luca Blight as cult support falls short
1722.narrative: Magus dominated Luca Blight in a low-interest match before his difficult second-round draw. The writeup uses Luca's weak showing and the quiet poll to argue that vocal cult support does not translate into broad contest strength.

1723.headline: Crono crushes Conker and advances toward another Mario rematch
1723.narrative: Crono demolished Conker and strengthened the argument that his previous result against Kefka did not require an SFF explanation. The writeup also criticizes Crono's seeding as an obvious attempt to force another Mario-Crono matchup.

1724.headline: Bowser crushes Guybrush in another obvious bracket setup
1724.narrative: Bowser overwhelmed Guybrush in a matchup the writeup considers a product of manipulated seeding rather than competitive bracket design. Guybrush is portrayed as overseeded fodder, while Bowser's reward is an intentionally unfavorable Mario matchup.

1725.headline: Mario finally delivers a convincing non-Nintendo opening blowout
1725.narrative: Mario finally delivered the kind of overwhelming first-round performance the writeup had long expected from him against a non-Nintendo opponent. The result is used to reassess earlier supposedly weak Mario showings as evidence that those opponents were stronger than believed.

1726.headline: Mega Man wins while Earthworm Jim earns affectionate praise
1726.narrative: Mega Man comfortably defeated Earthworm Jim, though the writeup spends much of its time celebrating Jim as a welcome contest newcomer and fan favorite. It ultimately judges Mega Man's showing impressive rather than weak.

1727.headline: Tidus controls a heavily hyped matchup with Shadow
1727.narrative: Tidus won the contest's first heavily debated matchup, taking control early enough that Shadow's later resistance never became a real comeback. The writeup says the final closeness overstated the drama but still gave both characters credit for holding up outside their expected voting periods.

1728.headline: Vercetti wins while Max Payne restores some contest credibility
1728.narrative: Tommy Vercetti beat Max Payne, but the writeup considers Max's respectable showing the more important result. Max avoided the feared same-company collapse and strengthened his case for remaining in the field, while Vercetti looked weaker than his old hype suggested.

1729.headline: Zero overwhelms Proto Man in a same-series SFF matchup
1729.narrative: Zero dominated Proto Man in a same-series matchup whose result the writeup warns should not be used to dismiss Proto Man as ordinary fodder. It treats the match as another example of the bracket manufacturing predictable company-based pairings.
1729.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes Zero versus Proto Man as a first-round SFF blowout within the Mega Man family, arguing that Proto Man's poor result understates his standalone strength.

1730.headline: Frog barely survives Liquid Snake in an instant classic
1730.narrative: Frog and Liquid Snake unexpectedly produced a wire-to-wire classic, repeatedly trading momentum and staying nearly dead even for hours. Frog finally created a small late cushion and barely survived Liquid's last push, giving both newcomers immediate contest credibility.

1731.headline: Master Chief crushes Crash and raises his contest stock
1731.narrative: Master Chief crushed Crash Bandicoot and looked far more formidable than the site's usual anti-Xbox reputation suggested. The writeup focuses equally on Master Chief's rising stock and Crash's dramatic fall from former high seed to expendable fodder.

1732.headline: Knuckles recovers from Kefka's surprising early resistance
1732.narrative: Kefka surprised the board by leading early and forcing Knuckles to recover despite expectations of an easy Knuckles win. The writeup ultimately treats Knuckles' showing as disappointing and debates whether Kefka's picture and broader Square support helped explain the resistance.
1732.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kefka's recurring lettuce picture may have helped him attract unusually strong early support, before Knuckles took control later in the match.

1733.headline: Snake destroys Tanner and creates a lasting fodder benchmark
1733.narrative: Solid Snake annihilated Tanner in a blowout the writeup treats as evidence of Tanner's exceptional weakness rather than Snake's true ceiling. The mismatch became a lasting Board 8 reference point for hopeless new entrants and entertainingly lopsided polls.

1734.headline: Cloud routs Duke despite a memorable milk-carton picture boost
1734.narrative: Cloud still routed Duke Nukem, but Duke's memorable milk-carton picture gave the underdog an unusual opening burst and complicated early Link-Cloud comparisons. The writeup frames the match as the start of a contest-long contest between the two favorites' performances.
1734.anomaly_note: The writeup says Duke Nukem's milk-carton match picture drew humorous support, helping him take an early lead and plausibly contributing to Cloud's slight underperformance.

1735.headline: Vyse handles Laharl in a low-stakes cult-character matchup
1735.narrative: Vyse beat Laharl without much difficulty in what the writeup dismisses as a matchup between two cult characters with limited broader support. Vyse's previous contest exposure and greater familiarity are presented as enough to make the result predictable.

1736.headline: Kirby comfortably dispatches Kain in another routine opener
1736.narrative: Kirby comfortably beat Kain in another routine early-round result. The writeup treats the match mainly as evidence that Legacy of Kain characters occupy contest slots without showing enough strength to justify them.

1737.headline: Squall beats Bomberman but raises new strength concerns
1737.narrative: Squall beat Bomberman but performed noticeably below the writeup's expectations from the previous year's standings. The result raised doubts about whether Squall had lost strength and reinforced frustration with a bracket designed to funnel him toward Cloud.

1738.headline: Ness exposes the hype around Jak with a convincing win
1738.narrative: Ness turned a heavily debated matchup into a convincing victory over Jak. The writeup argues that the board overvalued mainstream sales and undervalued how well a cult RPG character known to GameFAQs users could perform against another weak 3D platformer.

1739.headline: Auron crushes expectations against Scorpion and boosts his stock
1739.narrative: Auron beat Scorpion much more decisively than prior standings suggested and suddenly looked substantially stronger than expected. The writeup interprets the result mainly through possible distortion in Auron's previous Cloud matchup and Scorpion's continuing decline.

1740.headline: Vivi surprises Donkey Kong and makes an immediate impact
1740.narrative: Vivi turned a supposedly close match into a decisive win over Donkey Kong, immediately establishing himself as a serious newcomer. The writeup sees the result as both evidence of Vivi's appeal and another demonstration that Donkey Kong's icon status does not translate reliably into contest strength.

1741.headline: Sephiroth obliterates Sly in a predetermined Midgar matchup
1741.narrative: Sephiroth obliterated Sly Cooper in a match the writeup considers entirely predetermined. Its main complaint is that the company-based division reduced Sephiroth's early path to meaningless setup matches before the expected confrontation with Cloud.

1742.headline: Sonic crushes Terry as the Chaos Division begins
1742.narrative: Sonic comfortably crushed Terry Bogard in another predetermined first-round match. The writeup's greater interest is that the Chaos Division finally introduced a section of the bracket with genuine uncertainty about later rounds.

1743.headline: Ryu beats KOS-MOS while Samus emerges as the bigger story
1743.narrative: Ryu beat KOS-MOS as expected, but the writeup uses the result mainly to infer that Samus had grown much stronger than older standings indicated. That implication sharply reduced the plausibility of Sonic upsetting her later in the division.

1744.headline: Tails upsets Viewtiful Joe and finally earns a win
1744.narrative: Tails upset heavily favored Viewtiful Joe and finally earned his first contest win. The writeup says earlier results had begun to expose Tails as underestimated, but the reversal still destroyed many expectations and became a notable prediction upset.

1745.headline: Dante destroys Ratchet in another routine first-round mismatch
1745.narrative: Dante destroyed Ratchet in another straightforward opening match, though the writeup warns against reading too much into the margin. Ratchet is grouped with the contest's other badly performing 3D platformer characters rather than treated as evidence of elite Dante strength.

1746.headline: Sora handles HK-47 but leaves his true strength unresolved
1746.narrative: Sora beat newcomer HK-47 comfortably, but the writeup says the matchup offered little reliable information because HK-47 had no contest baseline. Attention immediately shifted to whether Sora's previous results had understated his real strength before the next round.

1747.headline: Ryu survives Jill after a glitch, restart, and marathon battle
1747.narrative: Ryu Hayabusa and Jill Valentine produced a celebrated marathon after a server glitch forced their fiercely contested poll to be restarted. The second poll featured another series of major swings before Ryu survived Jill's final comeback attempt by the narrowest of margins.

1748.headline: Sam Fisher extends GFNW but looks weak doing it
1748.narrative: Sam Fisher extended the Gordon Freeman Never Wins joke, but Freeman's unexpectedly competitive opening made Fisher look weak in his own right. The writeup treats the match more as another chapter in Freeman's losing legend than as a strong Fisher performance.

1749.headline: Samus crushes Lara and reveals a dramatic strength surge
1749.narrative: Samus demolished former top seed Lara Croft far more decisively than the writeup expected, turning an obvious win into a major statement about Samus's rising strength. Lara's showing is framed as another step in a steep decline from her early contest status.

1750.headline: Link obliterates Ganondorf in a historic SFF mismatch
1750.narrative: Link annihilated Ganondorf so thoroughly that the writeup treats the result as both a historic SFF extreme and a championship statement. Ganondorf's standalone strength effectively vanished against the flagship character of his own series.
1750.anomaly_note: The writeup calls Link's destruction of fellow Zelda character Ganondorf the largest SFF beating yet seen, arguing that Ganondorf's normal strength was almost completely suppressed by Link.

1751.headline: Yoshi beats Luigi in a predictable Nintendo SFF matchup
1751.narrative: Yoshi beat Luigi in a heavily debated Nintendo matchup that ultimately followed the available statistical clues more closely than the hype suggested. The writeup calls the result disappointingly predictable despite the same-fanbase conditions.
1751.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes Yoshi versus Luigi as an SFF affair between Nintendo characters, though it notes that older extrapolated standings still predicted the matchup unusually well.

1752.headline: Crono crushes Magus in another severe same-series SFF match
