1752.narrative: Crono crushed Magus in a matchup the writeup considers another casualty of the company-based bracket. Magus briefly led with Board 8 support, but the eventual SFF blowout left no useful opportunity to test his real strength.
1752.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Magus was hit by SFF against fellow Chrono Trigger character Crono, making the lopsided result a poor measure of Magus's standalone strength.

1753.headline: Mario routs Bowser in another bracket-driven SFF mismatch
1753.narrative: Mario routed Bowser in another predetermined Hyrule Division matchup, with the writeup again criticizing the bracket for sacrificing strong villains to company-based pairings. The result's main use was as an imperfect SFF comparison before Mario met Crono.
1753.anomaly_note: The writeup says Bowser was SFF'd heavily by Mario in their same-franchise matchup, and treats the result mainly as a distorted comparison point for the upcoming Mario-Crono rematch.

1754.headline: Mega Man crushes Tidus and vindicates Heroic Mario
1754.narrative: Mega Man demolished Tidus far more decisively than most of Board 8 expected, vindicating Heroic Mario's unusually confident prediction. The writeup treats Tidus's collapse as one of the contest's hardest results to explain.

1755.headline: Zero handles Vercetti and completes the Mega Man setup
1755.narrative: Zero handled Vercetti almost exactly as Board 8 expected in a match the writeup calls one of the contest's dullest. Its main significance was completing the obvious setup for Mega Man versus Zero.

1756.headline: Frog survives Master Chief in a controversial all-time classic
1756.narrative: Frog survived Master Chief in an all-time classic filled with huge momentum swings and a frantic finish. The writeup celebrates the drama while also arguing that outside Halo promotion and rampant multi-voting make the true result impossible to separate cleanly from the controversy.
1756.anomaly_note: The writeup says Halo sites linked to the poll during Master Chief's comeback, creating an outside rally. It also explicitly describes blatant multi-voting on both sides, especially in the final hour.

1757.headline: Snake beats Knuckles again as the rematch fatigue peaks
1757.narrative: Solid Snake beat Knuckles yet again, but the writeup is mostly exasperated that the same second-round pairing kept recurring. Knuckles looked better than in their earlier meetings, leaving open whether he improved or Snake declined.

1758.headline: Cloud beats Vyse but loses ground in the Link comparison
1758.narrative: Cloud disposed of Vyse exactly as expected, leaving little to discuss beyond comparisons with Link. The writeup argues that merely meeting expectations was no longer enough because Link had been exceeding his own.

1759.headline: Squall beats Kirby after the match picture shifts momentum
1759.narrative: Squall beat Kirby in another predictable Midgar match, though Kirby performed better than expected. The writeup's main curiosity is that Squall only began separating after the match picture appeared.
1759.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kirby and Squall were dead even before the match picture appeared, after which Squall began pulling away, and explicitly suggests that the picture may have mattered.

1760.headline: Auron beats Ness in another hard-to-read Midgar result
1760.narrative: Auron beat Ness in a result everyone expected, but Ness performed better than the old projections suggested. The writeup treats the outcome as another example of the bracket making individual strength difficult to interpret.

1761.headline: Sephiroth advances while Vivi resists the expected Square squeeze
1761.narrative: Sephiroth beat Vivi comfortably, but Vivi held up better than many expected against a fellow Square entrant. The writeup uses the result to argue that Square fanbases are less easily compressed than Nintendo fanbases.

1762.headline: Sonic beats Ryu but fails to answer the Samus surge
1762.narrative: Sonic beat Ryu without serious danger, but the writeup saw the performance as insufficient to threaten a surging Samus. The result reinforced the sense that Sonic had remained steady while Samus had improved.

1763.headline: Dante dispatches Tails in a routine second-round win
1763.narrative: Dante eliminated Tails in a match the writeup considered completely predictable and largely uninteresting. Its only real distinction was finally carrying Dante beyond the second round.

1764.headline: Sora routs Ryu Hayabusa in a major surprise
1764.narrative: Sora turned a matchup many expected Ryu Hayabusa to control into one of the contest's biggest surprises. The writeup treats the decisive win as proof that Sora had made an enormous jump in strength since the previous year.

1765.headline: Samus crushes Fisher and takes command of Chaos
1765.narrative: Samus annihilated Sam Fisher so thoroughly that early voters briefly suspected a broken poll. The writeup treats the blowout as confirmation that Samus was surging and had become the clear favorite to take the Chaos division.

1766.headline: Link overwhelms Yoshi in harsher-than-expected SFF
1766.narrative: Link destroyed Yoshi in a predictable same-company matchup, but the degree of suppression surprised even people expecting SFF. The writeup treats the result as another intimidating sign of Link's championship strength.
1766.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Link versus Yoshi a straight SFF match and says the fanbase effect was even harsher than most expected, heavily suppressing Yoshi.

1767.headline: Crono finally beats Mario in an anticlimactic revenge match
1767.narrative: Crono finally defeated Mario after their two legendary earlier meetings, but the long-awaited rematch was anticlimactic. Crono controlled the match while the writeup framed the result as overdue revenge and the likely end of the rivalry's classic era.

1768.headline: Mega Man beats Zero as the expected SFF barely appears
1768.narrative: Mega Man beat Zero as expected, but Zero resisted far better than a typical same-family opponent. The writeup argues that their distinct series fanbases may explain why the anticipated SFF barely appeared and why Mega Man looked vulnerable afterward.

1769.headline: Snake survives Frog but suffers another damaging performance
1769.narrative: Solid Snake survived Frog, but Frog's ability to stay competitive made Snake look like one of the contest's biggest disappointments. The writeup uses the match to criticize overly literal reliance on extrapolated standings.

1770.headline: Cloud dominates Squall in a predictable SFF matchup
1770.narrative: Cloud easily beat Squall in a heavily shared-fanbase matchup, but the result did little to improve his standing against Link. The writeup remembers the match mainly as another predictable step toward the planned final.
1770.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly frames Cloud versus Squall as a matchup with a massive amount of SFF, with Cloud dominating the fellow Final Fantasy entrant.

1771.headline: Sephiroth beats Auron but loses ground to Cloud
1771.narrative: Sephiroth beat Auron exactly as the bracket seemed designed to produce, leaving little suspense. The writeup's main takeaway is that Sephiroth looked clearly weaker than Cloud against a common opponent.

1772.headline: Sonic beats Dante as a bad picture muddies the comparison
1772.narrative: Sonic beat Dante in another predictable Chaos match and briefly renewed hope that he could challenge Samus. The writeup immediately tempers that optimism by pointing to Dante's poor picture as a possible reason for Sonic's apparent overperformance.
1772.anomaly_note: The writeup says Dante's match picture was exceptionally poor and suggests it may explain why Sonic performed better than the old projections expected.

1773.headline: Samus handles Sora and reinforces her Chaos advantage
1773.narrative: Samus dispatched Sora without drama and quickly erased the renewed optimism around Sonic. The writeup views the match as confirmation that Samus should win the division comfortably, even if Cloud remained beyond her reach.

1774.headline: Link crushes Crono and strengthens his championship favorite status
1774.narrative: Link crushed Crono in another late-round match whose winner was never seriously in doubt. The writeup treats the result as overwhelming evidence that Link had improved and remained well ahead of Cloud entering the final stages.

1775.headline: Mega Man beats Snake again as Snake's decline continues
1775.narrative: Mega Man beat Solid Snake in a repeat of the previous year's divisional final, with the writeup treating Snake's showing as another major flop. It also mocks the persistent tendency to underestimate Mega Man in bracket predictions.

1776.headline: Cloud handles Sephiroth and restores confidence before Link
1776.narrative: Cloud defeated Sephiroth comfortably despite the rematch carrying at least some plausible upset intrigue. The writeup says the win restored confidence in Cloud just before the expected showdown with Link.

1777.headline: Samus decisively settles her old rivalry with Sonic
1777.narrative: Samus decisively settled her famous rivalry with Sonic after their controversial classic two years earlier. The writeup credits Samus's run of new games and Sonic's stagnation, while dismissing excuses for the lopsided rematch.

1778.headline: Link destroys Mega Man and all but claims favorite status
1778.narrative: Link demolished Mega Man and effectively ended any remaining uncertainty about the contest favorite. The writeup attributes part of the rout to SFF but argues that Link's broader rise in strength was the more important story.
1778.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says there was a definite degree of SFF in Link's overwhelming win over Mega Man, though it argues Link's own rise mattered even more.

1779.headline: Cloud ends Samus's brief resistance and reaches the final
1779.narrative: Samus briefly made the semifinal look interesting with an early lead, but Cloud quickly took control and advanced as expected. The writeup treats the rest of the match as little more than preparation for the long-planned Link final.

1780.headline: Link avenges Cloud loss and wins the championship
1780.narrative: Link avenged his previous loss to Cloud and confirmed the strength he had shown throughout the contest. Cloud briefly threatened a comeback, but Link's daytime surge settled the championship without the picture excuses that had shadowed their earlier meeting.

1989.headline: Bowser crushes Pyramid Head to open the villains contest
1989.narrative: Bowser opened the villains contest by obliterating Pyramid Head, whose nomination the writeup credits largely to a dedicated Board 8 supporter. The result immediately placed Pyramid Head among the weakest entrants the contest had seen.

1990.headline: Sigma beats Andross but immediately loses his contender hype
1990.narrative: Sigma beat Andross but performed far worse than the pre-contest hype around Mega Man X suggested. The writeup calls the win pyrrhic and treats it as an early warning that Sigma had little chance against Bowser.

1991.headline: Ocelot beats Nemesis but sends his own stock tumbling
1991.narrative: Revolver Ocelot beat Nemesis but looked much weaker than Board 8 expected, throwing his projected path through the division into doubt. The writeup spends much of the match reopening arguments about Nemesis, Wesker, and Dr. Wily rather than celebrating Ocelot's win.

1992.headline: Wily handles Ultros and gains momentum before Ocelot
1992.narrative: Dr. Wily handled Ultros cleanly and looked stronger than Ocelot had the previous day. The writeup treats the match mostly as a preview that shifted confidence toward Wily in their looming second-round meeting.

1993.headline: Sephiroth destroys Ramirez and looks untouchable
1993.narrative: Sephiroth annihilated Ramirez in a deliberately lopsided matchup born from a Board 8 request. The writeup treats the result as confirmation that the overwhelming pre-contest favorite showed no sign of vulnerability.

1994.headline: Vergil beats Ghaleon after a disastrous picture hurts the underdog
1994.narrative: Vergil comfortably beat Ghaleon after a late wave of debate had given the cult RPG villain some support. The writeup argues that Ghaleon's terrible picture only made an already difficult matchup worse.
1994.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ghaleon's exceptionally poor match picture effectively erased whatever upset chance he had, while Vergil received the much more flattering image.

1995.headline: Lavos beats Mother Brain as the unexpected closeness raises questions
1995.narrative: Lavos beat Mother Brain as expected, but the match was considerably more competitive than many anticipated. The writeup uses Mother Brain's resistance mainly to raise expectations for Ridley in the later Ridley-Diablo matchup.

1996.headline: Liquid Snake crushes Tenpenny and validates his early hype
1996.narrative: Liquid Snake crushed Officer Tenpenny and initially justified the lofty reputation he had gained from his close 2004 loss to Frog. The writeup notes that nothing in this opener hinted at the weakness Liquid would show later.

1997.headline: Kefka beats Mithos but opens the door to upset talk
1997.narrative: Kefka beat Mithos comfortably but steadily lost ground as the day progressed, failing to look convincing for a top seed. The writeup says the result immediately encouraged arguments that Wesker could eliminate him in the next round.

1998.headline: Wesker beats Luca but destroys his own contender hype
1998.narrative: Wesker defeated Luca Blight but performed so poorly that the writeup immediately abandoned the idea of him threatening Kefka. A hyped potential contender became one of the contest's early disappointments in a single match.

1999.headline: Bison crushes Albedo and launches a night of Board 8 fads
1999.narrative: M. Bison demolished Albedo and sparked a night of Psycho Crusher jokes and Board 8 fads. The writeup also notes that Bison steadily lost ground later, a warning sign that would matter in his next matchup.

2000.headline: Diablo beats Ridley before an outside rally pads the win
2000.narrative: Diablo turned a heavily debated matchup with Ridley into a clear win and emerged as a serious divisional threat. An outside Diablo-site rally arrived later, but the writeup argues that the match had already been decided on its own merits.
2000.anomaly_note: The writeup says diabloii.net linked directly to the poll during the match, adding outside support for Diablo. It also stresses that Diablo had already taken firm control before the rally appeared.

2001.headline: Ganondorf crushes Giygas in a foregone conclusion
2001.narrative: Ganondorf obliterated Giygas in a matchup the writeup considered barely worth holding. The result simply reinforced Ganondorf's status as a pre-contest lock for the final while placing Giygas among the weakest entrants.

2002.headline: CATS nearly shocks Ansem and proves he can threaten someone
2002.narrative: Ansem eventually escaped CATS, but CATS led for hours and came far closer to a real win than Board 8 believed possible. The writeup remembers the match almost entirely as CATS proving that joke support could become meaningful against the right opponent.
2002.anomaly_note: The writeup says CATS finally received the recognizable picture fans associated with him rather than his old image, and argues that this likely made a major difference in his unusually strong showing.

2003.headline: Robotnik survives Sin amid a disastrous picture and rally attempt
2003.narrative: Robotnik held off Sin in a close matchup dominated by Board 8 arguments around one loud Sin supporter. The writeup says Sin mounted a respectable recovery despite a disastrous picture, while an attempted outside rally failed to overturn the result.
2003.anomaly_note: The writeup says Sin was badly hurt by one of the contest's worst match pictures, which reduced him to an unrecognizable dorsal fin. It also says a vocal Sin supporter tried to rally votes from outside websites during the match.

2004.headline: Master Hand humiliates Kuja in the contest's defining upset
2004.narrative: Master Hand stunned Kuja in the round's defining upset after almost everyone dismissed the glove as an automatic loss. The writeup remembers the result as both absurd and unforgettable, turning a supposedly obvious match into the contest's biggest board explosion.

2005.headline: Bowser destroys Sigma and strengthens the new-voting-trend debate
2005.narrative: Bowser crushed Sigma and deepened the sense that the villains contest was producing strength patterns unlike prior character contests. The writeup treats Sigma as one of the event's biggest disappointments and Bowser as increasingly formidable.

2006.headline: Ocelot handles Wily as another Mega Man villain disappoints
2006.narrative: Revolver Ocelot beat Dr. Wily more comfortably than the pre-match debate suggested, turning another hyped matchup into a dud. The writeup focuses less on Ocelot's strength than on Wily joining the growing list of disappointing Mega Man entrants.

2007.headline: Sephiroth buries Vergil in a completely predetermined matchup
2007.narrative: Sephiroth buried Vergil in a match whose result the writeup considered completely predetermined. Vergil had fulfilled his bracket role by beating Ghaleon, and this round offered no sign that Sephiroth would later encounter trouble.

2008.headline: Liquid survives Lavos as his inflated reputation takes a hit
2008.narrative: Liquid Snake defeated Lavos, but Lavos pushed him hard enough to undermine the lofty strength implied by the previous year's extrapolated standings. The writeup uses the match as a case study in how transitive statistical adjustments can produce misleading rankings.

2009.headline: Kefka destroys Wesker with help from an unusually strong picture
2009.narrative: Kefka demolished Wesker and erased the upset hype that had surrounded the matchup before the contest. The writeup calls it one of Kefka's best performances and says his unusually favorable picture may have contributed.
2009.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kefka received an exceptionally strong picture and suggests it was partly responsible for his unusually dominant performance against Wesker.

2010.headline: Diablo withstands Bison's comeback and pulls away late
2010.narrative: Bison and Diablo traded momentum through one of the contest's few genuinely competitive matches before Diablo finally broke away. The writeup emphasizes Bison's determined comeback attempt and Diablo's even stronger response once the afternoon vote arrived.

2011.headline: Ganondorf crushes Ansem despite a picture blamed for underperformance
2011.narrative: Ganondorf crushed Ansem as expected, though the writeup thought the favorite should have looked even stronger after Ansem's struggle with CATS. Much of the discussion blames Ganondorf's pig-form picture for the comparatively disappointing showing.
2011.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ganondorf's pig-like Ganon picture was widely blamed for an underperformance against Ansem, hurting the favorite despite the easy win.

2012.headline: Robotnik ends Master Hand's run but raises new doubts
2012.narrative: Robotnik ended Master Hand's surprise run without much trouble, but the writeup focuses on how much ground Robotnik surrendered later in the poll. That late fade made his coming match with Ganondorf look hopeless.

2013.headline: Bowser routs Ocelot and cruises to the division title
2013.narrative: Bowser turned what had once looked like a possible upset spot into an easy division-clinching win. The writeup treats Ocelot's collapse as evidence that Bowser may have grown stronger since earlier contests.

2014.headline: Sephiroth crushes Liquid and deepens the 20XX mystery
2014.narrative: Sephiroth crushed Liquid far more thoroughly than old projections suggested, leaving the writeup struggling to explain what had happened to Liquid and the 2004 20XX group. The result reinforced Sephiroth's overwhelming status while making earlier statistics look suspect.

2015.headline: Diablo overtakes Kefka and completes an unlikely Final Four run
2015.narrative: Kefka led early, but Diablo's familiar daytime strength erased the lead and eventually turned the match into a comfortable win. The writeup celebrates Diablo's unlikely run to the Final Four after very few brackets had trusted him to get this far.

2016.headline: Robotnik's rout becomes another chapter in Sonic-series disappointment
2016.narrative: The writeup spends most of its time reviewing years of disappointing Sonic-series contest performances, using Robotnik's lopsided loss to Ganondorf as the latest example.
2016.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ganondorf dominated despite an ugly Wind Waker picture and suggests Robotnik would have looked even worse against a stronger SSBM-style Ganondorf image.

2017.headline: Bowser gives Sephiroth a legendary early tie before fading
2017.narrative: Sephiroth was always expected to advance, but Bowser briefly held him even and produced a memorable exact tie at the thousand-vote mark. The writeup treats that early moment as the real legacy of an otherwise straightforward semifinal.

2018.headline: Ganondorf ends Diablo's surprise run without much resistance
2018.narrative: Diablo's surprising run ended abruptly against Ganondorf, who controlled the semifinal from the start. The writeup sees the match mainly as confirmation that the expected Sephiroth-Ganondorf final was inevitable.

2019.headline: Sephiroth beats Ganondorf to claim the villains championship
2019.narrative: Ganondorf gave Sephiroth some resistance early, but Sephiroth pulled away and won the villains championship as expected. The writeup is more interested in why Sephiroth looked less dominant against Bowser and Ganondorf than against his earlier opponents.

2066.headline: Mario opens the contest with an emphatic win over Joanna
2066.narrative: Mario opened the contest with the expected blowout, and the writeup mainly watches turnout and whether the result strengthened his case as the favorite. It also notes the Gamespot banner and the unusual ability to keep voting after the poll had technically ended.

2067.headline: Ness upsets CJ as the writeup turns to race controversy
2067.narrative: Ness's upset over CJ becomes the jumping-off point for a long discussion of the board's race arguments, representation in games, and whether Grand Theft Auto simply underperforms on GameFAQs.

2068.headline: Zero beats Ryu Hayabusa but leaves mild strength questions
2068.narrative: Zero beat Ryu Hayabusa comfortably in a deliberately uneventful match after the previous day's chaos. The writeup nevertheless saw Ryu's late recovery as a mild warning that Zero might be somewhat overrated.

2069.headline: Lloyd beats Wesker but badly misses Board 8 expectations
2069.narrative: Lloyd never seriously risked losing, but Wesker performed much better than the writeup expected against the Tales protagonist. The result was treated as a clear Lloyd underperformance and another sign that recent statistics were hard to trust.

2070.headline: Samus crushes Yuri and strengthens her championship case
2070.narrative: Samus demolished Yuri and strengthened the case that she could win the entire contest. The writeup treats the performance as an impressive answer to people who thought Mario should be favored in their anticipated matchup.

2071.headline: Frog survives Riku but sees his old reputation collapse
2071.narrative: Frog survived Riku, but Riku's sustained pressure convinced the writeup that Frog's celebrated 2004 strength had been badly overstated. Instead of reinforcing Frog's reputation, the close win turned him into one of the contest's biggest statistical question marks.

2072.headline: Ganondorf beats Yuna amid strength debate and cheating claims
2072.narrative: Ganondorf beat Yuna as expected while the writeup debated whether the result helped or hurt his standing against Auron. It also explicitly points to suspicious voting on Yuna's side.
2072.anomaly_note: The writeup says TRE identified numerous examples of blatant cheating coming from Yuna's side of the poll.

2073.headline: Auron cruises past Big Boss as the Ganondorf matchup looms
2073.narrative: Auron cruised past Big Boss in what the writeup treats mostly as a preview of Auron's coming match with Ganondorf. Big Boss's poor picture is singled out as a reason not to read too much into the size of the win.
2073.anomaly_note: The writeup argues that Big Boss's unrecognizable cartoon-style picture hurt him and that a recognizable Naked Snake image would have performed better against Auron.

2074.headline: Snake crushes Manny after Board 8 finally gets him in
2074.narrative: Snake predictably overwhelmed Manny, but the writeup treats Manny's appearance itself as a victory after a long Board 8 nomination campaign. Much of the discussion pushes back against claims that Snake's huge win was somehow disappointing.

2075.headline: Zelda crushes Vivi and undercuts the statistical case against her
2075.narrative: Zelda turned a heavily debated matchup into an easy win, badly undercutting the statistical case for Vivi. The writeup interprets the result as evidence of both Zelda's growth and the wider Nintendo boost that was becoming a major contest storyline.

2076.headline: Alucard beats Kratos but looks vulnerable heading toward Sora
2076.narrative: Alucard beat Kratos, but Kratos's strong daytime showing made the favorite look far less convincing than expected. The writeup saw the result as a warning that Alucard was aging and would be vulnerable against Sora.

2077.headline: Sora handles Agent 47 as attention shifts to Alucard
2077.narrative: Sora handled Agent 47 comfortably, yet the writeup still considered the performance mediocre for the matchup. More importantly, Riku's earlier showing against Frog had already shifted the coming Sora-Alucard debate strongly toward Sora.

2078.headline: Kirby destroys Cecil and ignites Nintendo boost talk
2078.narrative: Kirby demolished Cecil far beyond expectations and immediately looked much stronger than his seeding reputation suggested. The writeup credits both Kirby's rise and Cecil's terrible picture while treating the result as an early sign of a broad Nintendo boost.
2078.anomaly_note: The writeup calls Cecil's Amano image one of the worst match pictures in the contest and accepts that the picture likely contributed to how badly he underperformed against Kirby.

2079.headline: Tidus beats the King but loses more confidence before Kirby
2079.narrative: Tidus won comfortably, but the writeup turns the King of All Cosmos into a running joke while arguing that Tidus still performed too poorly to beat Kirby. The result became another strike against Tidus's old reputation as an elite-level character.

2080.headline: Bowser handles Chun-Li without settling the Ryu debate
2080.narrative: Bowser beat Chun-Li almost exactly as expected, leaving the writeup with little new information about his strength. The real focus remained the anticipated second-round showdown with Ryu.

2081.headline: Ryu beats Rikku but badly damages his case against Bowser
2081.narrative: Ryu beat Rikku but fell dramatically short of Board 8's expectations as his percentage kept sliding through the day. The writeup saw the performance as effectively ending the case for Ryu over Bowser before their match even arrived.

2082.headline: CATS overperforms again as Master Chief looks vulnerable
2082.narrative: Master Chief won easily enough, but CATS performed much better than expected and made the top seed look unimpressive. The writeup strongly credits CATS's recognizable face picture for helping him outperform his old numbers.
2082.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly argues that CATS's recognizable face picture helps him perform much better than the eggplant-style image used in other contests.

2083.headline: Donkey Kong beats Sam Fisher in an uneventful matchup
2083.narrative: Donkey Kong beat Sam Fisher in a match the writeup repeatedly calls dull. DK started above expectations but gradually gave enough back that the result offered little confidence about his next round.

2084.headline: Kefka and Vercetti classic erupts into a cheating scandal
2084.narrative: Kefka and Vercetti produced a long, volatile comeback battle that became one of the contest's biggest Board 8 explosions. The drama was ultimately overshadowed by confirmed and alleged vote-stuffing on both sides, turning a classic close match into a major cheating controversy.
2084.anomaly_note: The writeup documents extensive vote-stuffing and exploit use around both entrants, including votes removed by CJayC and admitted multi-voting by several users. It treats cheating as central to the match's final hours and aftermath.

2085.headline: Crono calmly dispatches Zidane after the previous day's chaos
2085.narrative: Crono easily dispatched Zidane in a remarkably steady poll after the chaos of Kefka-Vercetti. The writeup mainly wonders whether shared Square support suppressed Zidane, without reaching a firm conclusion.

2086.headline: Dante crushes Terra and ends the upset speculation quickly
2086.narrative: Dante crushed Terra and quickly ended what little upset speculation had existed around the matchup. The writeup treats Terra's weakness as another example of an ensemble-cast Final Fantasy character failing to translate game popularity into contest strength.

2087.headline: Vincent obliterates Kerrigan in a statement contest debut
2087.narrative: Vincent flattened Kerrigan in a match that many had overthought because of StarCraft's earlier contest success. The writeup treats Vincent's debut as a statement performance and Kerrigan's result as a major failure of Board 8 expectations.

2088.headline: Knuckles shocks Magus in a historic bracket-busting upset
2088.narrative: Knuckles stunned a board that had essentially treated Magus as a lock and even a possible division winner. Magus led early before Knuckles's daytime strength took over, producing one of the contest's most memorable bracket-busting upsets.

2089.headline: Squall overwhelms Geno as SFF shapes the Devil Division
2089.narrative: Squall overwhelmed Geno in a match whose main question was how much shared-fanbase suppression would appear. The result also helped frame the now-unpredictable Devil Division after Magus's upset loss.
2089.anomaly_note: The writeup says Squall likely applied some SFF to Geno, a Square-created side character from Super Mario RPG, and uses that as evidence for how Squall might have treated Magus.

2090.headline: Sonic beats Jin but leaves questions before Mega Man
2090.narrative: Sonic easily beat Jin, but Jin held up better than an unsupported newcomer was expected to. The writeup treats the result as mildly concerning for Sonic ahead of the anticipated Mega Man showdown.

2091.headline: Diablo handles Kratos and validates his spring performance
2091.narrative: Diablo beat Kratos Aurion without serious trouble and largely matched expectations from his strong villains-contest run. The writeup sees the result as a useful confirmation of Diablo's strength rather than a major storyline of its own.

2092.headline: Tifa crushes Vyse in a spectacular contest debut
2092.narrative: Tifa's long-awaited contest debut became a rout as she performed far beyond expectations against Vyse. The writeup immediately debates whether Tifa was truly elite or whether Vyse had simply been overrated for years.

2093.headline: Luigi routs KOS-MOS and strengthens the Nintendo boost case
2093.narrative: Luigi demolished KOS-MOS despite projections that had the matchup much closer. The writeup treats the result as one of the clearest early examples of the contest-wide Nintendo boost and a warning that Tifa's next match might not be easy.

2094.headline: Mega Man crushes Conker but gives Sonic supporters hope
2094.narrative: Mega Man crushed Conker but slipped below the performance the writeup wanted from him, giving new life to Sonic supporters. The result was treated mainly as an imperfect preview of their eventual divisional clash.

2095.headline: Leon extends Gordon Freeman's endlessly recurring losing streak
2095.narrative: Leon extended Gordon Freeman's famous losing streak, though Gordon once again performed better than a supposedly hopeless underdog should. The writeup turns the recurring GFNW joke into the main story of another Freeman defeat.

2096.headline: Yoshi handles Laharl in a routine first-round mismatch
2096.narrative: Yoshi handled Laharl almost exactly as expected in one of the first round's least eventful matches. The writeup treats it as little more than another easy Nintendo win before Yoshi's projected meeting with Mega Man.

2097.headline: Pac-Man shocks Ocelot and wipes out the perfect brackets
2097.narrative: Pac-Man upset heavily favored Ocelot in a close first-round finale that eliminated the remaining perfect brackets. The writeup celebrates Pac-Man's overdue major win while blaming Ocelot's poor picture for at least part of the upset.
2097.anomaly_note: The writeup argues that Ocelot's faded old-man picture hurt him in the close loss and says a recognizable in-game Metal Gear image likely would have improved his performance enough to win.

2098.headline: Mario obliterates Ness with exceptionally strong SFF
2098.narrative: Mario annihilated Ness in a result the writeup treats as an extreme SFF beating. The performance strengthened Mario's championship case while making Ness's earlier upset over CJ look even stranger statistically.
2098.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Mario SFFed Ness and argues that the suppression was even stronger than prior same-fanbase results involving Ness.

2099.headline: Zero dispatches Lloyd and advances toward the inevitable Mario test
2099.narrative: Zero dispatched Lloyd exactly as the bracket had seemed to prescribe from the start. The writeup mainly uses the match to reassess Lloyd's place among Tales characters and to leave Zero's real test for Mario.

2100.headline: Samus demolishes Frog and shatters his old contest mystique
2100.narrative: Samus demolished Frog and erased the mystique built by Frog's string of close 2004 matches. The writeup treats the rout as another sign that Frog had been badly overrated and as strong evidence that Samus remained a championship threat.

2101.headline: Ganondorf beats Auron as the hyped Gauntlet starts flat
2101.narrative: Ganondorf beat Auron more comfortably than the pre-match debate suggested, turning the first match of the much-hyped Gauntlet into an anticlimax. The writeup still credits Auron with legitimate strength while sending Ganondorf onward to Samus.

2102.headline: Snake crushes the Zelda bandwagon in another Gauntlet dud
2102.narrative: Snake quickly dismantled a Zelda upset bandwagon that had grown from mismatched old statistics and concern over his ugly picture. The writeup treats the match as another example of Board 8 talking itself into a close contest that never materialized.

2103.headline: Sora beats Alucard and delivers another blow to x-stats
2103.narrative: Sora turned one of the contest's most debated statistical matchups into a clear win over Alucard. The writeup argues that recent Kingdom Hearts momentum and Alucard's stagnation mattered far more than the old x-stats.

2104.headline: Kirby crushes Tidus and completes a dramatic expectations reversal
2104.narrative: Kirby decisively beat Tidus after the board had once treated Tidus as the overwhelming favorite. The writeup sees the result as both a major Kirby validation and another humiliation in Tidus's long decline from his 2003 reputation.

2105.headline: Bowser handles Ryu as the Gauntlet ends anticlimactically
2105.narrative: Bowser beat Ryu without the close fight that had once made the matchup a major bracket debate. The writeup treats the anticlimax as one more piece of evidence for a site-wide Nintendo boost and another failure of the Gauntlet hype.

2106.headline: Master Chief erases Donkey Kong's lead in a record comeback
2106.narrative: Donkey Kong unexpectedly built a substantial lead, only for Master Chief's daytime strength to erase it and carry him past DK. The writeup remembers the match as a rare surprise after the failed Gauntlet and as a record-setting comeback and vote swing.

2107.headline: Crono dispatches Vercetti and confirms his elite standing
2107.narrative: Crono easily disposed of Vercetti in a quiet follow-up to the chaos required for Vercetti to reach him. The writeup treats the match mainly as confirmation that Crono still belonged among the contest's elite characters.

2108.headline: Vincent beats Dante but loses much of his elite hype
2108.narrative: Vincent survived Dante after an unexpectedly competitive start, but the writeup treats the result as a major correction to weeks of Vincent hype. Dante's showing is framed as a moral victory that exposed Vincent as strong but not elite.

2109.headline: Squall ends the Knuckles bandwagon and buries old Magus stats
2109.narrative: Squall quickly ended the post-upset Knuckles bandwagon and controlled the match despite Knuckles' familiar daytime strength. The writeup uses the result to bury Magus's old statistical reputation and set up a difficult Vincent-Squall division final.

2110.headline: Sonic cruises while Diabloii.net support shows up late
2110.narrative: Sonic won an otherwise routine match that mainly served as a measuring stick for his coming clash with Mega Man. Diablo's performance improved after a Diabloii.net link appeared, reinforcing the writeup's view that outside-site support mattered to him.
2110.anomaly_note: The writeup says Diablo improved noticeably after Diabloii.net finally posted a link to the poll, costing Sonic about a percentage point and confirming that outside-site support was part of Diablo's strength.

2111.headline: Tifa wins while Luigi scores another Nintendo moral victory
2111.narrative: Tifa beat Luigi, but Luigi performed far better than the writeup says most of Board 8 expected. The result is framed as another warning against overvaluing one prior match and as more evidence of Nintendo's broader 2005 rise.

2112.headline: Leon overperforms as Mega Man advances without much drama
2112.narrative: Mega Man won comfortably, but Leon performed much better than older Resident Evil comparisons suggested. The writeup treats Leon's showing as evidence that previous statistics had badly understated the series.

2113.headline: Yoshi crushes Pac-Man and validates his place above Luigi
2113.narrative: Yoshi crushed Pac-Man in one of the contest's steadiest matches and confirmed that his 2004 strength was real. The writeup also uses the result to revisit the casual bracketmakers who had failed to trust Yoshi's path this far.

2114.headline: Mario SFFs Zero and strengthens his case as tournament favorite
2114.narrative: Mario turned a mildly debated division final into an immediate rout of Zero. The writeup treats the result as a major SFF statement and a warning that Mario and Nintendo were much stronger than the old statistics suggested.
2114.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Mario's win an SFF beatdown and argues that Mario was able to suppress Zero far beyond ordinary expectations.

2115.headline: Samus advances but her weak SFF showing raises alarms
2115.narrative: Samus advanced as expected, but the writeup considers her showing against Ganondorf disappointing next to Mario's destruction of Zero. Her weak SFF performance is presented as a serious warning before the coming Mario matchup.
2115.anomaly_note: The writeup says Samus barely managed to SFF Ganondorf, with only enough suppression to offset Ganondorf's recent Zelda-series boost.

2116.headline: Snake destroys Sora and reasserts himself as an elite threat
2116.narrative: Snake demolished Sora after entering the match somewhat underestimated. The writeup sees the result as both a statement of Snake's true strength and an example of a broader fanbase-overlap effect working against Sora.
2116.anomaly_note: The writeup rejects a simple PlayStation 2 explanation but argues that a broader form of SFF hurt Sora badly against Solid Snake.

2117.headline: Bowser survives Kirby but loses confidence before facing Snake
2117.narrative: Bowser survived a strong challenge from Kirby and gradually built enough of a lead to take the division. The close result weakened confidence in Bowser before Snake, with the writeup considering reverse SFF as one possible explanation.
2117.anomaly_note: The writeup presents reverse SFF as a viable explanation for Kirby keeping the match unusually close, with Kirby's starring role and bracket support potentially suppressing Bowser's expected advantage.

2118.headline: Crono wins while Master Chief's day vote raises fresh doubts
2118.narrative: Crono won comfortably, but Master Chief's powerful daytime recovery made the result look less convincing than expected. The writeup treats Chief as unusually non-transitive and questions whether Crono still looked capable of winning the tournament.

2119.headline: Vincent survives Squall in a bracket-busting Pyrrhic victory
2119.narrative: Vincent survived one of the contest's best matches after Squall repeatedly erased and rebuilt tiny leads throughout the day. The win was a huge bracket buster, but the writeup calls it a Pyrrhic victory because Squall's resistance further damaged Vincent's elite reputation.
2119.anomaly_note: The writeup says a slight amount of SFF, together with anti-votes, likely held Squall back in the close Final Fantasy matchup.

2120.headline: Sonic handles Tifa and sets up the long-awaited Mega Man clash
2120.narrative: Sonic shook off Tifa's early resistance and pulled away once his morning vote arrived. The writeup treats the match mostly as a final setup for the much less predictable Sonic-Mega Man quarterfinal.

2121.headline: Mega Man SFFs Yoshi and enters the Sonic match favored
2121.narrative: Mega Man easily dispatched Yoshi and ended the divisional round. The writeup attributes Yoshi's underperformance partly to SFF and uses that result to swing the coming Sonic-Mega Man debate toward Mega Man.
2121.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Mega Man likely SFFed Yoshi because voters associate Mega Man strongly with Nintendo-era games.

2122.headline: Mario crushes Samus and blows up the old statistical consensus
2122.narrative: Mario demolished Samus in the contest's most heavily debated quarterfinal and invalidated the old statistical case for a Samus win. The writeup later apologizes for its original hostility, but still treats the result as a decisive SFF showcase of Mario's 2005 strength.
2122.anomaly_note: The writeup repeatedly describes Mario's victory as an enormous SFF beating that overwhelmed Samus despite pre-match statistical expectations favoring her.

2123.headline: Snake survives Bowser's comeback despite another poor match picture
2123.narrative: Snake built a large lead before Bowser mounted a long afternoon comeback that fell just short. The writeup considers the close win a major validation for Snake and argues that his poor match picture made the result look closer than it otherwise would have.
2123.anomaly_note: The writeup argues that Snake's hard-to-recognize sprite hurt him while Bowser had a clear, recognizable picture, and says Snake likely wins by more with a fairer image.

2124.headline: Crono advances as Vincent creates another statistical puzzle
2124.narrative: Crono won without serious danger, but Vincent performed far better than comparable projections suggested and then held an unusually stable share for most of the match. The writeup treats the overperformance as a puzzle involving either reverse SFF or an Advent Children boost.
2124.anomaly_note: The writeup presents reverse SFF between newer and older Square fandom as one plausible reason Vincent performed unusually well against Crono, while also considering Advent Children as an alternative explanation.

2125.headline: Mega Man survives Sonic after two squandered comeback chances
2125.narrative: Sonic and Mega Man traded control in one of the contest's defining close matches, with Sonic twice appearing ready to take over before losing momentum. The writeup ultimately frames Mega Man's narrow win as another painful Sonic choke in a rivalry between nearly equal icons.

2126.headline: Mario handles Snake and keeps rolling toward the championship
2126.narrative: Mario controlled Snake throughout the semifinal, although Snake earned the moral victory his fans wanted by stealing a handful of updates. The writeup sees the overall margin as further proof that Mario had risen sharply and was the clear tournament favorite.

2127.headline: Crono edges Mega Man but fails to ease doubts about Mario
2127.narrative: Crono beat Mega Man in a close-looking semifinal without ever facing a sustained comeback threat. The writeup argues that the narrow margin did little to suggest Crono could stop the much stronger-looking Mario in the final.

2128.headline: Mario beats Crono and completes his dominant 2005 championship run
2128.narrative: Mario ended the latest chapter of his Crono rivalry with a convincing championship win, reversing the previous year's result without another dramatic finish. The writeup treats the entire contest as a showcase of Mario's enormous 2005 rise.

2129.headline: Cloud briefly leads before Link's day vote takes control
2129.narrative: Cloud briefly took the lead and performed better than many expected after Nintendo's huge year, but Link's morning and daytime strength eventually buried the comeback attempt. The writeup credits Advent Children with helping Cloud remain respectable in another loss to Link.

2130.headline: Sephiroth crushes champion Mario and showcases the Advent Children boost
2130.narrative: Sephiroth overwhelmed the newly crowned Mario and ended speculation that Nintendo's 2005 boost had lifted Mario above him. The writeup sees the result as strong evidence that Advent Children had substantially strengthened the Final Fantasy VII cast.

2131.headline: Link beats Sephiroth to finish the Tournament of Champions
2131.narrative: Link beat Sephiroth comfortably in a final that the writeup considered largely predetermined. Sephiroth still did better than expected, reinforcing the view that Advent Children had strengthened the Final Fantasy VII characters even though Link remained clearly on top.

2425.headline: Zelda opens Best Series Ever by shattering the vote record
2425.narrative: Zelda opened the Best Series Ever contest with a routine blowout that immediately became notable for its enormous vote total. The writeup says the performance set a new individual-vote record and started early talk that Zelda might challenge Final Fantasy for the title.

2426.headline: Mega Man X cruises past Suikoden into a hopeless Zelda matchup
2426.narrative: Mega Man X handled Suikoden exactly as expected in a lopsided but unremarkable opener. The writeup mostly focuses on X finally appearing prominently in a contest picture and on the poor bracket reward of facing Zelda next.

2427.headline: Pokémon crushes Star Ocean and finally gets its contest vindication
2427.narrative: Pokémon erased years of contest pessimism by crushing Star Ocean after even its own supporters had grown nervous about the matchup. The writeup treats the win as overdue vindication for a franchise with a history of disappointing contest results.

2428.headline: Metroid routs Kirby and ends the brief Pokémon bandwagon
2428.narrative: Metroid demolished Kirby and immediately killed the brief Pokémon-over-Metroid bandwagon. The writeup is unsure whether fanbase overlap mattered, ultimately leaning more toward Kirby's games simply being weaker than Kirby's character popularity suggests.

2429.headline: Metal Gear crushes Soul Calibur and exposes old statistical inflation
2429.narrative: Metal Gear crushed Soul Calibur and made its old Spring 2004 statistical standing look badly inflated. The writeup treats the result as the first warning that several highly rated series from that earlier bracket had been overrated.

2430.headline: Fire Emblem handles Silent Hill in the contest's expected stinker
2430.narrative: Fire Emblem won a matchup the writeup considered less uncertain than the near-even brackets suggested. The result is framed as a modest vindication for the growing Nintendo series and another reminder that Silent Hill remained highly niche on GameFAQs.

2431.headline: Castlevania upsets Halo and neutralizes its famous day vote
2431.narrative: Castlevania upset Halo and, more surprisingly, neutralized the daytime voting strength that had defined Halo and Master Chief in earlier contests. The writeup treats the result as both a satisfying upset and another exposure of Halo's unreliable contest reputation.

2432.headline: Kingdom Hearts routs Harvest Moon despite another round of doom talk
2432.narrative: Kingdom Hearts crushed Harvest Moon, yet the writeup says people still treated the performance as disappointing because Castlevania had just upset Halo. It rejects that panic and argues that Kingdom Hearts remained difficult to judge after its sequel.

2433.headline: Mario destroys Madden and takes another individual-vote record
2433.narrative: Super Mario Bros. annihilated Madden in the contest's signature joke-fodder matchup. The writeup highlights another individual-vote record and says the performance strengthened early belief that Mario could challenge Final Fantasy.

2434.headline: Warcraft rallies past GTA as vote stuffing hits the losing side
2434.narrative: Warcraft upset GTA in a close match dominated by outside-site campaigning, especially from the World of Warcraft community. The aftermath also confirmed vote stuffing, mostly for GTA, but the writeup stresses that Warcraft still won fairly without those fraudulent votes deciding the result.
2434.anomaly_note: The writeup says both sides rallied heavily, with World of Warcraft forum traffic giving Warcraft the decisive outside push. It also quotes CJayC confirming egregious vote stuffing, overwhelmingly for GTA, while stating that the fraudulent votes were insufficient to change Warcraft's legitimate win.

2435.headline: Sonic crushes Devil May Cry and builds momentum for Smash
2435.narrative: Sonic crushed Devil May Cry in a straightforward match that mattered mainly as a measuring stick for the coming Super Smash Bros. clash. The strong showing added momentum to arguments that Sonic could win that much more important second-round match.

2436.headline: Smash handles Dragon Quest while debate shifts toward Sonic
2436.narrative: Super Smash Bros. easily dispatched Dragon Quest while the writeup spends as much time on fan complaints as on the stable blowout itself. The result kept the coming Sonic matchup uncertain rather than answering whether Smash was truly strong enough.

2437.headline: Final Fantasy crushes Diablo but does not settle the title race
2437.narrative: Final Fantasy answered Zelda and Mario's huge opening performances with a massive blowout of Diablo. The writeup still stops short of calling the contest over, arguing that Diablo's limited series depth made the result less definitive than it first appeared.

2438.headline: Mega Man crushes Mario Kart after an overthought pre-match debate
2438.narrative: Mega Man decisively beat Mario Kart after Board 8 had spent far more time debating the matchup than the writeup thought necessary. The result is presented as a case of the board overthinking how voters would interpret the broad Mega Man series name.

2439.headline: Street Fighter crushes Elder Scrolls amid a noisy fanbase fight
2439.narrative: Street Fighter easily beat The Elder Scrolls despite loud pre-match confidence from some Elder Scrolls fans. The writeup remembers the poll largely for the ugly fan arguments it produced and for setting up a more meaningful Street Fighter-Resident Evil matchup.

2440.headline: Resident Evil obliterates Shadow Hearts in another joke-fodder blowout
2440.narrative: Resident Evil obliterated Shadow Hearts in another first-round mismatch and nearly reached the contest's biggest vote and percentage landmarks. The writeup treats Shadow Hearts as contest joke fodder and warns against reading too much strength into such a lopsided pairing.

2441.headline: Zelda SFFs Mega Man X and keeps pressure on Final Fantasy
2441.narrative: Zelda crushed Mega Man X in a second-round SFF matchup and kept pace with Final Fantasy in the contest's emerging strength race. The writeup treats the result mainly as another statement that Zelda could realistically win the tournament.
2441.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly treats Zelda versus Mega Man X as an SFF match, while noting that voters may differ on how strongly they associate Mega Man X with Nintendo.

2442.headline: Pokémon pushes Metroid hard and earns overdue contest respect
2442.narrative: Metroid beat Pokémon, but Pokémon stayed surprisingly competitive and won scattered updates throughout the match. The writeup treats the result as another example of Metroid struggling inside Nintendo and as long-overdue evidence that Pokémon was stronger than its old reputation suggested.
2442.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Pokémon versus Metroid an SFF match and treats overlapping Nintendo support as part of the context for Metroid's unexpectedly weak-looking win.

2443.headline: Metal Gear advances while Fire Emblem makes the win look ordinary
2443.narrative: Metal Gear beat Fire Emblem easily but did not dominate as thoroughly as the writeup expected. The result raised more doubts about Silent Hill's first-round strength than about Metal Gear's ability to reach the Final Four.

2444.headline: Kingdom Hearts rallies past Castlevania in a memorable fanbase war
2444.narrative: Castlevania led for much of the night and turned a previously routine Kingdom Hearts bracket slot into one of the contest's best matches. Kingdom Hearts eventually used its daytime strength to reverse the lead, while the writeup also remembers the match for exceptionally ugly board behavior from both fanbases.

2445.headline: Mario destroys Warcraft and strengthens his Final Fantasy case
2445.narrative: Mario annihilated Warcraft despite the outside support that had carried Warcraft past GTA. The writeup treats the scale of the beating as another strong sign that Mario had a real chance against Final Fantasy later in the bracket.

2446.headline: Smash shuts down Sonic and kills another Mario-Sonic opportunity
2446.narrative: Super Smash Bros. comfortably beat Sonic in one of the contest's most debated matchups and denied another chance to see Mario face Sonic. The writeup considers the result another major Sonic disappointment after the series had appeared well positioned for the upset.

2447.headline: Final Fantasy crushes Mega Man and remains the title favorite
2447.narrative: Final Fantasy crushed the broadly defined Mega Man series in another impressive second-round performance. The writeup sees nothing in the result to weaken Final Fantasy's position as the contest favorite.

2448.headline: Resident Evil survives Street Fighter in a tight Capcom showdown
2448.narrative: Resident Evil narrowly held off Street Fighter after a much closer fight than most of Board 8 expected. The writeup credits Street Fighter's favorable picture for helping the upset threat while arguing that current Capcom fanbase overlap ultimately leaned toward Resident Evil.
2448.anomaly_note: The writeup says the heavily Street Fighter-favored picture gave Street Fighter an advantage, while also arguing that Capcom fanbase overlap likely favored Resident Evil because Resident Evil 4 was then the stronger current draw.

2449.headline: Zelda SFFs Metroid in another brutal Nintendo family matchup
2449.narrative: Zelda crushed Metroid in the expected division final and produced another extreme Nintendo SFF result. The writeup treats the match as the latest entry in a long pattern of Samus and Metroid collapsing against stronger Nintendo opposition.
2449.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Zelda's suppression of Metroid was severe SFF and places it in a long history of Samus and Metroid performing badly against other Nintendo entrants.

2450.headline: Metal Gear handles Kingdom Hearts after a brief Castlevania poll glitch
2450.narrative: Metal Gear beat Kingdom Hearts comfortably after a brief poll glitch mistakenly displayed Castlevania as the opponent. Once corrected, the match followed the expected pattern and sent Metal Gear into the Final Four without much drama.

2451.headline: Smash resists expected SFF and dents Mario's title hopes
2451.narrative: Super Smash Bros. performed far better than expected against Mario and resisted the heavy SFF that many had predicted. The writeup says the result established Smash as a major series while largely killing talk of Mario upsetting Final Fantasy.

2452.headline: Final Fantasy cruises past Resident Evil into the semifinals
2452.narrative: Final Fantasy dispatched Resident Evil in a routine division final and completed the expected group of top seeds in the semifinals. The writeup treats the match mainly as another apparent confirmation that Final Fantasy remained championship material.

2453.headline: Zelda handles Metal Gear and advances to the final
2453.narrative: Zelda comfortably eliminated Metal Gear but looked a little less overwhelming than in earlier rounds. The writeup still saw Final Fantasy as the likely favorite for the final at this point, before the other semifinal changed that perception.

2454.headline: Final Fantasy survives Mario but exposes itself before Zelda
2454.narrative: Final Fantasy beat Mario, but Mario's unexpectedly strong challenge convinced the writeup that Final Fantasy was far more vulnerable than believed. The result effectively transformed the coming Zelda final from an underdog bid into a highly credible upset opportunity.

2455.headline: Zelda upsets Final Fantasy to win Best Series Ever
2455.narrative: Zelda took control early, survived Final Fantasy's night push, and finished the championship with the stronger daytime vote. The writeup treats the win as one of the era's biggest upsets and as a symbolic confirmation of GameFAQs' growing Nintendo tilt.

2499.headline: Samus handles Nidoran without settling any strength debates
2499.narrative: Samus opened the contest with an easy win over joke entrant Nidoran F, whose nomination had been heavily rallied before the bracket began. The writeup rejects the idea that Samus's less-than-absurd dominance revealed anything meaningful about her strength.

2500.headline: Ada dispatches Jade in an uninformative opening match
2500.narrative: Ada beat a little-known Jade without difficulty, leaving the writeup unsure whether Ada was strong or Jade was simply very weak. The main useful observation was another poor Resident Evil daytime performance.

2501.headline: Rikku routs Lenneth and validates her earlier contest strength
2501.narrative: Rikku overwhelmed an obscure Lenneth and reinforced the idea that her prior strong showing was no fluke. The writeup treats the result as a quiet but convincing confirmation of Rikku's midcard strength.

2502.headline: Kairi survives Claire before the Kingdom Hearts day vote erupts
2502.narrative: Kairi and Claire traded control through sharply different voting periods before Kingdom Hearts' daytime strength turned the late match decisively toward Kairi. The writeup also records a vote-stuffing allegation involving a Claire supporter.
2502.anomaly_note: The writeup says Smurf bragged about vote-stuffing for Claire and was banned during the match, while noting that whether he actually altered any votes remained unknown.

2503.headline: Tifa crushes Ivy and delivers an early statement performance
2503.narrative: Tifa produced the first performance the writeup considered truly dominant, while Ivy and the broader Soul Calibur cast looked increasingly weak. The unusually high interest around the match picture is treated more as spectacle than as an explanation for the result.

2504.headline: The Boss handles Celes and punctures another Final Fantasy hype job
2504.narrative: The Boss beat Celes comfortably after a pre-match debate the writeup considered badly overhyped. Much of the analysis argues that Final Fantasy VI's ensemble cast had repeatedly failed to translate the game's popularity into strong character results.

2505.headline: Jill beats Sheena but her day vote raises concerns
2505.narrative: Jill beat Sheena without being threatened, but her weak daytime performance concerned the writeup. The result is framed as an early warning that Jill could struggle badly if she reached a genuinely close match later.

2506.headline: Peach crushes Daisy while the writeup mostly wanders elsewhere
2506.narrative: The writeup is mostly a personal rant about Peach, Daisy, Mario, and Luigi; the match itself is treated as an effortless Peach win that strengthened confidence in her next round.

2507.headline: Zelda destroys Carmen and launches a serious Samus upset bandwagon
2507.narrative: Zelda demolished Carmen Sandiego in what the writeup calls one of the contest's most dominant performances. The showing immediately fueled a serious bandwagon that Zelda might threaten Samus later in the bracket.

2508.headline: Terra beats Kerrigan after a noisy match-picture controversy
2508.narrative: Terra beat Kerrigan in a match preceded by enough picture complaints that the official image was changed. The writeup says the altered picture did not rescue Kerrigan and instead treats the result as another example of weak PC-character strength.

2509.headline: KOS-MOS beats Amy despite a late Sonic day-vote recovery
2509.narrative: KOS-MOS beat Amy more easily than the writeup expected, helped by Amy's poor standing even among Sonic fans. Amy's strong daytime recovery was the only notable trend and foreshadowed how important that voting bloc could become later.

2510.headline: Aeris beats Marle but fails to strengthen her Zelda case
2510.narrative: Aeris beat Marle comfortably, with only a small amount of SFF according to the writeup. More concerning for Aeris was her failure to dominate the daytime vote, which weakened confidence that she could challenge Zelda later.
2510.anomaly_note: The writeup says Aeris and Marle showed some SFF from their overlapping Square and role-playing fanbases, but characterizes the effect as minimal rather than a major suppression.

2511.headline: Yuna quietly crushes Roll and answers early doubts
2511.narrative: Yuna quietly delivered a dominant opening win over Roll after being dismissed as a weak top seed. The writeup treats the performance as an early sign that Yuna was stronger than the division's reputation suggested.

2512.headline: Joanna handles Cortana and extends Halo's character-level struggles
2512.narrative: Joanna beat Cortana without much difficulty after brief early hopes for a closer match. The writeup frames Cortana's failure as another example of Halo-related entrants being overrated by people who confuse game popularity with character strength.

2513.headline: Chun-Li handles Kasumi despite another weak Street Fighter day vote
2513.narrative: Chun-Li beat Kasumi as expected and was never in danger, though her poor daytime vote gave back some of the early margin. The writeup considers the match largely routine despite pre-match discussion of possible fighting-game overlap.

2514.headline: Lara crushes Alyx without proving she has truly returned
2514.narrative: Lara looked dominant against Alyx, but the writeup argues that the performance was deceptive because Alyx was obscure and the match drew little interest. It rejects the result as evidence of a true Lara resurgence.

2515.headline: Snake crushes Soma and hints that this run may differ
2515.narrative: Snake overwhelmed Soma in a stronger opening performance than his familiar early-round fodder beatings. The writeup still notes his history of fading later, but treats the result as the first hint that this contest might be different.

2516.headline: Squall SFFs Tidus and briefly fuels upset talk against Snake
2516.narrative: Squall crushed Tidus in what the writeup calls an SFF beating through and through. The result further buried Tidus's old reputation while briefly making a later Squall upset of Snake seem plausible.
2516.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls the result an SFF beating, with Squall suppressing fellow Final Fantasy lead Tidus far beyond what their ordinary statistical gap suggested.

2517.headline: Yoshi beats Riku but loses confidence before facing Dante
2517.narrative: Yoshi beat Riku in a seeding upset but steadily lost ground after a blistering start. The writeup treats Riku's resistance as a moral victory and as a warning that Yoshi's coming match with Dante had become much less comfortable.

2518.headline: Dante handles Hayabusa and keeps the edge over Yoshi
2518.narrative: Dante beat Ryu Hayabusa almost exactly as the writeup's prior expectations suggested. The routine result kept Dante looking steadier than Yoshi heading into their debated second-round meeting.

2519.headline: Sora dispatches Tingle in a remarkably uneventful opener
2519.narrative: Sora beat the widely disliked Tingle in a completely stable and predictable match. The writeup finds almost no useful trend information in the result beyond another easy Kingdom Hearts win.

2520.headline: Gordon finally wins and ends the original GFNW joke
2520.narrative: Gordon Freeman ended the long-running GFNW joke by beating Board 8 favorite Phoenix Wright after an early Phoenix lead. The writeup argues that the Phoenix upset hype was mostly fad power rather than a realistic assessment of the matchup.

2521.headline: Ryu beats bracket favorite Kratos despite a strong day vote
2521.narrative: Ryu beat Kratos without serious danger even though casual brackets had strongly favored Kratos. The writeup is more interested in Kratos's powerful daytime recovery, which suggested he could become dangerous in a genuinely winnable future match.

2522.headline: Mega Man beats Axel while showing an early warning sign
2522.narrative: Mega Man beat Axel, but his strong early showing steadily deteriorated once the morning and daytime votes arrived. The writeup treats the decline as an overlooked warning of the much larger collapse that would become obvious later.

2523.headline: Sonic steamrolls CATS without resolving the old picture debate
2523.narrative: Sonic steamrolled perennial fodder CATS after the customary brief opening lead. The writeup discusses the familiar CATS picture debate but ultimately says the hybrid image makes the result too ambiguous for useful conclusions.

2524.headline: Vincent upsets Ganondorf and launches a Noble Nine breaker bandwagon
2524.narrative: Vincent won a heavily debated match after Ganondorf's early advantage faded with the opening Nintendo surge. The upset exposed problems in the old statistics and immediately triggered a large Vincent-over-Sonic bandwagon.

2525.headline: Kirby beats Prince but gives his backers another warning
2525.narrative: Kirby beat Prince of Persia but steadily lost ground after a stronger opening. The writeup credits Prince with proving respectable midcard strength while treating Kirby's performance as another bad sign before the next round.

2526.headline: Luigi stuns Zero and finally wins a major debated match
2526.narrative: Luigi demolished a favored Zero in the kind of debated match he had historically failed to win. The writeup treats the result as both a personal breakthrough for Luigi and a serious embarrassment for the statistical consensus.

2527.headline: Crono cruises past Falcon but again shows a weak day vote
2527.narrative: Crono comfortably beat Captain Falcon in his debut as a top seed. The only concern in the writeup is Crono's familiar daytime weakness, which allowed Falcon to recover substantially after the early stages.

2528.headline: Bowser wins as Leon exposes more doubts about old stats
2528.narrative: Bowser beat Leon, but Leon performed much better than the old projections suggested. Combined with Kirby's earlier showing, the result made the writeup question how legitimate their inflated prior-year statistical reputations had been.

2529.headline: Auron beats Alucard as the old upset hero keeps fading
2529.narrative: Auron beat Alucard comfortably, continuing a long decline from Alucard's early-contest upset reputation. The writeup is left debating whether Alucard had truly weakened or whether earlier statistical distortions had simply hidden his real level.

2530.headline: Sub-Zero upsets Master Chief and extends Halo's contest misery
2530.narrative: Sub-Zero upset Master Chief after taking control early and surviving the familiar Halo afternoon push. The writeup treats the loss as another chapter in Halo's recurring early-round failures and a memorable winning debut for Sub-Zero.

2531.headline: Samus crushes Ada while Resident Evil momentum stalls
2531.narrative: Samus disposed of Ada in another expected win, but the writeup considers Ada's performance disappointing after Resident Evil's recent momentum. It mentions possible overlap as one explanation but explicitly leaves the cause unresolved.

2532.headline: Rikku handles Kairi and shrugs off the Kingdom Hearts day vote
2532.narrative: Rikku handled Kairi almost exactly as the writeup expected, while the famous Kingdom Hearts day vote barely changed the match. The only surprise was how many brackets had trusted Kairi to advance.

2533.headline: Tifa wins easily while the writeup turns to fight hypotheticals
2533.narrative: The writeup treats Tifa's easy win as obvious, then spends most of its space arguing about a hypothetical physical fight between Tifa and The Boss rather than the poll itself.

2534.headline: Peach survives Jill in a classic marred by cheating attempts
2534.narrative: Peach and Jill traded control through radically different voting periods before a frantic final push left Jill just short. The writeup calls it a classic and records both heavy rallying and attempted vote-stuffing around the finish.
2534.anomaly_note: The writeup quotes CJayC describing heavy rallying on both sides and attempted vote-stuffing for both Jill and Peach. It says the blocked fraudulent votes did not alter the official result, while acknowledging lingering uncertainty over whether every improper vote was caught.

2535.headline: Zelda crushes Terra and puts real pressure on Samus
2535.narrative: Zelda demolished Terra far more convincingly than the old projections suggested. The writeup says the performance transformed Zelda from an obvious division favorite into a serious threat to Samus's title hopes.

2536.headline: Aeris beats KOS-MOS but looks doomed against Zelda
2536.narrative: Aeris beat KOS-MOS but performed much worse than the writeup believed she needed to before facing Zelda. Although some fans blamed the picture, the author rejects that explanation and treats the result as a straightforward warning of trouble ahead.

2537.headline: Yuna crushes Joanna and takes control of her division
2537.narrative: Yuna demolished Joanna and continued answering claims that she was the weakest top seed. The writeup treats the result as enough to make Yuna the clear favorite to take the division.

2538.headline: Chun-Li beats Lara but loses her Yuna upset case
2538.narrative: Chun-Li beat Lara, but a steady daytime collapse made the match much less impressive than the opening suggested. The writeup says the weak finish effectively killed the remaining Chun-Li-over-Yuna upset case.

2539.headline: Snake crushes Squall and reveals his major contest boost
2539.narrative: Snake crushed Squall in a match that had drawn meaningful upset discussion beforehand. The writeup calls it the first clear sign that Snake had made a major leap in strength during this contest.

2540.headline: Yoshi upsets Dante and vindicates years of hidden strength claims
2540.narrative: Yoshi upset Dante after dominating the Nintendo-friendly voting periods and surviving Dante's slow attempts to erase the leads. The writeup treats the result as a vindication of long-running claims that Yoshi's old statistics had understated him.

2541.headline: Sora ends Gordon's brief winning era with little trouble
2541.narrative: Sora comfortably ended Gordon Freeman's brief taste of success and then pulled farther away with the Kingdom Hearts day vote. The writeup treats the loss as another turning point in the fading GFNW tradition.

2542.headline: Mega Man beats Ryu while another collapse warning goes ignored
2542.narrative: Mega Man beat Ryu, but his steady loss of ground was another warning that his old strength was fading. The writeup says people initially blamed the poor showing partly on his bad picture, only realizing later that the decline was real.

2543.headline: Sonic beats Vincent but leaves both characters with changed expectations
2543.narrative: Sonic beat Vincent in a match whose final closeness overstated the actual danger, since Sonic controlled it from early on. Vincent nevertheless gained more Noble Nine breaker hype, while Sonic's own prospects against the bracket's elite took a hit.

2544.headline: Luigi beats Kirby as SFF settles the matchup early
2544.narrative: Luigi pulled away after an initially even start, and the writeup says the final closeness overstated how competitive the match really was. It also treats the result as further evidence that Kirby's prior Dream Division strength was misleading.
2544.anomaly_note: The writeup says SFF favored Luigi and made a Kirby comeback effectively impossible once Luigi pulled away.

2545.headline: Crono handles Bowser but his day vote raises alarms
2545.narrative: Crono handled Bowser without serious trouble, but his steady daytime decline stood out more than the result itself. The writeup treats the match as another warning that Crono's weak day vote would eventually cost him against stronger opposition.

2546.headline: Auron comfortably ends Sub-Zero's brief upset run
2546.narrative: Auron comfortably ended Sub-Zero's brief upset run in a match the writeup considered predictable. Most of the retrospective discussion uses the result to argue that Sub-Zero had nevertheless proved himself more deserving of contest attention than Scorpion.

2547.headline: Samus cruises through Rikku with no hint of trouble ahead
2547.narrative: Samus finished an entirely predictable run through her division by beating Rikku without danger. The writeup emphasizes how little the match hinted at the severe trouble Samus would encounter immediately afterward.

2548.headline: Tifa wins easily while Peach finally sheds her joke reputation
2548.narrative: Tifa won the division easily, but the writeup's main takeaway is that Peach had done enough during the contest to shed her old fodder reputation. The match itself offered little drama beyond confirming Tifa's comfortable superiority.

2549.headline: Zelda beats Aeris comfortably despite a respectable recovery
2549.narrative: Zelda looked dominant early before Aeris recovered enough to make the final result respectable, though the outcome was never in danger. The writeup mentions favorable circumstances for Aeris but leaves their actual impact unresolved.

2550.headline: Yuna routs Chun-Li and completes a surprisingly strong division run
2550.narrative: Yuna completed a surprisingly strong divisional run by beating Chun-Li far more convincingly than old upset talk had suggested. The writeup treats the performance as another sign that Yuna's pre-contest reputation had been too low before her coming test against Zelda.

2551.headline: Snake survives the sprite round and confirms his breakout year
2551.narrative: Snake avoided the sprite-round collapse many expected and handled Yoshi more respectably than his past history suggested. The writeup treats the result as another confirmation that Snake had become much stronger this year.

2552.headline: Mega Man beats Sora while his collapse becomes impossible to miss
2552.narrative: Mega Man beat Sora, but his performance deteriorated badly as the match progressed and the Kingdom Hearts day vote arrived. The writeup treats this as the match that fully exposed Mega Man's decline before his meeting with Snake.

2553.headline: Sonic ends Luigi's surprise run and reopens old strength questions
2553.narrative: Sonic beat Luigi without difficulty and brought Luigi's surprising earlier run back down to earth. The writeup uses the result mainly to question how much Kirby and especially Zero had really shown in losing to Luigi.

2554.headline: Crono beats Auron as another day-vote warning goes unanswered
2554.narrative: Crono controlled Auron but again lost ground as the day progressed, making the match feel like another warning rather than a meaningful test. The writeup treats it as the quiet end of the divisional rounds before the contest suddenly became historic.

2555.headline: Samus survives Tifa amid picture theories and rejected cheating votes
2555.narrative: Tifa pushed Samus to the brink and briefly took control before Samus's daytime recovery secured the win. The writeup frames it as Samus's worst performance, with picture theories and rejected fraudulent votes becoming central parts of the controversy.
2555.anomaly_note: The writeup treats Samus's Zero Suit picture as a plausible contributor to her severe underperformance, while rejecting it as a complete explanation. It also cites CJayC's report of large numbers of rejected cheating votes favoring Tifa.

2556.headline: Zelda beats Yuna but looks less frightening before Samus
2556.narrative: Zelda beat Yuna as expected, but Yuna held up considerably better than the writeup had anticipated. Zelda's less-than-perfect showing also cooled some of the immediate talk that she might exploit Samus's weakness in the next round.

2557.headline: Snake upsets Mega Man and turns 2006 into his year
2557.narrative: Snake decisively reversed his old history against Mega Man after Mega's earlier warning signs finally became impossible to dismiss. The writeup treats the upset as the moment the Year of the Snake fully arrived and Mega Man's long-term decline became a serious concern.

2558.headline: Sonic erases Crono's lead in a massive comeback upset
2558.narrative: Crono built a strong overnight lead, only for Sonic's daytime strength to erase it and carry Sonic to a major bracket upset. The writeup treats the enormous swing as the overdue punishment for Crono's chronic weakness outside the night vote.

2559.headline: Samus beats Zelda despite a likely reverse-SFF drag
2559.narrative: Samus beat Zelda in a steady semifinal that never became as dramatic as the preceding quarterfinals. The writeup nevertheless sees Zelda's unusually strong showing as evidence that shared Nintendo support suppressed Samus to some degree.
2559.anomaly_note: The writeup says Zelda probably reverse-SFFed Samus substantially, though not nearly enough to threaten Samus's victory.

2560.headline: Snake handles Sonic and extends his remarkable 2006 run
2560.narrative: After an erroneous opening poll was restarted, Snake took firm control and never let Sonic seriously threaten the result. Sonic recovered respectability during the day, but the writeup treats the win as the latest proof of Snake's remarkable 2006 surge.

2561.headline: Samus beats Snake for the title after a competitive start
