2561.narrative: Snake kept the championship close early, but Samus broke away once the morning vote arrived and finished the contest on top. The writeup still treats Snake as the spiritual star of the tournament, with his extraordinary run continuing into the Battle Royale.

2562.headline: Samus falls first as Nintendo SFF shapes the Battle Royale
2562.narrative: The first Battle Royale largely followed expectations at the top, while Samus became the first elimination after being squeezed by the other Nintendo heavyweights. Snake finishing ahead of Mario was the main unexpected development and set up the next day's drama.
2562.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link and Mario SFFed Samus heavily enough to drive her into last place and eliminate her.

2563.headline: Link SFFs Mario out while Snake keeps surprising
2563.narrative: Mario became the second elimination as Link absorbed the Nintendo support that had been shared with Samus the day before. Snake again outperformed expectations, while Sephiroth's repeated struggles to escape last place foreshadowed the next round.
2563.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link SFFed Mario to death, pushing Mario into last place despite his status as a traditional heavyweight.

2564.headline: Snake survives Sephiroth in a rallied and controversial finish
2564.narrative: Snake survived Sephiroth after a dramatic late comeback attempt and another last-minute Metal Gear response. The result became the capstone of Snake's extraordinary run, while Sephiroth was remembered as the Battle Royale's major disappointment.
2564.anomaly_note: The writeup says Cloud heavily SFFed Sephiroth, helping leave him vulnerable to Snake. It also describes intense late rallying and records cheating allegations around the finish, while noting that CJayC said no cheating was found.

2565.headline: Link and Cloud finally end Snake's extraordinary run
2565.narrative: With Sephiroth gone, the fourth day became a predictable Link-and-Cloud show and finally ended Snake's run. The writeup spends most of its attention celebrating how many elite opponents Snake had already survived before the two remaining giants eliminated him.

2566.headline: Link dominates Cloud to close the Battle Royale
2566.narrative: Link took control of the final Battle Royale matchup almost immediately and never gave Cloud a realistic chance to win. The writeup treats the result as another demonstration that Cloud was no longer a true threat to Link.

2863.headline: Knuckles survives Rikku as LFF debuts in the four-way format
2863.narrative: The first four-way contest match immediately showed how different the new format could be. Yoshi took first comfortably, while Knuckles survived Rikku after major voting swings and Vaan's shared fanbase hurt Rikku in the fight for second.
2863.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly identifies Vaan as the contest's first clear LFF case, saying his shared Square support drained enough from Rikku to cost her an advancing spot.

2864.headline: KOS-MOS advances as Blizzard LFF rewrites four-way expectations
2864.narrative: Mega Man took the expected first place, but the real story was KOS-MOS advancing while Diablo and Arthas split overlapping support. The writeup treats the result as the match that taught Board 8 how LFF worked in four-way polls.
2864.anomaly_note: The writeup says Diablo and Arthas weakened each other by sharing the same Blizzard fanbase, allowing KOS-MOS to advance despite neither Blizzard entrant being individually helpless.

2865.headline: Frog survives Axel after a huge comeback and late rally
2865.narrative: Frog built a large early cushion, lost it to Axel's powerful daytime comeback, and then recovered in the final stretch. The writeup treats the late Board 8 rally as decisive in Frog reclaiming the advancing spot.
2865.anomaly_note: The writeup describes Board 8 and other supporters openly rallying for Frog during the final stretch, with the late surge overturning Axel's comeback and restoring Frog to second place.

2866.headline: Scorpion crushes expectations while Midna badly underperforms
2866.narrative: Scorpion dominated a match many expected Midna to control, while Midna advanced only because the rest of the field was weak. The writeup treats the result as both a major Midna disappointment and evidence that Scorpion had been underestimated.

2867.headline: Kefka collapses to Marcus as Lettuce Kefka strikes again
2867.narrative: Kefka led comfortably through the early hours before collapsing completely to Marcus Fenix during the day. The writeup remembers the match as another classic Kefka choke, with the picture matchup adding to the explanation for the reversal.
2867.anomaly_note: The writeup repeatedly points to Kefka's infamous Lettuce Kefka image and Marcus Fenix's strong recognizable picture as factors that helped make Kefka's collapse look even worse.

2868.headline: Cloud dominates while Ocelot comfortably beats Jill for second
2868.narrative: Cloud dominated the field as expected, while Ocelot took second over Jill without ever facing serious danger. The writeup finds the result ordinary at the time but notable in retrospect because Jill would reverse the comparison a year later.

2869.headline: Auron cruises while Shadow disappoints and Pyramid Head surprises
2869.narrative: Auron took an easy first and Shadow an equally safe second, making the main result largely predetermined. The writeup instead focuses on Shadow looking much weaker than expected and Pyramid Head unexpectedly beating Chris Redfield for third.

2870.headline: Ryu wins as Nintendo LFF drags Bowser down
2870.narrative: Ryu took first in a result that surprised many bracket players but made sense once Bowser's two fellow Nintendo entrants were considered. Bowser still advanced, but the writeup treats his weak showing as a serious warning for later rounds.
2870.anomaly_note: The writeup says Bowser was weakened by sharing Nintendo support with both Mewtwo and Toad, allowing outside entrant Ryu to take first place comfortably.

2871.headline: Meta Knight shocks Peach to claim an easy advancing spot
2871.narrative: Sephiroth won as expected, but Meta Knight unexpectedly took a clear second over Peach and CATS. The writeup attributes much of the surprise to Meta Knight's pre-release Brawl visibility and treats Peach as poorly suited to the four-way format.

2872.headline: Fox dominates an all-Nintendo four-way through heavy SFF
2872.narrative: Fox dominated an all-Nintendo field far more thoroughly than expected, while Wario eventually secured the second advancing position over Captain Falcon. The writeup treats Fox's performance as one of the contest's strongest examples of SFF.
2872.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly characterizes Fox's dominant performance as Nintendo SFF and says Fox suppressed Captain Falcon more heavily than Wario.

2873.headline: Mario SFFs Pac-Man and hands Big Boss an easy advance
2873.narrative: Mario dominated as expected, but his suppression of Pac-Man made Big Boss's second-place finish much easier than many anticipated. The writeup treats Pac-Man's shared old-school appeal with Mario as the key reason the debated advancing spot became one-sided.
2873.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario was an especially disastrous matchup for Pac-Man because of their overlapping old-school appeal and describes Pac-Man as being SFFed to death.

2874.headline: Phoenix survives Bomberman's long comeback while Magus disappoints
2874.narrative: Magus took first but looked weak enough to damage any hopes of a deep run, while Phoenix Wright turned the fight for second into the real match. Bomberman mounted a long afternoon comeback, only for the heavily favored Board 8 character to hold on at the end.

2875.headline: Bidoof rallies past Edgeworth while Link destroys the field
2875.narrative: Link overwhelmed the entire field, while joke entrant Bidoof rode outside support past Miles Edgeworth for second. The writeup treats Bidoof's success as an important early step toward the larger joke-character runs that followed.
2875.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly credits a 4chan rally with giving Bidoof enough support to beat Miles Edgeworth for the second advancing position.

2876.headline: Vincent crushes Zelda while a close third-place fight goes unnoticed
2876.narrative: Vincent quickly turned the anticipated contest with Zelda into a comfortable first-place finish, while Zelda safely advanced with him. The writeup notes that the genuinely close Tails-The Boss fight for third mattered little because neither advancing spot was threatened.

2877.headline: Raiden survives Sam Fisher's comeback but loses future hype
2877.narrative: Crono took first without drama, while Raiden built a large enough cushion to survive Sam Fisher's strong daytime comeback for second. The writeup treats the finish as close on paper but never truly in danger, while Raiden's poor showing damaged his future expectations.

2878.headline: HK-47 advances from the infamous Jakpack of Suck
2878.narrative: Zero took the expected first place while HK-47 beat the favored Lloyd for second in a weak and widely disliked fourpack. The writeup calls it the Jakpack of Suck and argues that Lloyd's inability to win here became emblematic of Tales characters' contest failures.

2879.headline: Mudkip takes second and looks stronger than a simple joke rally
2879.narrative: Luigi took first easily, but Mudkip's stable support made the second advancing spot far less competitive than expected. The writeup explicitly argues that Mudkip's performance looked like genuine strength rather than a temporary rally and foreshadowed later joke-character fears.

2880.headline: Thrall's WoW rally nearly catches Vergil before the day vote
2880.narrative: Ganondorf won first easily, while Vergil and Thrall fought a much closer battle for the second advancing spot. A WoW rally helped Thrall make a serious overnight push, but Vergil pulled away decisively once daytime voting arrived.
2880.anomaly_note: The writeup describes a World of Warcraft forum thread rallying votes for Thrall and says the push helped him nearly catch Vergil before the daytime vote ended the threat.

2881.headline: Master Chief crushes Yuna as Halo 3 hype peaks
2881.narrative: Master Chief overwhelmed Yuna in a matchup many expected to be competitive, immediately changing expectations for the entire division. The writeup connects the result strongly to the enormous Halo 3 hype surrounding Chief that year.

2882.headline: Liquid steals first from Alucard in a controversial photo finish
2882.narrative: Alucard erased Liquid Snake's large daytime lead and briefly moved ahead at the very end, only for Liquid to snatch first on the final update. Because both characters advanced anyway, the writeup says the historic photo finish carried less consequence than a one-on-one result would have.
2882.anomaly_note: The writeup describes a last-minute Metal Gear rally after Alucard completed his comeback and records complaints that cheating or vote-stuffing may have influenced the razor-thin finish.

2883.headline: Amaterasu beats Little Mac and announces unexpected contest strength
2883.narrative: Dante took the expected first place, while Amaterasu quickly settled the debated fight for second by pulling away from Little Mac. The writeup treats the result as the first strong indication that Amaterasu was much more legitimate than many voters had assumed.

2884.headline: Ada wins easily as Balthier's newcomer hype collapses
2884.narrative: Ada took first with ease while heavily hyped newcomer Balthier badly disappointed in a weak field. The writeup treats the result as proof that Final Fantasy XII's popularity had not translated into the character strength many expected.

2885.headline: Pikachu routs Tidus and accelerates Pokémon's contest resurgence
2885.narrative: Pikachu beat Tidus far more easily than years of Pokémon contest weakness had led people to expect. The writeup debates several possible explanations for Tidus's underperformance but ultimately treats the match as another major step in Pokémon's rise to legitimate contest strength.

2886.headline: Leon and Vivi advance through an almost completely uneventful match
2886.narrative: Leon and Vivi took the two advancing spots in almost exactly the straightforward order expected. The writeup repeatedly calls the match boring and finds little meaning beyond setting up Vivi's coming encounter with Pikachu and Tidus.

2887.headline: L-Block shocks Laharl and briefly leads Kirby in its debut
2887.narrative: Kirby took first as expected, but L-Block immediately demolished expectations by beating Laharl for the other advancing spot and even briefly leading Kirby. The writeup remembers those opening minutes as the first astonishing sign of what L-Block would become later in the contest.

2888.headline: Kratos wins as Nintendo LFF weakens Donkey Kong and Marth
2888.narrative: Kratos took first in a result that surprised many casual brackets but looked straightforward to the writeup. Donkey Kong still advanced, though sharing Nintendo support with Marth made an already difficult matchup much worse for him.
2888.anomaly_note: The writeup says Donkey Kong and Marth drained each other's Nintendo support, making outsider Kratos's first-place finish effectively inevitable.

2889.headline: Snake cruises while Nightmare advances and Vyse badly disappoints
2889.narrative: Snake took first comfortably and Nightmare secured second without much difficulty, while the hoped-for strength of Vyse's cult fanbase failed to materialize. The writeup treats Vyse as another aging RPG character whose contest relevance had faded badly.

2890.headline: Ryu overwhelms the split Kingdom Hearts field
2890.narrative: Much of the writeup is an extended aside explaining who Haseo is; its match discussion emphasizes Ryu Hayabusa unexpectedly overpowering the split Kingdom Hearts field and making his later rematch with Riku look settled.

2891.headline: Squall settles the Aeris debate while Akuma debuts well
2891.narrative: Squall settled a long-running strength debate with Aeris, while Akuma's debut was respectable despite a field crowded with Square characters. The writeup treats Akuma's showing as evidence that better bracket placement could have produced wins.

2892.headline: Lara survives Wesker after a surprisingly competitive fight
2892.narrative: Sora controlled the match while Wesker briefly made the fight with Lara genuinely competitive. Lara eventually pulled away, but the writeup regards Wesker's showing as surprisingly strong despite a potentially damaging picture.
2892.anomaly_note: The writeup says Wesker's ugly match picture may have hurt him in his close fight with Lara for the second advancing spot.

2893.headline: Duke shocks Gordon while Ike nearly makes it chaotic
2893.narrative: A supposedly weak fourpack produced one of the round's funniest matches, with Duke unexpectedly taking control while Gordon Freeman disappointed again. Ike also impressed with a strong daytime push even though he never completed the comeback.

2894.headline: Sonic advances but delivers another warning sign
2894.narrative: Sonic and Sub-Zero advanced comfortably, but Sonic's performance was far weaker than expected for a Noble Nine character. The writeup treats it as another warning that the Sonic cast was declining badly.

2895.headline: Mega Man and Yoshi cruise as Knuckles disappoints again
2895.narrative: Mega Man and Yoshi advanced with little suspense after Knuckles's weak opening-round showing had already killed most of the debate. Knuckles again disappointed and never seriously threatened Yoshi.

2896.headline: Samus dominates while Scorpion advances past a weakened Midna
2896.narrative: Samus dominated while Scorpion comfortably secured the other advancing spot. Midna's earlier weakness and the Nintendo vote drain from Samus left her with little realistic path forward.
2896.anomaly_note: The writeup says Samus drained Nintendo support from Midna, worsening Midna's position against the outside contenders.

2897.headline: Fenix rides the day vote past Ocelot for second
2897.narrative: Cloud dominated as expected, while the real contest was a three-way fight for the other advancing position. Marcus Fenix used his strong daytime trend to erase Ocelot's advantage and complete the comeback.

2898.headline: Ryu beats Bowser again in another four-way mystery
2898.narrative: Auron looked excellent, but the lasting story was Ryu beating Bowser again even after the Nintendo overlap from their earlier meeting was gone. The writeup finds the result difficult to explain beyond the volatility of the four-way format.

2899.headline: Sephiroth and Fox advance through a predictable Nintendo field
2899.narrative: Sephiroth and Fox advanced exactly as expected in a match the writeup considers almost completely predetermined. Sephiroth nevertheless looked especially strong against a field otherwise composed entirely of Nintendo characters.

2900.headline: Naked Snake picture sends Big Boss past Magus
2900.narrative: Mario cruised while Big Boss demolished Magus for the other advancing spot. The writeup treats the newly revealed Naked Snake picture as the defining factor that transformed expectations before the poll even began.
2900.anomaly_note: The writeup calls Big Boss's Naked Snake image one of the clearest picture-factor examples, saying the strong recognizable picture helped turn the matchup against Magus decisively in Big Boss's favor.

2901.headline: Bidoof's suspected offsite push briefly terrifies Vincent
2901.narrative: Link and Vincent ultimately advanced comfortably, but Bidoof briefly turned the match into chaos by challenging Vincent early and even beating Link in the opening vote. The writeup remembers the surge as one of the contest's most surreal joke-character moments.
2901.anomaly_note: The writeup attributes Bidoof's extraordinary early surge to suspected offsite rallying, especially from 4chan, and also records suspicions of vote stuffing.

2902.headline: Zero makes Crono look vulnerable before Vincent
2902.narrative: Crono and Zero advanced as expected, but Zero stayed close enough to make Crono look vulnerable before his anticipated showdown with Vincent. Raiden also emerged as a major disappointment after failing to separate convincingly from HK-47.

2903.headline: Mudkip scares Nintendo before Luigi's morning comeback
2903.narrative: Mudkip turned the opening hours into a genuine scare by leading the Nintendo favorites, but Ganondorf recovered overnight and Luigi's morning vote erased Mudkip's remaining advantage. The writeup treats the match as proof that joke characters could no longer be dismissed.

2904.headline: Master Chief confirms his breakout with another dominant showing
2904.narrative: Master Chief followed his strong opening round with an even more convincing performance against improved competition. The writeup treats him as the clear star of the contest to that point and a heavy favorite to take the division.

2905.headline: Amaterasu survives a long three-way fight for second
2905.narrative: Dante ran away with first, while Amaterasu, Ada and Balthier spent much of the match in a tight fight for the other advancing spot. Amaterasu eventually emerged from what the writeup remembers as a genuine upset and one of the round's better races.

2906.headline: Square vote splitting sends Pikachu through again
2906.narrative: Leon won comfortably while Pikachu capitalized on the divided Square field to advance again. The writeup presents Tidus and Vivi as holding each other back and turning Pikachu's favorable draw into another survival.
2906.anomaly_note: The writeup says Vivi and Tidus split Square support badly enough that neither could catch Pikachu, allowing the outside Pokémon entrant to take the second advancing spot.

2907.headline: Nintendo vote splitting turns L-Block into a real threat
2907.narrative: Kratos took first, but the important result was L-Block advancing again while Kirby was weakened by Donkey Kong. The writeup marks this as the point when L-Block stopped looking like a harmless joke and became a serious contest threat.
2907.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Donkey Kong drained Nintendo support from Kirby, costing Kirby the advancing spot and allowing L-Block to move on.

2908.headline: Riku reverses the Ryu result as four-way logic breaks again
2908.narrative: Snake advanced easily, while Riku reversed his opening-round loss to Ryu Hayabusa and took the other spot. The writeup treats the reversal as another example of how unreliable direct comparisons could become in the four-way format.

2909.headline: Sora reverses Aeris as Squall drains her support
2909.narrative: Squall took control immediately, while Sora decisively reversed his old loss to Aeris. Aeris nearly fell behind Lara as well, making the writeup treat the result as a sharp confirmation of her decline.
2909.anomaly_note: The writeup argues that Squall's presence hurt fellow Square entrant Aeris far more than Sora, helping Sora reverse their old matchup and advance comfortably.

2910.headline: Brawl hype transforms Sonic's rematch with Sub-Zero
2910.narrative: Sonic crushed Sub-Zero much more convincingly than in their opening-round meeting after his Smash announcement changed the atmosphere around him. The writeup still finds the surrounding results too inconsistent to decide whether Sonic had truly returned to elite form.

2911.headline: Samus survives Mega Man despite Yoshi's Nintendo vote drain
2911.narrative: Samus and Mega Man produced a dramatic early duel before Samus eventually established control, while Yoshi and Scorpion fell away. The result strengthened the case that Samus had moved clearly ahead of Mega Man despite the unfavorable Nintendo overlap.
2911.anomaly_note: The writeup says Yoshi's Nintendo support hurt Samus more than Mega Man, making their early first-place battle much tighter than it otherwise would have been.

2912.headline: Cloud dominates while Final Fantasy overlap helps Ryu advance
2912.narrative: Cloud overwhelmed the field and further fueled speculation that he could challenge Link. Ryu advanced ahead of Auron, with the writeup treating Cloud's effect on Auron as central to the result.
2912.anomaly_note: The writeup says Cloud's shared Final Fantasy support held Auron down, allowing outside entrant Ryu to benefit and claim the other advancing position.

2913.headline: Sephiroth handles Mario while Mario crushes Fox's support
2913.narrative: Sephiroth beat Mario comfortably in a result that had become predictable by match day. The more notable secondary story was Fox collapsing in Mario's presence after looking strong against Nintendo opposition earlier.
2913.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario heavily suppressed fellow Nintendo entrant Fox, leaving Fox far weaker than his prior-round performance suggested.

2914.headline: Vincent breaks the Noble Nine by eliminating Crono
2914.narrative: The anticipated Crono-Vincent showdown delivered a close race for the second advancing position, and Vincent ultimately broke through. The writeup treats the result as the first true breach of the Noble Nine and a major contest milestone.

2915.headline: Pig Ganon picture helps Luigi reverse their matchup
2915.narrative: Master Chief took first, while Luigi defeated Ganondorf in the fight for the other advancing spot. The writeup repeatedly points to Ganondorf's unfavorable first-appearance sprite as the decisive handicap.
2915.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ganondorf's ugly pig sprite hurt him badly against Luigi and likely reversed a matchup Ganondorf had previously won.

2916.headline: Capcom vote splitting powers Pikachu to a stunning first
2916.narrative: Pikachu produced one of the contest's biggest shocks by taking first over a field of Capcom characters. The writeup treats the result as a major turning point in Pokémon's growing contest reputation.
2916.anomaly_note: The writeup says the three Capcom entrants divided overlapping support, creating the opening that allowed outside entrant Pikachu to beat them all.

2917.headline: L-Block nearly challenges Snake and becomes an elite threat
2917.narrative: Snake eventually won, but L-Block dominated the opening and advanced with ease over Kratos and Riku. The writeup marks this as the first match where the joke entrant looked capable of threatening the contest's established elite directly.

2918.headline: Sora's vote drain helps Sonic hold off Squall
2918.narrative: Sonic held off Squall for first, but Squall remained unexpectedly competitive despite sharing support with Sora. The writeup treats Sonic's narrow-looking advantage as another sign that four-way matches exposed his weaknesses.
2918.anomaly_note: The writeup says Sora drained enough Square support from Squall that Squall probably would have beaten Sonic without Sora in the poll.

2919.headline: Mega Man collapses as Cloud and Samus advance easily
2919.narrative: Cloud and Samus advanced through a quarterfinal that played out almost exactly as expected. The lasting story was Mega Man's poor showing, which ended any serious argument that he still belonged alongside Samus.

2920.headline: Mario's vote drain makes Link look briefly vulnerable
2920.narrative: Link and Sephiroth advanced as expected, but Mario held up better against Link than many anticipated. The writeup treats Link's diminished dominance as the first meaningful encouragement for people hoping Cloud could beat him later.
2920.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario clearly weakened fellow Nintendo entrant Link, narrowing Link's advantage over Sephiroth and briefly making Link look vulnerable.

2921.headline: Pikachu's Nintendo vote drain helps eliminate Luigi
2921.narrative: Master Chief took first while Dante survived for the other advancing spot. Luigi led early but could not overcome the continued presence of Pikachu, whose run ended while also dragging a major Nintendo character out with it.
2921.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pikachu continued to siphon Nintendo support from Luigi, helping Dante take the second advancing position and eliminating Luigi.

2922.headline: L-Block rallies past Snake and shatters bracket expectations
2922.narrative: L-Block led from the opening minutes and held off a long Snake comeback to take first. The writeup identifies this as the match where the joke entrant became a genuine Internet-backed force capable of defeating Noble Nine characters.
2922.anomaly_note: The writeup describes L-Block's growing Internet support as an active rally and says a late counter-push helped stop Snake's comeback.

2923.headline: Link and Cloud advance while Samus surprisingly tops Sephiroth
2923.narrative: Link and Cloud advanced through a semifinal whose top order was never seriously in doubt. Samus nevertheless outperformed Sephiroth, providing the only notable wrinkle in an otherwise predictable heavyweight match.
2923.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link heavily suppressed Samus through their overlapping Nintendo support, even though Samus still performed surprisingly well relative to Sephiroth.

2924.headline: Internet attention sends L-Block charging into the final
2924.narrative: L-Block's Internet momentum exploded as outside sites discovered the run, and Snake was left fighting Master Chief for the other final spot. The writeup treats this as the moment the joke had grown beyond Board 8 into a broad online bandwagon.
2924.anomaly_note: The writeup says outside attention from Kotaku, 4chan, Vote for the Worst and other sites expanded L-Block's support, including a visible surge after a Kotaku link.

2925.headline: L-Block's Internet rally dethrones Link in the final
2925.narrative: L-Block completed its improbable run by beating Link in a final dominated by an enormous Internet bandwagon. The writeup remembers the result as the ultimate joke-character triumph and the defining match of the contest.
2925.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes the final as driven by massive rallying and broad Internet support for L-Block, which overwhelmed Link's attempted comeback.

2926.headline: ? Block gets revenge on L-Block in the bonus poll
2926.narrative: The bonus poll gave the contest's joke objects one last showcase, with ? Block mounting a comeback against the newly crowned L-Block. The writeup treats the result as amusing backlash rather than anything that diminished L-Block's championship.

3244.headline: Zack opens 2008 with an immediate bracket surprise
3244.narrative: The opening match immediately produced a surprise, with Zack outperforming the expected Nintendo advantage and establishing himself as much stronger than many anticipated. Cecil, meanwhile, disappointed badly despite renewed Final Fantasy IV visibility.

3245.headline: Zidane shocks Shadow while Link resumes dominating
3245.narrative: Link began his post-L-Block campaign in dominant fashion, while Zidane unexpectedly beat Shadow for the other advancing position. The writeup treats Shadow's failure as a major early bracket bust and another sign of Sonic Team's decline.

3246.headline: Duke shocks the field as Kefka collapses
3246.narrative: A heavily debated fodder match became genuinely strange when Duke surged into contention and Kefka collapsed to the bottom. Marth eventually took first, but Duke's unexpected advancement became the match's defining surprise.

3247.headline: Altair dominates his debut while Lucario barely survives
3247.narrative: Altair dominated his contest debut while Lucario barely held off Isaac for the second advancing spot. The writeup regards Lucario as one of the contest's biggest disappointments given Pokémon's strength and his prominent Smash appearance.

3248.headline: Liquid's strong showing complicates Luigi's next round
3248.narrative: Luigi and Liquid advanced in an otherwise predictable match, but Liquid stayed much closer to Luigi than expected. The writeup treats Liquid's strength as a new complication for the Nintendo-heavy matchup waiting in the next round.

3249.headline: Bowser cruises while Phoenix looks increasingly legitimate
3249.narrative: Bowser and Phoenix advanced with almost no suspense, giving the contest a rare straightforward result. The writeup's main takeaway is that Phoenix now looked more like a naturally competitive entrant than a Board 8 novelty.

3250.headline: Zelda resists Mario and ends Knuckles's opening-round streak
3250.narrative: Mario won as expected, but Zelda resisted the feared fanbase suppression and comfortably held the second advancing spot over Knuckles. The writeup treats the result as another blow to Sonic Team's standing and a strong performance for Zelda.

3251.headline: Mudkip advances but lacks the bracket for another L-Block run
3251.narrative: Mega Man X dominated while Mudkip comfortably claimed the other advancing spot, confirming that the joke character still had substantial support. The writeup nevertheless argues that Mudkip's bracket placement made another L-Block-style run unrealistic.

3252.headline: Samus and Nightmare advance through an uneventful opener
3252.narrative: Samus and Nightmare advanced through one of the round's least eventful matches. The writeup finds little to learn beyond Samus taking care of business and the weaker entrants remaining firmly in fodder territory.

3253.headline: Frog holds off KOS-MOS despite the picture controversy
3253.narrative: Ganondorf won comfortably while Frog held off KOS-MOS without the expected daytime collapse. The delayed match picture caused controversy, but once it appeared the writeup says it did little to change the Frog-KOS-MOS race.
3253.anomaly_note: The writeup says the eventual match picture hurt Ganondorf while giving KOS-MOS no meaningful advantage over Frog, even though KOS-MOS supporters had expected her image to help.

3254.headline: Falco and GLaDOS outperform expectations behind Vincent
3254.narrative: Vincent advanced as expected, but Falco looked substantially stronger than anticipated and GLaDOS also exceeded the writeup's low expectations. Wander remained complete fodder, making the middle of the field more interesting than the winner.

3255.headline: Gordon's resurgence continues behind Scorpion
3255.narrative: Scorpion took first, while Gordon Freeman continued his post-GFNW rehabilitation with another strong advancement. The writeup sees the Orange Box era as having transformed Gordon from a perennial choke artist into a genuinely respectable entrant.

3256.headline: Crono and Amaterasu cruise through a predictable opener
3256.narrative: Crono and Amaterasu advanced through a largely predictable match, with neither Frank West nor Kaim posing a meaningful threat. The writeup treats it as another routine Noble Nine opening-round performance.

3257.headline: L-Block outlasts Ryu in a low-stakes thriller
3257.narrative: The defending champion showed little sign of fading, and the writeup remembers its duel with Ryu as an excellent fight that the four-way format robbed of real stakes. Meta Knight's weak showing was the main disappointment.

3258.headline: Captain Falcon finally breaks through behind Alucard
3258.narrative: Alucard advanced as expected, but Captain Falcon's strong showing overturned his reputation as perennial fodder and sent him through as well. Diddy Kong's failure was the sharper disappointment.

3259.headline: Arthas advances as Pikachu's presence hurts Ike
3259.narrative: Pikachu took control while Arthas converted a favorable draw into a surprising advancement. The result also punctured another piece of the pre-contest Brawl hype surrounding Ike.
3259.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pikachu's overlapping Nintendo and Smash support put Ike in a bad LFF situation, helping Arthas take the other advancing spot.

3260.headline: The Cube advances while Donkey Kong disappoints again
3260.narrative: Weighted Companion Cube turned a heavily debated Tidus-Donkey Kong match into another joke-character success, while Tidus narrowly secured the other advancing position. Donkey Kong's failure added another chapter to his contest reputation for disappointing.

3261.headline: Mega Man and Nero cruise through a predictable fourpack
3261.narrative: Mega Man and Nero advanced in a match the writeup considered almost completely predetermined. The only real takeaway was how little the Brawl-backed Nintendo fodder could do.

3262.headline: Ryu edges Zero as more Brawl hype fizzles
3262.narrative: Ryu Hayabusa and Zero were always the serious contenders, but Ryu's ability to take first made the match more interesting than expected. Dedede and Pit reinforced the writeup's view that Brawl alone could not manufacture contest strength.

3263.headline: Snake dominates another straightforward first-round match
3263.narrative: Snake and Vivi advanced exactly as the writeup expected, with little genuine suspense. Snake's strong showing was more notable than the order of finish and fed expectations for a major run.

3264.headline: Sora and Fox advance without any real drama
3264.narrative: Sora and Fox produced the expected advancing pair in a match without meaningful swings. Chris Redfield did better than his prior contest reputation suggested, but never threatened the leaders.

3265.headline: Squall crushes Yoshi far harder than expected
3265.narrative: Squall overwhelmed a Yoshi who had been expected to remain much closer, continuing Squall's unusually strong multiway form. The writeup treats Yoshi's performance as the real shock.

3266.headline: Cloud and Midna dispatch an overmatched field
3266.narrative: Cloud and Midna advanced in another first-round match the writeup regarded as essentially decided before it began. Edgeworth and Axel never generated the upset or novelty support needed to matter.

3267.headline: Mewtwo crushes Ness and sends Pac-Man through
3267.narrative: Mewtwo erased the embarrassment of his earlier contest debut with an emphatic performance. Ness collapsed against the stronger Nintendo presence, allowing Pac-Man to advance instead.
3267.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Mewtwo SFFed Ness badly, leaving Ness far weaker than expected and opening the second advancing spot for Pac-Man.

3268.headline: Big Boss stuns Kirby in a massive opening-round upset
3268.narrative: Big Boss delivered a result the writeup remembers as almost unimaginable at the time, beating a heavily favored Kirby outright. The upset immediately turned Big Boss into one of the contest's biggest talking points.
3268.anomaly_note: The writeup says Jinjo and Lucas hurt Kirby by splitting Nintendo support, though it also stresses that this alone cannot explain the scale of Big Boss's upset.

3269.headline: Master Chief advances but loses his previous year's aura
3269.narrative: Master Chief and Raiden advanced as expected, but Chief looked much less imposing than during his celebrated previous run. The writeup treats that decline as the match's main warning sign.

3270.headline: Leon and Riku advance through a routine opener
3270.narrative: Leon and Riku advanced in the expected order, with none of the feared choke or upset scenarios materializing. The writeup treats it as another largely forgettable first-round result.

3271.headline: Hogger's rally steals second from a collapsing Ramza
3271.narrative: Dante was never threatened, but the fight behind him became a three-way scramble in which Hogger surged past Ramza and Laharl. The result became an early signature moment for Ramza's reputation as a contest choker.
3271.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Hogger drew an Internet rally during the day, turning a deficit into a lead and ultimately denying Ramza the advancing spot.

3272.headline: Sandbag rallies past Magus for a major joke upset
3272.narrative: Sonic won comfortably, but Sandbag's comeback against Magus supplied the real drama. The upset confirmed both Magus's long-running reputation for disappointing and the continuing power of joke entrants.
3272.anomaly_note: The writeup says Sandbag's comeback went beyond a normal daytime trend and identifies a rally as the reason the joke entrant surged past Magus.

3273.headline: Auron cruises as Marcus Fenix falls back to earth
3273.narrative: Auron and Sub-Zero advanced in the expected order, leaving little suspense at the top. Marcus Fenix's collapse after his prior deep run was the main story and effectively ended his relevance to later contests.

3274.headline: Tifa withstands Sephiroth better than expected
3274.narrative: Sephiroth and Tifa advanced as expected, but Tifa held up far better against Sephiroth than many feared. The writeup treats that resistance as an encouraging sign rather than a true upset story.

3275.headline: Jill reverses Ocelot as Metal Gear hype falls flat
3275.narrative: Kratos advanced comfortably, while Jill reversed the prior year's result against Ocelot and took the other spot. Ocelot's failure to capitalize on fresh Metal Gear momentum made him the match's major disappointment.

3276.headline: ZackFAQs takes off behind another dominant Link win
3276.narrative: Link dominated, but the match is remembered as the real beginning of ZackFAQs. Zack's convincing advancement transformed him from a promising newcomer into one of the contest's central bandwagon stories.
3276.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link SFFed Wario into irrelevance, leaving the meaningful race to Zack and Zidane.

3277.headline: Duke and Altair advance as Marth gets squeezed out
3277.narrative: Duke and Altair emerged from a chaotic matchup that punished Marth and further damaged the pre-contest Brawl narrative. Duke's unlikely run continued while Lucario confirmed his disappointing debut.
3277.anomaly_note: The writeup says Lucario's presence badly hurt fellow Nintendo entrant Marth, helping outside contenders Duke and Altair take the advancing positions.

3278.headline: Nintendo vote splitting sends Liquid to first
3278.narrative: Liquid took advantage of a badly divided field to win, while Luigi survived for the other advancing spot and Bowser fell out. The writeup uses the result as another example of four-way fanbase splitting producing strange outcomes.
3278.anomaly_note: The writeup says the Nintendo-oriented support was split among Luigi, Bowser and Phoenix, allowing Liquid Snake to benefit as the outside option.

3279.headline: Mario survives Mega Man X as Mudkip's joke run fades
3279.narrative: Mega Man X seriously challenged Mario for first before Mario's morning surge reversed the race. Zelda narrowly escaped last place but was eliminated, while Mudkip's inability to reproduce a joke run made the match a turning point for bandwagon expectations.
3279.anomaly_note: The writeup characterizes the all-Nintendo field as a heavily leeched matchup and describes Zelda's elimination as another result shaped by overlapping support.

3280.headline: Samus and Ganondorf provide a quiet rest break
3280.narrative: Samus and Ganondorf advanced through what the writeup openly calls a rest-break match. Frog's old upset magic never appeared, and the result remained straightforward throughout.

3281.headline: Gordon shocks Scorpion and keeps the GFNW reversal going
3281.narrative: Vincent advanced comfortably, while Gordon Freeman completed another major step in his reversal of the old GFNW reputation by beating Scorpion for the second spot. Falco never became a serious factor.
3281.anomaly_note: The writeup says Scorpion's poor match picture was not the sole reason he lost, but explicitly states that it hurt his chances against Gordon Freeman.

3282.headline: L-Block advances but finally looks vulnerable
3282.narrative: Crono and L-Block advanced in a much quieter sequel to L-Block's chaotic opening match. The defending champion looked strikingly ordinary, creating the first real sense that the repeat bid might be beatable.

3283.headline: Pikachu finally escapes a stubborn Alucard challenge
3283.narrative: Pikachu and Alucard advanced after an unexpectedly fierce battle for first that swung repeatedly across the day. The writeup treats the duel as another good match diminished by the top-two-advance format.
3283.anomaly_note: The writeup says Captain Falcon's overlapping Nintendo support held Pikachu down, helping turn Pikachu's fight with Alucard into a much closer race than their standalone strength suggested.

3284.headline: The Cube advances again without needing any chaos
3284.narrative: Mega Man and Weighted Companion Cube advanced in an anticlimactic match whose outcome settled almost immediately. The Cube now looked less like a volatile joke rally and more like a stable, legitimately dangerous entrant.

3285.headline: Snake dominates while Zero survives Vivi's late push
3285.narrative: Snake delivered another statement performance, while Zero and Vivi fought a much more entertaining battle for the second advancing spot. Zero survived, but Vivi's late resistance made the race memorable.

3286.headline: Fox's presence helps Sora leave Yoshi behind
3286.narrative: Squall and Sora advanced together yet again, while Yoshi collapsed far more badly than expected. The result reinforced the strange independence of the Squall-Sora pairing and exposed Yoshi's vulnerability in the field.
3286.anomaly_note: The writeup says Fox's presence hurt fellow Nintendo entrant Yoshi, while Sora remained largely independent of Squall and benefited from the contrast.

3287.headline: Cloud dominates while Mewtwo quietly survives Midna
3287.narrative: Cloud overwhelmed the field, while Mewtwo held off Midna for the other advancing position without the race ever becoming the epic duel its closeness suggested. The writeup sees Cloud's dominance as the larger statement.

3288.headline: Master Chief rallies past Big Boss for second
3288.narrative: Kirby advanced, but the real battle was Master Chief's comeback against Big Boss. Chief's late surge turned a long, competitive fight into another memorable rally-driven reversal.
3288.anomaly_note: The writeup says Master Chief's fans rallied hard enough to erase Big Boss's lead and secure advancement. It also says Raiden's near-total Metal Gear overlap drained support from Big Boss.

3289.headline: Dante and Leon restore order after a lively start
3289.narrative: Dante and Leon advanced in the same order their prior meetings suggested, despite a brief burst of early excitement. Riku and Hogger never developed the upset or bandwagon threat some had imagined.

3290.headline: Auron stuns Sonic and exposes a Noble Nine weakness
3290.narrative: Auron decisively beat Sonic in one of the contest's most shocking strength results, even though the format still allowed Sonic to advance. The writeup treats the performance as a genuine breach in the Noble Nine's aura.

3291.headline: Sephiroth suppresses Tifa and opens the door for Kratos
3291.narrative: Sephiroth took first as expected, while Kratos again benefited from a field that disadvantaged one of his stronger rivals. Tifa's elimination made the fanbase dynamics more important than the nominal matchup strength.
3291.anomaly_note: The writeup says Sephiroth's shared Final Fantasy support suppressed Tifa, allowing Kratos to take advantage and claim the other advancing spot.

3292.headline: ZackFAQs surges onward behind an unstoppable Link
3292.narrative: Link continued his dominant run, but Zack became the emotional center of the match by advancing again and driving the ZackFAQs bandwagon deeper into the bracket. Duke and Altair exited with respectable runs of their own.

3293.headline: Mario suppresses Luigi while Mega Man X advances
3293.narrative: Mario and Mega Man X advanced after an early fight that briefly made another Mario upset look possible. Luigi's collapse under Mario's presence removed the feared family interference and left Liquid out as well.
3293.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario directly SFFed Luigi, leaving his brother far weaker than his standalone strength and clearing the way for Mega Man X to advance.

3294.headline: Nintendo overlap buries Ganondorf while Samus advances
3294.narrative: Samus and Vincent advanced as expected, but Ganondorf collapsed so badly that Gordon Freeman escaped last place. The writeup treats the fanbase interaction as the defining feature of an otherwise predictable divisional final.
3294.anomaly_note: The writeup describes Ganondorf as heavily suppressed by Samus through their shared Nintendo support. It also says Ganondorf's presence drained Samus enough to tighten her comparison with outside contender Vincent.

3295.headline: Pikachu ends L-Block's reign and changes Pokémon's image
3295.narrative: Pikachu finally ended L-Block's title defense after a tense early struggle, marking a major shift in both joke-character expectations and Pokémon's standing on the site. Crono advanced comfortably alongside him.
3295.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Crono SFFed Alucard into the floor, leaving the real advancing fight to Pikachu and L-Block.

3296.headline: The Cube rallies past Mega Man for another upset
3296.narrative: Snake controlled the match, while Mega Man and Weighted Companion Cube fought for the other advancing spot. The Cube's late surge completed another inanimate-object upset and ended Mega Man's run.
3296.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Weighted Companion Cube rallied during its fight with Mega Man, producing the decisive swing that carried the Cube into the next round.

3297.headline: Cloud's Square suppression sends Mewtwo into the quarterfinals
3297.narrative: Cloud dominated, while Mewtwo turned a seemingly unfavorable draw into one of the contest's largest surprises. Squall and Sora were left fighting each other for scraps behind the advancing pair.
3297.anomaly_note: The writeup says Cloud's presence created massive Square SFF against Squall and Sora, allowing outside entrant Mewtwo to capitalize and advance.

3298.headline: Kirby keeps rolling while Dante eliminates Master Chief
3298.narrative: Kirby continued his unexpected run by taking first, while Dante beat Master Chief in the meaningful fight for the other advancing position. The writeup remembers the match as a fun clash of very different contest identities.

3299.headline: Sephiroth suppresses Auron as Sonic safely advances
3299.narrative: Sephiroth and Sonic advanced in a match the writeup considered essentially predetermined once Auron shared the field with Sephiroth. Sonic's solid showing quieted some of the criticism generated by his earlier loss.
3299.anomaly_note: The writeup says Sephiroth SFFed fellow Final Fantasy entrant Auron badly, preventing Auron from reproducing his prior win over Sonic.

3300.headline: Mario survives ZackFAQs under Link's crushing shadow
3300.narrative: Link remained untouchable, while Zack made a dramatic but ultimately unsuccessful attempt to steal the other advancing spot from Mario. The loss ended one of the contest's most popular bandwagon runs.
3300.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link SFFed both Mario and Mega Man X, with Mega Man X falling to a distant position after initially challenging Mario.

3301.headline: Board 8 rallies Crono through his long-awaited redemption
3301.narrative: The writeup treats Crono versus Vincent as the emotional centerpiece of the contest, built on years of Crono near-misses and frustration. Crono's late comeback finally reversed their previous result and completed the redemption story.
3301.anomaly_note: The writeup says Board 8 rallied intensely for Crono late in the match, turning the final fight with Vincent into a successful comeback for the advancing spot.

3302.headline: Cloud and Snake advance as the Cube fades quietly
3302.narrative: Cloud and Snake advanced through a deliberately uneventful quarterfinal after the drama of the prior match. The Cube's quiet exit confirmed that the inanimate-object wave had largely run out of steam.

3303.headline: Kirby eliminates Sonic after years of warning signs
3303.narrative: Kirby delivered another major shock by advancing ahead of Sonic, whose long decline finally produced a costly elimination. The writeup treats Sonic's failure as the culmination of years of warning signs rather than a random fluke.

3304.headline: Nintendo vote drain carries Crono past Mario into the final
3304.narrative: Link took the expected first position, while Crono finally reached a true contest final by reversing his old rivalry with Mario. The writeup frames it as the payoff to Crono's long redemption arc.
3304.anomaly_note: The writeup says Link and Samus drained Nintendo support from Mario, allowing outside entrant Crono to beat Mario comfortably for the other final berth.

3305.headline: Snake exploits the split field and beats Cloud
3305.narrative: Snake converted the divided field into a surprise first-place finish, while Cloud recovered enough to secure the other final berth. Sephiroth's collapse and Kirby's early pressure made the semifinal far stranger than expected.
3305.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kirby SFFed Sephiroth badly, leaving Sephiroth unusually weak. It also says Sephiroth leeched enough Final Fantasy support from Cloud to keep Cloud from catching outside contender Snake.

3306.headline: Link reclaims the crown while Snake completes his bandwagon run
3306.narrative: Link completed his revenge tour and reclaimed the championship, but Snake supplied the final surprise by finishing ahead of Cloud. The writeup treats Snake's run as the culmination of years of gradual growth and one of the contest's defining stories.
3306.anomaly_note: The writeup describes Solid Snake as the contest's biggest rallied bandwagon, saying his accumulated support carried him to a shocking second-place finish in the championship.

3308.headline: Classic Link wins the ultimate same-character SFF joke
3308.narrative: The bonus poll was built around the joke of Link facing alternate versions of himself. CD-I Link briefly rode the novelty vote before Classic Link overwhelmed the field, producing a record-setting and deliberately absurd finish.
3308.anomaly_note: The writeup calls this the strongest SFF case imaginable: Classic Link suppressed other versions of the same character, including Young Link, Toon Link and CD-I Link.

3446.headline: Donkey Kong survives Punch-Out as Tetris dominates
3446.narrative: The first 2009 match centered on Donkey Kong versus Punch-Out for the second advancing spot. Donkey Kong survived an early scare and a reputation for choking to pull away, while Tetris dominated the field.
3446.anomaly_note: The writeup says Tetris imposed old-school overlap on Space Invaders and likely hurt Donkey Kong as well, though Donkey Kong was still strong enough to beat Punch-Out.

3447.headline: Oregon Trail fades while Mega Man 2 underwhelms
3447.narrative: The Oregon Trail briefly looked capable of becoming the contest's next joke bandwagon, but collapsed after a few hours and left Pac-Man safely in second. Mega Man 2 won easily yet looked much weaker than its pre-contest hype suggested.

3448.headline: Mario buries Duck Hunt with same-cartridge SFF
3448.narrative: Mario dominated so completely that Duck Hunt could not mount a comeback against Ninja Gaiden for the second advancing spot. The writeup treats the result as a textbook example of extreme overlap overwhelming an otherwise stronger game.
3448.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Mario's suppression of Duck Hunt 'Same Cartridge SFF,' since the two games famously shared an NES cartridge.

3449.headline: Zelda crushes Metroid while Contra fails to capitalize
3449.narrative: Zelda dominated as expected, and Metroid still advanced despite taking a severe fanbase hit. Contra's failure to capitalize became the larger surprise and began a recurring pattern of disappointing shooter performances.
3449.anomaly_note: The writeup says Zelda heavily SFFed Metroid, while also entertaining the possibility that Contra suffered some Nintendo-related overlap of its own.

3450.headline: Sonic routs Street Fighter II in a major surprise
3450.narrative: Sonic defeated Street Fighter II far more easily than the consensus expected, while Castlevania III briefly made the bottom of the poll interesting. The writeup reads the result as another sign that fighting games simply lacked GameFAQs strength.

3451.headline: Mario 3 obliterates the field while Monkey Island survives
3451.narrative: Super Mario Bros. 3 delivered one of the most overwhelming four-way performances ever, leaving the weak supporting field to fight over scraps. Secret of Monkey Island eventually emerged from that battle for the other advancing spot.

3452.headline: Battletoads rallies but Mario World and Final Fantasy cruise
3452.narrative: Super Mario World and Final Fantasy advanced without real drama, while Battletoads became notable mainly for a highly visible 4chan push. Prince of Persia produced one of the contest's weakest performances.
3452.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes a pre-planned 4chan rally for Battletoads. It says the push inflated Battletoads' total but never came close to threatening the advancing games.

3453.headline: Final Fantasy IV cruises in a completely predictable match
3453.narrative: Final Fantasy IV and Mega Man 3 advanced in exactly the order expected, with little suspense. The result strengthened Final Fantasy IV's standing and largely ended the idea that the original Final Fantasy was clearly stronger.

3454.headline: Super Metroid edges Mario Kart in a strange classic
3454.narrative: Super Metroid and Super Mario Kart produced a remarkably close, trend-defying fight for first while both were already safe to advance. Sonic 3's poor showing was the bigger strategic surprise, and the writeup reports but does not endorse cheating accusations.

3455.headline: Donkey Kong Country survives Zelda SFF as Doom collapses
3455.narrative: A Link to the Past dominated while Donkey Kong Country repeatedly flirted with choking away second place. Doom nevertheless failed to capitalize, turning what looked like a favorable upset setup into another shooter disappointment.
3455.anomaly_note: The writeup says A Link to the Past clearly SFFed Donkey Kong Country, though Doom was too weak to take advantage of the favorable situation.

3456.headline: Link's Awakening breaks out while Mega Man X exits
3456.narrative: Link's Awakening decisively beat Mega Man X for the second advancing spot and immediately established itself as a legitimate Zelda threat rather than a minor handheld entry. Final Fantasy VI advanced but looked weaker than its 2004 reputation.

3457.headline: Sonic 2 advances but adds to Sonic's warning signs
3457.narrative: Sonic 2 and Mortal Kombat II advanced in the expected order, leaving little actual drama. Secret of Mana looked respectable, but Sonic's modest winning performance reinforced the view that the Sonic games were weaker than expected.

3458.headline: GoldenEye and Mario RPG advance as DKC2 hype collapses
3458.narrative: GoldenEye and Super Mario RPG advanced from a debated fourpack, while Resident Evil 2 remained respectable but never broke through. Donkey Kong Country 2's long-running hype ended in a disappointing SFF-affected debut.
3458.anomaly_note: The writeup says Super Mario RPG SFFed Donkey Kong Country 2, helping reduce a heavily hyped game to a weak opening-round showing.

3459.headline: Final Fantasy VII mauls the N64 field
3459.narrative: Final Fantasy VII dominated a pair of respectable Nintendo 64 games and looked every bit as strong as its old reputation suggested. Mario Kart 64 comfortably took the other advancing spot over Star Fox 64.
3459.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario Kart 64 predictably SFFed Star Fox 64, leaving the second advancing position effectively settled from the opening moments.

3460.headline: Mario 64 crushes Kirby as Symphony of the Night advances
3460.narrative: Super Mario 64 dominated the poll, while Symphony of the Night comfortably beat Resident Evil for the other advancing spot. Kirby Super Star collapsed badly in Mario's presence.
3460.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Super Mario 64 SFFed Kirby Super Star heavily, using Kirby's collapse to argue that Kirby's character strength does not come primarily from his games.

3461.headline: Chrono Trigger dominates while EarthBound's upset hope dies
3461.narrative: Chrono Trigger annihilated the field and looked fully restored to elite strength, while Yoshi's Island easily held off an EarthBound upset push that never materialized. The match was effectively decided immediately.

3462.headline: Pokémon RBY demolishes Majora's Mask and announces itself
3462.narrative: Pokémon RBY overwhelmed Majora's Mask in a matchup many expected to be close, immediately elevating Pokémon into the contest's top tier. The two other N64 games were largely squeezed out of relevance.
3462.anomaly_note: The writeup attributes Banjo-Kazooie and Perfect Dark's weak showings partly to heavy N64 and Nintendo overlap in a field led by Majora's Mask and Pokémon.

3463.headline: Pokémon Gold and Silver sends Final Fantasy Tactics home
3463.narrative: Metal Gear Solid won, but Pokémon Gold and Silver looked strong enough to pressure it early and comfortably beat Final Fantasy Tactics. Tactics' decline from its 2004 form became the main casualty.

3464.headline: Final Fantasy VIII destroys StarCraft's repeat-run hopes
3464.narrative: Final Fantasy VIII crushed StarCraft far more decisively than many expected and established itself as a serious contender. The writeup rejects the idea that StarCraft's old rally magic would automatically translate to another deep run.

3465.headline: Ocarina dominates while Final Fantasy IX beats Half-Life
3465.narrative: Ocarina of Time dominated an otherwise straightforward poll, while Final Fantasy IX beat Half-Life for the second advancing position. Half-Life's failure became another example of shooters disappointing in the bracket.

3466.headline: Final Fantasy X and MGS2 cruise without drama
3466.narrative: Final Fantasy X and Metal Gear Solid 2 advanced in a perfectly ordered match that the writeup considers almost devoid of story. Silent Hill 2 and Morrowind never threatened the top pair.

3467.headline: Paper Mario's vote drain helps Vice City eliminate Prime
3467.narrative: Kingdom Hearts took first comfortably, but Vice City overturned the expected Nintendo advantage and beat Metroid Prime for second. The writeup treats Paper Mario's presence as the key reason Prime could not capitalize.
3467.anomaly_note: The writeup says Paper Mario leeched enough Nintendo support from Metroid Prime to cost Prime the second advancing spot against Vice City.

3468.headline: Diablo II wins a four-way thriller as Halo escapes
3468.narrative: All four games remained competitive, with Diablo II unexpectedly taking first while Halo needed its familiar afternoon strength to catch Knights of the Old Republic for second. KOTOR's near-advancement became one of the round's most impressive losses.

3469.headline: Melee advances while Fire Emblem gets double-SFFed
3469.narrative: Melee and Wind Waker advanced exactly as expected, but Wind Waker held up well enough to raise concerns about Melee's future ceiling. Fire Emblem collapsed under an especially hostile overlap situation.
3469.anomaly_note: The writeup says Fire Emblem was SFFed from two directions by Wind Waker and by Melee, the game that had helped introduce the series to many voters.

3470.headline: Oblivion wins as Tales shocks God of War late
3470.narrative: Oblivion won a chaotic four-way race, while Tales of Symphonia recovered from a late deficit to steal second from God of War. San Andreas, the consensus favorite, fell to last, making the match one of the contest's defining upsets.

3471.headline: World of Warcraft advances as Halo 2 nearly bottoms out
3471.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 won comfortably, while World of Warcraft beat Halo 2 for the other advancing spot without needing the massive rally many had predicted. Halo nearly fell to last and continued the contest's shooter slump.

3472.headline: Resident Evil 4 narrowly holds off Kingdom Hearts II
3472.narrative: Resident Evil 4 built an overnight lead and then endured a long Kingdom Hearts II day-vote challenge without ever fully losing control. The narrow win advanced RE4 but also badly weakened its case as a potential finalist.

3473.headline: Twilight Princess dominates while Half-Life 2 survives
3473.narrative: Twilight Princess dominated the field, while Half-Life 2 built enough of an early cushion to keep Final Fantasy XII from seriously threatening second. The result briefly elevated Twilight Princess into finals discussion.

3474.headline: Brawl dominates as Street Fighter IV nearly finishes last
3474.narrative: Brawl crushed the field while GTA IV took an easy second, leaving Street Fighter IV in an embarrassing fight with Persona 4 just to avoid last place. The writeup treats Street Fighter IV as one of the contest's biggest disappointments.

3475.headline: Call of Duty 4 exposes a badly underperforming Galaxy
3475.narrative: Call of Duty 4 decisively beat Super Mario Galaxy in a result that immediately damaged Galaxy's pre-contest reputation. Even allowing for Pokémon overlap, the writeup sees Galaxy's performance as a major warning before facing Brawl.
3475.anomaly_note: The writeup treats Pokémon Diamond and Pearl's overlapping Nintendo support as a major factor in Super Mario Galaxy's unexpectedly weak performance.

3476.headline: Portal comfortably beats BioShock behind Metal Gear Solid 4
3476.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 4 won as expected, while Portal comfortably beat BioShock for the second advancing spot after an early lead that never became seriously threatened. The match stayed quieter than its uncertain pre-match setup suggested.

3477.headline: Fallout 3 and Halo 3 close Round One quietly
3477.narrative: Fallout 3 and Halo 3 advanced in a nearly perfect staircase, making the final first-round match one of the contest's least eventful. The shared Xbox and genre-heavy field produced very little movement.
3477.anomaly_note: The writeup attributes some of Mass Effect's weak showing to overlap with fellow Western RPG Fallout 3 in an unusually homogeneous field.

3478.headline: Tetris confirms its edge over Mega Man 2
3478.narrative: Tetris beat Mega Man 2 comfortably and was never seriously threatened after the opening moments. Mega Man 2 nevertheless held up better than its first-round showing suggested, while the writeup declines to pin the result on SFF.

3479.headline: Mario beats Zelda decisively in their first 2009 meeting
3479.narrative: Mario defeated Zelda much more easily than many expected, while Metroid and Ninja Gaiden were reduced to afterthoughts. The result appeared to settle the old NES hierarchy before later rounds complicated it again.
3479.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario and Zelda crushed Metroid and Ninja Gaiden through heavy Nintendo overlap, leaving the real contest entirely between the two NES giants.

3480.headline: Mario 3 suppresses Sonic, but Sonic still advances
3480.narrative: Mario 3 dominated the field, while Sonic recovered from an overnight Street Fighter II lead and used its strong day vote to secure second. The match reinforced both Mario-Sonic overlap and Street Fighter's limited strength.
3480.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Super Mario Bros. 3 SFFed Sonic, though Street Fighter II still could not take advantage enough to advance.

3481.headline: Mario World surges as Final Fantasy IV settles the debate
3481.narrative: Super Mario World transformed its shaky first-round image into a dominant second-round performance. Final Fantasy IV clearly beat the original Final Fantasy, while Mega Man 3 continued the series' disappointing contest.
3481.anomaly_note: The writeup describes substantial overlap between the two Final Fantasy entries in the field, with the split weakening the original Final Fantasy while Final Fantasy IV still secured second.

3482.headline: Super Metroid beats Mario Kart again under Zelda's shadow
3482.narrative: A Link to the Past dominated, while Super Metroid and Super Mario Kart repeated almost the same close race and voting trends as their first-round meeting. Metroid again survived, but the rematch lacked the tension its margin suggested.
3482.anomaly_note: The writeup says A Link to the Past was clearly SFFing all three fellow SNES and Nintendo-era games in the poll.

3483.headline: Link's Awakening scare exposes Final Fantasy VI's decline
3483.narrative: Final Fantasy VI won a perfectly ordered match, but Link's Awakening staying even with it in the opening minutes badly damaged FF6's elite reputation. The writeup treats those few minutes as more important than the eventual easy finish.

3484.headline: Final Fantasy VII dominates as GoldenEye takes second
3484.narrative: Final Fantasy VII again dominated strong opposition, while GoldenEye clearly beat Super Mario RPG and Mario Kart 64 for second. The writeup mainly uses the result to continue the FF7-versus-Ocarina strength comparison.

3485.headline: Mario 64 overturns Chrono Trigger and changes the bracket
3485.narrative: Chrono Trigger built an overnight lead on Mario 64, only to collapse badly once Mario's morning vote arrived. Mario 64 turned the match into a convincing win and shattered expectations for Chrono Trigger's deeper run.
3485.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Yoshi's Island was SFFed into a very weak last-place showing, with Mario 64 providing the clearest source of the overlap.

3486.headline: Pokémon splitting hands Metal Gear Solid first place
3486.narrative: Metal Gear Solid won, but Pokémon RBY remained impressive despite sharing the poll with Gold and Silver and Majora's Mask. The result made MGS look vulnerable for the next round while rehabilitating Majora's Mask somewhat.
3486.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pokémon Gold and Silver leeched heavily from Pokémon RBY and cost the older generation first place against Metal Gear Solid.

3487.headline: Final Fantasy VIII ends StarCraft's last comeback hope
3487.narrative: StarCraft briefly revived memories of 2004 by taking an early second-place lead, but Final Fantasy VIII erased it quickly once the overnight vote arrived. Ocarina of Time dominated throughout.
3487.anomaly_note: The writeup says Final Fantasy IX leeched support from Final Fantasy VIII early, briefly allowing StarCraft to threaten the second advancing position.

3488.headline: Kingdom Hearts shines while Final Fantasy X looks vulnerable
3488.narrative: Final Fantasy X won a crowded all-PS2 field, while Kingdom Hearts comfortably beat Metal Gear Solid 2 for second. Kingdom Hearts' strong showing and FFX's modest margin made the winner look less secure than the placement suggested.

3489.headline: Diablo II advances again as Halo falls to last
3489.narrative: Melee won easily, while Diablo II repeated its first-round success and comfortably advanced again. Halo collapsed to last behind a SFF-affected Wind Waker, producing another major embarrassment for the series.
3489.anomaly_note: The writeup says Melee SFFed Wind Waker, though Wind Waker still held up better than expected and even finished ahead of Halo.

3490.headline: Oblivion outlasts World of Warcraft in a long stall
3490.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 won comfortably, while Oblivion survived a long duel with World of Warcraft for second. The writeup notes multiple rally attempts but concludes that none meaningfully changed the result.

3491.headline: Resident Evil 4 survives Kingdom Hearts again
3491.narrative: Twilight Princess won, but Resident Evil 4 and Kingdom Hearts II again produced a close fight for the other advancing spot. RE4 survived a late collapse, while Twilight Princess itself looked less dominant than a finalist was expected to look.
3491.anomaly_note: The writeup says Twilight Princess absorbed enough of Kingdom Hearts II's usual day-vote support to help Resident Evil 4 survive another close rematch.

3492.headline: Brawl destroys Galaxy in a historic SFF beating
3492.narrative: Brawl annihilated Galaxy and sent Call of Duty 4 through in second, turning Galaxy's disappointing first round into a full collapse. The writeup elevates Brawl into serious finals contention after the result.
3492.anomaly_note: The writeup calls Brawl's suppression of Super Mario Galaxy one of the most meaningful SFF beatings in contest history.

3493.headline: Metal Gear Solid 4 and Fallout 3 advance quietly
3493.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 4 and Fallout 3 advanced in an orderly match with little suspense, while Portal briefly made the lower positions interesting. The writeup treats it mainly as a quiet setup for later rounds.

3494.headline: Zelda closes the gap on Mario in a strange rematch
3494.narrative: Mario still beat Zelda without being seriously threatened, but the margin collapsed compared with their prior matchup. The writeup treats the shift as evidence that Mario split more badly with the surrounding field and as setup for later surprises.
3494.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mega Man 2 and Tetris hurt Mario's support more than Zelda's, helping narrow the Mario-Zelda gap sharply from their previous meeting.

3495.headline: Mario 3 survives Mario World but looks vulnerable
3495.narrative: Mario 3 survived a sustained challenge from Mario World, but the writeup treats the narrow escape as evidence that World's relative strength had risen sharply. It also frames the result as part of a broader generational shift on GameFAQs.
3495.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario 3 clearly SFFed Sonic. It also says the other older games leeched Mario World more heavily, making World's near-win over Mario 3 especially striking.

3496.headline: Link to the Past and Final Fantasy VI advance routinely
3496.narrative: A Link to the Past and Final Fantasy VI advanced in a match the writeup considered almost completely predetermined. The only notable fanbase effect was Link's Awakening taking especially heavy suppression.
3496.anomaly_note: The writeup says A Link to the Past SFFed Link's Awakening heavily and left both lower Nintendo games suppressed beneath Final Fantasy VI.

3497.headline: Mario 64 survives another Chrono Trigger afternoon collapse
3497.narrative: Final Fantasy VII dominated, while Chrono Trigger built a real lead on Mario 64 before collapsing again with the afternoon vote. Mario 64's late recovery ended another promising Chrono Trigger upset attempt.
3497.anomaly_note: The writeup says GoldenEye clearly leeched Mario 64, giving Chrono Trigger a much better chance to steal the second advancing position.

3498.headline: Pokémon breaks through against Metal Gear Solid
3498.narrative: Ocarina of Time won comfortably, while Pokémon RBY finally broke through against Metal Gear Solid and advanced. The result elevated Pokémon into the site's highest tier and exposed a recurring overlap between Metal Gear and Final Fantasy.
3498.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ocarina of Time imposed Nintendo SFF on Pokémon RBY, though Pokémon resisted it unusually well. It also says Final Fantasy VIII leeched Metal Gear Solid and helped Pokémon take second.

3499.headline: Melee and Final Fantasy X cruise through a staircase
3499.narrative: Melee and Final Fantasy X advanced through a largely featureless staircase match. Kingdom Hearts briefly fought Diablo II for position but never threatened the top two once the PS2 split took hold.
3499.anomaly_note: The writeup says Kingdom Hearts was held down by its PS2 overlap with Final Fantasy X, preventing it from mounting a serious challenge for second.

3500.headline: Resident Evil 4 slowly comes back on Metal Gear Solid 3
3500.narrative: Twilight Princess took first, but Metal Gear Solid 3 built a substantial lead over Resident Evil 4 before RE4 spent most of the day slowly erasing it. Resident Evil 4 completed another close comeback and advanced.

3501.headline: Brawl crushes Metal Gear Solid 4 and confirms its strength
3501.narrative: Brawl decisively reversed its close Game of the Year history with Metal Gear Solid 4 and dominated the divisional final. The writeup treats the result as final proof that Brawl's contest strength was legitimate.

3502.headline: Mario 3 survives Zelda in a controversial final-minute finish
3502.narrative: Super Mario World took first, while Zelda erased a huge deficit and nearly stole second from Mario 3 in the final minutes. A suspicious late swing for Mario 3 turned an already dramatic finish into a lasting Board 8 controversy.
3502.anomaly_note: The writeup describes heavy Mario-on-Mario SFF and a three-Mario split that greatly helped Zelda. It also alleges that a suspicious late swing in Mario 3's favor may have involved cheating, though the official result ultimately stood.

3503.headline: Link to the Past barely survives Mario 64
3503.narrative: Final Fantasy VII dominated, while A Link to the Past survived a late Mario 64 comeback by a narrow margin. The writeup also sees the result as another sign that newer voters were gradually reshaping the site's preferences.
3503.anomaly_note: The writeup says Final Fantasy VII SFFed Final Fantasy VI heavily, reducing FF6 to a minor factor while the real race developed between Link to the Past and Mario 64.

3504.headline: Ocarina suppresses Nintendo rivals and sends Final Fantasy X through
3504.narrative: Ocarina of Time dominated the Nintendo-heavy field, while Final Fantasy X used the favorable bracket setup to advance. Melee fell to last and Pokémon could not overcome Ocarina's presence.
3504.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ocarina of Time heavily SFFed both Melee and Pokémon RBY, with Pokémon resisting the Nintendo suppression better than Melee.

3505.headline: Metal Gear Solid 4 barely holds off Brawl
3505.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 4 built a large overnight lead, then barely survived a massive Brawl afternoon comeback. The two advanced together from an unusually balanced field, while Twilight Princess and Resident Evil 4 were eliminated.
3505.anomaly_note: The writeup says Brawl SFFed Twilight Princess enough to knock Zelda out of the advancing positions.

3506.headline: Final Fantasy VII dominates a predictable semifinal
3506.narrative: Final Fantasy VII and A Link to the Past advanced from a semifinal the writeup considered nearly predetermined. FF7's dominant showing became the main talking point heading into the championship.
3506.anomaly_note: The writeup says Nintendo SFF inflated Final Fantasy VII's advantage, while the split between the two Mario games helped Link to the Past secure the other final berth.

3507.headline: Final Fantasy X passes Metal Gear Solid 4 for the final
3507.narrative: Ocarina of Time secured first easily, while Final Fantasy X erased Metal Gear Solid 4's early lead overnight and advanced to the championship. Brawl's run ended under an especially unfavorable Nintendo matchup.
3507.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ocarina of Time SFFed Brawl out of contention, leaving Final Fantasy X and Metal Gear Solid 4 to fight for the other final spot.

3508.headline: Ocarina defeats Final Fantasy VII and wins the championship
3508.narrative: Ocarina of Time took control almost immediately and defeated Final Fantasy VII despite FF7 looking stronger in earlier rounds. The writeup treats the result as a fair Team Zelda victory and Ocarina's arrival as the site's new top game.

3509.headline: Ocarina confirms its Final Fantasy VII win in a rematch
3509.narrative: The 1v1 bonus rematch again belonged to Ocarina of Time, reinforcing the championship result against Final Fantasy VII. The writeup also uses the high-turnout rematch to argue strongly for returning future contests to 1v1 brackets.

3730.headline: Link wins easily as 1v1 contests return
3730.narrative: Link won easily, but the writeup considered the performance mildly disappointing by his usual blowout standards and attributed some of that to anti-Link sentiment. The match also marked the return of a true 1v1 contest after four years.

3731.headline: Alucard crushes Magus in a supposedly even matchup
3731.narrative: A heavily debated 8/9 matchup ended almost immediately when Alucard took control and never yielded an update. The writeup treats the rout as further evidence that Magus and Chrono Trigger had continued to decline.

3732.headline: Red comes back late to edge Revolver Ocelot
3732.narrative: Pokémon Trainer Red built an early lead, lost it overnight to Ocelot, then erased Ocelot's advantage with a late-morning surge. The close comeback established Red as legitimate and reinforced Pokémon's powerful daytime trend.

3733.headline: Mega Man X exposes a badly misseeded opener
3733.narrative: Mega Man X won comfortably in a matchup the writeup considered badly misseeded. Captain Price performed somewhat better than expected, but never made the result competitive.

3734.headline: Luigi advances as Meta Knight draws another Nintendo trap
3734.narrative: Luigi won comfortably, while the writeup focused more on Meta Knight's repeated bad bracket luck than on the match itself. It argues that Meta Knight was stronger than the result made him look.
3734.anomaly_note: The writeup calls the matchup another Nintendo SFF-fest and argues that Meta Knight's strength was hidden by being repeatedly drawn against overlapping Nintendo opponents.

3735.headline: Amaterasu beats Shadow and deepens Sonic Team doubts
3735.narrative: Amaterasu took control early and beat Shadow far more comfortably than many expected, despite the match occurring during Sonic Team's preferred daytime hours. The result fueled the contest's early anti-Sonic sentiment.
