3736.headline: The Cube demolishes an overmatched Sandal
3736.narrative: Weighted Companion Cube overwhelmed Sandal in a deliberately silly matchup. The writeup attributes the scale of the rout more to Sandal's weakness than to any revival of the Cube's old championship-level bandwagon.

3737.headline: The Boss quietly upsets Nathan Drake
3737.narrative: The Boss took an early lead over Nathan Drake and held a remarkably stable advantage for nearly the entire match. Drake's Uncharted 2 boost made him respectable, but not strong enough to avoid the upset.

3738.headline: Sonic wins but sparks serious upset speculation
3738.narrative: Sonic defeated a character whose game had not yet released in North America, but looked much weaker than expected while doing it. The showing immediately triggered serious talk of Ganondorf or Kirby breaking the Noble Nine.

3739.headline: Knuckles beats Cecil but looks alarmingly weak
3739.narrative: Knuckles eventually pulled away from Cecil, but the match stayed far too close for far too long given Sonic Team's daytime advantage. The writeup treats the result as another major embarrassment for the Sonic cast.

3740.headline: Ganondorf wins routinely but fails to build Sonic hype
3740.narrative: Ganondorf defeated Mewtwo in an uneventful all-Nintendo matchup and landed close to expectations. The writeup nevertheless saw the showing as too ordinary to support growing hopes of an upset over Sonic.

3741.headline: Ken comes back on Wesker in a rare fun thriller
3741.narrative: Wesker led much of a close, heavily quoted match before Ken's California-heavy afternoon vote finally carried him past. The writeup explicitly rejects the routine cheating accusations and remembers the contest mainly for how much fun Board 8 had watching it.

3742.headline: Kirby wins routinely but weakens his upset case
3742.narrative: Kirby beat Rikku almost exactly as expected in a match with little suspense. Because Kirby needed an overperformance to sustain hopes of challenging Sonic, the merely routine win was treated as disappointing.

3743.headline: GLaDOS cruises past Fawful in a quiet match
3743.narrative: GLaDOS defeated Fawful easily in a low-turnout matchup. Much of the writeup is devoted to rejecting the idea that GLaDOS should be classified as a joke character rather than discussing any real competitive drama.

3744.headline: Vivi repeats his old Donkey Kong win almost exactly
3744.narrative: Vivi and Donkey Kong essentially replayed their 2004 matchup, with almost no change in the underlying result. The writeup treats the uncanny repetition as more notable than the match itself.

3745.headline: Altair crushes Liquid with a major picture advantage
3745.narrative: Altair destroyed Liquid Snake in a matchup where the stats had favored Liquid, producing one of the round's strangest results. The writeup highlights Altair's presentation as an important part of the surprise.
3745.anomaly_note: The writeup says Altair's excellent match picture gave him a major advantage, especially against a Liquid Snake image that inspired little confidence.

3746.headline: Mario buries Falco with overwhelming Nintendo SFF
3746.narrative: Mario overwhelmed Falco and delivered one of the rare extreme blowouts of the contest. The writeup treats the result as a straightforward display of Mario's fanbase dominance.
3746.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mario dropped an SFF nuke on fellow Nintendo entrant Falco, producing one of the contest's largest blowouts.

3747.headline: Big Boss becomes Metal Gear's first-round bright spot
3747.narrative: Big Boss crushed Miles Edgeworth and became the only Metal Gear character the writeup thought looked genuinely good in the opening round. The dominant win briefly restored some pride to the series.

3748.headline: Zidane wins but damages his upset hopes
3748.narrative: Zidane beat Claptrap comfortably, but not by anything close to the margin expected against such weak opposition. The underperformance sharply reduced enthusiasm for a second-round upset of Ike.

3749.headline: Ike outdoes Zidane with an even worse underperformance
3749.narrative: Ike followed Zidane's weak showing with an even more disappointing performance against Prinny. His strong afternoon vote improved the final appearance, but the writeup still treats the match as a major embarrassment.

3750.headline: Mega Man continues a strong series-wide rebound
3750.narrative: Mega Man handled Cid comfortably and continued a broader rebound for the Mega Man cast. The writeup uses the result to argue that Mega Man had returned close to his old contest strength.

3751.headline: Zack destroys Yuna and validates ZackFAQs again
3751.narrative: A matchup that drew substantial pre-match debate turned into an easy Zack win almost immediately. The writeup treats the result as further confirmation that Zack's 2008 run was legitimate and that Yuna remained overrated.

3752.headline: Ryu Hayabusa wins but badly disappoints against Crash
3752.narrative: Ryu Hayabusa beat Crash but looked far weaker than expected and even lost the morning vote. The result initially killed much of the hype for a second-round upset over Master Chief.

3753.headline: A 4chan Spy rally exposes another Master Chief flop
3753.narrative: Master Chief beat Spy but spent the entire match looking much weaker than expected and never produced his trademark afternoon surge. The writeup calls the showing an embarrassment despite the comfortable win.
3753.anomaly_note: The writeup says 4chan mounted a massive rally for Spy, helping drag Master Chief down throughout an already disappointing performance.

3754.headline: Sora advances without ever looking dominant
3754.narrative: Sora beat Midna comfortably but again failed to produce the huge blowout expected from a top seed against weak opposition. The writeup treats this as a stable feature of Sora's highly anti-voted 1v1 profile.

3755.headline: Laharl finally earns his first contest win
3755.narrative: Laharl won an otherwise low-interest matchup between two cult characters and finally earned his first contest victory. The writeup finds the structural similarity to his 2004 match with Vyse more interesting than the vote itself.

3756.headline: Kefka destroys guru favorite Arthas
3756.narrative: Kefka completely dismantled a heavily favored Arthas and turned a major guru pick into a rout. The writeup treats the result as both a Kefka revival and another warning against translating four-way strength directly into 1v1s.

3757.headline: Bowser handles Frog in an expected result
3757.narrative: Bowser beat Frog almost exactly as expected, giving little new information about Bowser's next matchup. Much of the writeup instead argues that Frog's reputation had been inflated by suspicious results from earlier contests.

3758.headline: L-Block wins but looks fully mortal
3758.narrative: L-Block beat HK-47 comfortably but looked like a normal, transitive midcard entrant rather than the unstoppable joke champion of 2007. The writeup sees this as the clearest sign that the old bandwagon had permanently faded.

3759.headline: Isaac finally gets his long-awaited first win
3759.narrative: Isaac overwhelmed Professor Layton in a match with virtually no competitive suspense. The important storyline was that Isaac finally earned his first contest win after seven years of appearances.

3760.headline: Charizard crushes Duke and ends the debate quickly
3760.narrative: Charizard ended a surprisingly persistent pre-match debate almost immediately by crushing Duke Nukem. The writeup says Duke's weakness limits what can be learned, but Charizard still looked clearly legitimate.

3761.headline: Kratos beats Tails but loses his favorite status
3761.narrative: Kratos defeated Tails but looked badly underwhelming for a highly seeded character, especially because his usual daytime strength never appeared. The showing made Charizard look much more dangerous for the next round.

3762.headline: Samus opens her run with a dominant rout
3762.narrative: Samus overwhelmed Prince of Persia from the opening vote and never gave the match any suspense. The writeup treats the dominant start as the beginning of an especially strong run for Samus.

3763.headline: Jill crushes Niko as Resident Evil strength rises
3763.narrative: Jill Valentine crushed Niko Bellic and looked stronger than expected, while Niko continued the pattern of Grand Theft Auto characters fading quickly from relevance. The writeup also identifies the match as early evidence of a broader Resident Evil boost.

3764.headline: Heavy's 4chan rally dents Roxas without threatening him
3764.narrative: Roxas remained in control, but Heavy's 4chan support produced the only real movement in an otherwise straightforward match. The morning vote restored most of Roxas's lost ground.
3764.anomaly_note: The writeup says 4chan mounted a large rally for Heavy, pulling Roxas down substantially for part of the night without ever making the match competitive.

3765.headline: Tidus adds another loss to his long pattern
3765.narrative: The writeup treats Tidus as chronically overrated and views this as another supposedly winnable matchup where he never seriously threatened. Sub-Zero's performance is presented as part of that larger pattern rather than a surprise of its own.

3766.headline: Jecht validates himself as Phoenix disappoints
3766.narrative: Phoenix was a Board 8 favorite in a heavily debated matchup, but Jecht took control quickly and removed the hoped-for rally scenario. The writeup treats Jecht as a legitimate newcomer and Phoenix as disappointing in a match he could plausibly have won.

3767.headline: Ratchet finally wins against extreme fodder
3767.narrative: Ratchet finally earned a contest win against exceptionally weak opposition. The writeup's main takeaway is less Ratchet's strength than how poor Eddie Riggs looked.

3768.headline: Zelda advances despite a mild underperformance
3768.narrative: Zelda advanced comfortably but looked weaker than the writeup expected, while Travis benefited from recent No More Heroes visibility. The result did little to alter Zelda's projected path.

3769.headline: Ezio advances but loses his upset hype
3769.narrative: A brief poll glitch and name correction made the opening messy, but Ezio eventually pulled away from Simon Belmont. Even so, the writeup considers Ezio's showing poor enough to kill serious upset hype for his next match.

3770.headline: Cloud looks weak while Ridley exceeds expectations
3770.narrative: Cloud looked unexpectedly vulnerable for much of the match, prompting concern that he had lost strength. Ridley's showing is treated as surprisingly good even after allowing for the favorable picture situation.
3770.anomaly_note: The writeup says Cloud received a bad picture while Ridley was finally recognizable, presenting those image conditions as part of why Cloud looked weaker than expected.

3771.headline: Chris wins as Call of Duty struggles again
3771.narrative: Chris Redfield won a straightforward match that landed close to the writeup's expectations. MacMillan's result did little to reverse the broader impression that Call of Duty characters were performing badly.
3771.anomaly_note: The writeup says the poor match-picture situation likely helped Captain MacMillan perform slightly better than expected.

3772.headline: Riku advances cleanly with no warning signs
3772.narrative: Riku handled Ramza without major difficulty, though not as comfortably as some expected. The writeup sees the performance as perfectly respectable and gives no warning of Riku's later upset.

3773.headline: The writeup mostly rants about Wander
3773.narrative: The writeup is mostly an extended attack on Wander and Shadow of the Colossus, with Captain Falcon's easy win serving mainly as an excuse for that rant.

3774.headline: Vault Boy impresses against an uneven Leon
3774.narrative: Vault Boy performed much better than the writeup expected and is defended as a legitimate Fallout representative rather than a joke entrant. Leon's unusually weak-looking win is treated as further evidence that his strength behaves strangely within the Resident Evil cast.

3775.headline: Sackboy embarrasses the guru consensus
3775.narrative: Sackboy decisively beat the guru-favored Kratos Aurion, with the Super Bowl creating an unusual temporary trend swing. The writeup also treats the result as evidence that LittleBigPlanet had previously been held down by difficult poll company.

3776.headline: The writeup mostly attacks Final Fantasy XII
3776.narrative: Most of the writeup is a broad rant about Final Fantasy XII, with Ryu's easy win over Balthier receiving only brief attention.

3777.headline: Dante strengthens his case while Kingdom Hearts slips
3777.narrative: Dante exceeded the comparison the writeup had set using Ryu and looked clearly superior going into their anticipated meeting. Axel's weak performance also added to growing concern that Kingdom Hearts had declined.

3778.headline: Snake wins but again looks strange against Nintendo
3778.narrative: Snake won comfortably but again looked oddly weak against a Nintendo-associated opponent. The writeup uses the match to argue that some of Snake's newer support disappears against Nintendo characters.

3779.headline: Fox ends his drought against weak Tales opposition
3779.narrative: Fox ended a long 1v1 win drought with an easy victory over Lloyd Irving. The writeup uses the match mainly to argue that Tales characters are chronically over-nominated relative to their contest strength.

3780.headline: Pikachu SFFs Banjo and confirms Pokémon's rise
3780.narrative: Pikachu's rise from an anti-voted early-contest character to a dominant Pokémon representative is the main story. Banjo's latest Nintendo-heavy loss leaves his true standalone strength difficult to judge.
3780.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Pikachu's win an SFF blowout and says Banjo has repeatedly been suppressed by Nintendo opponents.

3781.headline: Shepard looks newly legitimate against weak opposition
3781.narrative: Commander Shepard crushed Ellis shortly after Mass Effect 2's release and looked much more credible than in his earlier contest appearances. The writeup treats Ellis as obvious fodder and Shepard as a newly legitimate entrant.

3782.headline: Auron meets expectations without strengthening his Squall case
3782.narrative: Auron performed almost exactly where the writeup expected against Aeris, which did little to resolve the larger Auron-versus-Squall debate. The writeup argues that merely meeting expectations was not enough to strengthen Auron's upset case.

3783.headline: Zero reinforces the Mega Man rebound
3783.narrative: Zero comfortably defeated Marcus Fenix and continued what the writeup saw as a broader Mega Man-series rebound. Fenix, by contrast, is treated as another fading Xbox-era character whose strength had not lasted.

3784.headline: Dissidia-boosted Terra overturns the Revan consensus
3784.narrative: Terra reversed the pre-match consensus and beat Revan, with the writeup attributing her new strength primarily to Dissidia's exposure of older Final Fantasy characters. Revan is defended as reasonably strong despite the loss.

3785.headline: Squall offers little evidence before the Auron test
3785.narrative: Squall stayed near expectations against Akuma, providing little useful evidence for the looming Squall-Auron debate. The writeup considers the match largely inconclusive.

3786.headline: Sephiroth opens with an immediate warning sign
3786.narrative: Sephiroth's opening performance looked weak compared with Snake's, which immediately raised concern about his path through the contest. The writeup views this as the first clear warning that Sephiroth was in trouble.

3787.headline: Vincent exposes Guybrush as contest fodder again
3787.narrative: Vincent destroyed Guybrush in a match the writeup regards as proof that Guybrush was badly over-nominated and had little competitive value. The commentary is more about Guybrush's weakness than Vincent's strength.

3788.headline: Yoshi cruises through an uneventful matchup
3788.narrative: Yoshi beat Jak in a matchup the writeup considered an easy prediction and one of the least eventful polls of the round. Jak is grouped with recognizable platform characters who never developed meaningful contest strength.

3789.headline: Missingno rallies past Crono in the contest's defining upset
3789.narrative: The writeup calls this the contest's defining match: Missingno built a bandwagon-backed lead, Crono mounted multiple comebacks, and the glitch character repeatedly fought them off. The upset ended the Noble Nine's unbeaten 1v1 streak against outsiders and became the centerpiece of the contest.
3789.anomaly_note: The writeup repeatedly says Missingno was sustained by organized bandwagon rallying. It also records attempted cheating from both fanbases, while explicitly concluding that those attempts did not invalidate Missingno's win.

3790.headline: Big Daddy exposes Soap and Call of Duty hype
3790.narrative: Big Daddy turned a debated matchup into an emphatic rejection of Soap's high seed and Call of Duty hype. The writeup treats Soap as one of the worst high-seeded entrants in contest history while crediting Big Daddy with real strength.

3791.headline: Ness SFFs Geno and restores his standing
3791.narrative: Ness overwhelmed Geno and restored confidence in himself before the next round. Geno's inability to resist even Ness's fanbase overlap is treated as evidence that he should no longer receive regular contest nominations.
3791.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Ness SFFed Geno, using the scale of Geno's collapse to argue that he had little independent contest strength.

3792.headline: Tifa SFFs another weak Tales entrant
3792.narrative: Tifa crushed Yuri in a result the writeup considered entirely predictable. The commentary uses the blowout mainly to continue its broader argument that Tales characters are consistently over-nominated.
3792.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes Tifa's rout of Yuri Lowell as SFF.

3793.headline: Gordon survives a glitch but loses his Tifa hype
3793.narrative: A poll glitch briefly made Peach look capable of producing a historic Gordon Freeman collapse, but the problem was resolved and Gordon recovered. Even with the win, the writeup treats his final performance as weak enough to end serious upset hype against Tifa.

3794.headline: Link wins while anti-Link voting becomes noticeable
3794.narrative: Link beat Alucard comfortably but looked weaker than the writeup expected for a second straight match. The commentary identifies growing anti-Link voting as a new factor even though it was not yet threatening his championship path.

3795.headline: Red loses respectably and strengthens Pokémon's rise
3795.narrative: Mega Man X controlled the match, but Red still impressed enough to establish himself as a legitimate midcard entrant. The writeup treats the performance as further evidence of Pokémon's broad contest surge.

3796.headline: Amaterasu impresses again despite losing to Luigi
3796.narrative: Luigi won, but Amaterasu resisted him far better than expected and continued her reputation for outperforming difficult draws. The result also made earlier Sonic Team losses to her look less embarrassing.

3797.headline: The Cube advances but its old bandwagon is gone
3797.narrative: Weighted Companion Cube beat The Boss but looked ordinary doing so, which the writeup takes as proof that another major joke-character bandwagon was not developing. The match also illustrates how much harder 1v1s are for novelty entrants.

3798.headline: Sonic SFFs Knuckles despite old fan-poll results
3798.narrative: Sonic comfortably suppressed Knuckles and used the result to undercut the idea that single-series favorite polls translate directly into contest matchups. Knuckles's brief early lead supplied the only real drama.
3798.anomaly_note: The writeup says Sonic easily SFFed Knuckles despite Knuckles having won an old Sonic-series favorite poll.

3799.headline: The writeup mostly becomes a Street Fighter IV rant
3799.narrative: The writeup gives Ganondorf's easy win over Ken only brief attention before turning into a long aside about why the author dislikes Street Fighter IV.

3800.headline: Kirby wins but his Sonic upset case collapses
3800.narrative: Kirby beat GLaDOS in a predictable match but fell far short of the strength his prior contest run implied. The writeup treats this as the point where serious Kirby-over-Sonic upset hopes collapsed.

3801.headline: Vivi punctures Altair's breakout hype
3801.narrative: Vivi decisively beat a heavily hyped Altair, reversing the impression created by Altair's first-round rout of Liquid Snake. The writeup views Altair and Liquid as especially unreliable contest reads after the result.

3802.headline: Another Mario-Big Boss rematch exposes four-way volatility
3802.narrative: Mario and Big Boss produced yet another rematch, and the writeup uses their history mainly to illustrate how unstable four-way extrapolations can be. The match itself adds little new beyond that comparison.

3803.headline: Daytime format swings a close match toward Ike
3803.narrative: Ike beat Zidane in a close matchup the writeup says was strongly shaped by the daytime schedule. It argues that a night match would likely have favored Zidane instead.

3804.headline: Mega Man crushes Zack and strengthens his rebound
3804.narrative: Mega Man exceeded expectations against a legitimate Zack and reinforced the impression that his series had returned to stronger form. The writeup treats the result as a major statement rather than a routine advancement.

3805.headline: Ryu Hayabusa creates the Master Flop upset
3805.narrative: Ryu Hayabusa overturned a matchup that the writeup had expected Master Chief to control and turned 'Master Flop' into the dominant story. The loss is framed as another example of Chief's severe anti-vote problem in 1v1 contests.

3806.headline: Sora advances but makes Bowser look inevitable
3806.narrative: Sora beat Laharl but performed so poorly relative to expectations that the writeup declared a future Bowser win virtually certain. The result is treated as part of a contest-wide decline for Kingdom Hearts.

3807.headline: Kefka finally looks respectable against Bowser
3807.narrative: Bowser eventually handled Kefka, but the writeup focuses on how well Kefka held up early after years of weak or badly presented performances. It treats Kefka's broader contest run as a notable revival.

3808.headline: L-Block advances on bracket luck rather than old strength
3808.narrative: L-Block beat Isaac in an almost motionless match, but the writeup argues that the former champion had become much weaker and was surviving mainly through favorable bracket placement. A mistaken Isaac picture was corrected but is not said to have affected the vote.

3809.headline: Charizard rallies past Kratos and becomes a real threat
3809.narrative: Charizard turned a heavily anticipated upset attempt into a convincing breakthrough over Kratos. The result launched a serious deep-run scenario for Charizard and confirmed that his first-round strength had been meaningful.
3809.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says both Charizard and Kratos were heavily rallied, though Charizard's support proved much more effective.

3810.headline: Samus crushes Jill and raises Cloud upset talk
3810.narrative: Samus overwhelmed Jill early and still finished with a strong enough performance to make a potential upset of Cloud feel plausible. The writeup treats this as the start of an especially impressive Samus run.

3811.headline: Sub-Zero completes another underdog route to Round Three
3811.narrative: Sub-Zero beat Roxas comfortably and became one of several low-prediction entrants to reach the third round. Roxas's late-day improvement is treated as one of the few positive Kingdom Hearts trends in the contest.

3812.headline: Ratchet surprises despite another Jecht win
3812.narrative: Jecht advanced as expected but looked surprisingly weak against Ratchet, who performed far better than his old contest history suggested. The writeup credits Ratchet with finally showing some real improvement.

3813.headline: Zelda kills the Ezio upset hype immediately
3813.narrative: Zelda erased the pre-match upset hype almost immediately and won comfortably. Ezio's later daytime gains were respectable but never made the contest meaningfully competitive.

3814.headline: Cloud rebounds while Chris collapses under likely SFF
3814.narrative: Cloud rebounded from his weak first-round showing and dominated an RE5-boosted Chris far more decisively than expected. The writeup treats fanbase overlap as the most plausible explanation for Chris collapsing so badly.
3814.anomaly_note: The writeup says Final Fantasy VII-over-Resident Evil SFF is the likeliest explanation for Chris Redfield performing worse against Cloud than Ridley had.

3815.headline: Captain Falcon validates himself as Kingdom Hearts slips
3815.narrative: Captain Falcon finally received a clean 1v1 opportunity after years of bad Nintendo-heavy draws and used it to beat Riku convincingly. The writeup treats the result as both Falcon validation and another sign of Kingdom Hearts decline.

3816.headline: Leon advances but loses his upset hype
3816.narrative: Leon handled Sackboy without much difficulty, but the writeup thought Leon still looked slightly off compared with expectations. That muted performance ended most remaining hype for him upsetting the Ryu-Dante winner.

3817.headline: Olympic hockey creates the memorable Hockey Factor
3817.narrative: Most of the writeup recounts the Canada-USA Olympic hockey final, then uses the game to explain the 'Hockey Factor': Dante improved while North American voters were occupied, before Ryu recovered after the game ended.

3818.headline: Snake shrugs off another weak board vote
3818.narrative: Snake again started poorly with the board vote before recovering into a solid win. The writeup finds Fox a difficult measuring stick because so many of his prior losses involved Nintendo overlap.

3819.headline: Shepard's Mass Effect 2 boost survives a Pikachu test
3819.narrative: Pikachu won without the dramatic daytime surge often associated with Pokémon, while Shepard continued his enormous improvement after Mass Effect 2. The writeup treats Shepard's respectable loss as one of the more impressive growth stories in the field.

3820.headline: Auron meets expectations while Zero restores some credibility
3820.narrative: Auron won about as comfortably as expected, which the writeup saw as insufficient evidence for an upset of Squall. Zero's respectable showing instead reinforced the idea that his recent weakness had been exaggerated by bad Nintendo-heavy draws.

3821.headline: Terra makes Squall look unexpectedly vulnerable
3821.narrative: Squall won comfortably but looked surprisingly weak against Terra despite his history of crushing lesser Final Fantasy characters. The result reopened doubts about whether Squall was safely above Auron.

3822.headline: Vincent exposes Sephiroth's growing anti-vote problem
3822.narrative: Sephiroth failed to suppress Vincent nearly as hard as expected, and the writeup explicitly rejects ordinary SFF as a sufficient explanation. It instead frames the result as evidence that severe anti-voting had become a structural weakness for Sephiroth and Final Fantasy VII.

3823.headline: Missingno rallies past Yoshi but wins on real strength
3823.narrative: Yoshi resisted the Missingno bandwagon far better than expected and held the lead for hours, but Missingno eventually broke through during the Pokémon afternoon vote. The writeup insists the win reflected legitimate strength more than a joke rally.
3823.anomaly_note: The writeup says rallying aided Missingno's decisive sequence of afternoon gains against Yoshi, while also stressing that rallying was not the main reason Missingno won.

3824.headline: Big Daddy overcomes Ness after a close opening
3824.narrative: Big Daddy overcame an early Ness lead and turned a close start into a comfortable advancement. The writeup highlights the striking contrast in their match picture but does not claim the image decided the result.

3825.headline: Tifa ends Gordon Freeman's revived hype
3825.narrative: Tifa ended Gordon Freeman's run in a match the writeup viewed as predictable after Gordon nearly lost to Peach. Gordon's weak showing also undercut the significance of his recent outside-contest success.

3826.headline: Link advances while Mega Man X raises another question
3826.narrative: Link advanced comfortably, but the writeup regarded the result as another slightly weak showing by his historical standards. Mega Man X's performance kept alive the possibility that Link had lost a little of his old invincibility.

3827.headline: Luigi extinguishes the Cube's remaining joke hype
3827.narrative: Luigi eliminated Weighted Companion Cube without any sign of the old joke-character surge. The writeup treats the loss as further proof that the Cube was now operating on ordinary strength rather than a bandwagon.

3828.headline: Sonic crushes years of Ganondorf upset hype
3828.narrative: Years of Ganondorf-over-Sonic upset hype collapsed when Sonic controlled the match from the start. The writeup treats the result as a major correction to the idea that four-way contests had revealed Sonic to be much weaker.

3829.headline: Kirby advances but his Sonic case disappears
3829.narrative: Kirby beat Vivi without difficulty, but failed to look strong enough to preserve serious hopes of upsetting Sonic. The writeup treats Kirby's old four-way bandwagon strength as clearly gone.

3830.headline: Mario buries Ike with total Nintendo SFF
3830.narrative: Mario crushed Ike in a result the writeup considered inevitable once they met. The scale of the Nintendo suppression made the matchup effectively noncompetitive.
3830.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Mario's win over fellow Nintendo entrant Ike a total SFF beating.

3831.headline: Mega Man's rebound becomes impossible to dismiss
3831.narrative: Mega Man produced a third straight performance far above the writeup's expectations and overwhelmed Ryu Hayabusa. Rather than settling on SFF or picture factor, the writeup treats the streak itself as proof that Mega Man had returned near his old strength.

3832.headline: Bowser eliminates Sora and deepens Kingdom Hearts decline
3832.narrative: Bowser completed a bracket-busting upset that had become increasingly predictable after Sora's poor first two rounds. The writeup treats the loss as the clearest sign yet that Kingdom Hearts had fallen sharply.

3833.headline: Charizard replaces L-Block as the new bandwagon star
3833.narrative: Charizard decisively eliminated former champion L-Block in what the writeup frames as a literal changing of the guard between two bandwagon-friendly entrants. L-Block's long decline was now impossible to miss.

3834.headline: Samus posts another elite-looking performance
3834.narrative: Samus crushed Sub-Zero and briefly looked strong enough to challenge even Cloud's level. Although she cooled from that early pace, the writeup still considers the result one of her strongest performances.

3835.headline: Jecht surprises Zelda on Final Fantasy release day
3835.narrative: Zelda advanced as expected, but Jecht performed much better than his prior results suggested and ignored the usual daytime trend expectations. The writeup suspects the contemporaneous Final Fantasy release helped explain the odd showing.

3836.headline: Captain Falcon adds to the evidence of Cloud decline
3836.narrative: Cloud won comfortably, but Captain Falcon still performed better than several much more established characters had managed against him. The writeup treats Falcon's showing as further evidence that Cloud had weakened.

3837.headline: Leon survives an awful sprite but Ryu advances
3837.narrative: Ryu won clearly, but Leon resisted far better than the disastrous sprite led people to expect and even held up well during his preferred daytime period. The writeup leaves open whether a fairer picture could have made the match significantly closer.
3837.anomaly_note: The writeup says Leon's ugly Resident Evil: Gaiden sprite hurt his chances and suggests the matchup might have been different with more even pictures.

3838.headline: Pikachu scares Snake before Snake takes control
3838.narrative: Pikachu briefly led Snake behind a strong opening vote before Snake finally took control and pulled away. The writeup remembers the opening as entertaining but ultimately sees Snake's recovery as convincing.

3839.headline: Squall settles the Auron strength debate
3839.narrative: Squall settled a long-running near-elite debate by beating Auron in a match that finished close but was rarely in serious doubt after the opening exchanges. The writeup treats Squall as clearly the stronger of the two.

3840.headline: Missingno's planned rally collapses against Sephiroth
3840.narrative: Missingno built the expected early lead through bandwagon support, but Sephiroth erased it decisively once the night vote arrived. The writeup treats the loss as the end of Missingno's remarkable run and as fuel for even more anti-Sephiroth sentiment.
3840.anomaly_note: The writeup says Missingno's rallying was organized in advance and powered a substantial early lead, though the push was nowhere near enough to survive Sephiroth's overnight strength.

3841.headline: Tifa advances through apparent Missingno backlash
3841.narrative: Tifa beat Big Daddy, but the writeup thought she looked oddly weak compared with her prior performance. It attributes the flat showing to backlash from Missingno supporters after Sephiroth had eliminated their favorite.

3842.headline: Link returns to godslayer form against Luigi
3842.narrative: Link finally produced the dominant performance the writeup had been waiting for and overwhelmed Luigi. The result largely erased doubts created by Link's earlier, more ordinary-looking matches.

3843.headline: Sonic shuts down the Kirby upset case
3843.narrative: Sonic beat Kirby comfortably and completed the collapse of years of hype that Ganondorf or Kirby might break the Noble Nine through him. The writeup treats Sonic as restored to roughly his traditional place.

3844.headline: Mario stops Mega Man's comeback to elite form
3844.narrative: Mega Man's excellent run made the divisional final look more interesting than it had pre-contest, but Mario still won as expected. The writeup treats the result as another example of Mario resisting would-be upsets regardless of surrounding form.

3845.headline: HeartGold and SoulSilver timing powers Charizard past Bowser
3845.narrative: Charizard upset Bowser on the release day of Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, which the writeup treats as exceptionally favorable timing for the Pokémon bandwagon. The convincing win completed one of the bracket's least likely divisional runs.

3846.headline: Samus SFFs Zelda and strengthens her Cloud case
3846.narrative: Samus beat Zelda far more decisively than their previous meeting suggested was normal. The writeup sees a mix of Zelda decline and newly visible Nintendo suppression from Samus, further strengthening Samus's case against Cloud.
3846.anomaly_note: The writeup says Samus appears to have SFFed Zelda, contributing to a much stronger result than their earlier 1v1 history suggested.

3847.headline: Cloud delivers his strongest-looking performance against Ryu
3847.narrative: Cloud produced one of his strongest matches of the contest by overwhelming the usually consistent Ryu. The writeup treats it as a much-needed reminder that Cloud remained elite despite visible decline elsewhere.

3848.headline: Snake strengthens again and turns Sephiroth into the underdog
3848.narrative: Snake improved again against Squall in their latest rematch and looked strong throughout. The writeup treats the result as the point where a Snake upset of Sephiroth became the dominant expectation.

3849.headline: Tifa exposes Sephiroth's anti-vote collapse
3849.narrative: Sephiroth struggled badly against Tifa in what the writeup calls his worst performance, framing the weakness as extreme anti-voting magnified by anger over Missingno's elimination. The result effectively ended confidence in Sephiroth beating Snake.

3850.headline: Link SFFs Sonic in a crushing quarterfinal
3850.narrative: Link crushed Sonic far more severely than a normal Noble Nine matchup suggested, restoring his aura of invincibility. The writeup views fanbase suppression as an important part of why the gap became so extreme.
3850.anomaly_note: The writeup endorses SFF as a plausible explanation for Link's unusually severe beating of Sonic, noting that Link looked invincible mainly against overlapping characters such as Luigi and Sonic.

3851.headline: Charizard loses to Mario but completes Pokémon's breakout
3851.narrative: Charizard's bandwagon could not seriously threaten Mario, but the Pokémon star still performed well enough to complete a remarkable contest run. The writeup treats the loss as further proof that Pokémon had become one of the site's strongest franchises.

3852.headline: Samus pushes Cloud hard before the night vote wins
3852.narrative: Samus repeatedly fought Cloud back to even during the opening hours and came closer to the upset than their older history suggested possible. Cloud finally took control during his strongest overnight period, but the writeup regards Samus's resistance as a major statement.

3853.headline: Snake finally breaks Sephiroth and targets Cloud
3853.narrative: Snake defeated Sephiroth in a matchup that had shifted from pre-contest dream upset to expected result as Sephiroth deteriorated. The writeup treats Snake's control as decisive and immediately turns attention toward whether he could beat Cloud.

3854.headline: Link SFFs Mario in another one-sided semifinal
3854.narrative: The rematch of the original character-contest final produced much the same hierarchy, with Link suppressing Mario and winning comfortably. The writeup notes that even widespread anti-Link sentiment did little to change the matchup.
3854.anomaly_note: The writeup invokes Link's 'King of SFF' reputation to explain why Mario again performed much worse against Link than people hoped.

3855.headline: Cloud survives Snake after a long semifinal deadlock
3855.narrative: Snake spent hours trading the lead with Cloud and even stalled through Cloud's normally dominant overnight period, creating genuine upset hope. Cloud's morning strength finally broke the deadlock and ended Snake's deep run.

3856.headline: Link beats Cloud again as bracket fatigue peaks
3856.narrative: Link defeated Cloud yet again, but Cloud recovered from a poor opening to make the final much more respectable than expected. The writeup's larger complaint is that Link's dominance had become so repetitive that he no longer belonged in ordinary brackets.

4069.headline: Fallout 3 opens Game of the Decade with authority
4069.narrative: Fallout 3 opened the Game of the Decade contest with a dominant win and immediately established itself as a serious entry. The writeup notes the unusual absence of Nintendo from the traditional opening slot.

4070.headline: Deus Ex extends the second-match jinx
4070.narrative: Deus Ex upset Rock Band 2 and joined the long tradition of second-match bracket wreckers. The writeup says the apparent closeness was misleading because Deus Ex built a lead early and merely gave some of it back later, while Europe's stronger support proved important.

4071.headline: Batman cruises through an uninformative opener
4071.narrative: Batman overwhelmed Psychonauts in a match the writeup considered almost entirely devoid of useful information. Psychonauts was simply too weak to reveal much about Batman's later prospects.

4072.headline: Team Fortress 2 survives an all-time Fable thriller
4072.narrative: Team Fortress 2 and Fable traded the lead repeatedly for nearly the entire poll, producing one of the closest wire-to-wire matches the writeup could remember. Team Fortress 2's dedicated fanbase and bracket support proved just enough to survive.

4073.headline: Legend of Dragoon validates itself in defeat
4073.narrative: Uncharted 2 beat The Legend of Dragoon, but the writeup considered Dragoon's respectable showing proof that its vote-in success had been legitimate. Uncharted remained on course for the deeper run many expected.

4074.headline: Street Fighter IV shocks Sonic Adventure 2
4074.narrative: Street Fighter IV upset Sonic Adventure 2 in a result the writeup treats as both long-overdue redemption for the series and a harsh verdict on 3D Sonic games. The match also became a major guru failure.

4075.headline: Halo 3 ends Super Mario Sunshine hype immediately
4075.narrative: Halo 3 beat Super Mario Sunshine and immediately punctured the strong pre-contest hype behind Sunshine. The writeup treats the result as the beginning of a rare positive contest for Halo.

4076.headline: Halo wins quietly and sets up the series showdown
4076.narrative: Halo: Combat Evolved handled Ninja Gaiden without reproducing the character-contest chaos associated with Master Chief and Ryu Hayabusa. The straightforward result instead set up the more meaningful Halo-versus-Halo comparison ahead.

4077.headline: Metroid Prime opens the Northeast with authority
4077.narrative: Metroid Prime opened the Northeast with the dominant performance expected from a divisional favorite. The writeup treats the match mainly as confirmation that the real questions would come against the stronger games later in the bracket.

4078.headline: Devil May Cry 3 wins but badly underperforms
4078.narrative: Devil May Cry 3 won comfortably but looked much weaker than the writeup and prediction community had expected against an unreleased-in-America Mother 3. The result made DMC3 one of the round's clearest underperformers.

4079.headline: Mega Man 9 settles a supposed tossup quickly
4079.narrative: A widely debated tossup became much less dramatic once Mega Man 9 took control early. The writeup remembers the match more for how thoroughly it punished a substantial expert lean toward the other side than for any sustained suspense.

4080.headline: Okami keeps gaining legitimacy in a routine win
4080.narrative: Okami handled the match exactly as expected and continued its steady rise in GameFAQs legitimacy. The showing also sharply reduced any remaining belief in a Mega Man 9 upset next round.

4081.headline: Tales survives Resident Evil 5 and keeps the bracket open
4081.narrative: Tales of Symphonia survived a matchup where Resident Evil 5 had become a fashionable upset pick. The writeup sees the result as the beginning of a genuinely competitive lower half of the Northeast bracket.

4082.headline: God of War strengthens its case against Tales
4082.narrative: God of War produced a stable, unsurprising performance against weak opposition. Its clean result made the upcoming Tales of Symphonia matchup look more favorable for God of War than it had before the round.

4083.headline: Grand Theft Auto III's hot start quickly fades
4083.narrative: Grand Theft Auto III briefly inspired exaggerated early-match hype before settling into a much more ordinary performance. The writeup treats the final impression as further evidence that Half-Life 2 was the stronger lower-bracket threat.

4084.headline: Half-Life 2 dominates its Valve sibling
4084.narrative: Half-Life 2 looked extremely strong in an intrafran­chise matchup and became the clear favorite to emerge from the Northeast's lower half. The writeup also uses the result to fuel speculation about a later Metroid Prime comparison.
4084.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly frames Half-Life 2 versus Left 4 Dead 2 as an SFF match, with the stronger Valve title suppressing the weaker one.

4085.headline: Melee opens with a historic blowout
4085.narrative: Melee delivered one of the contest's largest blowouts and immediately framed the East as a coming Melee-versus-Brawl showdown. The writeup also treats the result as further evidence that rhythm games had collapsed on GameFAQs.

4086.headline: Morrowind reverses Warcraft in a strange PC duel
4086.narrative: Morrowind came back from a bad opening to win a close PC-versus-PC matchup that Board 8 had leaned the other way on. The writeup is especially amused that a Blizzard game lost a close contest without the expected rally magic.

4087.headline: N64 SFF makes Perfect Dark-Conker hard to read
4087.narrative: Perfect Dark advanced through a matchup the writeup considered almost useless for strength analysis because of the N64 overlap. The commentary finds the presentation more memorable than the competitive result.
4087.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Perfect Dark versus Conker an N64 SFF match, with the stronger shared-console title suppressing the weaker one.

4088.headline: Call of Duty 4 wins and still embarrasses itself
4088.narrative: Call of Duty 4 won but performed far below the enormous casual confidence placed in it. The writeup treats the showing as another clear example of GameFAQs hostility toward the Call of Duty series.

4089.headline: Pokémon DPP opens with a major warning sign
4089.narrative: Pokémon Diamond, Pearl and Platinum looked much weaker than expected against Metroid Fusion. The writeup treats the result as an early warning that the post-RBY Pokémon games had lost strength rather than as a fluke.

4090.headline: Fire Emblem obliterates a debated wrestling matchup
4090.narrative: A matchup that had attracted some Board 8 debate turned into a complete Fire Emblem rout almost immediately. The writeup treats the result as proof that wrestling games had very little contest appeal.

4091.headline: Valkyria Chronicles cements the top-option heuristic
4091.narrative: Valkyria Chronicles survived a low-interest fodder matchup that the writeup uses to popularize the 'top option' heuristic. The match stayed relatively close on paper but generated almost no rallying or broader attention.

4092.headline: Brawl answers Melee with an even stronger opening
4092.narrative: Brawl produced an extraordinary performance against a legitimate Mario Kart game and immediately looked at least as impressive as Melee. The writeup sees the result as the stronger opening statement in their looming divisional showdown.

4093.headline: Galaxy's supposedly weak opener ages very differently
4093.narrative: Super Mario Galaxy's opening performance was widely read as disappointing at the time because the opposition was assumed to be very weak. The writeup emphasizes how misleading that interpretation looked once Galaxy's later strength became clear.

4094.headline: A 4chan rally helps Pokémon RSE flip GTA IV
4094.narrative: A heavily debated matchup swung sharply after the afternoon vote and outside support arrived for Pokémon. The writeup celebrates the result as another humiliation for Grand Theft Auto and as a major bracket upset.
4094.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says 4chan rallied Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald during the close match, contributing to the swing against Grand Theft Auto IV.

4095.headline: The writeup mostly turns into an Anagram comedy bit
4095.narrative: The writeup is mostly an extended joke about a Board 8 user's long-running Dragon Age rants, with the actual match serving mainly as the setup.

4096.headline: Twilight Princess fuels ZeldaFAQs complaints and title hype
4096.narrative: Twilight Princess delivered an elite-looking blowout that triggered another round of ZeldaFAQs complaints. The writeup nevertheless treats the strength shown here as genuinely important for the later Smash matchup.

4097.headline: BioShock opens strong and sparks Kingdom Hearts speculation
4097.narrative: BioShock's convincing opener generated immediate speculation that it could beat both Kingdom Hearts games. The writeup sees the performance as evidence that voters were taking the 'Game of the Decade' framing seriously.

4098.headline: Kingdom Hearts II beats Halo without revealing much
4098.narrative: Kingdom Hearts II handled Halo 2 in a surprisingly trendless daytime match despite both series having strong expected afternoon behavior. The writeup considers the result poor evidence for comparing the two Kingdom Hearts games because Halo was so heavily anti-voted.

4099.headline: Dissidia exposes Call of Duty's GameFAQs weakness
4099.narrative: Modern Warfare 2 won, but Dissidia performed far better than the enormous casual confidence behind Call of Duty suggested it should. The writeup treats the result as another striking example of the site's growing anti-Call-of-Duty sentiment.

4100.headline: Kingdom Hearts seizes control of the sequel debate
4100.narrative: Kingdom Hearts delivered a much stronger-looking opener than its sequel had and became the clear favorite in their eventual head-to-head matchup. The writeup especially notes its powerful afternoon trend.

4101.headline: Final Fantasy X wins but looks vulnerable
4101.narrative: Final Fantasy X recovered from a weak opening but still looked less imposing than a potential contest champion was expected to look. The writeup treats the early struggle as the first clear sign that FFX was vulnerable.

4102.headline: Borderlands restores order to a chaotic 8/9 round
4102.narrative: Borderlands won one of the few first-round 8/9 matches that behaved roughly as expected. The writeup uses the result mainly to reiterate that Board 8 tends to overrate the Tales series.

4103.headline: Golden Sun looks far stronger than expected
4103.narrative: Golden Sun looked unexpectedly legitimate against weak but recognizable opposition. The writeup immediately turns the result into a warning for Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas in the next round.

4104.headline: San Andreas fails to answer Golden Sun's challenge
4104.narrative: San Andreas produced only an average performance at exactly the wrong time, with a new Golden Sun release looming over their next matchup. The writeup treats the result as a serious blow to GTA's chances.

4105.headline: KOTOR wins but bleeds away its upset case
4105.narrative: Knights of the Old Republic won but steadily bled strength throughout the match. The writeup sees the decline as a major warning before its projected clash with Final Fantasy IX.

4106.headline: Fire Emblem makes Tony Hawk look overmatched
4106.narrative: Fire Emblem made a previously debated matchup with Tony Hawk look easy after its sister title had already crushed WWF No Mercy. The writeup treats the result as another rejection of sports and sports-adjacent games on the site.

4107.headline: Persona 3 gives the top-option rule another win
4107.narrative: Persona 3 won a low-interest tossup that the writeup again uses to champion the 'top option' heuristic in pure fodder matches. The result mattered more for bracket psychology than for either game's strength.

4108.headline: Final Fantasy IX's day-vote weakness shows again
4108.narrative: Final Fantasy IX handled Phoenix Wright comfortably but again displayed its famously weak afternoon trend. The writeup treats that pattern as an important warning for its upcoming daytime match with KOTOR.

4109.headline: Resident Evil 4 opens like a true title contender
4109.narrative: Resident Evil 4 delivered the kind of emphatic opening expected from a serious title contender. The writeup argues that the 'Game of the Decade' framing may have boosted the game's already substantial respect.

4110.headline: Vice City delivers one of the contest's worst performances
4110.narrative: Vice City performed so poorly that the writeup calls it one of the contest's biggest stinkers. The result is used as further evidence that Grand Theft Auto had become one of GameFAQs' most heavily disliked series.

4111.headline: Dead Rising survives a long TWEWY battle
4111.narrative: The World Ends With You and Dead Rising produced a long, genuinely competitive match with several lead changes and a strong overnight Square push. The writeup treats the result as the real beginning of a tightly contested three-game section of the bracket.

4112.headline: Persona 4 advances without settling the next round
4112.narrative: Persona 4 advanced as expected but did not dominate enough to become a clear favorite over Dead Rising. The writeup sees the performance as mildly disappointing given Braid's presumed weakness.

4113.headline: Portal explodes into a serious divisional threat
4113.narrative: Portal crushed a game that had performed very well in the vote-ins and immediately locked down the Southwest's lower half. The writeup sees both its cult status and recent free availability as plausible contributors to its surge.

4114.headline: Final Fantasy XII wins a Pyrrhic victory
4114.narrative: Final Fantasy XII won but looked weak enough against Crisis Core that the writeup labels the result a Pyrrhic victory. The showing effectively made Portal the clear favorite for their later matchup.

4115.headline: Skies survives a dramatic Baldur's Gate collapse
4115.narrative: Skies of Arcadia built a huge early advantage and then spent the rest of the match steadily giving it back. The writeup remembers the percentage collapse as unusually dramatic even though Baldur's Gate II never quite completed the comeback.

4116.headline: Mass Effect underperforms despite sequel-fueled hype
4116.narrative: Mass Effect's prediction support reflected a major boost from its sequel, but the actual performance fell well short of that reputation. The writeup considers this enough to make Portal the clear lower-bracket favorite.

4117.headline: Metal Gear Solid 3 opens with a warning sign
4117.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 won easily yet still looked weak for a top seed against a vote-in survivor. The writeup calls this an early warning for the entire Metal Gear division and for the series' contest strength.

4118.headline: SRK rallies Marvel past New Super Mario Bros. Wii
4118.narrative: A close Mario lead gradually disappeared once the fighting-game community began rallying for Marvel vs. Capcom 2. The writeup remembers the result as one of the contest's largest public rally successes and a major bracket killer.
4118.anomaly_note: The writeup says Shoryuken.com organized an effective rally for Marvel vs. Capcom 2, producing the decisive late swing against New Super Mario Bros. Wii.

4119.headline: Paper Mario looks far more legitimate than expected
4119.narrative: Paper Mario looked far stronger than many pre-contest projections had suggested and immediately weakened the case for a World of Warcraft upset next round. The writeup also notes how much Katamari's old Board 8 popularity had faded.

4120.headline: World of Warcraft collapses under massive anti-voting
4120.narrative: World of Warcraft badly underperformed against one of Nintendo's weakest contest entrants despite receiving enormous bracket confidence. The writeup treats the result as a striking demonstration of how much anti-WoW sentiment mattered on GameFAQs.

4121.headline: Metal Gear Solid 4 underperforms despite a picture disadvantage
4121.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 4 won but looked substantially weaker than its 2009 form, reinforcing the emerging narrative that the entire series had declined. The writeup acknowledges the unfavorable picture while still treating the performance as poor.
4121.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Metal Gear Solid 4 had a picture disadvantage against Assassin's Creed, though it argues that the disadvantage does not fully excuse MGS4's weak showing.

4122.headline: Diablo II becomes Blizzard's bright spot
4122.narrative: Diablo II produced a notably strong opening while the other Blizzard games were struggling badly. The writeup treats it as evidence that Diablo had benefited more than its Blizzard siblings from the contest's decade framing.

4123.headline: Metal Gear Solid 2 gives no warning of what comes next
4123.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 2 looked solid enough against Banjo-Tooie that nothing in the first round hinted at its coming loss to Shadow of the Colossus. The writeup emphasizes how misleading the opening-round evidence turned out to be.

4124.headline: Shadow of the Colossus wins without revealing its future upset
4124.narrative: Shadow of the Colossus handled The Sims comfortably despite surprisingly weak prediction support. The writeup stresses that the result still offered almost no reason to expect the major upset waiting in the next round.

4125.headline: Majora's Mask opens with championship-level strength
4125.narrative: Majora's Mask opened with a performance the writeup retrospectively identifies as championship caliber. The result is presented as the first real evidence that the supposedly secondary Zelda title could win the entire contest.

4126.headline: Chrono Cross restores order in an SFF-tinged 8/9 match
4126.narrative: Chrono Cross delivered one of the rare first-round 8/9 results that behaved roughly as expected. The writeup mostly celebrates the absence of another bracket disaster after a long run of chaotic 8/9 matches.
4126.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Chrono Cross versus Dragon Quest VIII a JRPG SFF match, with the stronger shared-audience title suppressing the weaker one.

4127.headline: Mario Kart Wii barely avoids a Phoenix Wright embarrassment
4127.narrative: Mario Kart Wii needed its morning strength to escape a surprisingly persistent Phoenix Wright challenge. The writeup treats the near-upset as one of the clearest embarrassments for the Wii in the contest.

4128.headline: Pokémon GSC wins but loses ground in the title debate
4128.narrative: Pokémon Gold, Silver and Crystal won easily but bled enough support to strengthen the writeup's belief that Majora's Mask was the stronger title. The match is framed as an early warning for Pokémon's championship hopes.

4129.headline: Wind Waker wins while old Celda hostility resurfaces
4129.narrative: Wind Waker began overwhelmingly but lost a remarkable amount of support across the match. The writeup reads the collapse as evidence that lingering hostility toward the game still mattered and that it was in trouble against the Majora-GSC winner.

4130.headline: Assassin's Creed II advances in a difficult match to read
4130.narrative: Assassin's Creed II won a largely static and hard-to-read match between lightly tested games. The writeup mostly uses the result to puzzle over the relative strength of Assassin's Creed, ICO and Metal Gear.

4131.headline: Paper Mario punishes the casual Gears of War pick
4131.narrative: Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door comfortably beat a Gears of War side that casual brackets had favored heavily. The writeup treats the result as a clear victory for expert expectations over casual name recognition.

4132.headline: Oblivion closes a wild first round without drama
4132.narrative: Oblivion dispatched SoulCalibur II without the usual last-match-of-round chaos. The writeup mainly uses the quiet finish to reflect on an unusually entertaining and upset-heavy first round.

4133.headline: Fallout 3 restores order against Deus Ex
4133.narrative: Fallout 3 crushed first-round upset winner Deus Ex and restored the expected hierarchy. The writeup briefly entertains SFF as a possibility but ultimately treats Deus Ex as simply weak and focuses on Fallout's strong daytime profile.

4134.headline: Batman crushes Team Fortress 2 and sparks new upset talk
4134.narrative: Batman turned a matchup that had gained upset buzz after Team Fortress 2's first-round thriller into a one-sided win. The result immediately generated a new wave of Batman-over-Fallout speculation.

4135.headline: Uncharted 2 wins a pyrrhic victory over Street Fighter IV
4135.narrative: Uncharted 2 won, but its steady percentage loss to Street Fighter IV made the victory feel hollow. The writeup treats the result as a warning that either Halo game would be favored next round.

4136.headline: Halo 1 settles the series hierarchy over Halo 3
4136.narrative: Halo: Combat Evolved decisively beat Halo 3 and settled the series hierarchy in favor of the original. The writeup notes that the result was not an extreme same-series suppression, but was still a clear inter-series win.

4137.headline: Metroid Prime advances but leaves divisional questions
4137.narrative: Metroid Prime comfortably eliminated Devil May Cry 3, though the winner's substantial percentage bleed kept questions alive about the divisional race. The writeup finds the match picture more memorable than the result.

4138.headline: Mega Man 9 impresses despite an easy Okami win
4138.narrative: Okami beat Mega Man 9 comfortably, but Mega Man still performed well above the broader prediction consensus. The writeup treats the loss as validation that Mega Man 9 was a surprisingly legitimate entrant.

4139.headline: God of War breaks a five-hour Tales deadlock
4139.narrative: God of War and Tales of Symphonia spent hours in a true deadlock before God of War's morning vote broke the match open. The writeup remembers the long stall and decisive finish as one of the contest's best matches.

4140.headline: GTA III earns respect while Half-Life 2 shows weakness
4140.narrative: Grand Theft Auto III gave Half-Life 2 a strong challenge without ever threatening the actual result. The writeup treats GTA3 as the clear exception to the series' poor contest and sees Half-Life 2's steady bleed as a warning before stronger day-match opponents.

4141.headline: Melee wins big but the Brawl warning signs grow
4141.narrative: Melee posted another blowout, but its overnight and morning trends looked increasingly unfavorable for the looming match with Brawl. The writeup treats the performance as one of several signs that Brawl had become the favorite.

4142.headline: Perfect Dark embarrasses Call of Duty despite the picture
4142.narrative: Call of Duty 4 won but was badly embarrassed by an otherwise unproven Perfect Dark. The writeup sees the poor showing as further evidence of deep anti-Call-of-Duty sentiment on GameFAQs.
4142.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly describes a picture imbalance against Perfect Dark and notes that Perfect Dark still performed well despite its weaker image.

4143.headline: Pokémon DPP advances without inspiring title confidence
4143.narrative: Pokémon Diamond, Pearl and Platinum eliminated Fire Emblem as expected, but failed to look strong enough to support the most ambitious Pokémon projections. The writeup treats the match as bad news for hopes of a broader Pokémon surge.

4144.headline: Brawl cruises but gives Melee one small opening
4144.narrative: Brawl demolished Valkyria Chronicles, though the writeup considers this one of the few matches where Brawl looked merely comparable to Melee rather than clearly superior. The result itself was never competitive.

4145.headline: Galaxy wins an oddly weak match against Pokémon RSE
4145.narrative: Super Mario Galaxy beat Pokémon RSE but looked much weaker than expected while doing so. The writeup retrospectively treats the result as a strange outlier in an otherwise strong Galaxy contest.

4146.headline: Twilight Princess dispatches a badly placed Dragon Age
4146.narrative: Twilight Princess comfortably eliminated Dragon Age in a match whose seeding and bracket placement left little suspense. The writeup argues that Dragon Age could have done more in a less hostile part of the bracket.

4147.headline: Kingdom Hearts II survives heavy BioShock respect
4147.narrative: Kingdom Hearts II beat a highly respected BioShock despite much of the prediction community siding against it. The writeup sees BioShock's strong loss as evidence of a contest-title boost while also noting how easily KH2 survived.

4148.headline: Kingdom Hearts humiliates Modern Warfare 2
4148.narrative: Kingdom Hearts doubled Modern Warfare 2, an especially harsh result because Kingdom Hearts rarely produces or suffers major blowouts. The writeup treats the match as another humiliating verdict on Call of Duty's standing on the site.

4149.headline: Final Fantasy X finally delivers a clean blowout
4149.narrative: Final Fantasy X delivered one of its few clean performances of the contest by overwhelming Borderlands and holding steady throughout the match. The writeup still regards the result as an exception rather than proof that FFX had fully returned to old form.

4150.headline: Golden Sun upsets San Andreas with everything breaking its way
4150.narrative: Golden Sun upset San Andreas on the release day of Dark Dawn, with RPG-friendly site conditions and a prominent home-page ad further favoring the winner. The writeup sees the timing as unusually hostile to GTA and the result as a major casual-bracket shock.
4150.anomaly_note: The writeup says Golden Sun's match picture looked exceptionally strong while San Andreas looked exceptionally poor, describing the image as one of several factors stacked against GTA.

4151.headline: KOTOR wins but loses its Final Fantasy IX hype
4151.narrative: KOTOR beat Fire Emblem but struggled enough to erase most hopes of an upset over Final Fantasy IX. The writeup regards Fire Emblem as respectable but not strong enough to excuse KOTOR's middling performance.

4152.headline: Final Fantasy IX finally avoids a daytime collapse
4152.narrative: Final Fantasy IX routed Persona 3 and, unusually, avoided its customary daytime collapse. The writeup treats the result as routine but mildly encouraging for FFIX's trend profile.

4153.headline: Resident Evil 4 bleeds away its title hype
4153.narrative: Resident Evil 4 began with championship-level numbers against Vice City, then bled support for the entire match. The writeup treats the final result as a major warning that RE4's deeper title aspirations were unrealistic.

4154.headline: Persona 4 survives Dead Rising in a late thriller
4154.narrative: Persona 4 survived a long Dead Rising comeback in one of the round's closest races, reclaiming control late after briefly falling behind. The writeup credits Persona's more committed fanbase and possibly its picture for the narrow escape.
4154.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Persona 4's strong match picture may deserve credit for the narrow win over Dead Rising.

4155.headline: Portal blows away Final Fantasy XII
4155.narrative: Portal demolished Final Fantasy XII in a matchup that had been heavily debated before the contest. The writeup celebrates the result as both a Portal statement and a decisive rejection of old four-way extrapolations favoring FFXII.

4156.headline: Mass Effect ends Skies of Arcadia's upset run
4156.narrative: Mass Effect ended Skies of Arcadia's upset run with a predictable blowout. The writeup treats the match mainly as confirmation of the large boost Mass Effect received from its sequel.

4157.headline: MGS3 wins while Marvel looks more legitimate
4157.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 beat Marvel vs. Capcom 2, but looked weak enough to worry observers who had dismissed MvC2's first-round rally-assisted upset. The writeup retrospectively credits MvC2 with more legitimate strength than it initially received.

4158.headline: Paper Mario humiliates heavily favored World of Warcraft
4158.narrative: Paper Mario decisively eliminated World of Warcraft in a matchup casual brackets had badly misread. The writeup treats the result as the clearest humiliation of WoW's inflated seeding and popularity expectations.

4159.headline: Diablo II exposes a weakened Metal Gear Solid 4
4159.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 4 won but steadily lost ground to Diablo II and looked far weaker than its prior-year form. The writeup also gives Diablo II substantial credit as the strongest traditional Western RPG in the field.

4160.headline: Shadow of the Colossus survives MGS2 in a classic
4160.narrative: Shadow of the Colossus survived an all-day war of attrition against Metal Gear Solid 2 and won by the narrowest margin in the contest. The writeup treats the upset as the launch of the contest's Cinderella run and one of its best matches.
4160.anomaly_note: The writeup calls Shadow of the Colossus's image the biggest picture disadvantage of the contest and says it would have won more easily under fairer pictures. It also explicitly describes a late Shadow of the Colossus counter-rally after MGS2 retook the lead.

4161.headline: Majora's Mask sets the benchmark for Pokémon GSC
4161.narrative: Majora's Mask crushed Chrono Cross in a routine second-round blowout. The writeup uses the result mainly to establish a benchmark for Pokémon GSC before their anticipated clash.

4162.headline: Pokémon GSC keeps pace with Majora's Mask
4162.narrative: Pokémon GSC answered Majora's benchmark with an even larger blowout of Mario Kart Wii. The result kept their coming matchup debatable while also extending the writeup's criticism of Wii-era contest strength.

4163.headline: Assassin's Creed II makes Wind Waker look vulnerable
4163.narrative: Wind Waker began overwhelmingly against Assassin's Creed II and then bled support at a rate the writeup considered shocking for Zelda. The result both lowered confidence in Wind Waker and established Assassin's Creed II as a legitimate contest game.

4164.headline: Paper Mario exposes Oblivion as a four-way wonder
4164.narrative: Oblivion beat Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door, but the margin was far too small to sustain pre-contest talk of challenging Wind Waker. The writeup treats Paper Mario's resistance as another strong showing for the series.

4165.headline: Batman validates itself in a respectable Fallout loss
4165.narrative: Fallout 3 beat Batman without suspense, but Batman's respectable showing reinforced the writeup's view that Arkham Asylum was a genuinely strong new entrant. The match mattered more for Batman's validation than for the winner.

4166.headline: Halo's ASV overwhelms Uncharted 2
4166.narrative: Halo transformed an almost even opening hour against Uncharted 2 into a decisive win through its trademark afternoon vote. The writeup treats the swing as a classic demonstration of Halo's unusually powerful ASV.

4167.headline: Okami earns respect in defeat against Metroid Prime
4167.narrative: Metroid Prime advanced as expected, but Okami's resistance impressed the writeup and validated how far the game had risen since its earliest contest appearances. The result briefly made Prime's next match look more uncertain than it ultimately was.

4168.headline: Half-Life 2 crushes the God of War upset case
4168.narrative: Half-Life 2 immediately shut down pre-match God of War upset talk and delivered one of its strongest performances. The result turned the coming Metroid Prime matchup into a genuine tossup.

4169.headline: Melee wins while the Brawl warning signs pile up
4169.narrative: Melee beat Call of Duty 4 easily but again bled enough support to make the writeup increasingly pessimistic about its chances against Brawl. The poor bracket confidence around Melee added to the warning signs.

4170.headline: Brawl mauls Pokémon and takes the Melee edge
4170.narrative: Brawl destroyed Pokémon DPP even in a daytime match favorable to Pokémon. The writeup treats the performance as decisive evidence that Brawl had overtaken Melee in the divisional rivalry.

4171.headline: Galaxy loses to Zelda but earns new respect
4171.narrative: Twilight Princess eliminated Super Mario Galaxy, but Galaxy performed far better than the old Mario-versus-Zelda history suggested it might. The writeup treats the loss as a moral victory that helped rehabilitate Galaxy's contest reputation.

4172.headline: Kingdom Hearts II wins the series showdown
4172.narrative: Kingdom Hearts II upset the original Kingdom Hearts in a direct series showdown, repeatedly repelling small comeback attempts before its strong afternoon vote pulled away. The writeup treats the result as decisive evidence that the sequel had become the stronger game.

4173.headline: Final Fantasy X survives another ugly performance
4173.narrative: Final Fantasy X beat Golden Sun but looked embarrassingly weak early in a matchup where the writeup expected major same-genre suppression. Its overnight recovery helped, yet the result reinforced the view that FFX had declined substantially since 2004.

4174.headline: Final Fantasy IX survives a respectable KOTOR challenge
4174.narrative: Final Fantasy IX held off KOTOR in a matchup that had been a legitimate pre-contest upset possibility. KOTOR's respectable loss and FFIX's predictable daytime decline left the writeup satisfied with both games' performances.

4175.headline: Resident Evil 4 revives its Final Fantasy X upset case
4175.narrative: Resident Evil 4 rebounded from its weak Vice City match by crushing Persona 4. Combined with Final Fantasy X's poor showing, the result revived serious discussion of an RE4 upset in the next round.

4176.headline: Mass Effect shines in defeat against Portal
4176.narrative: Portal beat Mass Effect comfortably, but the writeup considers Mass Effect's showing one of the best losses of the contest and clear proof of a major sequel-driven boost. Portal still looked strong, just not strong enough to threaten Resident Evil 4.

4177.headline: Paper Mario exits with its credibility intact
4177.narrative: Paper Mario's run ended against Metal Gear Solid 3, but the writeup treats its performance as fully legitimate after the earlier World of Warcraft upset. It also mocks how badly casual brackets had overestimated WoW's chances in this section.

4178.headline: Shadow of the Colossus confirms its Cinderella run
4178.narrative: Shadow of the Colossus followed its MGS2 upset by beating Metal Gear Solid 4 and turning a possible fluke into the contest's defining Cinderella run. A late MGS4 rally cut into the lead but is explicitly dismissed as meaningless.

4179.headline: Majora's Mask destroys the Pokémon GSC hype
4179.narrative: Majora's Mask ended the heavily hyped Pokémon GSC run almost immediately and overturned the comparisons many people had drawn from the prior four-way contest. The writeup treats the result as another major rejection of four-way extrapolation.

4180.headline: Wind Waker quietly ends Oblivion's hoped-for challenge
4180.narrative: Wind Waker handled Oblivion without the competitive drama some had expected before the contest. Oblivion improved during the day but never became one of the Western games the writeup considered especially impressive.

4181.headline: Fallout 3 delivers its first fully convincing statement
4181.narrative: The poll disappeared entirely for the opening hour, but the eventual match gave Fallout 3 its first clear statement against a proven contest game. The writeup treats the result as the moment serious upset talk against Fallout largely died.

4182.headline: Prime advances as Half-Life 2 exposes a timing problem
4182.narrative: Metroid Prime controlled the match, while Half-Life 2's late gains suggested that a different time window might have produced a much closer result. The writeup explicitly says the heavily discussed pictures did not matter.

4183.headline: Brawl comes back on Melee in a divisive rivalry match
4183.narrative: Melee built the early lead, but Brawl's European and morning strength completed the comeback and settled the rivalry for the bracket. The writeup argues that the timing format may have mattered enough to make the result less definitive than the rivalry deserved.

4184.headline: Twilight Princess makes the four-way comparison look useless
4184.narrative: Twilight Princess overwhelmed Kingdom Hearts II far more decisively than their earlier four-way meeting had suggested. The writeup uses the result as another example of Zelda's exceptional 1v1 strength and the unreliability of four-way comparisons.

4185.headline: Final Fantasy X cruises through a mild Square SFF match
4185.narrative: The same-series divisional final was never presented as a serious rivalry, and Final Fantasy IX was simply outclassed by Final Fantasy X. The writeup mostly uses the match to criticize how easy the division had been for FFX.
4185.anomaly_note: The writeup treats this as a Square SFF matchup, noting that Final Fantasy IX was suppressed by Final Fantasy X even if the effect was milder than some older Square pairings.

4186.headline: Portal exits with one of the contest's best runs
4186.narrative: Portal's run ended against Resident Evil 4, but the writeup still considers the showing highly respectable and much stronger than old four-way statistics would have implied. It treats Portal as one of the contest's major success stories.

4187.headline: Night voting ends the Shadow of the Colossus run
4187.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 ended the Shadow of the Colossus Cinderella run in a match the writeup believes was heavily shaped by being held at night. Shadow stayed close, but MGS3's overnight strength controlled the decisive portion.

4188.headline: Majora's Mask settles the Wind Waker debate
4188.narrative: Majora's Mask settled a long-running Zelda-series debate by beating Wind Waker decisively. The writeup argues the result did not require any special contest bandwagon because Majora was simply the more beloved title.

4189.headline: Fallout 3 survives Prime in a timing-sensitive quarterfinal
4189.narrative: Fallout 3 survived a strong Metroid Prime challenge, with the writeup again arguing that match timing may have changed the outcome. The recent New Vegas release is also cited as a plausible boost for Fallout.

4190.headline: Brawl suppresses Twilight Princess and strengthens its title case
4190.narrative: Twilight Princess briefly led before Brawl took over and won comfortably. The result made Brawl look increasingly difficult to stop and strengthened the belief that it was the contest favorite.
4190.anomaly_note: The writeup says Brawl versus Twilight Princess can be considered SFF because of their shared Nintendo/Wii audience, with Brawl suppressing Zelda's support.

4191.headline: Final Fantasy X destroys the Resident Evil 4 upset hype
4191.narrative: Final Fantasy X erased the pre-match Resident Evil 4 upset hype almost immediately and produced the writeup's strongest championship-looking performance of its run. RE4 is treated as a major disappointment for failing to make the match competitive.

4192.headline: Majora's Mask turns into a genuine title threat
4192.narrative: Majora's Mask overwhelmed Metal Gear Solid 3 and fully emerged as a credible championship threat. The writeup considers MGS3 the one quarterfinalist that looked clearly out of place this deep in the bracket.

4193.headline: Fallout 3 gives Brawl a major semifinal warning
4193.narrative: Fallout 3 performed far better against Brawl than the writeup expected and resisted even Brawl's normally dominant daytime strength. The result is framed as an excellent loss and as evidence of growing voter fatigue with Nintendo and Square dominance.

4194.headline: Majora's Mask rallies through an all-time semifinal classic
4194.narrative: Final Fantasy X controlled much of the first half, Majora's Mask mounted a huge daytime comeback, and FFX nearly answered again late. The writeup calls it the best match of the contest and a throwback to the site's classic close-match era.
4194.anomaly_note: The writeup says Majora's Mask was rallied more heavily and that its fans pushed harder during the decisive stages of the close semifinal.

4195.headline: Majora's Mask wins the Game of the Decade crown
