4195.narrative: Majora's Mask carried its momentum into the final and built enough of an early advantage to survive Brawl's later daytime recovery. The writeup frames the result as both a Good-vs-Evil fanbase victory and a symbolic win for older games over newer ones.

4196.headline: Santa holds up respectably against Link in the bonus
4196.narrative: Santa Claus performed respectably against Link in the Christmas bonus despite never being treated as a real upset threat. The writeup uses the match to argue for a future contest that allows broader fictional characters.

4510.headline: Mario opens with a blowout and alarming turnout
4510.narrative: Mario and Bowser opened the rivalry contest with the expected blowout, but the writeup focuses on the embarrassingly low turnout even for a marquee Nintendo pairing. It blames the contest format rather than overall site traffic.

4511.headline: Ike ends the Conker debate almost immediately
4511.narrative: Ike and Black Knight quickly ended a matchup that had received more pre-contest debate than the writeup thought it deserved. Conker still managed one of his better contest showings before another hopeless bracket draw.

4512.headline: Kirby and Meta Knight punish a risky guru pick
4512.narrative: Kirby and Meta Knight turned a debated opener against Jill and Nemesis into a rout. The writeup remembers the match mostly for a disastrous guru pick and for how quickly the supposed uncertainty vanished.

4513.headline: The Catherine pair earns a respectable niche showing
4513.narrative: Sonic and Robotnik dominated as expected, but the Catherine pairing still produced a respectable showing for such a niche Atlus entry. The writeup treats that result as a small feel-good story rather than a competitive threat.

4514.headline: Mega Man X and Zero validate their guru nomination
4514.narrative: Mega Man X and Zero produced one of the strongest opening-round performances and validated the guru effort that had helped nominate them. The writeup also considers them one of the bracket's genuinely strong rivalries.

4515.headline: Bartz and Gilgamesh expose Guybrush again
4515.narrative: Bartz and Gilgamesh comfortably advanced while the writeup again complains that Guybrush keeps receiving nominations despite repeated weak contest performances. The match itself produced little suspense.

4516.headline: King K. Rool helps Donkey Kong erase the Ezio debate
4516.narrative: Donkey Kong and King K. Rool settled a heavily debated matchup quickly, with the writeup crediting K. Rool as a genuinely liked partner while Rodrigo Borgia dragged down Ezio's side. The result becomes an example of rivalry quality overcoming a stronger individual character.

4517.headline: The Mortal Kombat pair exposes a weak rivalry concept
4517.narrative: Sub-Zero and Scorpion won comfortably, while the writeup spends most of its match analysis arguing that Leon and Ada were never a real rivalry. The result is presented as another failure of the bracket's rivalry concept.

4518.headline: The trainers fade despite a major picture advantage
4518.narrative: Red and Blue still faded substantially after a huge start, which the writeup found surprising given how favorable their picture was. The showing is treated as an early hint that the trainers relied heavily on momentum.
4518.anomaly_note: The writeup says the match picture was heavily in favor of Red and Blue, giving the Pokémon trainers a clear presentation advantage over Raynor and Kerrigan.

4519.headline: A Waluigi match becomes the contest's early thriller
4519.narrative: Luigi and Waluigi survived what became the closest match of the contest's early rounds, while Cecil and Golbez performed far better than expected. The writeup uses the matchup as proof of how little competitive drama the format was producing.

4520.headline: Ryu and Ken open with a misleadingly huge statement
4520.narrative: Ryu and Ken delivered a dominant opening that initially looked even more impressive than the Pokémon trainers' first-round result. The writeup later treats that comparison as misleading once the rest of the bracket played out.

4521.headline: Fox and Wolf punish a star-and-anchor pairing
4521.narrative: Fox and Wolf beat a side built around the stronger Yuna but weakened by Seymour, which the writeup uses as another example of a balanced rivalry beating a star-and-anchor pairing. Much of the commentary also revisits the controversial match picture without claiming it changed the vote.

4522.headline: Samus and Ridley give no early warning signs
4522.narrative: Samus and Ridley overwhelmed the joke-game pairing and gave no early indication that Ridley might later hold Samus back. The writeup treats the result as another example of how easily a strong rivalry could destroy weak opposition.

4523.headline: Terra and Kefka finally look contest-legitimate
4523.narrative: Terra and Kefka produced an unexpectedly enormous blowout that the writeup celebrates as evidence that Dissidia had finally made the Final Fantasy VI cast contest-relevant. Any possible SFF against the weaker side is treated as secondary to that broader revival.

4524.headline: Dan and Sagat turn a nomination joke into a flop
4524.narrative: Chris and Wesker demolished Dan and Sagat, turning a Board 8 joke-nomination success into one of the writeup's biggest disappointments of the contest. The rally discussed in the source concerns getting Dan and Sagat nominated, not match voting.

4525.headline: Tidus anti-voting sinks another debatable matchup
4525.narrative: Big Boss and The Boss won a heavily debated opener despite The Boss being viewed as the weak link of their pair. The writeup again blames Tidus's persistent anti-voting for preventing the Final Fantasy X rivalry from converting its individual strength.

4526.headline: Link dominates amid low turnout and an ugly picture
4526.narrative: Link and Ganondorf opened with the expected rout, but the writeup again focuses on poor turnout and a widely disliked match picture. Neither issue is presented as threatening the result.

4527.headline: Amaterasu survives an anchor against a joke-nominated pair
4527.narrative: Amaterasu and Orochi advanced despite Orochi being described as a major anchor, while Tom Nook and Crazy Redd benefited from a joke nomination campaign. The source does not describe that campaign as a match-vote rally.

4528.headline: A bad picture drags down Zidane and Kuja
4528.narrative: Zidane and Kuja won, but the writeup considers their performance terrible and directly attributes part of the weakness to the match picture. The source treats this as unusually visible evidence of picture factor.
4528.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Zidane and Kuja performed better before the match picture appeared, then dropped immediately once their unattractive Trance artwork was shown.

4529.headline: Banjo runs into another Nintendo-style SFF matchup
4529.narrative: Mega Man and Wily advanced comfortably, while the writeup laments that Banjo again received a matchup that obscured his standalone strength. The result is framed as another wasted opportunity to test Banjo fairly.
4529.anomaly_note: The writeup says Banjo has faced Nintendo SFF in every contest match and treats Mega Man's Nintendo-adjacent fanbase as another case suppressing Banjo and Gruntilda.

4530.headline: Phoenix finally wins by exploiting Gordon's anchor
4530.narrative: Phoenix and Edgeworth finally gave Phoenix a meaningful contest win by beating a Gordon Freeman side crippled by Dr. Breen. The writeup treats the result as one of the best demonstrations that two coherent rivals could overcome one much stronger character paired with an anchor.

4531.headline: Saren's weakness drags Shepard below Alucard
4531.narrative: Alucard and Dracula comfortably beat a Shepard side dragged down by Saren. The writeup again uses the match to argue that a strong individual could not reliably carry an unbalanced rivalry team.

4532.headline: Portal advances without looking especially convincing
4532.narrative: Chell and GLaDOS advanced, but the writeup found the performance difficult to interpret and weaker than expected after Portal 2's release. Most of the enthusiasm is reserved for the match picture rather than the result.

4533.headline: Frog and Magus advance without seizing the division
4533.narrative: Frog and Magus advanced but looked weak enough to keep the Southwest wide open. The writeup notes that Raiden and Vamp had shown some legitimacy in the vote-ins and treats the next Portal matchup as genuinely uncertain.

4534.headline: Cloud and Sephiroth fire a major warning salvo
4534.narrative: Cloud and Sephiroth won easily, but the writeup considers their showing shockingly weak for a top pairing and immediately writes off their chances against Link. The broader explanation is growing anti-Final-Fantasy-VII voting.

4535.headline: Kratos advances through another low-impact matchup
4535.narrative: Kratos and Zeus advanced without difficulty, though the writeup notes Kratos's characteristically poor board vote. The bracket placement made the result largely irrelevant beyond that observation.

4536.headline: Pac-Man's picture edge helps make the matchup feel predetermined
4536.narrative: Pac-Man and Blinky advanced in a very low-turnout match that the writeup never regarded as a serious tossup despite pre-match debate. Crash's faded relevance and Pac-Man's presentation both made the result feel inevitable.
4536.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pac-Man was effectively guaranteed the better picture and treats his favorable classic sprite presentation as another factor making the matchup feel predetermined.

4537.headline: Crono loses despite a huge picture advantage
4537.narrative: Snake and Liquid comfortably ended another Crono run despite the source saying Crono had a major picture advantage. The writeup treats the loss as a bleak sign that Crono's old Noble Nine strength was gone for good.
4537.anomaly_note: The writeup says Crono and Lavos received one of the most unbalanced picture advantages imaginable, favoring their side even though Lavos remained too large an anchor to overcome.

4538.headline: Squall and Seifer open with a warning salvo
4538.narrative: Squall and Seifer advanced but looked much weaker than expected against Laharl and Mid-Boss. The writeup retrospectively treats the performance as an early warning that the next Kingdom Hearts matchup could be far more dangerous than assumed.

4539.headline: The writeup mostly defends Ramza and Delita's rivalry
4539.narrative: The writeup is mostly an extended defense of Ramza and Delita as genuine rivals, with only a brief note that the Soul Calibur pair advanced.

4540.headline: A huge Dante win gives way to a long Capcom rant
4540.narrative: After briefly praising Dante and Vergil's enormous win, the writeup turns mostly into a long rant about the direction of Devil May Cry and other games.

4541.headline: 4chan dents Sora briefly in the contest's strangest match
4541.narrative: The strangest first-round pairing briefly became a 4chan target, but the rally faded once it was clear the upset was not happening. Sora and Riku recovered comfortably, closing a first round the writeup considered deeply disappointing.
4541.anomaly_note: The writeup says 4chan rallied the Wolfenstein side hard enough to drag Sora and Riku down temporarily. It also says the Wolfenstein team had a picture advantage because the Sora/Riku image looked poor.

4542.headline: Mario and Bowser begin Round Two with another bad rematch
4542.narrative: Mario and Bowser repeated a matchup the writeup felt had effectively happened only a year earlier. The rout is remembered mainly as another example of the bracket producing bad rematches.

4543.headline: Sonic and Robotnik erase the Kirby upset hype
4543.narrative: Sonic and Robotnik demolished the pre-match upset case built around Kirby and Meta Knight. The writeup treats the result as evidence that iconic rivalry strength mattered more than people expected.

4544.headline: Mega Man X and Zero cruise through a forgettable matchup
4544.narrative: Mega Man X and Zero overwhelmed Bartz and Gilgamesh in a nearly content-free match. The writeup mainly uses the result to emphasize how weak Guybrush had looked in the prior round.

4545.headline: The Mortal Kombat pair punishes another Donkey Kong overestimate
4545.narrative: Sub-Zero and Scorpion beat Donkey Kong and King K. Rool comfortably despite surprisingly low prediction confidence. The writeup treats the result as another example of Donkey Kong being chronically overrated.

4546.headline: The trainers demolish Luigi and Waluigi
4546.narrative: Red and Blue crushed Luigi and Waluigi, exposing how much an unpopular partner could drag down a stronger character in the rivalry format. The writeup openly calls its own Luigi upset pick a major mistake.

4547.headline: Ryu and Ken validate their rivalry boost
4547.narrative: Ryu and Ken handled Fox and Wolf without difficulty and confirmed that they too were receiving a substantial rivalry boost. The trainers nevertheless remained the clearer favorite for the next round.

4548.headline: Ridley turns Samus's win into a Pyrrhic victory
4548.narrative: Samus and Ridley advanced, but Ridley held Samus down badly enough that the writeup calls the win a Pyrrhic victory. The performance made a deep Samus run look increasingly unrealistic.

4549.headline: The Bosses outperform expectations against Resident Evil
4549.narrative: Big Boss and The Boss beat Chris and Wesker more comfortably than the writeup expected. The result is presented as evidence that the Metal Gear pairing benefited more from the rivalry format than anticipated.

4550.headline: Link's rout renews the retirement debate
4550.narrative: Link and Ganondorf obliterated Amaterasu and Orochi and effectively ended remaining hopes for a normal upset of Link. The match reignited the long-running argument that Link should be retired from future contests.

4551.headline: Mega Man and Wily advance through another dull match
4551.narrative: Mega Man and Wily beat Zidane and Kuja in another second-round match the writeup considered largely pointless. The picture receives more praise than the actual result.

4552.headline: Alucard and Dracula erase Phoenix's early board-vote surge
4552.narrative: Phoenix and Edgeworth's huge opening board vote briefly made the matchup look interesting, but Alucard and Dracula took over and pulled away decisively. The vampires' performance confirmed their status as the division's stronger pairing.

4553.headline: Frog and Magus survive one of the contest's rare close matches
4553.narrative: Frog and Magus held off Chell and GLaDOS in one of the contest's rare genuinely close-looking matches. The writeup celebrates it mainly because almost every other rivalry matchup had been so uncompetitive.

4554.headline: Cloud and Sephiroth cruise through a low-interest matchup
4554.narrative: Cloud and Sephiroth dispatched Kratos and Zeus in a match the writeup barely considered worth analyzing. The only notable wrinkle was Cloud finally enjoying a relatively good board vote against an even more anti-voted opponent.

4555.headline: Snake advances while Metal Gear decline becomes harder to ignore
4555.narrative: Snake and Liquid beat Pac-Man and Blinky in an unusually low-interest poll, but the writeup considers Snake's performance another sign that Metal Gear had declined. The result effectively killed any upset hope against Cloud and Sephiroth.

4556.headline: Squall advances with an underperformance nobody could use
4556.narrative: Squall and Seifer advanced without much drama, but the margin was weaker than the writeup expected from a top-seeded pairing. Because Squall's bracket path looked predetermined, the underperformance received little weight.

4557.headline: Dante's overnight comeback falls short against Sora
4557.narrative: Dante and Vergil erased Sora and Riku's overnight lead, only for Kingdom Hearts' daytime strength to restore control and secure the win. The writeup regards it as the first truly good match of the contest even though the comeback failed.

4558.headline: Mario SFFs Sonic in their first rivalry-contest meeting
4558.narrative: The first Mario-versus-Sonic rivalry matchup in contest history turned into a one-sided win for Mario and Bowser. The writeup treats the result as another example of Sonic collapsing under Mario overlap.
4558.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Mario and Bowser's win over Sonic and Robotnik an SFF beating.

4559.headline: The ninjas make Mega Man X sweat unexpectedly
4559.narrative: Mega Man X and Zero won, but Sub-Zero and Scorpion stayed much closer than anyone expected despite never truly threatening the result. The writeup credits the Mortal Kombat pair with an unusually strong rivalry boost.

4560.headline: The trainers crush Ryu and Ken and become contest stars
4560.narrative: Red and Blue demolished Ryu and Ken in what had been a heavily anticipated rivalry matchup. The result made the Pokémon trainers the clear stars of the contest and a genuine threat to the remaining elite pairings.

4561.headline: Samus survives another Pyrrhic victory with Ridley
4561.narrative: Samus and Ridley survived Big Boss and The Boss, but only after another performance badly weakened by Ridley's presence. The writeup calls it a second Pyrrhic victory and sees the upcoming trainers matchup as hopeless.

4562.headline: Link and Ganondorf roll through another predictable match
4562.narrative: Link and Ganondorf crushed Mega Man and Wily in another matchup the writeup considered too predictable to analyze at length. Link's dominance remained the only real story.

4563.headline: Alucard and Dracula complete the contest's biggest prediction upset
4563.narrative: Alucard and Dracula comfortably stopped Frog and Magus despite extremely low bracket confidence in the vampire pairing. The writeup calls their divisional win the contest's largest prediction upset.

4564.headline: Cloud and Sephiroth expose a sharply weakened Snake
4564.narrative: Cloud and Sephiroth unexpectedly rolled over Snake and Liquid, leaving the writeup searching among Metal Gear decline, Liquid's weakness, and possible overlap for an explanation. It treats the result mainly as evidence that Snake had fallen sharply.

4565.headline: Squall survives Sora in the best counted match
4565.narrative: Squall and Seifer survived Sora and Riku after a long match whose trends repeatedly defied expectations. Sora erased much of Squall's lead late, but his weak morning showing left too much ground to recover.

4566.headline: Mario repeats an old Mega Man rout almost exactly
4566.narrative: Mario and Bowser crushed Mega Man X and Zero by almost the same proportion as an old Mario-Mega Man matchup. The writeup uses the repeat-like result to complain about how lifeless the late rounds had become.

4567.headline: The trainers topple Samus and signal a changing guard
4567.narrative: Red and Blue decisively eliminated Samus and Ridley and became the first outside pairing to beat a Noble Nine member in a full-day head-to-head contest setting. The writeup frames it as a clear changing of the guard toward Pokémon.

4568.headline: Link ends the vampire run without resistance
4568.narrative: Link and Ganondorf overwhelmed Alucard and Dracula in a quarterfinal that closely echoed old Link blowouts of midcard opposition. The result added nothing new to the writeup's view of Link as untouchable.

4569.headline: Cloud and Sephiroth win but confirm their Link problem
4569.narrative: Cloud and Sephiroth crushed Squall and Seifer by almost the same proportion as an old Final Fantasy VII-versus-VIII matchup. The writeup treats the lack of improvement as a warning that they had no chance against Link.

4570.headline: Mario survives the trainers after an early semifinal scare
4570.narrative: Red and Blue stayed even with Mario and Bowser for roughly the opening hour before Mario pulled away across the rest of the day. The trainers lost, but the writeup still regards them as the contest's breakout stars.

4571.headline: Link's semifinal rout becomes the case for retirement
4571.narrative: Link and Ganondorf demolished Cloud and Sephiroth so badly that the writeup treats the match as final proof Link should be retired. Cloud's late recovery merely kept the final percentage from looking even worse.

4572.headline: Link wins a dull final as Oracle decides perfect brackets
4572.narrative: Mario and Bowser led briefly behind bracket voting and anti-Link sentiment, but Link and Ganondorf soon took control and won the championship. The final is remembered more for the Oracle tiebreak among perfect brackets than for competitive drama.

4573.headline: The trainers win an all-time bonus classic by inches
4573.narrative: The non-bracket bonus became the contest's true classic, with the trainers and Cloud/Sephiroth trading leads, stalling for hours, and reaching a tied late update before Pokémon survived by a handful of votes. The writeup ranks it among the best contest matches ever.
4573.anomaly_note: The writeup says rallies occurred during the match and describes Pokémon rallying especially hard in the final hour as the lead repeatedly changed.

5143.headline: Link wins as SFF pushes Tingle behind Isaac
5143.narrative: Link won the three-way opener as expected, while Isaac took second in the Expert Challenge ordering after Tingle faded under Link overlap. The writeup also treats Link's less-than-total domination as another sign he had declined from his peak.
5143.anomaly_note: The writeup says Tingle initially competed well for second before Link's SFF kicked in and pushed him behind Isaac.

5144.headline: Raiden shuts down Waluigi's joke hopes quickly
5144.narrative: Waluigi drew early joke support and briefly inspired another L-Block-style fantasy, but Raiden quickly took control and won comfortably. Alan Wake never threatened even the second-place Expert Challenge position.

5145.headline: Solaire wins the picture battle for second
5145.narrative: Yoshi won easily, while Solaire took second in the Expert Challenge ordering over Demi-Fiend. The writeup also laments Yoshi's poor bracket draw because his next match was against Link.
5145.anomaly_note: The writeup says the debate over second place effectively ended once the picture appeared, with Solaire's image making him look more distinctive and appropriate than Demi-Fiend.

5146.headline: Shepard's easy win turns into a FemShep voice-acting rant
5146.narrative: After noting Shepard's easy win and Olimar's expected second-place finish, the writeup mostly becomes an extended argument about why FemShep's voice performance is superior.

5147.headline: A 4chan rally saves Tharja from Tiny Tina
5147.narrative: Tharja built a large early lead, Tiny Tina slowly erased it, and the two reached a true late deadlock before outside support swung the match back to Tharja. The writeup considers it a rare first-round match that would have benefited from a longer poll.
5147.anomaly_note: The writeup says 4chan noticed Tiny Tina's comeback and rallied Tharja, pushing Tharja back ahead and preserving the win.

5148.headline: Dragon Quest Hero shocks Rinoa for second place
5148.narrative: Aerith won as expected, but the real surprise was Dragon Quest V's Hero taking second in the Expert Challenge ordering over Rinoa. The writeup celebrates the result as an improbable Board 8-style upset and a guru buster.

5149.headline: League rallies launch Draven from last place to first
5149.narrative: Jak and Chie controlled the match until League rallying arrived, after which Draven erased a huge deficit and surged into first. The writeup identifies this as the beginning of the rally-driven Draven run that would define the contest.
5149.anomaly_note: The writeup says League of Legends subreddit rallies transformed Draven from a distant last-place character into the winner within a few hours.

5150.headline: Ryu wins while Yuri comfortably takes second
5150.narrative: Ryu won comfortably, while Yuri Lowell secured the second-place Expert Challenge position over Face McShooty without much suspense. The writeup is more pleased by Yuri's placement than interested in the actual competitiveness of the match.

5151.headline: Mega Man X dominates as Jigglypuff finally debuts
5151.narrative: Mega Man X dominated the field and sparked discussion about whether his strength had reached the lower Noble Nine tier. The writeup is equally delighted that Jigglypuff finally appeared in a contest and finished second.

5152.headline: Sonic wins while the writeup becomes a Street Fighter ranking
5152.narrative: Sonic's easy win receives little attention because the writeup mostly turns into a lengthy ranking and discussion of Street Fighter IV characters.

5153.headline: Caim turns a routine Dracula win into a futility record
5153.narrative: Dracula won as expected and Lucina took second, while Caim produced a historically weak last-place showing. The writeup treats Caim's tiny support as the only memorable feature of the match.

5154.headline: Barret wins while Final Fantasy VII decline worsens
5154.narrative: Barret won the three-way poll, but looked alarmingly weak against Professor Layton and Reimu before recovering with the Final Fantasy VII daytime vote. The writeup treats the result as another clear sign of franchise-wide FFVII decline.

5155.headline: Phoenix Wright dispatches Marth and sheds the joke label
5155.narrative: Phoenix Wright beat Marth and Nightmare without the close fight many had anticipated. The writeup uses the result to argue that Phoenix had fully outgrown his old joke-character status.

5156.headline: Vincent wins but exposes deeper Final Fantasy VII decline
5156.narrative: Vincent won but performed far below what his old contest strength suggested against KOS-MOS and Dunban. The writeup sees the result as another unmistakable sign that Final Fantasy VII had fallen sharply.

5157.headline: Mewtwo crushes while Chester becomes a Board 8 record
5157.narrative: Mewtwo delivered the round's largest blowout, but the writeup focuses on Board 8 mascot Chester deliberately becoming a historic futility benchmark. Chester's last-place finish is celebrated as the intended joke rather than treated as a failed campaign.

5158.headline: The Boss wins as Heavy finishes last again
5158.narrative: The Boss won and Chrom took second without either position being seriously threatened, while Heavy finished last yet again. The writeup treats the result as another reminder that Team Fortress characters had never translated their popularity into contest strength.

5159.headline: Sub-Zero's classic look helps sink Garrus
5159.narrative: Sub-Zero beat Garrus in a result the writeup finds disappointing given Mass Effect's broader strength that year. Garrus still looked respectable, while Sub-Zero's showing reinforced his status as the stronger Mortal Kombat contest character.
5159.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly credits Sub-Zero's classic-costume picture with helping him, saying the old look made him substantially more dangerous in the matchup.

5160.headline: Bowser SFFs Meta Knight in another bad draw
5160.narrative: Bowser won comfortably while Meta Knight again failed to get a clean read because of Nintendo overlap. Archer's respectable showing is treated more as a byproduct of the bad setup than as evidence of major strength.
5160.anomaly_note: The writeup says Meta Knight was once again being SFFed in a first-round Nintendo matchup, this time under Bowser.

5161.headline: Sephiroth wins while Final Fantasy VII decline deepens
5161.narrative: Sephiroth won easily, but Midna and Little Mac still held up far better than the writeup thought should be possible against a former champion. The match is framed as another unmistakable sign of Final Fantasy VII decline.

5162.headline: Morrigan punishes another overthought upset pick
5162.narrative: Morrigan comfortably beat Edgeworth and Agent 47 despite substantial pre-match support for an upset. The writeup treats her win as another example of people underrating a long-established midcard character.

5163.headline: Spyro crushes Clementine and the Walking Dead hype
5163.narrative: Spyro crushed a heavily debated field and made the Clementine upset case look badly overhyped. The writeup treats the result as early proof that recent Western-game buzz was translating poorly into character-contest strength.

5164.headline: A routine Luigi win becomes an FFXII digression
5164.narrative: After noting Luigi's completely routine win, the writeup mostly digresses into discussion of Final Fantasy XII and Beyond Good & Evil.

5165.headline: Big Boss dominates as Viridian surprises Peacock
5165.narrative: Big Boss dominated while Captain Viridian unexpectedly took second in the Expert Challenge ordering over Peacock. The writeup treats the lower-place upset as a minor curiosity beside Big Boss's overwhelming showing.

5166.headline: Ness dismisses the Locke upset case quickly
5166.narrative: Ness beat Locke without the trouble some expected from Old Square's recent improvement. The writeup uses the result to argue that Final Fantasy VI characters without Dissidia exposure still lacked meaningful contest strength.

5167.headline: Elizabeth wins after a brief Poison rally
5167.narrative: Elizabeth won and Poison took second in an otherwise settled match, while Thrall disappointed again. The only meaningful disturbance was a short-lived 4chan push for Poison.
5167.anomaly_note: The writeup says Poison received an early 4chan rally that produced one large cut before the push faded and stopped affecting the match.

5168.headline: Terra shines while Peach drains Kirby's support
5168.narrative: Kirby won, but Terra's performance was the surprise as she benefited from Peach draining Nintendo support from Kirby. The writeup treats Terra's Dissidia-era strength as increasingly legitimate.
5168.anomaly_note: The writeup says Peach LFFed Kirby, helping Terra look unusually strong against him. It also explicitly calls Kirby's simple spherical design a major picture advantage.

5169.headline: Crash upsets Wheatley and earns a rare contest moment
5169.narrative: Crash finally produced another memorable contest win by upsetting Wheatley after years of mostly losing early. Tommy Vercetti's weak last-place showing is treated as further proof that Grand Theft Auto characters had collapsed.

5170.headline: Snake opens with a statement and fuels title talk
5170.narrative: Snake delivered a dominant opening and immediately looked more dangerous than Link had in his own first-round match. The writeup treats the performance as serious evidence that Snake could contend for the contest if the bracket broke correctly.

5171.headline: Alucard survives Falcon in the first true photo finish
5171.narrative: Captain Falcon built a substantial early lead, but Alucard erased it overnight and then survived an unexpectedly weak Nintendo daytime response. The narrow finish became the contest's first true photo finish and one of its most entertaining early matches.

5172.headline: Bayonetta dispatches N and punctures Pokefear
5172.narrative: Bayonetta comfortably beat N and Wander in a matchup many had overcomplicated because of Pokémon fear. The writeup treats the result as a straightforward victory for the most recognizable and currently relevant entrant.

5173.headline: GLaDOS restores Portal pride after Wheatley's flop
5173.narrative: GLaDOS crushed Cole and Ragna after Wheatley's earlier flop, reinforcing the writeup's view that Portal's character strength was concentrated heavily in GLaDOS herself. The match otherwise generated little suspense.

5174.headline: Ike barely holds off an unexpectedly strong Proto Man
5174.narrative: Ike narrowly held off Proto Man in a slow-moving fight that never quite became a full comeback. The writeup treats Proto Man's performance as unexpectedly strong and Ike's as a major warning sign.

5175.headline: Epona turns years of nomination campaigning into a win
5175.narrative: Epona won comfortably over Mordin and Niko after years of Board 8 nomination campaigning finally put the horse into the bracket. The writeup treats the result as a harmless payoff to an old community joke rather than a serious L-Block successor.

5176.headline: Shulk hype collapses despite the Monado picture
5176.narrative: Altair won while Ratchet beat a heavily hyped Shulk for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup notes that even Shulk's best-possible presentation could not rescue the Xenoblade hype.

5177.headline: The Tomb Raider reboot revives Lara's contest strength
5177.narrative: Lara Croft delivered her strongest-looking contest performance in years after the series reboot, while Slime took second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup treats Lara's resurgence as the main surprise.

5178.headline: Kefka trolls the bracket with another impossible-looking upset
5178.narrative: Kefka upset both Zack and Ryu Hayabusa in a result that wrecked the prevailing guru logic and continued his reputation for producing bizarre contest outcomes. The writeup credits Dissidia and improved presentation as plausible background factors without declaring a picture anomaly here.

5179.headline: Cloud wins big and still looks worryingly weak
5179.narrative: Cloud won the expected blowout, but the writeup still considered the performance too weak for a former top-tier character facing extreme fodder. The match becomes another warning about Final Fantasy VII's decline.

5180.headline: Viewtiful Joe surprises Handsome Jack behind Frog
5180.narrative: Frog won easily while Viewtiful Joe unexpectedly beat Handsome Jack for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The result gave Joe a rare positive contest moment and undercut the broader Borderlands character hype.

5181.headline: Lugia turns Pokefear into another blowout
5181.narrative: Lugia crushed Sly and York far more decisively than some expected, reinforcing the contest-wide fear of Pokémon strength. Sly's second-place Expert Challenge finish is treated as a small consolation after years away from the bracket.

5182.headline: Dante wins big but nobody trusts the blowout
5182.narrative: Dante routed Laharl and Raz, but the writeup refused to read much into another first-round blowout because Dante had repeatedly looked strong before later choking. The entire match is framed around the coming Squirtle test.

5183.headline: Squirtle makes Dante's next match look dangerous
5183.narrative: Squirtle beat Ramza comfortably enough to make the upcoming Dante matchup look dangerous immediately. The writeup treats the result as another piece of evidence that Pokémon strength was surging across the bracket.

5184.headline: Ridley earns respect behind a routine Zidane win
5184.narrative: Zidane won while Ridley took second in the Expert Challenge ordering and performed more respectably than his old contest history suggested. The Board 8 joke entrant Spring Breeze Dancin' finished last as expected.

5185.headline: Shadow wins a weak field without much drama
5185.narrative: Shadow beat Yu and Kat in a weak field that the writeup considered far less debatable than pre-match Pokémon-style fear had made it seem. The result gave Shadow a rare clean contest win without saying much about his broader strength.

5186.headline: Leon SFFs Wesker in a brutal same-series draw
5186.narrative: Leon won a badly drawn same-series match that effectively denied Wesker a fair first-round opportunity. Even under severe overlap, Wesker still beat Oliver for second in the Expert Challenge ordering.
5186.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Wesker was heavily SFFed by fellow Resident Evil entrant Leon, leaving Wesker far weaker than his standalone strength.

5187.headline: Gordon cruises as Hades fails to threaten Simon
5187.narrative: Gordon Freeman won comfortably, while Simon Belmont held second despite an unpopular match picture and pre-match fears of a Hades upset. The writeup treats Hades's failure as an early warning for the Kid Icarus cast.

5188.headline: A dog picture helps Missile embarrass Kerrigan
5188.narrative: The writeup is mostly an enormous StarCraft and Blizzard rant; the actual match is remembered for Missile unexpectedly taking second over Kerrigan behind a highly favorable cute-dog presentation.
5188.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Missile's cute-dog presentation the ultimate picture factor and treats it as part of why he could beat Kerrigan.

5189.headline: Lloyd barely survives Big Daddy behind Pikachu
5189.narrative: Pikachu had first place secured, but Lloyd and Big Daddy produced a genuine photo finish for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Lloyd's early lead survived a slow Big Daddy comeback by the narrowest margin.

5190.headline: Magus finally wins a debated matchup cleanly
5190.narrative: Magus finally won a heavily debated match by beating Otacon and Jade comfortably enough to make the pre-match panic look excessive. The writeup treats the victory as rare positive news in Magus's long history of contest disappointments.

5191.headline: Sora handles Scorpion in a routine three-way
5191.narrative: Sora beat Scorpion and Aya without any meaningful suspense, and the writeup dismisses speculation that Aya would drain enough Square support to matter. The match is mostly treated as a routine Kingdom Hearts win.

5192.headline: Gilgamesh crushes Booker and starts the division chaos
5192.narrative: Gilgamesh demolished the heavily favored Booker DeWitt and turned the division into an upset zone immediately. The writeup treats Booker's collapse as another example of recent Western protagonists failing badly in character contests.

5193.headline: Yoshimitsu and Lu Bu both embarrass Groose
5193.narrative: Yoshimitsu stunned the heavily favored Groose, while Lu Bu also passed the Zelda entrant for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup celebrates the result as a Board 8-friendly rejection of Zelda name recognition.

5194.headline: Game & Watch beats Lee despite Meat Boy vote drain
5194.narrative: Mr. Game & Watch upset Lee Everett despite sharing part of his natural novelty audience with Meat Boy. The writeup treats the result as another example of recent Western-game popularity failing to translate into character-contest votes.
5194.anomaly_note: The writeup says Meat Boy's similar oddball appeal stole support from Game & Watch, and argues that Game & Watch would have beaten Lee much more decisively without him.

5195.headline: Nathan Drake survives Pac-Man with help from Steve's vote drain
5195.narrative: Nathan Drake survived a long, slow fight with Pac-Man, while Steve's presence is blamed for helping keep Pac-Man from completing the upset. The result stayed close enough to preserve Pac-Man's reputation as a dangerous wildcard.
5195.anomaly_note: The writeup says Steve stole votes from Pac-Man through similar broad casual appeal and argues that Pac-Man likely wins the matchup without Steve in the poll.

5196.headline: Blue beats Fox in a heavily distorted Nintendo matchup
5196.narrative: Pokémon Trainer Blue beat Fox even though Wolf created what many expected to be a highly favorable Nintendo-overlap setup. The writeup's larger point is that Blue's strength remained hard to read because the bracket handed him such unusual conditions.

5197.headline: Sandbag survives Samus SFF to take second
5197.narrative: Samus dominated as expected, but Sandbag still beat Isaac Clarke for second in the Expert Challenge ordering despite Nintendo overlap. The writeup treats that as another sign of Sandbag's unusually durable joke support.
5197.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Sandbag was SFFed by Samus, making Sandbag's second-place Expert Challenge finish more impressive.

5198.headline: Catherine's picture edge helps her outlast Neku
5198.narrative: Catherine and Neku spent hours trading tiny leads before Catherine finally pulled away late. The upset is presented as a rare fodder match where a cult following and strong presentation combined into a memorable win.
5198.anomaly_note: The writeup says Catherine had a huge picture advantage and later credits her visual appeal as part of why she won the close matchup.

5199.headline: Celes shocks Seifer behind an easy Knuckles win
5199.narrative: Knuckles won as expected, but Celes unexpectedly took second in the Expert Challenge ordering over Seifer. The writeup treats Seifer's collapse as one of the contest's most embarrassing failures of supposedly obvious expert logic.

5200.headline: Bomberman vote drain helps Ezio beat Tails
5200.narrative: Ezio beat Tails and Bomberman after a short early challenge, with the writeup blaming some of Tails's weakness on the similar third entrant. The result also undercut attempts to revive Tails through old extrapolated statistics.
5200.anomaly_note: The writeup says Tails and Bomberman had overlapping appeal and that their shared support helped Ezio pull away after Tails briefly led.

5201.headline: Auron dominates while Ocelot's picture steals the discussion
5201.narrative: Auron dominated Roxas and Ocelot, while the infamous Ocelot picture became the main discussion point despite the writeup explicitly rejecting it as enough to explain the result. Auron's strength is treated as the real story.

5202.headline: The Teemo rally never arrives and L-Block wins
5202.narrative: L-Block won while the expected League of Legends rally for Teemo never materialized, leaving Teemo in last place behind Palutena. The writeup treats the failed rally expectation as the match's defining joke.

5203.headline: Dragonborn wins but Skyrim hype collapses
5203.narrative: Dragonborn won, but performed far below the hype created by Skyrim's enormous popularity. Tom Nook took second in the Expert Challenge ordering, and the writeup immediately downgraded Dragonborn's chances against Tifa.

5204.headline: Yuna hands Master Chief another predictable disappointment
5204.narrative: Yuna beat Master Chief and Claire in a result the writeup says simply felt inevitable given Chief's long history of volatile strength and anti-voting. The match added another disappointment to Halo's contest record.

5205.headline: Tifa dominates while Cirno vote stuffing is removed
5205.narrative: Tifa dominated Chun-Li and Cirno, but the match is remembered mainly for fraudulent Cirno votes being removed. The controversy did not threaten Tifa's overwhelming win.
5205.anomaly_note: The writeup says fraudulent votes were removed from Cirno during the match and attributes the stuffing to a Touhou supporter, while extra notes acknowledge that the identity of the stuffer remained debatable.

5206.headline: Mario looks untouchable immediately before the Vivi shock
5206.narrative: Mario produced a completely routine top-seed blowout over Duke and Fawful, giving no hint that his next match would become one of the contest's major shocks. The writeup is striking mainly in hindsight.

5207.headline: Vivi wins as Marisa vote stuffing disrupts the poll
5207.narrative: Vivi won comfortably over Adam Jensen and Marisa, but the match was repeatedly disrupted by fraudulent votes for Marisa being removed. The writeup treats the cheating as the main story before Vivi's later breakout.
5207.anomaly_note: The writeup says fraudulent Marisa votes were removed both during and after the poll, with the site administrator explicitly announcing the vote stuffing while the match was live.

5208.headline: Guybrush finally succeeds despite removed fraudulent votes
5208.narrative: Ganondorf won easily, while Guybrush finally earned a meaningful contest success by taking second in the Expert Challenge ordering over Max Payne. The removed fraudulent votes tainted the match without changing that placement.
5208.anomaly_note: The writeup says fraudulent votes for Guybrush were removed during the match, while also stating that Guybrush still would have beaten Max Payne without them.

5209.headline: Squall's routine win becomes a Bit.Trip digression
5209.narrative: Squall's easy win mainly served as a strength check before Missingno, while much of the writeup digresses into praise for the Bit.Trip games and Rayman discussion.

5210.headline: Amaterasu dominates one of Round One's dullest matches
5210.narrative: Amaterasu dominated one of the round's dullest matches and looked strong enough to inspire later what-if discussion about a deeper run. Vyse comfortably took second in the Expert Challenge ordering over Adol.

5211.headline: Missingno barely survives Tidus amid rallying and vote stuffing
5211.narrative: Tidus erased a large early deficit, took the lead, and nearly completed one of the contest's biggest upsets before Missingno recovered in the final stretch. The cheating revelation immediately spoiled what had looked like a heroic Tidus near-win.
5211.anomaly_note: The writeup reports a small Reddit rush for Missingno in the final hour. It also quotes SBAllen saying anti-bot measures caught vote stuffing at roughly a two-to-one ratio favoring Tidus.

5212.headline: Wario shuts down MINEFEAR without drama
5212.narrative: Wario dismissed the brief MINEFEAR speculation and won comfortably, while Creeper took second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The King of All Cosmos never became a real factor.

5213.headline: Red combines overwhelming strength with a huge picture advantage
5213.narrative: Pokémon Trainer Red crushed the field and reinforced the sense that he was one of the contest's strongest characters. Corvo took second over Sissel in the Expert Challenge ordering.
5213.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Red's nostalgic match picture a huge and unfair advantage, saying it packed much of the author's childhood into one image.

5214.headline: Wrex shocks Pit and Cecil in a debated three-way
5214.narrative: Wrex upset both Pit and Cecil in one of Round One's most debated three-way matches, surviving a brief Cecil challenge before pulling clear. The writeup celebrates the win as a rare success for a Western character and another disappointment for Final Fantasy IV.

5215.headline: Mega Man absorbs Magikarp's planned rally and cruises
5215.narrative: Mega Man weathered Magikarp's pre-planned push and then dominated, while Geno was crushed into last. The result became the first major test of Mega Man against the contest's Pokémon rally threat.
5215.anomaly_note: The writeup says Magikarp entered the match with a pre-planned rally and briefly stayed even with Mega Man before the favorite pulled away.

5216.headline: A developer rally lifts Recette over Travis
5216.narrative: Kratos won easily, but Recette unexpectedly beat Travis for second in the Expert Challenge ordering after outside support boosted the niche indie character. Travis's comeback attempt never fully recovered the early deficit.
5216.anomaly_note: The writeup says Recette received a small organized push from the game's developer, with possible additional support from 4chan.

5217.headline: Jill crushes the field as Haggar takes second
5217.narrative: Jill dominated as expected, while Mike Haggar comfortably beat Red Bird for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup treats the supposed Marvel-versus-Capcom SFF idea mostly as a joke rather than a serious explanation.

5218.headline: Kratos Aurion barely survives Boko behind Zero
5218.narrative: Zero dominated while Kratos Aurion and Boko spent nearly the entire match in a dead heat for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Kratos survived by only a handful of votes after a photo-finish ending.

5219.headline: Lenneth nearly steals second from Claptrap
5219.narrative: Weighted Companion Cube won as expected, but Lenneth made a surprisingly credible overnight attempt to catch Claptrap for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Borderlands' daytime strength eventually ended the comeback.

5220.headline: Rikku retires another inanimate joke favorite
5220.narrative: Rikku comfortably ended the favorite status built around ?-Block's old bonus-poll reputation. The writeup treats the result as another sign that inanimate joke characters had lost much of their old power.

5221.headline: Zelda rebounds by crushing two Western mascots
5221.narrative: Zelda crushed two Western franchise mascots and looked far healthier than she had in 2010. John Marston took second in the Expert Challenge ordering without ever threatening the winner.

5222.headline: Donkey Kong crushes Lightning as Falco gets SFFed
5222.narrative: Donkey Kong unexpectedly made a supposedly debatable match trivial and punished the heavily disliked Lightning. Falco collapsed under the Nintendo overlap and finished well behind both.
5222.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Falco was SFFed in the Nintendo-heavy match, leaving him far weaker than Donkey Kong.

5223.headline: Charizard closes Round One with a PokéFEAR rout
5223.narrative: Charizard demolished Riku and Nier to close Round One and push PokéFEAR even higher. The writeup treats the match as both a Charizard statement and a fitting end to an overlong opening round.

5224.headline: Chester completes his quest for ultimate last place
5224.narrative: The bonus poll deliberately matched the three weakest Round One entrants, with Chester completing his intended quest to become the contest's ultimate futility benchmark. Caim won the meaningless race at the top.

5225.headline: Link SFFs Yoshi as Raiden takes second
5225.narrative: Link won comfortably while Raiden secured second after Yoshi faded under heavy Nintendo overlap. The writeup also treats Link's low turnout as another sign that voters were tiring of his dominance.
5225.anomaly_note: The writeup says Yoshi tried to resist Link's SFF but could not stay competitive, allowing Raiden to take second in the Expert Challenge ordering.

5226.headline: Shepard comes back and upsets Aeris
5226.narrative: Aeris led for hours before Shepard erased the gap and then pulled away decisively, producing one of the contest's most satisfying upsets for Mass Effect fans. Tharja's presence and Final Fantasy VII anti-voting are discussed as background factors rather than formal anomalies.

5227.headline: League rallying turns Draven into an overwhelming force
5227.narrative: Draven transformed from a low natural share into an overwhelming rally-powered winner over Mega Man X and Ryu. The performance convinced much of Board 8 that he had become a credible threat to win the entire contest.
5227.anomaly_note: The writeup says massive League of Legends rallying turned Draven into an overwhelming force and drove historically enormous vote totals.

5228.headline: Barret barely beats Dracula as FFVII decline deepens
5228.narrative: Sonic cruised while Barret only narrowly separated from Dracula for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The weak Barret showing became another warning that Final Fantasy VII's decline had reached well beyond Cloud.

5229.headline: Vincent's sabotaged picture becomes the match's defining controversy
5229.narrative: Mewtwo won convincingly while Phoenix unexpectedly pushed Vincent into last place. The notorious Vincent picture became one of the contest's biggest presentation controversies and overwhelmed much of the discussion.
5229.anomaly_note: The writeup says Vincent received an intentionally terrible Dirge of Cerberus picture and directly blames the image for worsening his performance enough that Phoenix could pass him.

5230.headline: Sub-Zero outlasts The Boss in a strange trend battle
5230.narrative: Bowser won as expected, but The Boss and Sub-Zero spent most of the match almost perfectly tied for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Sub-Zero unexpectedly won the evening trend and finally pulled away.

5231.headline: Morrigan repeats her old edge over Spyro
5231.narrative: Sephiroth won a routine rematch setting while Morrigan again finished ahead of Spyro, echoing their famous 2002 upset. The writeup finds Sephiroth's modest dominance more notable than the actual ordering.

5232.headline: Ness vote drain helps Big Boss edge Luigi
5232.narrative: Big Boss and Luigi stayed tied for hours before Metal Gear's stronger late trend finally separated them. Ness's presence is treated as the key fanbase drain that prevented Luigi from taking fuller advantage of Big Boss's weak daytime vote.
5232.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ness leeched Luigi's Nintendo support and made the difference in a match where Luigi and Big Boss were otherwise close in strength.

5233.headline: Crash nearly steals second and revives his reputation
5233.narrative: Kirby won comfortably while Crash nearly completed a morning comeback on Elizabeth for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup celebrates the loss as Crash's best contest showing in years and a major warning about BioShock Infinite's strength.

5234.headline: Snake quietly delivers another dominant statement
5234.narrative: Snake crushed Alucard and Bayonetta in a match with almost no suspense. The performance later became important because Snake was one of the few Noble Nine members still looking consistently dominant.

5235.headline: Epona embarrasses Ike behind an easy GLaDOS win
5235.narrative: GLaDOS won easily, but Epona stole the attention by beating an awful Ike for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup treats the result as a fittingly comic high point for Epona and a confirmation of Ike's collapse.

5236.headline: Kefka wins as Altair barely survives Lara
5236.narrative: Kefka completed another bracket-wrecking upset by beating both Altair and Lara, while the two Western icons fought to the final minutes for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Altair barely survived Lara's late comeback.
5236.anomaly_note: The writeup says Altair and Lara likely drained each other through overlapping Western-franchise appeal, helping Kefka dominate while their second-place fight stayed unusually close.

5237.headline: Frog beats Lugia despite Cloud vote drain
5237.narrative: Cloud won comfortably while Frog overcame an early Lugia lead and took second in the Expert Challenge ordering despite sharing some Square support with Cloud. Lugia's collapse weakened the broader PokéFEAR narrative.
5237.anomaly_note: The writeup says Cloud was stealing support from Frog, making Frog's recovery past Lugia more impressive.

5238.headline: Squirtle destroys Dante and the DmC hype
5238.narrative: Squirtle crushed Dante and made the pre-match Dante support look wildly misplaced, while Zidane never seriously threatened either contender. The writeup frames Dante's defeat as the inevitable result of backlash against the DmC reboot.

5239.headline: Leon wins a strange but never truly close match
5239.narrative: Leon beat Gordon and Shadow in a low-turnout match whose trends repeatedly hinted at drama without ever producing a real comeback. The writeup suspects overlap between Leon and Gordon but leaves the explanation uncertain.

5240.headline: Pikachu exploits Crono-Magus SFF and eliminates Crono
5240.narrative: Pikachu decisively eliminated Crono after Magus collapsed under same-series overlap. The result became one of the clearest signs that the old Noble Nine hierarchy no longer controlled the bracket.
5240.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Magus was SFFed into the ground by Crono, giving Pikachu the opening it needed.

5241.headline: Sora cruises through a badly needed breather
5241.narrative: Sora comfortably beat two first-round upset winners in a deliberately uneventful match. The result was interpreted as evidence that he could survive the Pokémon-heavy matchup waiting in Round Three.

5242.headline: Blue turns PokéFEAR into a dominant statement
5242.narrative: Pokémon Trainer Blue dominated Nathan Drake and Mr. Game & Watch, turning earlier PokéFEAR into a concrete strength statement. The writeup treats Blue's performance as proof that he belonged among the contest's serious threats.

5243.headline: Samus stays steady while Catherine validates herself
5243.narrative: Samus overwhelmed Knuckles and Catherine and remained one of the few Noble Nine characters consistently meeting expectations. Catherine's respectable share is treated as proof that her first-round upset was not pure luck.

5244.headline: 4chan rallies L-Block past Auron
5244.narrative: Auron controlled stretches of the match, but 4chan's support repeatedly pulled L-Block back and eventually carried the former champion to another upset. The result revived speculation that L-Block could become an anti-Draven rally vehicle.
5244.anomaly_note: The writeup says 4chan rallied L-Block, repeatedly erasing Auron's small leads before eventually pushing the former champion clear.

5245.headline: Tifa wins as Dragonborn's hype fully collapses
5245.narrative: Tifa won comfortably while Dragonborn again looked far weaker than Skyrim's game-level popularity had suggested. Yuna's respectable third-place showing despite the Square overlap made Dragonborn's collapse look even worse.
5245.anomaly_note: The writeup treats Tifa and Yuna's shared Final Fantasy support as a real vote split, noting that Yuna stayed surprisingly close to Dragonborn even while Tifa was in the poll.

5246.headline: Vivi shocks Mario in a contest-defining upset
5246.narrative: Vivi produced one of the contest's defining upsets by holding off repeated Mario comeback attempts and finally eliminating him. Nintendo vote splitting and a modest outside push helped create the opening, but the writeup still celebrates Vivi's composure against Mario's legendary clutch.
5246.anomaly_note: The writeup says Ganondorf leeched Nintendo support from Mario and that 4chan also rallied Vivi during the close fight.

5247.headline: Squall ends Missingno's comeback hopes cleanly
5247.narrative: Squall absorbed Missingno's expected early surge and took control far sooner than the glitch character's supporters hoped. The result ended Missingno's run and left Squall's division shaped by an awkward future matchup with Vivi.

5248.headline: Red SFFs Wario and clears second for Wrex
5248.narrative: Red dominated while Wrex took advantage of Wario's severe Nintendo overlap to claim second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The result made Wrex's first-round upset look more legitimate.
5248.anomaly_note: The writeup says Red SFFed Wario, allowing Wrex to pass the Nintendo character comfortably for second in the Expert Challenge ordering.

5249.headline: Mega Man cruises as Jill beats a declining Kratos
5249.narrative: Mega Man delivered another clean top-seed performance, while Jill beat the declining Kratos for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. The writeup treats Jill's placement as an upset only by seed rather than by actual strength.

5250.headline: Zero wins as Rikku retires another joke contender
5250.narrative: Zero won easily while Rikku gradually pulled away from Weighted Companion Cube for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Strategic Mega Man fans voting away from Zero are discussed, but the outcome was never in doubt.

5251.headline: Charizard rallies past Zelda in a Pyrrhic victory
5251.narrative: Zelda repeatedly looked on the verge of beating Charizard, but Pokémon's morning strength and late outside support dragged Charizard through a final-update escape. The writeup treats the win as a major warning that Charizard had been overrated.
5251.anomaly_note: The writeup says Donkey Kong's presence created heavy Nintendo vote splitting that badly hurt Charizard. It also says late rallies were necessary for Charizard to erase Zelda's lead and survive.

5252.headline: Mario settles the Crono debate in a bonus rematch
5252.narrative: Mario comfortably settled the old rivalry with Crono in a bonus poll despite the presence of Mega Man X. The writeup treats the result as final confirmation that their classic debate was long over.
5252.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mega Man X stole votes from Mario and also notes some SNES-era overlap around Crono, with Mario believed to be hurt more by the third entrant.

5253.headline: Draven survives Link in a rally-fueled contest landmark
5253.narrative: Draven built a huge rally-driven lead, Link mounted two enormous comeback pushes, and a lengthy site slowdown became the center of a bitter controversy before Draven survived. The writeup treats the match as one of the most consequential and divisive events in GameFAQs contest history.
5253.anomaly_note: The writeup describes enormous organized rallies for both Draven and Link throughout the match. It also alleges obvious late vote stuffing from Link's side, while quoting SBAllen's analysis that found no evidence of massive systematic stuffing overall.

5254.headline: Rally spillover helps Mewtwo crush Sonic
5254.narrative: Mewtwo crushed Sonic in a result made even more shocking by Sonic's failure to mount his usual daytime comeback. The win turned Mewtwo into the preferred anti-Draven hope for the remainder of the contest.
5254.anomaly_note: The writeup says rally spillover from the Link-Draven battle materially boosted Mewtwo, with Zen arguing that Sonic probably wins without that outside support.

5255.headline: Sephiroth stops Kirby after a long early deadlock
5255.narrative: Sephiroth survived an expected Kirby upset attempt after a long early deadlock, then unexpectedly dominated the morning and daytime vote. The writeup treats the result as a rare 2013 case where a Final Fantasy VII heavyweight reasserted himself.

5256.headline: Snake cruises as GLaDOS barely survives Kefka
5256.narrative: Snake won easily while GLaDOS and Kefka spent nearly the entire match in an extraordinarily tight fight for second in the Expert Challenge ordering. GLaDOS finally survived by only a tiny margin after repeated lead changes.

5257.headline: Squirtle topples Cloud as Leon drains support
5257.narrative: Squirtle beat Cloud outright in one of the contest's coolest Noble Nine upsets, surviving Cloud's overnight recovery and pulling away again late. The writeup emphasizes that Cloud's broader Final Fantasy VII decline made the impossible-looking result suddenly believable.
5257.anomaly_note: The writeup says Leon's overlapping PlayStation-oriented support hurt Cloud and played an important role in opening the door for Squirtle's upset.

5258.headline: Pikachu survives Blue's vote drain and Sora's comeback
5258.narrative: Pikachu built a large lead, survived Sora's late comeback, and won despite sharing the poll with Pokémon Trainer Blue. The result sent another Pokémon character into the contest's final stretch and underscored how little strength Sora had left.
5258.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Pikachu resisted Blue's LFF and that the second Pokémon entrant was the main reason Sora could keep the match competitive.

5259.headline: Samus cruises through the quietest divisional final
5259.narrative: Samus controlled the simplest divisional final, with Tifa quickly taking second in the Expert Challenge ordering and L-Block never recreating its old magic. The writeup treats the match as a rare breather in an otherwise chaotic stretch.

5260.headline: Vivi rides his momentum past Squall
5260.narrative: Red won comfortably, but Vivi's momentum carried him past Squall for second in the Expert Challenge ordering after the Mario upset. The writeup treats Vivi's placement as one of the contest's strangest strength reversals.

5261.headline: Mega Man rallies past Charizard despite Zero vote drain
5261.narrative: Mega Man survived both Zero's overlap and Charizard's late lead, then completed a furious final push to take the match. The writeup remembers the finish as the long-awaited close-match breakthrough for a character with years of contest heartbreak.
5261.anomaly_note: The writeup says Zero clearly drained Mega Man through their heavy overlap. It also describes a massive late Mega Man fan rally that overturned Charizard's lead in the final minutes.

5262.headline: Draven's restored rally wipes out Mewtwo's lead
5262.narrative: Mewtwo looked ready to win while the League rally was offline, but Draven surged back the moment outside support returned. The match became one of the clearest demonstrations of how completely rally access controlled Draven's run.
5262.anomaly_note: The writeup says Draven's Reddit rally was briefly removed, allowing Mewtwo to build a large lead, then returned and erased that lead almost immediately.

5263.headline: Pokémon vote splitting hands Snake an easy path
5263.narrative: Snake advanced to the final while the two Pokémon entrants split their shared fanbase and fought over second in the Expert Challenge ordering. Pikachu ultimately beat Squirtle after the morning vote.
5263.anomaly_note: The writeup says Squirtle and Pikachu cannibalized each other's Pokémon support, destroying their chances of challenging Snake for first.

5264.headline: Samus survives Mega Man in a Nintendo-heavy semifinal
5264.narrative: Mega Man briefly led and genuinely threatened Samus, but Samus eventually took control and won the semifinal. Red remained competitive enough to finish a strong contest run despite the Nintendo-heavy field.
5264.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly attributes the result to Mega Man's heavy Nintendo-adjacent overlap in a match with Samus and Red.

5265.headline: Mega Man wins as the Pokémon pair suppress each other
5265.narrative: Mega Man won the bonus as Mewtwo and Pikachu split Pokémon support. Mewtwo nevertheless beat Pikachu in their internal comparison, adding another wrinkle to the series hierarchy.
5265.anomaly_note: The writeup says the two Pokémon entrants heavily suppressed each other, allowing Mega Man to win the bonus match comfortably.

5266.headline: Draven's Reddit rally overwhelms Snake in the final
5266.narrative: Snake closed most of Draven's lead with celebrity-backed support before a much larger Reddit surge ended the comeback and delivered Draven the championship. The writeup treats the final as the culmination of the contest's rally controversy.
5266.anomaly_note: The writeup says rallies determined the championship: David Hayter helped Snake mount a comeback, then a large Reddit push for Draven overwhelmed him and decided the result.

5267.headline: Link restores order in the post-contest bonus
5267.narrative: Link beat Snake in the post-contest bonus despite several Snake cuts, giving GameFAQs a more traditional closing matchup after the Draven controversy. The writeup treats Link's win as clear but notes that Snake still looked unusually strong.

6051.headline: Chrono Trigger opens 2015 in championship form
6051.narrative: Chrono Trigger opened the 2015 game contest with a far stronger blowout than many expected and immediately looked like a true title contender. The writeup treats the result as the first major sign that older games would dominate the bracket.

6052.headline: Dragon Quest VIII extends the second-match curse
6052.narrative: Dragon Quest VIII overturned the prevailing Persona 3 lean after an initially close start and gradually pulled away. The writeup folds the upset into Board 8's long-running joke that the second match of a contest is cursed.

6053.headline: Mega Man X dismisses the Batman hype
6053.narrative: Mega Man X won a debated 12-over-5 matchup far more comfortably than Batman supporters expected. The writeup treats the result as another failure of licensed-game hype to translate into contest strength.

6054.headline: Final Fantasy X wins while Chrono Trigger looks stronger
6054.narrative: Final Fantasy X handled Half-Life without suspense, but looked much less impressive than Chrono Trigger had in the same division. The writeup treats that comparison as the first clear warning for their coming matchup.

6055.headline: Melee handles Portal without revealing much
6055.narrative: Melee beat Portal comfortably in an otherwise uneventful opener, with its usual early strength followed by percentage bleed. The writeup says the result gave little hint of how badly a later Chrono Trigger matchup would go.

6056.headline: Pokémon GSC crushes The World Ends With You
6056.narrative: Pokémon Gold and Silver overwhelmed The World Ends With You in one of the round's cleanest blowouts. The writeup treats the result mainly as confirmation that GSC remained a major Pokémon game on the site.

6057.headline: Kingdom Hearts II exposes Metal Gear Solid 4 decline
6057.narrative: Kingdom Hearts II beat Metal Gear Solid 4 decisively and immediately established the latter as part of a broader Metal Gear decline. The writeup views the result as a major reversal from MGS4's stronger reputation in earlier years.

6058.headline: The Last of Us adds to Halo's contest misery
6058.narrative: The Last of Us doubled Halo 3 in a straightforward blowout. The writeup treats Halo's poor showing as another chapter in the series' long history of underperforming on GameFAQs.

6059.headline: Final Fantasy VI announces the Year of the 90s
6059.narrative: Final Fantasy VI crushed Assassin's Creed II and looked dramatically stronger than its older comparison with Wind Waker. The writeup treats the performance as early proof that 1990s Square games were operating on another level.

6060.headline: Paper Mario survives Tales without a true photo finish
6060.narrative: Paper Mario built an early advantage over Tales of Symphonia and never truly surrendered control despite several small cuts. The writeup calls it the contest's first close-looking match, though the result felt decided well before the finish.

6061.headline: KOTOR wins while Xenogears finally shows hidden strength
6061.narrative: KOTOR beat Xenogears in a debated matchup, but Xenogears stayed close enough to suggest it had more hidden strength than its old bad draws implied. The writeup argues that reversed seeding might even have changed the result.

6062.headline: Wind Waker advances without resolving the Final Fantasy VI debate
6062.narrative: Wind Waker beat Pokémon X/Y comfortably, while the writeup rejects the idea that Pokémon suffered meaningful SFF here. The result kept Wind Waker respectable but still left Final Fantasy VI favored for the next round.

6063.headline: Smash 4 crushes Planescape in a routine opener
6063.narrative: Smash 4 crushed the obscure Planescape: Torment and looked like a legitimate modern Smash entry rather than a repeat of Brawl's stigma. The writeup treats the match itself as essentially content-free.

6064.headline: Mass Effect outlasts Galaxy 2 in the first true thriller
6064.narrative: Mass Effect erased Galaxy 2's early lead, spent hours in a deadlock, then pulled away during the afternoon. The writeup remembers it as the contest's first genuine close match and a major embarrassment for the Board 8 consensus.

6065.headline: Halo stops Minecraft before the feared rally can begin
6065.narrative: Halo held Minecraft to a steady loss and prevented the rally-driven title run many bracketmakers had feared. The writeup notes that people correctly anticipated an outside-rally threat in the contest, but targeted the wrong game.

6066.headline: Final Fantasy VII opens with a championship-level rout
6066.narrative: Final Fantasy VII demolished Journey and looked every bit like a championship contender. The writeup treats the blowout as a welcome return to straightforward elite-level dominance.

6067.headline: Mario 3 opens with one of the contest's biggest blowouts
6067.narrative: Super Mario Bros. 3 delivered one of the contest's largest blowouts, exactly as expected from a top seed against weak opposition. The writeup notes with hindsight that this would be Mario 3's only win of the contest.

6068.headline: Pokémon RBY beats Tetris without the expected SFF
6068.narrative: Pokémon RBY beat Tetris comfortably, but many observers wrongly interpreted the margin through old Nintendo SFF comparisons. The writeup explicitly argues that Pokémon showed little or no SFF here and was stronger than the raw comparison suggested.

6069.headline: Sonic 2 pulls away from Portal 2
6069.narrative: Sonic 2 turned an early deadlock with Portal 2 into a comfortable win and overturned the pre-match favorite. The writeup treats it as another example of Portal 2 lacking the original game's old internet buzz.

6070.headline: Uncharted 2 routs another weak licensed-game entry
6070.narrative: Uncharted 2 doubled The Walking Dead in a matchup the writeup considered predictable from the start. The result is used mainly to argue that licensed popularity rarely translates into GameFAQs contest strength.

6071.headline: Undertale spillover exposes Fallout 3's rally vulnerability
6071.narrative: Fallout 3 was cruising on the release day of Fallout 4 until Undertale rally spillover suddenly made Life is Strange much stronger. The winner remained safe, but the late bleed exposed how vulnerable Fallout could be to outside traffic.
6071.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's simultaneous outside rally spilled into this poll and directly shifted votes toward Life is Strange, sharply reducing Fallout 3's percentage without threatening the result.

6072.headline: Undertale rallies from a massive deficit to win
6072.narrative: Undertale transformed a routine loss into the largest comeback in contest history once outside support arrived late in the day. The win launched the rally-driven run that would eventually decide the entire tournament.
6072.anomaly_note: The writeup says a massive outside rally erased Mass Effect 3's enormous late lead and carried Undertale to a record-setting comeback.

6073.headline: Final Fantasy VIII wins with a small rally-spillover boost
6073.narrative: Final Fantasy VIII beat Vice City as expected, while the simultaneous Undertale rally nudged the result further toward Square. The writeup treats Vice City's respectable loss as one of the few less embarrassing GTA performances.
6073.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale rally spillover also affected this simultaneous poll, modestly boosting Final Fantasy VIII against Vice City.

6074.headline: Animal Crossing surges on Undertale rally spillover
6074.narrative: Super Mario World began with an enormous rout, but Animal Crossing suddenly gained ground once Undertale's outside rally flooded the simultaneous polls. The result stayed a blowout, yet the spillover showed how dramatically shared traffic could distort percentages.
6074.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale rally spillover strongly boosted Animal Crossing late in the match, producing unusual cuts against Super Mario World.

6075.headline: Phoenix briefly leads Skyrim on rally spillover
6075.narrative: Phoenix Wright briefly led behind Board 8 support and Undertale spillover, but Skyrim recovered and eventually won comfortably. Even with the distorted opening, the writeup considered Skyrim's performance too weak for a serious title contender.
6075.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale rally spillover favored Phoenix Wright from the opening minutes and helped create an early lead before Skyrim recovered.

6076.headline: GoldenEye beats Diablo II in a debated old-school matchup
6076.narrative: GoldenEye beat Diablo II in a debated 8/9 matchup and continued the broader old-game advantage of the contest. The writeup notes possible minor rally spillover but treats it as too uncertain to explain the win.

6077.headline: Metroid Prime wins while exposing its daytime weakness
6077.narrative: Metroid Prime beat Morrowind but lost substantial ground over the course of the day. The writeup treats the trend as an early warning that Prime's weak daytime vote could become costly in close matches.

6078.headline: Half-Life 2 advances through a routine setup match
6078.narrative: Half-Life 2 handled Demon's Souls in a largely trendless and predictable match. The writeup mainly uses the result to set up the expected Metroid Prime rematch in Round Two.

6079.headline: Mario 64 demolishes Mario Kart 8
6079.narrative: Super Mario 64 crushed Mario Kart 8 and looked like a serious deep-run threat. Although one analysis calls the result an SFF beating, the other explicitly doubts meaningful SFF, so the writeup ultimately leaves the mechanism uncertain.

6080.headline: Final Fantasy Tactics wins a debated matchup comfortably
6080.narrative: Final Fantasy Tactics beat Resident Evil 2 in a debated matchup that became comfortable almost immediately. The writeup also treats Resident Evil's loss as part of a broader series decline.

6081.headline: Twilight Princess wins but loses its Mario 64 hype
6081.narrative: Twilight Princess crushed Skies of Arcadia in a predictable opener, but the result did little to sustain upset hopes against Mario 64. The writeup instead uses the match to compare Twilight Princess with Wind Waker.

6082.headline: Persona 4 crushes 999 without needing SFF
6082.narrative: Persona 4 destroyed 999 and made the weaker visual novel look like one of the bracket's lowest-tier entrants. The writeup explicitly rejects SFF as an explanation and treats 999 as simple fodder.

6083.headline: Ocarina obliterates Hearthstone in a legendary blowout
6083.narrative: Ocarina of Time produced one of the contest's legendary blowouts against Hearthstone and showed no vulnerability to the rally threat some had feared. The result looked like a championship statement at the time.

6084.headline: Suikoden II settles an overdebated 8/9 matchup
6084.narrative: Suikoden II won a heavily debated 8/9 matchup that the writeup retrospectively treats as much simpler than people made it. The result becomes another example of old Japanese RPG familiarity beating a newer unknown.

6085.headline: Okami comfortably sends Warcraft III home
6085.narrative: Okami beat Warcraft III comfortably and continued its unusual history of avoiding extreme 1v1 results in either direction. The writeup treats the result as another failure for Blizzard's contest strength.

6086.headline: Final Fantasy IX defies the trends and upsets Kingdom Hearts
6086.narrative: Final Fantasy IX upset Kingdom Hearts after surviving the matchup phase where Kingdom Hearts was normally strongest. The writeup treats the trend reversal as a major surprise and evidence of an FFIX boost.

6087.headline: DKC2 survives Xenoblade in a wire-to-wire classic
6087.narrative: Donkey Kong Country 2 and Xenoblade traded tiny leads for most of the day before DKC2 finally held on through a record-setting wire-to-wire close match. The upset ruined a popular Xenoblade deep-run pick and gave DKC2 long-overdue contest respect.

6088.headline: Awakening destroys Mario Maker's rally-and-meme hype
6088.narrative: Fire Emblem Awakening demolished Super Mario Maker in a matchup many expected to be close. The writeup calls Mario Maker one of the contest's biggest disappointments and treats the result as a complete collapse of its rally-and-meme hype.

6089.headline: Banjo wins while its deep-run hype evaporates
6089.narrative: Banjo-Kazooie beat Baldur's Gate II but bled enough support to kill most hopes of a deeper run. The writeup sees the win as disappointing rather than validating old theories that Banjo had hidden strength.

6090.headline: Symphony of the Night announces itself with a rout
6090.narrative: Symphony of the Night crushed Trials and Tribulations and clearly separated itself from the crowded midcard pack in its section. The writeup treats the blowout as the strongest first-round showing among the division's plausible contenders.

6091.headline: A Link to the Past delivers another Zelda godstomp
