6091.narrative: A Link to the Past delivered the second-largest blowout of the contest against Cave Story and looked like a genuine top-tier game. The writeup places the result alongside Ocarina's as a championship-caliber Zelda statement.

6092.headline: Final Fantasy IV dispatches Deus Ex without drama
6092.narrative: Final Fantasy IV turned a matchup the writeup considered completely noncompetitive into an easy rout of Deus Ex. The commentary also celebrates FFIV's durability and laments that its next draw prevented a more informative contest run.

6093.headline: Metal Gear Solid V wins but badly disappoints
6093.narrative: Metal Gear Solid V beat Perfect Dark but looked far weaker than expected for a recent mainline Metal Gear release. The writeup treats the result as another sign that the series had declined rather than received the hoped-for boost.

6094.headline: Dark Souls opens strongly and targets Metal Gear
6094.narrative: Dark Souls comfortably doubled Civilization V and immediately looked capable of exploiting Metal Gear Solid V's weakness in the next round. The writeup treats the showing as an impressive debut for a recent game.

6095.headline: Super Metroid delivers a shocking first-round rout
6095.narrative: Super Metroid demolished Call of Duty 4 far more severely than expected and transformed its contest reputation overnight. The writeup treats the performance as evidence of both Call of Duty decline and a major Super Metroid resurgence.

6096.headline: Galaxy wins while Super Metroid steals the spotlight
6096.narrative: Super Mario Galaxy handled Dragon Age about as expected, but Super Metroid's simultaneous blowout made the win look ordinary by comparison. The writeup immediately shifted the next-round favorite toward Super Metroid.

6097.headline: Final Fantasy XII uses nostalgia to beat Bloodborne
6097.narrative: Final Fantasy XII beat the newer Bloodborne in a matchup the writeup uses as another example of nostalgia overpowering recent-game acclaim. The result also continued the perfect first-round run for Final Fantasy entries.

6098.headline: Majora's Mask cruises through an unfortunate bracket path
6098.narrative: Majora's Mask crushed Valkyria Chronicles in a routine top-seed blowout and largely matched its prior contest reputation. The writeup's main complaint is that the bracket wasted Majora by placing it near another Zelda heavyweight.

6099.headline: Grand Theft Auto V wins and still gets exposed
6099.narrative: Grand Theft Auto V beat Shenmue but looked embarrassingly weak for a top seed against such limited opposition. The writeup treats the result as immediate confirmation that GTA5 was doomed in Round Two.

6100.headline: Super Mario RPG beats Oblivion and seizes the division
6100.narrative: Super Mario RPG won a heavily debated matchup with Oblivion and became the clear favorite to escape the surrounding eightpack. Its severe overnight percentage bleed is attributed to the game's historically poor European availability rather than a real comeback.

6101.headline: San Andreas wins while GTA decline becomes comical
6101.narrative: San Andreas beat Shovel Knight but again looked far too weak for a major Grand Theft Auto title. The writeup treats the result as another clear demonstration of the site's long-running anti-GTA sentiment.

6102.headline: Chrono Cross humiliates World of Warcraft
6102.narrative: Chrono Cross comfortably upset World of Warcraft despite overwhelming casual confidence in WoW. The writeup celebrates the result as an expert-friendly rejection of casual brand recognition and a perfect bracket break for Chrono Cross.

6103.headline: The Witcher 3 opens with rare modern-game strength
6103.narrative: The Witcher 3 crushed The Binding of Isaac and looked unusually strong for a current-year release. The writeup also flags the game's known rally potential as a future threat, but no rally was needed in this match.

6104.headline: Metal Gear Solid 2 wins without looking convincing
6104.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 2 beat Resident Evil but bled support throughout the match and continued the series' disappointing contest. The result made the coming Witcher 3 matchup look much more dangerous than expected.

6105.headline: Fallout 4 momentum carries New Vegas past BioShock Infinite
6105.narrative: Fallout: New Vegas beat BioShock Infinite in a matchup the writeup felt had been settled by fresh Fallout 4 attention and BioShock's weaker sequel reputation. The result stayed close enough to be respectable but never looked like an upset.

6106.headline: Resident Evil 4 wins with an early warning sign
6106.narrative: Resident Evil 4 beat Paper Mario but lost enough support to create an immediate warning about its deeper prospects. The writeup uses comparisons with other Mario RPGs to argue that RE4 already looked weaker than its prior contest form.

6107.headline: Metal Gear Solid becomes the series' lone bright spot
6107.narrative: Metal Gear Solid crushed Splatoon and became the only Metal Gear entry the writeup thought looked genuinely solid in Round One. The result offered a brief exception to the series-wide decline narrative.

6108.headline: EarthBound finally breaks out by crushing Borderlands 2
6108.narrative: EarthBound overturned the Board 8 favorite and crushed Borderlands 2, finally translating its cult reputation into a meaningful contest win. The writeup treats the result as one of the clearest signs of the contest's enormous SNES and nostalgia boost.

6109.headline: Shadow of the Colossus revives its upset reputation
6109.narrative: Shadow of the Colossus demolished Team Fortress 2 and revived memories of its earlier deep run. The writeup immediately began looking ahead to whether it could again challenge Metal Gear opposition.

6110.headline: Red Dead Redemption restores order against Bayonetta 2
6110.narrative: Red Dead Redemption beat Bayonetta 2 comfortably after the writeup had overthought the possibility of a Wii U upset. The result validated RDR as a legitimate midcard game while further embarrassing the Wii U.

6111.headline: Metal Gear Solid 3 wins an embarrassing blowout
6111.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 beat Mother 3 by a wide margin but still performed far below what the writeup expected against a Japan-only title. The result became another major warning that the entire Metal Gear series had weakened.

6112.headline: BioShock advances while Silent Hill earns some respect
6112.narrative: BioShock beat Silent Hill 2 in a straightforward matchup, though Silent Hill performed better than its old contest history suggested. The win set up a more interesting test against a vulnerable Metal Gear Solid 3.

6113.headline: StarCraft crushes Destiny and revives its old menace
6113.narrative: StarCraft destroyed Destiny far more decisively than expected and suddenly looked capable of threatening Mass Effect 2. The writeup treats the blowout as a welcome revival for a game with an old rally-driven contest legacy.

6114.headline: Mass Effect 2 closes Round One with an easy rout
6114.narrative: Mass Effect 2 demolished Virtue's Last Reward in the final match of Round One. The blowout itself was routine, but the writeup saw StarCraft and Metal Gear Solid 3 as meaningful threats waiting in the division.

6115.headline: Chrono Trigger enters god mode against Dragon Quest VIII
6115.narrative: Chrono Trigger annihilated Dragon Quest VIII and produced one of the rare post-opening-round blowouts of this scale. Both analyses explicitly resist treating SFF as the main explanation and instead frame Chrono Trigger as operating at elite strength.

6116.headline: Mega Man X exposes a badly weakened Final Fantasy X
6116.narrative: Final Fantasy X beat Mega Man X but looked disastrously weak relative to expectations, while Mega Man X exited with its reputation greatly improved. The result effectively ended belief that FFX could stop Chrono Trigger.

6117.headline: Melee's rally turns a safe win into a statement
6117.narrative: Melee was already winning comfortably when its fanbase began a successful rally that inflated the final result. The writeup later treats this as an early trial run for the far larger Melee rallying still to come.
6117.anomaly_note: The writeup says Melee fans organized a noticeable rally despite already leading comfortably, boosting Melee substantially over its natural level against Pokémon GSC.

6118.headline: Kingdom Hearts II handles a respectable Last of Us
6118.narrative: Kingdom Hearts II beat The Last of Us comfortably and removed any realistic thought of an upset. The writeup still credits The Last of Us with impressive strength for a recent, original franchise.

6119.headline: Final Fantasy VI cruises toward the Wind Waker test
6119.narrative: Final Fantasy VI handled Thousand-Year Door exactly as expected in a largely uneventful setup match. The writeup immediately turns toward the much more meaningful Wind Waker comparison waiting next.

6120.headline: Wind Waker beats KOTOR without settling the FFVI debate
6120.narrative: Wind Waker beat KOTOR by roughly the margin expected and did little to settle the upcoming debate with Final Fantasy VI. The writeup treats the result as useful mainly because the next match remained genuinely uncertain.

6121.headline: Smash 4 survives a respectable Mass Effect challenge
6121.narrative: Smash 4 beat Mass Effect in a respectable but unspectacular result for both games. The writeup sees the Wii U title as legitimately strong, while Mass Effect's loss still validated its prior upset of Galaxy 2.

6122.headline: Final Fantasy VII crushes Halo and restores title confidence
6122.narrative: Final Fantasy VII crushed Halo and produced what the writeup considers its strongest natural performance of the contest. The result briefly restored championship confidence before the rally-driven chaos of later rounds.

6123.headline: Undertale spillover turns Pokémon's win into a rout
6123.narrative: Pokémon RBY was already beating Mario 3 before outside traffic arrived, but Undertale spillover transformed the result into a rout. The writeup treats the natural matchup as a legitimate Pokémon win and the final margin as heavily distorted.
6123.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's outside rally spilled into this simultaneous poll and heavily boosted Pokémon RBY, turning an already likely Pokémon win into a much larger blowout.

6124.headline: Sonic 2 wins big with a small rally boost
6124.narrative: Sonic 2 was already winning decisively before the simultaneous rally traffic arrived, then gained a few more points from spillover. The writeup treats the underlying result as a genuine old-games victory rather than a rally-created upset.
6124.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale rally spillover modestly favored Sonic 2 over Uncharted 2, making an already comfortable Sonic win somewhat larger.

6125.headline: Undertale rallies from a huge deficit to beat Fallout 3
6125.narrative: Fallout 3 looked safe for most of the match before Undertale's rally transformed the poll into a historic comeback and then a decisive win. The result launched the rally momentum that would dominate the rest of the contest.
6125.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's massive outside rally erased Fallout 3's huge lead in only a few hours and continued accelerating after taking first.

6126.headline: Rally spillover boosts Mario World before the Undertale showdown
6126.narrative: Super Mario World was already controlling Final Fantasy VIII before rally spillover made the margin substantially larger. The result fueled enormous anticipation for Mario World's coming encounter with Undertale.
6126.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's simultaneous rally traffic heavily favored Super Mario World, inflating an already comfortable win over Final Fantasy VIII.

6127.headline: Skyrim shuts down the GoldenEye upset talk
6127.narrative: Skyrim produced its strongest performance of the contest by comfortably beating GoldenEye and silencing the upset murmurs created by its weak opener. The writeup notes that this match was notably unaffected by rally spillover.

6128.headline: Metroid Prime wins the Half-Life rematch decisively
6128.narrative: Metroid Prime decisively won its rematch with Half-Life 2 and erased the memory of their much closer earlier contest meeting. The result established Prime as a credible threat to Skyrim in the next round.

6129.headline: Mario 64 crushes Tactics but shows one small crack
6129.narrative: Super Mario 64 crushed Final Fantasy Tactics, though its percentage bleed gave a small opening for later Twilight Princess speculation. The writeup otherwise treats Mario 64 as the obvious division heavyweight.

6130.headline: Twilight Princess routs Persona but still trails Mario 64
6130.narrative: Twilight Princess doubled Persona 4 and exceeded its old Game of the Decade comparison. The result validated Persona somewhat while still leaving the writeup convinced Mario 64 was far stronger.

6131.headline: Ocarina wins while Zelda fatigue finally surfaces
6131.narrative: Ocarina of Time beat Suikoden II but looked shockingly weak for the site's traditional top game. The writeup interprets the performance as the first strong evidence of widespread anti-Zelda voting and contest fatigue.

6132.headline: Final Fantasy IX confirms its modern strength
6132.narrative: Final Fantasy IX beat Okami comfortably enough to confirm its modern rise in strength, while Okami again avoided being completely blown out. The result sent FFIX into Round Three with more credibility than in older contests.

6133.headline: DKC2 survives Awakening and keeps the miracle run alive
6133.narrative: Donkey Kong Country 2 survived another close match, this time against Fire Emblem Awakening, and continued one of the contest's most unexpected runs. The writeup explicitly frames DKC2 as resisting the Nintendo SFF reputation rather than suffering from it.

6134.headline: Symphony of the Night dismisses the Banjo hype
6134.narrative: Symphony of the Night handled Banjo-Kazooie comfortably despite some pre-match upset buzz. The writeup treats the result as another demonstration of how much internet respect the Castlevania classic had accumulated.

6135.headline: Link to the Past wins but fuels Zelda-fatigue concerns
6135.narrative: A Link to the Past beat Final Fantasy IV easily, but the writeup still considered the performance too ordinary for a championship favorite. The result joins Ocarina's showing as evidence of growing Zelda fatigue.

6136.headline: Dark Souls ends Metal Gear Solid V quietly
6136.narrative: Dark Souls comfortably eliminated Metal Gear Solid V and confirmed that the new Metal Gear entry had never gained meaningful contest strength. The writeup treats Dark Souls as a rare modern game capable of surviving NostalgiaFAQs.

6137.headline: Super Metroid breaks the Mario hierarchy
6137.narrative: Super Metroid crushed Super Mario Galaxy and finally broke the long-standing expectation that Metroid would collapse against Mario. The writeup treats this as a landmark result that ended much of the site's belief in automatic Mario dominance.

6138.headline: Majora's Mask becomes Zelda's Round Two bright spot
6138.narrative: Majora's Mask handled Final Fantasy XII easily and became the only Zelda entry the writeup thought looked genuinely strong in Round Two. The result largely validated its prior Game of the Decade strength.

6139.headline: Super Mario RPG knocks out top-seeded GTA V
6139.narrative: Super Mario RPG beat the top-seeded GTA V exactly as Board 8 expected, turning casual bracket confidence into another easy target. The writeup treats the upset as obvious to experts despite the seeding.

6140.headline: Chrono Cross humiliates San Andreas and casual brackets
6140.narrative: Chrono Cross comfortably upset San Andreas and completed a second straight demolition of casual-favored opponents. The writeup attributes the result to GTA's severe anti-voting and Chrono Cross receiving the perfect bracket path.

6141.headline: MGS2 survives the Witcher rally that never happened
6141.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 2 narrowly beat The Witcher 3 despite widespread attempts by Witcher fans to attract outside support. The writeup stresses that the hoped-for developer rally never materialized, making the result a case study in how difficult successful rallying can be.

6142.headline: Resident Evil 4 wins but reveals a warning sign
6142.narrative: Resident Evil 4 beat New Vegas comfortably, but both analyses retrospectively treat the result as the first real warning that RE4 had lost strength. Fallout 4 hype made New Vegas look stronger, which helped hide the warning at the time.

6143.headline: EarthBound makes Metal Gear Solid look badly weakened
6143.narrative: Metal Gear Solid advanced, but EarthBound came much closer than the writeup thought a former top-tier game should allow. The result reinforced the contest-wide impression that Metal Gear had declined while EarthBound had gained real strength.

6144.headline: Shadow wins while rally spillover slightly helps Red Dead
6144.narrative: Shadow of the Colossus won comfortably and revived memories of its earlier Metal Gear upset run. Red Dead Redemption's respectable showing was helped slightly by rally spillover, but the next-round Shadow-versus-Metal-Gear debate remained intact.
6144.anomaly_note: The writeup says Red Dead Redemption received a small boost from the simultaneous StarCraft and Mass Effect 2 rallies, slightly improving its showing without threatening Shadow of the Colossus.

6145.headline: BioShock rallying turns an MGS3 win into an embarrassment
6145.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 built an early lead, then spent most of the match unable to extend it as BioShock's rally support surged. MGS3 survived, but the unusually close finish became another major warning about Metal Gear's strength.
6145.anomaly_note: The writeup says BioShock was boosted by both direct rallying and spillover from the StarCraft-Mass Effect rally war, allowing it to run even with Metal Gear Solid 3 for much of the day.

6146.headline: Mass Effect 2 wins a full-scale rally war with StarCraft
6146.narrative: StarCraft seemed to have revived its old rally magic before Mass Effect 2 answered with an even stronger counter-push. The repeated swings made this one of the round's best matches and ended with Mass Effect 2 winning the rally war.
6146.anomaly_note: The writeup describes a sustained rally war: StarCraft first erased Mass Effect 2's lead, then Mass Effect 2 counter-rallied and eventually pulled away after its subreddit allowed rally threads.

6147.headline: Chrono Trigger annihilates Final Fantasy X and looks elite
6147.narrative: Chrono Trigger destroyed Final Fantasy X in a matchup that had been heavily debated before the contest. The blowout erased old concerns about Chrono Trigger's decline and made it look like the strongest game on the site without outside intervention.

6148.headline: Melee advances but looks doomed against Chrono Trigger
6148.narrative: Melee beat Kingdom Hearts II as expected, but bled enough support to look doomed against the newly dominant Chrono Trigger. The writeup also notes that the Melee rally from the previous round did not return here.

6149.headline: Final Fantasy VI finally beats Zelda in a debated match
6149.narrative: Final Fantasy VI won a debated matchup with Wind Waker without ever facing a sustained comeback. The result became a rare modern example of Final Fantasy beating Zelda in a close-looking contest matchup and validated FFVI's stronger 2015 form.

6150.headline: Final Fantasy VII crushes Smash 4 and restores its aura
6150.narrative: Final Fantasy VII crushed Smash 4 and looked far stronger than Final Fantasy VI had in the neighboring match. The writeup treats the result as decisive evidence that FFVI was not going to win their coming same-series showdown.

6151.headline: Rally spillover amplifies Pokémon's already dominant Sonic rout
6151.narrative: Pokémon RBY was already routing Sonic 2 before Undertale rally spillover pushed the result even higher. The underlying blowout made Pokémon look like a true title contender even after separating out the outside traffic.
6151.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's simultaneous rally traffic spilled into the Pokémon poll and further boosted Pokémon RBY beyond an already dominant natural performance.

6152.headline: Undertale rallies past Super Mario World and survives controversy
6152.narrative: Super Mario World built the expected early advantage, but Undertale's rally started earlier than in prior rounds and eventually overwhelmed it. The match also produced a major cheating scare that the writeup says was unsupported.
6152.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's expanding social-media rallies steadily erased Super Mario World's lead and eventually carried Undertale comfortably ahead. Cheating accusations are explicitly rejected by the administrator.

6153.headline: Skyrim overcomes a spillover-boosted Metroid Prime lead
6153.narrative: Metroid Prime built a large early lead, then Skyrim used its stronger morning and daytime trends to erase it and win. The writeup treats Prime's familiar trend collapse as the decisive factor after an opening aided partly by rally spillover.
6153.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale rally spillover helped Metroid Prime's unusually strong opening and boosted turnout, although Prime's normal early strength also contributed.

6154.headline: Mario 64 overcomes Zelda's rally and picture advantages
6154.narrative: Twilight Princess looked unusually competitive at the start, but Mario 64 recovered and settled into a comfortable win. The writeup attributes much of Zelda's early strength to rally spillover and the lopsided match pictures.
6154.anomaly_note: The writeup says Twilight Princess benefited early from Undertale rally spillover and from a major picture imbalance: Mario 64 received a poor image while Twilight Princess received an especially strong Link image.

6155.headline: A bad picture adds to Ocarina's warning signs
6155.narrative: Ocarina of Time won easily but again looked weaker than expected for the site's traditional top game. Final Fantasy IX's strong showing, aided by the picture matchup, became another warning that Ocarina was vulnerable later.
6155.anomaly_note: The writeup directly blames Ocarina of Time's weak-looking performance in part on a poor Ocarina picture paired against one of Final Fantasy IX's best possible images.

6156.headline: Symphony ends Donkey Kong Country 2's Cinderella run
6156.narrative: Symphony of the Night decisively ended Donkey Kong Country 2's surprise run once the low seed finally met a proven heavyweight. The writeup still considers DKC2's overall contest a major success.

6157.headline: Link to the Past crushes Dark Souls without Zelda fatigue
6157.narrative: A Link to the Past crushed Dark Souls and looked largely immune to the Zelda fatigue affecting other entries in the series. The writeup treats the dominant result as evidence that LTTP remained a genuine elite game.

6158.headline: Majora survives Super Metroid in a pure contest classic
6158.narrative: Super Metroid and Majora's Mask traded tiny leads for hours before Majora finally pulled away with the later vote. Both analyses remember it as one of the contest's best pure matches, notably without rally controversy.

6159.headline: Super Mario RPG keeps its miracle run alive
6159.narrative: Super Mario RPG beat Chrono Cross comfortably and continued a run that had exceeded almost every pre-contest expectation. Chrono Cross still earned respect by keeping the result more respectable than many of Mario RPG's earlier opponents.

6160.headline: Resident Evil 4 wins while another warning sign flashes
6160.narrative: Resident Evil 4 beat Metal Gear Solid 2 without danger but again landed far below the strength expected of it. The result made Super Mario RPG look increasingly likely to take the division.

6161.headline: Metal Gear Solid finally stops Shadow of the Colossus
6161.narrative: Metal Gear Solid survived the feared rematch with Shadow of the Colossus and never allowed another Cinderella upset to develop. The writeup treats the result as a welcome piece of redemption for an otherwise poor Metal Gear contest.

6162.headline: A powerful Big Boss picture helps MGS3 rout Mass Effect
6162.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 unexpectedly routed Mass Effect 2 after most predictions had expected a very close match. The writeup gives major credit to MGS3's exceptionally strong picture and treats the win as the series' best result of the contest.
6162.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Metal Gear Solid 3's excellent Big Boss image was the real reason it performed so strongly, calling it one of the best possible pictures for the game.

6163.headline: Melee rallies past Chrono Trigger and changes the contest
6163.narrative: Chrono Trigger looked ready to crush Melee until Smash fans mobilized across Reddit, social media and community sites. The rally flipped the match and stopped each comeback, ending Chrono Trigger's apparent path toward the championship.
6163.anomaly_note: The writeup says a rapidly spreading Smash community rally erased Chrono Trigger's large early lead and repeatedly countered every later Chrono comeback attempt.

6164.headline: Melee rally spillover amplifies Final Fantasy VII's series win
6164.narrative: Final Fantasy VI's early board-vote resistance quickly disappeared as Final Fantasy VII took control. Spillover from the Melee rally widened an already likely FFVII win and erased hopes based on an earlier non-contest poll.
6164.anomaly_note: The writeup says the simultaneous Melee rally favored Final Fantasy VII over Final Fantasy VI and amplified FFVII's existing lead, helping turn the match into a larger rout.

6165.headline: Undertale wins a massive rally war against Pokémon
6165.narrative: Pokémon RBY appeared to have finally stopped Undertale after building a massive lead while matching its early rallying. A sudden late social-media flood then overwhelmed Pokémon and turned the match into one of Undertale's defining comebacks.
6165.anomaly_note: The writeup describes a full rally war: Pokémon built a huge lead with its own outside support, then an enormous late Undertale Twitter surge erased the deficit and reversed the match.

6166.headline: Rally spillover boosts Mario 64 in an easy Skyrim win
6166.narrative: Super Mario 64 beat Skyrim comfortably while the neighboring rally war boosted Mario's support. The match remained stable despite the outside traffic and ended Skyrim's respectable run.
6166.anomaly_note: The writeup says the simultaneous Pokémon-Undertale rally traffic favored Super Mario 64 and inflated its showing against Skyrim, even though it did not change the winner.

6167.headline: Ocarina routs Symphony but still looks a step slow
6167.narrative: Ocarina of Time routed Symphony of the Night in the divisional final, but still looked weaker than historical comparisons suggested. The writeup explicitly says rally spillover had virtually no effect here.

6168.headline: Link to the Past overcomes Majora's early rally surge
6168.narrative: Majora's Mask rode spillover and presentation advantages to a large early lead, but A Link to the Past slowly erased it and won with the morning vote. The match became a clear demonstration of how quickly rally spillover could fade.
6168.anomaly_note: The writeup says rally spillover from the previous Undertale-Pokémon match strongly favored Majora's Mask early. It also says Majora had a clear picture advantage over A Link to the Past.

6169.headline: Super Mario RPG completes its breakout over Resident Evil 4
6169.narrative: Super Mario RPG completed its breakout by decisively upsetting Resident Evil 4 after several rounds of RE4 warning signs. The writeup treats the win as the payoff to Mario RPG's nostalgia-driven run and Resident Evil's decline.

6170.headline: Metal Gear Solid 3 wins the long-awaited series showdown
6170.narrative: Metal Gear Solid 3 narrowly beat the original Metal Gear Solid in the long-awaited intra-series comparison. The writeup celebrates the close but stable result as a rare feel-good moment in an otherwise disappointing contest for the franchise.

6171.headline: Melee rallies past Final Fantasy VII in a major reversal
6171.narrative: Final Fantasy VII briefly led, but Melee's outside support quickly took control and turned the quarterfinal into a comfortable upset. The result reversed their old hierarchy and ended Final Fantasy's main title hopes.
6171.anomaly_note: The writeup says Melee's community rally engine took over after Final Fantasy VII's brief early lead and then drove the rest of the match decisively toward Melee.

6172.headline: Undertale rallies through repeated Mario 64 resistance
6172.narrative: Mario 64 repeatedly fought Undertale back into a close match, but every meaningful threat triggered another surge of outside Undertale support. Undertale eventually pulled clear and continued toward the semifinal.
6172.anomaly_note: The writeup says Undertale's rally erased Mario 64's early lead within hours and repeatedly answered Mario whenever he briefly retook control. Simultaneous Melee rallying may also have helped Mario somewhat.

6173.headline: Ocarina beats Link to the Past without the expected SFF
6173.narrative: Ocarina of Time beat A Link to the Past, but failed to produce the devastating same-series suppression many expected from their old four-way comparison. Both analyses conclude that little or no meaningful SFF was visible in the current match.

6174.headline: Super Mario RPG completes its miracle semifinal run
6174.narrative: Super Mario RPG ended Metal Gear Solid 3's run and completed an improbable trip to the semifinals. The writeup treats the victory as the culmination of a huge nostalgia-driven bandwagon rather than a picture-driven result.

6175.headline: Undertale survives Melee in an enormous rally-war classic
6175.narrative: Melee and Undertale mobilized massive outside communities and produced one of the highest-profile matches in site history. Undertale finally won the rally war after repeated swings, while a caught botting attempt added another layer of controversy.
6175.anomaly_note: The writeup describes an enormous two-sided rally war between Undertale and Melee. It also quotes the administrator saying an attempted automated vote-stuffing operation for Melee was caught and its fraudulent votes ignored.

6176.headline: Ocarina ends Super Mario RPG's miracle run
6176.narrative: Ocarina of Time demolished Super Mario RPG in a semifinal that everyone expected to be one-sided. Early spillover inflated turnout but did not create a meaningful competitive effect, and Mario RPG's miracle run ended quietly.

6177.headline: Undertale's internet rally overwhelms Ocarina in the final
6177.narrative: Undertale's rally had reached full internet scale by the championship, and Ocarina never mounted a serious challenge. The writeup frames the blowout as the crowning of a new contest paradigm and the completion of Undertale's historic run.
6177.anomaly_note: The writeup says broad internet attention and Undertale's massive outside support overwhelmed Ocarina of Time from the opening moments, turning the final into a one-sided coronation.

6178.headline: Melee takes third place in a quiet bonus poll
6178.narrative: Melee easily beat Super Mario RPG in the third-place bonus poll, with almost no movement across the day. The writeup treats the result as a useful but low-stakes validation of Melee's strong contest form.

6179.headline: Chrono Trigger comfortably wins the fallen-seeds bonus
6179.narrative: Chrono Trigger comfortably beat Final Fantasy VI in a bonus matchup between fallen top seeds. The writeup specifically notes that the result did not look like the massive SFF beating one might expect from two closely related Square classics.

6180.headline: Pokémon beats Mario 64 and strengthens its elite case
6180.narrative: Pokémon RBY beat Super Mario 64 in a bonus poll pairing two games previously eliminated by Undertale. The result strengthened the writeup's belief that Pokémon had become stronger than any of the major Mario games.

6181.headline: Ocarina beats Final Fantasy VII again in the bonus
6181.narrative: Ocarina of Time again beat Final Fantasy VII in their recurring bonus rivalry, and the gap continued moving in Zelda's favor. The writeup treats the result as another painful marker of FFVII's long-term decline.

6686.headline: 2009 wins the first wildcard amid historically low turnout
6686.narrative: The first wildcard poll produced extremely low turnout and an entirely predictable win for 2009 over 1979. The writeup focuses on how weak the contest's vote totals had become and on the new head-to-head play-in format.

6687.headline: 1989 dispatches 1983 in another predictable wildcard
6687.narrative: 1989 comfortably eliminated 1983 in another predictable wildcard matchup. The writeup frames 1983 primarily through the North American video-game crash and finds little competitive case for it.

6688.headline: 2006 escapes a wildcard it never should have needed
6688.narrative: 2006 easily beat 1981, and the writeup argues that 2006 never belonged in a wildcard poll at all. It still gives 1981 credit for an unusually strong arcade lineup built around games such as Donkey Kong, Ms. Pac-Man and Galaga.

6689.headline: 2005 crushes an underappreciated 1978 wildcard
6689.narrative: 2005 crushed 1978 in the final wildcard matchup, though the writeup argues that 1978 deserved more respect for foundational arcade games such as Space Invaders and Breakout. The scale of the blowout reinforced how poor the play-in seeding was.

6690.headline: 1995 opens the bracket with a record blowout
6690.narrative: 1995 opened the main bracket with the contest's largest blowout over 1986. The writeup treats 1995 as an exceptionally deep year led by Chrono Trigger, Yoshi's Island and EarthBound, while also lamenting very low turnout and the use of American release dates.

6691.headline: 1987 SFFs 1985 through the old Zelda-Mario hierarchy
6691.narrative: 1987 beat 1985 decisively, with the writeup reducing the matchup to the site's familiar Zelda-over-Mario fanbase hierarchy. It still gives 1985 considerable sentimental credit for Super Mario Bros., Duck Hunt and Oregon Trail.
6691.anomaly_note: The writeup says 1987's Zelda-centered strength SFFed the Mario-centered 1985 side, treating the matchup as effectively Zelda 1 versus Mario 1.

6692.headline: A stacked 2001 overwhelms 2014
6692.narrative: 2001 demolished 2014 behind a lineup the writeup considers overwhelmingly deeper, including Melee, Final Fantasy X, Metal Gear Solid 2 and many other major releases. The commentary finds little reason to regard 2014 as competitive.

6693.headline: 2008 comfortably wins the late-2000s matchup
6693.narrative: 2008 beat 2009 with a lineup the writeup considers clearly stronger, led by Brawl, Metal Gear Solid 4 and Fallout 3. Most of the commentary is a retrospective on notable releases from the two years rather than any uncertainty about the result.

6694.headline: 1997's depth overwhelms a top-heavy 1999
6694.narrative: 1997 comfortably beat 1999 because the writeup sees it as having far greater depth beyond its marquee releases. Final Fantasy VII, Symphony of the Night, GoldenEye and Star Fox 64 gave 1997 too many major anchors for 1999 to match.

6695.headline: 2007 beats a weak and rehash-heavy 2012
6695.narrative: 2007 beat 2012 in a matchup the writeup views as more an indictment of 2012 than a celebration of 2007. Portal, BioShock, Mass Effect and several other strong releases gave 2007 enough depth to win comfortably.

6696.headline: The picture format reveals 2000's superior depth
6696.narrative: The writeup says the rotating-picture format made year depth much more important than expected and turned the author's original 1990 pick into an obvious mistake. Most of the commentary then celebrates the unusually deep lineup and personal memories attached to 2000.

6697.headline: 1996 advances behind a few heavyweight classics
6697.narrative: 1996 is portrayed as a thin year carried by a few excellent games, while 1989 is described as even weaker outside Mega Man 2. The writeup is especially personal, using Mario RPG and Diablo as anchors for memories tied to the year.

6698.headline: 1991 crushes a surprisingly weak 1988
6698.narrative: The writeup finds the scale of 1991's win surprising because much of its lineup looks mid-tier outside Super Mario World. It treats 1988 as an awkward year of sequels and experiments that was far weaker than the Zelda name alone might imply.

6699.headline: The match becomes an anti-Warcraft 3 rant
6699.narrative: The writeup is mostly an extended anti-Warcraft 3 and anti-2002 rant, with only a brief argument that 2010 had the better overall lineup.

6700.headline: 1994 punishes casual faith in 2004
6700.narrative: The writeup calls this the first match where casual brackets were badly burned, with 2004 inflated by World of Warcraft and other mainstream names. It treats 1994 as vastly deeper and more aligned with GameFAQs tastes.

6701.headline: 2011 wins the first genuinely competitive year matchup
6701.narrative: A debated matchup stayed competitive early before 2011 took control and pulled away. The writeup argues that 2011 was simply the deeper and better year despite 2006's Zelda and Kingdom Hearts headliners.

6702.headline: 1998 opens like the obvious contest favorite
6702.narrative: 1998 is presented as the overwhelming contest favorite and treated as championship caliber from its first appearance. The writeup deliberately saves most of its 1998 retrospective for the final while giving 1993 credit for several beloved cult games.

6703.headline: 1992 kills the feared 2016 rally before it can start
6703.narrative: The writeup uses 2016 as an example of why rally potential depends heavily on bracket placement, arguing that no outside push could realistically save it here. It then frames 1992's lineup, led by A Link to the Past and Sonic 2, as overwhelming.

6704.headline: 2003 settles a heavily debated year matchup
6704.narrative: A heavily debated year matchup became straightforward once 2003 established control. The writeup says a mainline console Zelda title gave 2003 the decisive edge over 2013's strong but less imposing lineup.

6705.headline: 2005 ends 2015's rally hopes and a miserable round
6705.narrative: The feared Undertale rally never mattered because 2015 was immediately placed against a year the writeup considered much stronger. The result closes an opening round the author regards as one of the least entertaining in contest history.

6706.headline: 1995 advances with a major warning sign
6706.narrative: 1995 advanced but looked far too weak for the overall top seed, stalling for hours against 1987 before finally separating. The writeup treats this as the point where its anticipated showdown with 2001 stopped looking competitive.

6707.headline: 2001 keeps Blowout City rolling
6707.narrative: 2001 crushed a 2008 lineup the writeup considered legitimately solid, reinforcing how extreme the contest's round-to-round blowouts had become. The result also made the coming 2001-versus-1995 matchup look heavily tilted toward 2001.

6708.headline: 1997 looks like a title contender against 2007
6708.narrative: 1997's rout looked like a championship-quality performance at the time and seemed to set up a serious challenge to 1998. In hindsight, the writeup treats the result more as evidence that 2007 was unusually weak.

6709.headline: Picture selection costs 2000 a fair fight
6709.narrative: The match stayed close overnight before 1996 pulled away once the morning vote arrived. The writeup considers the final result tainted by a picture policy that failed to represent 2000's strongest possible lineup.
6709.anomaly_note: The writeup says 2000 was effectively denied a fair chance because Pokémon GSC was omitted from its match picture while 1996 received an unusually strong set of representative games. It explicitly argues that the picture imbalance likely decided the match.

6710.headline: 1991 survives but loses its upset case
6710.narrative: 1991's weak performance against 2002 immediately damaged the author's upset hopes for its next match. The writeup argues that the contest's year format had made normal transitive strength comparisons almost useless.

6711.headline: 1994 makes the 1991 debate look one-sided
6711.narrative: 1994 comfortably beat 2011 and looked substantially stronger than 1991 had in the neighboring matchup. The writeup treats the result as confirmation that their next-round debate was already effectively settled.

6712.headline: 1998 demolishes 1992 and seizes the championship
6712.narrative: 1998 demolished a year centered on A Link to the Past and produced what the writeup calls the best performance of the round. The result is treated as conclusive evidence that only a major rally could stop 1998 from winning the contest.

6713.headline: 2003 advances directly into the 1998 buzzsaw
6713.narrative: 2003 handled a matchup some had worried about and advanced without serious danger. The writeup mostly uses the result to emphasize how hopeless 2003 looked against 1998 in the next round.

6714.headline: 2001 wins a fair fight against fading 1995
6714.narrative: 1995 briefly made its matchup with 2001 look like a classic before 2001 began pulling away and never looked back. The writeup explicitly calls it a fair fight and rejects picture excuses for the result.

6715.headline: 1997 keeps looking like a finalist
6715.narrative: 1997 crushed 1996 and appeared almost as dominant as 1998, making a 1997-versus-1998 final feel inevitable. The writeup stresses how impressive such a blowout looked this deep in the bracket.

6716.headline: Missing console pictures taint 1994's win over 1991
6716.narrative: 1991 won the opening board vote and then was steadily run over by 1994. The writeup's main story is anger that system releases were omitted from a contest supposedly about entire gaming years.
6716.anomaly_note: The writeup argues that excluding console launches from every match picture unfairly hurt 1991 in particular because the Super Nintendo was one of its strongest assets. It says 1994 may still have won, but the picture policy made the matchup fundamentally unfair.

6717.headline: 1998 SFFs 2003 into the ground
6717.narrative: 1998 produced another enormous late-round blowout and made 2003 look completely outclassed. The writeup treats the result as the year-contest equivalent of a dominant same-fanbase Zelda matchup.
6717.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly likens 1998's rout of 2003 to a Zelda SFF beating, with Ocarina of Time effectively suppressing a Wind Waker-centered year.

6718.headline: 2001 shocks 1997 in an inexplicable semifinal upset
6718.narrative: 2001 pulled off what the writeup considers one of the most inexplicable non-rally upsets in contest history. After a long early struggle, 2001 controlled both the overnight and daytime portions and never allowed 1997 a real comeback.

6719.headline: 1998 cruises through a predictable semifinal
6719.narrative: 1998 comfortably eliminated 1994 in a semifinal that was notable mainly for how predictable the contest had become. The writeup uses the result to compare late-round blowout records rather than to describe any real competitive drama.

6720.headline: 1998 closes the contest with a historic championship rout
6720.narrative: 1998 ended the contest with a historically dominant championship performance and completed the run the writeup had expected from the start. The analysis turns into a long celebration of the year's unusually deep lineup and of many beloved games finally being attached to a contest winner.

7238.headline: Dante opens comfortably but looks weak for the top seed
7238.narrative: Dante won the opening matchup comfortably but failed to look as overwhelming as the writeup expected from the contest's top overall seed. Cuphead's respectable showing is treated as evidence that the indie newcomer was underseeded rather than truly dangerous.

7239.headline: Lightning crushes Chloe and ends the second-match paranoia
7239.narrative: Lightning turned a match that had generated second-match paranoia into an immediate blowout. The writeup treats Chloe as likely bottom-tier fodder and says the result did little to prove Lightning had genuinely recovered.

7240.headline: Chun-Li survives Spyro without any Jug Factor
7240.narrative: Chun-Li beat Spyro in a debated matchup, but Spyro stayed competitive enough to validate his recent nostalgia-driven recovery. The writeup explicitly rejects the old Jug Factor as the reason for the result.

7241.headline: Ganondorf opens with a huge Zelda-era statement
7241.narrative: Ganondorf crushed Neku far more severely than expected and immediately looked like the division favorite. The writeup treats the result as an early sign that Zelda, Switch and Smash hype would dominate the contest.

7242.headline: Vivi stays strong while Square collapses around him
7242.narrative: Vivi handled Yu Narukami in a routine blowout and stood out as one of the few Final Fantasy characters still retaining old strength. The writeup mentions possible Square overlap only as an uncertainty rather than a confirmed explanation.

7243.headline: Aya Brea crushes the Victor Sullivan debate
7243.narrative: Aya Brea turned a heavily debated matchup into a stable, comfortable win over Victor Sullivan. The writeup treats the result as another example of 1990s GameFAQs nostalgia beating a newer Western series.

7244.headline: Donkey Kong wins the battle of legendary chokers
7244.narrative: Donkey Kong demolished Tidus in a matchup built around two characters with long reputations for choking. The writeup attributes the result to Donkey Kong's renewed relevance, broader Nintendo momentum and Tidus's continued decline.

7245.headline: Leon opens strongly against Dragonborn
7245.narrative: Leon comfortably beat Dragonborn and looked strong enough to justify confidence in a deep run. Dragonborn's large recovery over the day is treated as a trend quirk rather than a meaningful threat.

7246.headline: Zero wins while Primrose earns a little respect
7246.narrative: Zero handled Primrose in a routine top-seed matchup, though the writeup gives Primrose credit for avoiding a complete collapse. Any possible benefit from the simultaneous Monika rally is described as unclear.

7247.headline: Knuckles beats Zidane with help from rally spillover
7247.narrative: Knuckles crushed a matchup many experts had favored Zidane to win and extended his remarkable history of first-round success. Rally spillover from the neighboring Monika poll is treated as an extra tailwind, not the sole reason for the upset.
7247.anomaly_note: The writeup says the simultaneous Monika rally brought in outside voters who disproportionately favored Knuckles, with one analysis explicitly saying Square was hurt by the spillover.

7248.headline: Master Hand humiliates Noctis in a debated matchup
7248.narrative: Master Hand crushed Noctis in a matchup that had been treated as a true tossup beforehand. The writeup sees the result as one of the clearest signs that modern Final Fantasy had fallen badly while Smash-era Nintendo strength had risen.

7249.headline: Monika rallies but never seriously threatens Wario
7249.narrative: Monika drew the outside support many bracketmakers feared, but Wario remained safely in control throughout. The writeup treats the failed upset as evidence that small fandom rallies were much less dangerous under the contest's anti-rally setup.
7249.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Monika received a real Reddit and community rally, visible in the higher turnout and several stalls or small cuts, but that the push was far too weak to threaten Wario.

7250.headline: Yoshi crushes Shantae and starts a fodder argument
7250.narrative: Yoshi delivered the expected blowout over Shantae, but the match sparked a disproportionate argument over whether Shantae had any meaningful contest strength. The writeup ultimately treats her as ordinary fodder with a dedicated niche fanbase.

7251.headline: Velvet gives Tales a rare clean character win
7251.narrative: Velvet turned a mildly debated matchup with James Sunderland into an easy win and gave the Tales series a rare character-contest victory. The writeup mentions recognizability and presentation as possible helpers but still treats the result as fundamentally legitimate.

7252.headline: Pikachu announces himself as a near-elite threat
7252.narrative: Pikachu overwhelmed a stable measuring-stick opponent in Scorpion and immediately looked near-elite. The writeup treats the result as the first major evidence that Pokémon, and Pikachu specifically, would be a serious force in the contest.

7253.headline: Kratos SFFs John Marston in a huge statement
7253.narrative: Kratos produced by far one of the strongest performances of his contest career while Marston looked far weaker than his game-level popularity suggested. The writeup attributes much of the gap to same-audience suppression.
7253.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Kratos's unusually large win over John Marston SFF, arguing that two similar Western tough-guy fanbases overlapped heavily and that the stronger, more established Kratos suppressed Marston.

7254.headline: Sora wins but immediately looks vulnerable
7254.narrative: Sora won easily but failed the writeup's real test: looking strong enough for a top seed before the coming Red matchup. Ryo's modest resistance immediately became another warning sign for Sora's familiar pattern of high seeding and underachievement.

7255.headline: Red crushes Neptune and puts Sora on notice
7255.narrative: Pokémon Trainer Red crushed an unusually high-seeded newcomer and looked stronger than Sora had in the neighboring top-seed matchup. The result made their impending Round Two contest feel like a genuine tossup.

7256.headline: Crash turns Cecil Harvey Never Wins into canon
7256.narrative: Crash decisively beat Cecil in another matchup the Final Fantasy IV protagonist had been widely expected to win. The writeup treats the result as both a Crash nostalgia boost and the formal birth of the Cecil Harvey Never Wins meme.

7257.headline: Big Boss withstands Ridley's Smash boost
7257.narrative: Big Boss beat a Smash-boosted Ridley comfortably, though Ridley performed well enough to show clear improvement. The writeup frames the result as a rare case where an established non-Nintendo character resisted the contest's Nintendo surge.

7258.headline: Alucard calmly handles the Peach upset hype
7258.narrative: Alucard beat Peach without much drama in a matchup that some had overhyped because of Nintendo momentum. The writeup sees both characters as having looked respectable and rejects any need for a firm SFF explanation.

7259.headline: Yuna crushes a beloved Board 8 newcomer
7259.narrative: Yuna overwhelmed the Board 8-favorite Godot in a matchup that was never competitive after the opening moments. The writeup treats Godot's appearance as a community victory even though the broader site gave him little support.

7260.headline: Kefka routs L-Block in a classic prediction trap
7260.narrative: Kefka turned one of Round One's hardest prediction calls into a comfortable win over former champion L-Block. The writeup treats the result as another example of Kefka's unpredictability and of fading support for rallybait joke characters.

7261.headline: Bomberman embarrasses an overseeded Kiryu
7261.narrative: Bomberman demolished the heavily overseeded Kiryu and produced one of the bracket's clearest seeding embarrassments. The writeup treats the result as evidence that recognizability still mattered more than recent niche popularity.

7262.headline: 2B validates herself against bottom-tier Cayde
7262.narrative: 2B crushed Cayde-6 and immediately proved she had legitimate contest strength even if her top seeding was inflated. Cayde is treated as one of the weakest entrants in the entire field.

7263.headline: Ness quietly outlasts Shadow in a debated opener
7263.narrative: Ness won a debated matchup that stayed fairly close and stable, with Shadow never quite finding enough momentum to complete the comeback. The writeup treats the result as proof that Ness had quietly become a more reliable midcarder.

7264.headline: Charizard survives Terra but looks badly weakened
7264.narrative: Charizard survived a surprisingly strong challenge from Terra after spending much of the early match looking vulnerable. The writeup treats the narrow win as a major warning that Charizard was far weaker than his earlier contest reputation suggested.

7265.headline: Bowser obliterates Gordon and ignites Nintendo hype
7265.narrative: Bowser demolished Gordon Freeman far more thoroughly than historical comparisons suggested he should. The writeup treats the result as one of the clearest early signs that Nintendo characters had received a major boost.

7266.headline: Phoenix confirms his rise with a clean Chris win
7266.narrative: Phoenix Wright beat Chris Redfield comfortably enough to confirm his gradual rise from joke status into legitimate midcard strength. The writeup also notes Phoenix's strong early vote and harsher decline as the poll continued.

7267.headline: Ike crushes Joel and strengthens his Phoenix case
7267.narrative: Ike overwhelmed Joel and looked substantially stronger than Phoenix had in the neighboring matchup. The writeup treats the performance as evidence that Fire Emblem's growth and Ike's Smash popularity had translated into real contest strength.

7268.headline: Isaac cleanly enforces the fodder line
7268.narrative: Isaac comfortably dispatched a Board 8-backed newcomer and reinforced his role as a reliable dividing line between fodder and real midcarders. The writeup treats Estelle's appearance itself as the bigger community achievement.

7269.headline: Kirby adds another blowout to Nintendo's surge
7269.narrative: Kirby delivered another huge Nintendo blowout while Guile never became remotely competitive. The writeup treats the result as part of the contest-wide pattern of Smash and Nintendo characters outperforming expectations.

7270.headline: Squall wins big but still looks disappointing
7270.narrative: Squall crushed Hat Kid but still looked weaker than expected for a character some had placed near the top of the non-Noble-Nine field. The writeup treats the early struggle as another warning about Final Fantasy's broader decline.

7271.headline: Garrus survives Ramza in the first true thriller
7271.narrative: Garrus and Ramza traded leads for most of the match before Garrus finally gained enough daytime separation to survive. The writeup remembers it as the contest's first true nailbiter and one of its best early matches.

7272.headline: The Boss ends Metal Sonic's community-backed run
7272.narrative: The Boss beat Metal Sonic after a community nomination effort unexpectedly turned the Sonic side into a respectable opponent. The writeup gives most of the credit to the Board 8 campaign that got Metal Sonic into the bracket at all.

7273.headline: Zelda destroys Ezio and seizes the division
7273.narrative: Zelda crushed Ezio far more severely than in their earlier contest meeting and effectively ended debate about the division's natural favorite. The writeup treats the performance as another major Zelda and Nintendo statement.

7274.headline: D.Va beats Aloy without the feared rally
7274.narrative: D.Va won a close newcomer matchup against Aloy, but the heavily discussed possibility of an outside rally never materialized. The writeup treats the result as evidence that rallybait alone no longer guaranteed anything on GameFAQs.

7275.headline: Fox survives Jill but looks unexpectedly vulnerable
7275.narrative: Fox narrowly beat Jill in a match the writeup considers much closer than a Smash-boosted Nintendo character should have allowed. Jill's respectable loss and Fox's weak showing left both characters difficult to evaluate.

7276.headline: Captain Toad narrowly validates the Nintendo pick
7276.narrative: Captain Toad edged Shovel Knight in one of the most debated first-round matches, rewarding the simple 'pick Nintendo' logic over the indie favorite. The writeup treats the result as another bracket embarrassment for casual expectations.

7277.headline: Aerith ends Waluigi's meme hopes without trouble
7277.narrative: Aerith comfortably beat Waluigi after fears of joke votes or a meme rally failed to materialize. The writeup treats Waluigi's loss as another example of rallybait collapsing under the contest's quieter environment.

7278.headline: Geralt survives Rosalina and validates his top seed
7278.narrative: Geralt survived an alarming opening against Rosalina and eventually pulled away, avoiding what would have been a humiliating top-seed upset. The writeup treats the result as validation that a recent Western character could still possess real contest strength.

7279.headline: Smash and presentation lift Simon past Ryu Hayabusa
7279.narrative: Simon Belmont upset Ryu Hayabusa after taking an early lead and resisting a long, slow comeback. The writeup credits Simon's Smash announcement and improved presentation for transforming a historically weak character into a legitimate threat.
7279.anomaly_note: The writeup says Simon Belmont's new Smash design was shown especially well in the match picture and treats that presentation as part of the boost that helped him beat Ryu Hayabusa.

7280.headline: Pac-Man crushes Sans as RallyFEAR collapses
7280.narrative: Pac-Man annihilated Sans in a matchup many had debated because of Undertale's rally history. The expected outside push never appeared, and the writeup treats Sans's natural weakness as one of the contest's biggest disappointments.

7281.headline: Bayonetta obliterates Riku and reveals a massive boost
7281.narrative: Bayonetta demolished Riku in a matchup many had expected to be close or even favor Kingdom Hearts. The writeup treats the result as one of the contest's largest apparent boosts, driven by Bayonetta's Nintendo and Smash relevance.

7282.headline: Auron handles Lucina and remains the division favorite
7282.narrative: Auron comfortably beat Lucina, though Lucina performed well enough to demonstrate the growth of Fire Emblem and Smash-era Nintendo strength. The writeup still regards Auron as the clear favorite to emerge from the division.

7283.headline: Vincent barely survives fellow fallen star Magus
7283.narrative: Vincent survived a surprisingly strong Magus challenge in a matchup between two former contest heavyweights who had both declined badly. The writeup treats the narrow win as evidence that Vincent's fall had been even steeper than expected.

7284.headline: Sub-Zero calmly shuts down the Shulk boost
7284.narrative: Sub-Zero beat Shulk without serious difficulty despite expectations that Smash and Xenoblade growth might produce a stronger challenge. The writeup treats Sub-Zero as one of the most durable non-Nintendo midcarders.

7285.headline: Claire beats Joker amid a major presentation controversy
7285.narrative: Claire beat Joker after an initially close match turned sharply in Resident Evil's favor. The writeup considers the result clouded by Joker's naming and picture controversy and uses it as evidence that presentation can materially affect a close contest match.
7285.anomaly_note: The writeup says Joker's nonstandard name and unmasked picture hurt his recognition and explicitly argues the match would have been closer with a proper Joker presentation, even though Claire's picture was also poor.

7286.headline: Luigi crushes Edgeworth in another Nintendo rout
7286.narrative: Luigi produced one of the round's largest blowouts against Edgeworth and continued the contest-wide Nintendo surge. The writeup treats the result as another reminder of Luigi's unusually strong first-round history.

7287.headline: Frog crushes Monokuma as rallybait fails again
7287.narrative: Frog demolished Monokuma after another heavily discussed rallybait character failed to attract meaningful outside support. The writeup treats Monokuma as genuine bottom-tier fodder rather than a suppressed rally threat.

7288.headline: Master Chief wins but still looks embarrassingly weak
7288.narrative: Master Chief beat Majima comfortably but still performed far below what the writeup expected against such weak opposition. The showing is framed as another example of GameFAQs' longstanding hostility toward Halo and Xbox.

7289.headline: Tails upsets Nathan Drake and punishes the consensus
7289.narrative: Tails upset Nathan Drake after most casual and expert predictions had favored the Uncharted protagonist. The writeup celebrates the result as both a fan-favorite victory and another failure of recent Western characters to translate into contest strength.

7290.headline: Tifa crushes Geno and preserves her strength
7290.narrative: Tifa routed Geno and remained one of the few Final Fantasy VII characters still looking consistently strong. The writeup also uses the match to revisit Geno's extraordinary history of repeated contest appearances without a win.

7291.headline: Mewtwo answers the fraud talk with a clean win
7291.narrative: Mewtwo beat GLaDOS comfortably and resisted pre-match claims that his earlier deep runs had made him look stronger than he really was. The writeup treats the performance as a solid validation of his natural mid-to-high strength.

7292.headline: Ocelot survives Dedede with help from a small rally
7292.narrative: Ocelot survived Dedede in a wire-to-wire thriller where neither side ever established a secure advantage. The writeup remembers the match as a record-level close contest and notes that even a small outside push mattered.
7292.anomaly_note: The writeup says a small Reddit rally helped Revolver Ocelot avoid an upset during an extremely close match with King Dedede.

7293.headline: Mega Man X delivers a throwback-level blowout
7293.narrative: Mega Man X obliterated Isabelle and immediately looked like one of the strongest characters in the main bracket. The writeup treats the blowout as a rare modern performance resembling the massive margins of the earliest contests.

7294.headline: Sephiroth wins while his old dominance keeps fading
7294.narrative: Sephiroth beat Wesker comfortably but failed to look as dominant as a Noble Nine character once would have against similar opposition. The writeup treats the result as another sign that Sephiroth had clearly declined from his peak.

7295.headline: Captain Falcon shuts down Richter's Smash hype
7295.narrative: Captain Falcon beat newly Smash-boosted Richter comfortably and erased the upset hype created by Richter's recent announcement. The writeup treats Falcon's long Smash pedigree as more valuable than Richter's fresh exposure.

7296.headline: Amaterasu destroys Draven as the rally era collapses
7296.narrative: Amaterasu annihilated former champion Draven after the League rally machine that carried him in 2013 failed to return. The writeup treats the result as both catharsis and the contest's clearest proof that old rallybait had lost its power.

7297.headline: Lara ends Metal Man's Board 8 novelty run
7297.narrative: Lara Croft comfortably beat a Board 8-backed Robot Master whose real accomplishment was reaching the bracket. The writeup frames the match primarily as a celebration of the community nomination campaign behind Metal Man.

7298.headline: Ryu dispatches Lloyd in a routine veteran win
7298.narrative: Ryu routed Lloyd in another demonstration that the Tales series had little character-contest strength. The writeup treats Ryu as a durable veteran who remained comfortably above ordinary fodder despite years of decline.

7299.headline: Shepard survives King K. Rool after an early scare
7299.narrative: Commander Shepard survived an unexpectedly strong King K. Rool challenge after trailing for much of the opening portion of the match. The writeup blames Mass Effect's decline and K. Rool's Smash boost for making the result far closer than expected.

7300.headline: KOS-MOS beats Ellie despite an outside vote push
7300.narrative: KOS-MOS upset Ellie despite an outside appeal for The Last of Us fans to vote. The writeup treats the result as another case where GameFAQs' old-JRPG preferences overwhelmed the popularity of a major recent Western game.
7300.anomaly_note: The writeup quotes an Ellie supporter posting to The Last of Us community and explicitly asking people to visit GameFAQs and vote for her during the match.

7301.headline: Aqua quietly closes the first round over Quiet
7301.narrative: Aqua comfortably beat Quiet in a matchup that had looked more debatable before the contest exposed Metal Gear Solid V's weakness. The writeup treats the result as a routine close to an overlong first round.

7302.headline: Dante cruises past Lightning without drama
7302.narrative: Dante opened the next stage by comfortably eliminating Lightning, whose Final Fantasy XIII baggage left her unable to threaten him. The writeup treats the result as another solid Dante performance without much suspense.

7303.headline: Ganondorf wins but badly damages his division case
7303.narrative: Ganondorf beat Chun-Li but looked far weaker than expected for a character many had viewed as a likely division winner. The writeup treats the poor performance as a major warning, while explicitly dismissing earlier complaints about his sprite picture.

7304.headline: Vivi crushes Aya and suddenly looks dangerous
7304.narrative: Vivi demolished Aya Brea and looked much stronger than Ganondorf had in the neighboring match. Because Vivi's first two opponents were both weak, the writeup still hesitates to declare exactly how strong he really was.

7305.headline: Donkey Kong shocks Leon in a clean veteran upset
7305.narrative: Donkey Kong upset Leon in one of the contest's most surprising veteran-versus-veteran results, punishing an overwhelming expert lean toward Resident Evil. The writeup treats the match as clean evidence of Nintendo's rise and Leon's weakness.

7306.headline: Zero ends another brutally unlucky Knuckles run
7306.narrative: Zero beat Knuckles by almost exactly the sort of margin historical strength estimates suggested, ending another unlucky Knuckles run against elite opposition. The writeup treats Knuckles as legitimate despite yet another early exit.

7307.headline: Wario ends Master Hand's joke run cleanly
7307.narrative: Wario comfortably eliminated Master Hand after the joke and rally support some expected for the Smash boss never appeared. The writeup treats Wario's first deeper run as more a product of bracket luck than newfound strength.

7308.headline: Yoshi crushes Velvet without proving much
7308.narrative: Yoshi crushed Velvet in another unusually lopsided later-round match, though the writeup warns that both of Yoshi's opponents had been extremely weak. The result leaves his true strength unresolved heading into a much harder matchup.

7309.headline: Pikachu handles a newly boosted Kratos
7309.narrative: Pikachu beat a recently boosted Kratos comfortably and continued to look like the strongest Pokémon character in the bracket. The writeup treats Kratos's God of War revival as making the win more impressive than the raw matchup first appears.

7310.headline: A Pokémon rally helps Red survive Sora's comeback
7310.narrative: Red built a large lead, watched Sora erase much of it, then survived with help from a late Pokémon subreddit push. The writeup treats the match as both a legitimate close contest and a direct example of a small rally deciding the outcome.
7310.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pokémon Trainer Red was rallied through posts to the Pokémon subreddit during Sora's comeback, and explicitly states that the outside traffic made the difference.

7311.headline: Big Boss barely survives a resurgent Crash
7311.narrative: Big Boss barely beat Crash in a matchup that was expected to be routine, turning a presumed blowout into another warning about Metal Gear's collapse. The writeup gives Crash substantial credit for his continuing nostalgia-driven rebound.

7312.headline: Alucard routs Yuna and keeps his deep run alive
7312.narrative: Alucard beat Yuna far more comfortably than pre-contest expectations suggested and continued his recurring habit of producing deep contest runs. The writeup treats Yuna's loss as another sign of Final Fantasy X's long-term decline.

7313.headline: Kefka cruises through his free second-round win
7313.narrative: Kefka followed his first-round escape with a routine blowout of Bomberman. The writeup finds the near-repeat of Kefka's prior percentage on L-Block funnier than the actual match.

7314.headline: 2B upsets Ness but still looks overseeded
7314.narrative: 2B upset the Board 8 favorite Ness and established herself as a legitimate midcard character, though the writeup still considers her badly overseeded as a top seed. The win is attributed to real strength rather than any outside intervention.

7315.headline: Bowser avenges Charizard and restores the hierarchy
7315.narrative: Bowser decisively avenged his old loss to Charizard and ended hopes of another deep Pokémon run from the dragon. The writeup treats Bowser as fully legitimate and Charizard's earlier peak as heavily timing-dependent.

7316.headline: Registered-user weighting flips Phoenix over Ike
7316.narrative: Phoenix Wright narrowly advanced over Ike because registered-user votes counted double, even though Ike won the raw vote. The writeup treats the result as a rules-driven flip and another major disappointment in Ike's contest history.

7317.headline: Kirby SFFs Isaac in a handheld-heavy matchup
7317.narrative: Kirby demolished Isaac in a matchup the writeup considers heavily distorted by shared Nintendo and handheld appeal. The blowout further strengthened Kirby's status as a division favorite.
7317.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Kirby versus Isaac an SFF match, arguing that Kirby's handheld-heavy Nintendo fanbase strongly overlaps with Golden Sun's audience.

7318.headline: Squall beats Garrus but shows a warning sign
7318.narrative: Squall beat Garrus as expected but failed to dominate as strongly as the writeup anticipated. The result is remembered as an early warning sign that Squall's top-seed run was much shakier than it appeared.

7319.headline: Zelda crushes The Boss and looks near-elite
7319.narrative: Zelda crushed The Boss and made her coming match with Squall look increasingly favorable. The writeup treats Breath of the Wild and broader Nintendo momentum as convincing explanations for Zelda's dramatic rise.

7320.headline: Fox crushes D.Va inside a massive Blizzard rant
7320.narrative: The writeup is mostly an enormous political and Blizzard retrospective; the actual match is summarized as Fox crushing a weak D.Va after the feared rally never appeared.

7321.headline: Aerith becomes the first 15-seed with three wins
7321.narrative: Aerith beat Captain Toad without much movement and became the first 15-seed to win three matches. The writeup treats her run as a historic seeding oddity even though the path itself was unusually weak.

7322.headline: Geralt outlasts Simon in another close duel
7322.narrative: Simon led early and kept Geralt tied for hours before Geralt took control late at night. The writeup celebrates the match as another close, entertaining step in Geralt's newcomer run.

7323.headline: Bayonetta wins a close-looking but static match
7323.narrative: Bayonetta beat Pac-Man in a match that stayed close by percentage but never developed into an actual rally or comeback. The writeup is more puzzled by Pac-Man's unexpected strength than impressed by the drama.

7324.headline: Auron exposes Vincent's long-term decline
7324.narrative: Auron comfortably beat Vincent and reinforced the writeup's view that Vincent had fallen sharply from his mid-2000s peak. Board 8 overwhelmingly expected the result despite old faith in Final Fantasy VII's intra-series strength.

7325.headline: Sub-Zero dispatches Claire exactly as expected
7325.narrative: Sub-Zero doubled Claire in the straightforward result the writeup expected from this fourpack. Claire's easy defeat is used as another example of Resident Evil's damaged contest strength.

7326.headline: Luigi handles Frog in a routine second-round win
7326.narrative: Luigi beat Frog comfortably in a routine matchup that offered little suspense. The source's 'Green SFF' line is a color joke rather than a substantive claim about shared fanbases.

7327.headline: Tails upsets Master Chief and reaches Round Three
7327.narrative: Tails upset Master Chief and controlled the match from early on, turning a fan-favorite gamble into one of the writeup's most satisfying picks. The result also continued Master Chief's long contest decline.

7328.headline: Tifa demolishes Mewtwo and exposes old hype
7328.narrative: Tifa crushed Mewtwo in a matchup many had once imagined favoring the Pokémon character. The writeup uses the result to reject Mewtwo's rally-inflated 2013 reputation and to establish Tifa as a serious threat.

7329.headline: Mega Man X crushes Ocelot and looks near-elite
7329.narrative: Mega Man X overwhelmed Ocelot and finally produced a clean comparison that made X look near-elite. Ocelot's poor showing added to the wider Metal Gear decline narrative.

7330.headline: Sephiroth dismisses Captain Falcon and the decline talk
7330.narrative: Sephiroth briefly allowed Captain Falcon an opening before settling into the expected comfortable win. The writeup treats the result as evidence that claims of Sephiroth's collapse had been exaggerated.

7331.headline: Amaterasu survives Lara without looking dominant
7331.narrative: Amaterasu beat Lara despite low pre-contest confidence, but the writeup considers the modest margin another example of Amaterasu rarely producing decisive results. Lara's modern games are said to have done little for her contest standing.

7332.headline: Ryu overwhelms Shepard and exposes Mass Effect decline
7332.narrative: Ryu crushed Commander Shepard and made Mass Effect's character decline look severe. The writeup treats Ryu's Smash exposure as part of a broader rise while Shepard never recovered old strength.

7333.headline: KOS-MOS upsets Aqua and reaches Round Three
7333.narrative: KOS-MOS upset Aqua and reached Round Three for the first time, despite much of the writeup framing her as an unlikely survivor of an exceptionally weak fourpack. The result is linked to renewed visibility from guest appearances rather than cheating.

7334.headline: Ganondorf exposes Dante as an unworthy top seed
7334.narrative: Ganondorf comfortably eliminated the contest's top overall seed Dante in a match that barely moved. The writeup treats the loss as proof Dante was badly overseeded rather than evidence of a close divisional race.

7335.headline: Vivi beats Donkey Kong for the third time
7335.narrative: Vivi beat Donkey Kong for the third time in nearly identical fashion, continuing one of the contest's strangest recurring rivalries. The writeup concludes that Donkey Kong's apparent revival had been overstated.

7336.headline: Zero ends Wario's lucky run without trouble
7336.narrative: Zero comfortably ended Wario's run through a weak part of the bracket and looked exactly like the reliable upper-midcard favorite expected of him. Wario's respectable share still surprised the writeup.

7337.headline: Pikachu beats Yoshi and keeps Pokémon hopes alive
7337.narrative: Pikachu beat Yoshi in their long-awaited first direct matchup and looked like the only Pokémon character consistently meeting high expectations. The Detective Pikachu trailer arriving the same day is noted as favorable timing.

7338.headline: Red survives Big Boss and raises more strength questions
7338.narrative: Red beat Big Boss but struggled enough to make both Pokémon and Metal Gear strength difficult to interpret. The writeup uses the close result as evidence that Red's multiway reputation had overstated his 1v1 power.

7339.headline: Alucard crushes Kefka and seizes the division
7339.narrative: Alucard crushed pre-contest favorite Kefka and turned what had looked like a wide-open division into his breakout run. The writeup attributes Alucard's rise to a mix of Castlevania revival, Netflix exposure and Smash visibility.

7340.headline: 2B earns legitimacy while Bowser exposes her seeding
7340.narrative: 2B performed respectably in defeat against Bowser and convinced the writeup she belonged in the midcard. At the same time, the loss confirmed that her top seed was far too generous.

7341.headline: Kirby crushes Phoenix and becomes the new favorite
7341.narrative: Kirby demolished Phoenix and erased the significance of Phoenix's narrow rules-assisted win over Ike. The blowout made Kirby the popular favorite over Bowser despite older evidence favoring Bowser.

7342.headline: Zelda destroys Squall and enters near-Noble-Nine territory
7342.narrative: Zelda destroyed Squall in the match that fully established her as the star of the main bracket. The writeup treats the scale of the win as evidence of a genuine Breath of the Wild and Smash-era boost, not a rally.

7343.headline: Aerith extends her record 15-seed run over Fox
7343.narrative: Aerith beat Fox in a nearly static match and extended the deepest run ever by a 15-seed. The writeup emphasizes the historic seeding achievement more than the competitiveness of the poll.

7344.headline: Geralt comes back on Bayonetta and keeps rolling
7344.narrative: Bayonetta led for much of the match, but Geralt again used the overnight and morning vote to complete a comeback. The writeup treats the win as another entertaining step in an unusually strong newcomer run.

7345.headline: Auron beats Sub-Zero in another familiar rematch
7345.narrative: Auron beat Sub-Zero in another remarkably similar rematch between two characters who had repeatedly met before. The writeup finds the consistency more interesting than the outcome itself.

7346.headline: Luigi SFFs Tails and ends his surprise run
7346.narrative: Luigi demolished Tails in the biggest blowout of the round and ended Tails's surprise run. The writeup treats the result as another example of the Mario side dominating Sonic-family characters under overlapping fanbases.
7346.anomaly_note: Tsunami explicitly calls Luigi versus Tails an SFF matchup and argues that Mario-family strength suppresses the Sonic-side character in this cross-franchise Nintendo-adjacent rivalry.

7347.headline: Tifa wins a rally war over Mega Man X
7347.narrative: Mega Man X and Tifa traded leads throughout one of the contest's best matches before outside support became decisive late. Tifa's final rally push erased X's last advantage and carried her through the divisional thriller.
7347.anomaly_note: The writeup describes organized pushes for both Mega Man X and Tifa, including subreddit and outside-site rallies. It explicitly says Tifa's broader rally sources supplied the final push that decided the match.

7348.headline: Sephiroth beats Amaterasu but shows another warning
7348.narrative: Sephiroth beat Amaterasu in the familiar pattern of losing early support and steadily climbing, but the writeup considers the final showing weaker than his old form. The result is treated as a subtle warning before stronger opposition.

7349.headline: Ryu ends KOS-MOS's improbable Round Three run
