7349.narrative: Ryu comfortably ended KOS-MOS's unlikely run through one of the weakest sections of the bracket. The writeup treats the result as a return to normal after KOS-MOS reached Round Three for the first time.

7350.headline: Ganondorf narrowly holds off a strong Vivi challenge
7350.narrative: Ganondorf beat Vivi after an early struggle, but Vivi stayed close enough to reinforce his reputation as an unusually durable Final Fantasy character. The writeup believes Nintendo and Zelda momentum were just enough to decide the matchup.

7351.headline: Pikachu rolls past Zero and wins the division
7351.narrative: Pikachu beat Zero comfortably and won another division, continuing the mascot's standout run while most other Pokémon characters disappointed. The writeup sees Pikachu as clearly stronger than the rest of his franchise's field.

7352.headline: Alucard completes The Plan and wins the division
7352.narrative: Alucard decisively beat Pokémon Trainer Red and completed the unexpected divisional run almost no one had predicted before the contest. The writeup celebrates the long-running 'Plan' joke finally paying off.

7353.headline: Bowser upsets Kirby and punishes the consensus
7353.narrative: Bowser upset the heavily favored Kirby and repeated his old head-to-head superiority despite most mid-contest predictions flipping toward Kirby. The writeup treats Bowser's broader Mario appeal and recent relevance as more durable than Kirby's apparent momentum.

7354.headline: Zelda ends Aerith's record run in a rout
7354.narrative: Zelda crushed Aerith and finished a division where every win had looked dominant. The writeup treats Aerith's record 15-seed run as impressive but completely overmatched once it reached Zelda.

7355.headline: Auron ends Geralt's newcomer run and wins the division
7355.narrative: Auron finally ended Geralt's string of close wins and claimed the division, though Geralt remained competitive enough to validate his newcomer run. The writeup treats the result as the natural endpoint once Geralt met a proven upper-midcarder.

7356.headline: Tifa beats Luigi cleanly and completes a brutal division
7356.narrative: Tifa beat Luigi after a close opening and pulled away without needing the rallying that had decided her Mega Man X match. The win completed one of the main bracket's toughest divisional paths.

7357.headline: Sephiroth crushes Ryu and revives his reputation
7357.narrative: Sephiroth unexpectedly crushed Ryu and produced by far his strongest-looking result of the main bracket. The writeup uses the match to argue that reports of Sephiroth's collapse had gone too far.

7358.headline: Link SFFs Ganondorf in the Legends opener
7358.narrative: Link opened the Legends Bracket by crushing Ganondorf, though the margin was less extreme than their famous older matchup. The writeup treats the result as heavily distorted by Zelda-series overlap rather than a clean measure of Ganondorf's strength.
7358.anomaly_note: The writeup treats Link's domination of Ganondorf as a clear SFF result, noting that Ganondorf is much stronger than the raw margin suggests and that Zelda resists Link's SFF better.

7359.headline: Pikachu breaks the Noble Nine in a classic
7359.narrative: Pikachu beat Mega Man in a record-setting wire-to-wire thriller after multiple lead changes and a final late push. The writeup treats the result as the first clean 24-hour 1v1 Noble Nine break, even though Mega Man won the raw vote before registered-user weighting.

7360.headline: Cloud wins while Alucard validates his breakout
7360.narrative: Cloud beat Alucard comfortably, but Alucard performed far better than in their early-contest meetings. The writeup treats the loss as confirmation that Alucard's breakout run reflected genuine strength rather than only a weak division.

7361.headline: Crono finally wins another clean 1v1 match
7361.narrative: Crono beat Bowser without much danger and finally earned his first 1v1 contest win in many years. The writeup treats the result as a modest restoration of Crono's old status rather than a return to championship form.

7362.headline: Zelda suppresses Snake and buries the old hierarchy
7362.narrative: Zelda narrowly beat Solid Snake after a long fight in which Snake repeatedly threatened to retake control. The writeup treats the victory as the match that buried the old Noble Nine order and confirmed Zelda's elite-level rise.
7362.anomaly_note: The writeup says Snake's Nintendo-derived support consistently abandons him against Nintendo characters and identifies that overlap, combined with Zelda's boost, as a major reason he lost this match.

7363.headline: Sonic beats Auron but looks unimpressive
7363.narrative: Sonic beat Auron without serious danger, but the writeup considers the showing weak for a Noble Nine character. Auron's respectable resistance reinforced doubts about Sonic's 2018 form.

7364.headline: Samus crushes Tifa and exposes her ceiling
7364.narrative: Samus demolished Tifa and erased memories of their much closer 2006 meeting. The writeup treats the rout as proof that Tifa's excellent main-bracket run still had a clear ceiling against truly elite opposition.

7365.headline: Mario finally gets his revenge on Sephiroth
7365.narrative: Mario finally avenged years of losses to Sephiroth by beating him decisively. The writeup frames the result as the emotional payoff to one of Mario's oldest contest frustrations and another sign of Sephiroth's decline.

7366.headline: Mega Man routs Ganondorf and rejects the sprite excuse
7366.narrative: Mega Man routed Ganondorf in the losers bracket and made the pre-match expectations look far too conservative. The writeup spends much of its analysis rejecting claims that Ganondorf's sprite picture caused the poor result.

7367.headline: Bowser ends Alucard's run after a respectable fight
7367.narrative: Bowser eventually pulled away from Alucard, but Alucard stayed competitive long enough to validate his surprising divisional run. The writeup treats the loss as a strong final statement for Alucard rather than an embarrassment.

7368.headline: Snake crushes Auron and buries the sprite excuse
7368.narrative: Solid Snake crushed Auron and used the matchup as another counterexample to complaints that Snake's old sprite hurts him. The writeup treats Auron as the weakest Legends Bracket entrant and Snake as clearly above him.

7369.headline: Tifa reverses SFF and finally beats Sephiroth
7369.narrative: Tifa upset Sephiroth after controlling the early hours and held on despite his later recovery. The writeup treats the result as the burial of Sephiroth's old elite status and one of Tifa's defining wins.
7369.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Tifa's win the first confirmed case of Reverse SFF, with the usual same-fanbase hierarchy flipping against Sephiroth.

7370.headline: Link crushes Pikachu despite limited SFF
7370.narrative: Link overwhelmed Pikachu and continued his untouchable 2018 run. Pikachu's result is still framed positively because he had already broken the Noble Nine and appeared to resist most of Link's usual same-fanbase suppression.
7370.anomaly_note: The writeup says Pikachu likely suffered a small amount of Nintendo SFF under Link, while emphasizing that Pokémon resisted the effect unusually well.

7371.headline: Cloud crushes Crono and validates his Smash boost
7371.narrative: Cloud beat Crono much more comfortably than the pre-match upset discussion suggested. The writeup explicitly rejects SFF as the explanation and credits Cloud's Smash appearance with restoring enough strength to dominate the matchup.

7372.headline: Zelda humiliates Sonic and keeps rewriting the hierarchy
7372.narrative: Zelda demolished Sonic in the largest of the contest's Noble Nine-breaking results. The writeup treats Zelda as plainly stronger rather than rally-assisted and calls the loss one of Sonic's worst career performances.

7373.headline: Mario narrowly settles the old Samus debate
7373.narrative: Mario beat Samus in their long-awaited 1v1 rematch, but the match stayed close enough to validate years of arguments that Samus could compete with him. The writeup treats the result as an unusually satisfying resolution to their old rivalry.

7374.headline: Mega Man reverses the Pikachu result
7374.narrative: Mega Man reversed his earlier loss to Pikachu and controlled the rematch after the opening minutes. The writeup calls the revenge satisfying but less meaningful because it happened in the losers bracket.

7375.headline: Crono repeats the same Bowser win almost exactly
7375.narrative: Crono beat Bowser in an almost exact repeat of their earlier Legends Bracket match. The writeup criticizes the double-elimination layout for producing a rematch with nearly identical trends and no new information.

7376.headline: Snake beats Sonic and breaks the transitive logic
7376.narrative: Solid Snake beat Sonic more decisively than Zelda had, reigniting arguments about the usefulness of extrapolated statistics after Zelda had beaten Snake directly. The writeup uses the result to emphasize that individual matchups do not obey clean transitive logic.

7377.headline: Samus repeats her Tifa rout almost exactly
7377.narrative: Samus crushed Tifa again in a nearly identical rematch of their earlier Legends Bracket meeting. The writeup sees the repeat as unnecessary but definitive proof that Tifa was not on Samus's level.

7378.headline: Link dominates Cloud again and looks untouchable
7378.narrative: Link continued the long-running Link-Cloud rivalry with another dominant win and looked more overwhelming than ever. The writeup treats Cloud's inability to threaten him as evidence that Link remained completely untouchable without extraordinary outside intervention.

7379.headline: Zelda beats Mario with a late rally tailwind
7379.narrative: Zelda beat Mario after leading essentially the entire match and pulled away late to deepen her extraordinary 2018 run. The writeup treats the win as a genuine strength result even though some outside rallying also occurred.
7379.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says Zelda received porn-site rallies during the match, while also stating that she was strong enough to beat Mario without them.

7380.headline: Crono finally wins a close match late
7380.narrative: Crono erased Mega Man's lead, survived a long stretch of back-and-forth voting, and finally won a close match late. The writeup celebrates the result as rare clutch success for a character associated with painful contest losses.

7381.headline: Samus crushes Snake in a bad Nintendo matchup
7381.narrative: Samus crushed Solid Snake and reinforced the writeup's long-held view that Snake loses much of his support against Nintendo characters. Historical rallying from their 2013 meeting is discussed, but not treated as part of this match.

7382.headline: Cloud repeats the Crono win with only minor SFF
7382.narrative: Cloud beat Crono again by almost the same margin as their sprite-round meeting. The writeup uses the near-identical rematch to reject claims that the earlier sprite pictures materially distorted the result.
7382.anomaly_note: The writeup says there was likely a small amount of SFF between Cloud and Crono because their fanbases overlap as flagship Square RPG protagonists.

7383.headline: Mario survives Samus in a chaotic all-time classic
7383.narrative: Mario survived Samus by the narrowest margin after hours of lead changes and an extraordinary final stretch. The writeup treats it as the best match of the contest and a reopening of their supposedly settled rivalry.
7383.anomaly_note: The writeup describes active late match vote pushes, including Samus rallies, porn-site rallies, workplace solicitation and the author's own last-minute requests for Mario votes. It also reports contemporaneous accusations that Mario supporters were vote stuffing, though no fraud is established.

7384.headline: Link SFFs Zelda but cannot erase her breakout
7384.narrative: Link erased Zelda's brief opening lead and won the Legends Bracket comfortably. The writeup treats Zelda's relatively strong same-series showing as one more sign that her 2018 boost was real.
7384.anomaly_note: The writeup frames Link as the site's strongest SFF character and treats Zelda's ability to retain substantial support in a direct same-series match as unusually impressive resistance.

7385.headline: Cloud finally gets his Mario rematch revenge
7385.narrative: Cloud finally beat Mario in their long-awaited 1v1 rematch, reversing the old trend pattern and surviving Mario's late reputation for clutch finishes. The writeup credits Cloud's Smash-era boost and possible anti-Mario sentiment rather than a confirmed current rally.

7386.headline: Cloud ends Zelda's run with another comeback
7386.narrative: Cloud erased Zelda's early lead with the same night-to-day trend reversal he had just used against Mario. The writeup treats the loss as Zelda finally running out of momentum after her extraordinary run rather than evidence that her breakout was false.

7387.headline: Link closes the contest with another Cloud win
7387.narrative: Link beat Cloud again in the grand final and completed an overwhelmingly dominant championship run. The writeup treats Cloud merely breaking through Link's usual ceiling as the only real drama and uses the finale to reflect on the contest's collapsing turnout.

7915.headline: Breath of the Wild opens in championship form
7915.narrative: Breath of the Wild opened the contest with an enormous rout and immediately looked like the obvious championship favorite. The writeup frames the result as the start of a Zelda redemption tour after the prior games contest.

7916.headline: Halo survives another round of anti-Halo doubt
7916.narrative: Halo: Reach beat Life is Strange despite significant pre-match distrust rooted in Halo's long history of underperforming on GameFAQs. The writeup treats the win as routine enough while still emphasizing how far Halo's reputation had fallen.

7917.headline: Final Fantasy XV wins with an immediate warning
7917.narrative: Final Fantasy XV beat one of the bracket's weakest-looking indie entries but not by enough to impress the writeup. The result is treated as the first warning that FFXV might struggle badly against Hollow Knight.

7918.headline: Hollow Knight embarrasses Board 8 and looks dangerous
7918.narrative: Hollow Knight crushed Tales of Berseria after many Board 8 experts had talked themselves out of the obvious pick. The blowout immediately made the coming Final Fantasy XV matchup look much more dangerous.

7919.headline: Monster Hunter wins a mirror-image newcomer matchup
7919.narrative: Monster Hunter: World beat Bravely Default in a stable newcomer matchup whose trends closely mirrored the simultaneous Sekiro poll. The writeup sees the result as solid but not decisive evidence for the next round.

7920.headline: Sekiro wins a nearly identical newcomer matchup
7920.narrative: Sekiro beat Ni no Kuni in almost the same pattern as Monster Hunter's simultaneous win, leaving their future head-to-head hard to project. The writeup's most distinctive commentary is the unusually strong Board 8 dislike for Ni no Kuni.

7921.headline: Bastion upsets The Walking Dead and punishes the safe pick
7921.narrative: Bastion upset The Walking Dead and reinforced the writeup's view that the franchise's mainstream popularity never translated into GameFAQs contest strength. The result also rewarded skepticism toward supposedly safer casual picks.

7922.headline: Dragon Quest XI SFFs Trails and finally looks strong
7922.narrative: Dragon Quest XI crushed the Board 8-backed Trails in the Sky SC and finally gave Dragon Quest a genuinely strong contest performance. The writeup views the blowout as partly amplified by extreme fanbase overlap.
7922.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says the matchup reeks of SFF, arguing that Dragon Quest XI and Trails in the Sky SC appeal to an unusually overlapping JRPG audience.

7923.headline: Mass Effect 2 wins and immediately looks vulnerable
7923.narrative: Mass Effect 2 beat Resident Evil 7 but looked far too weak for a supposed division favorite facing a 16-seed. The writeup treats Resident Evil 7 as clearly underseeded and the result as an immediate warning for Mass Effect.

7924.headline: Fallout 4 hides its Bethesda problem for one round
7924.narrative: Fallout 4 handled VVVVVV and initially seemed to avoid the Bethesda backlash many expected. The writeup later treats that apparent stability as misleading once Fallout's deeper weaknesses became clearer.

7925.headline: Borderlands 2 wins with a major warning sign
7925.narrative: Borderlands 2 beat Bloodstained but performed much worse than expected for the fourpack favorite. The writeup treats Bloodstained as respectable while still calling the result a major warning for Borderlands.

7926.headline: Horizon crushes Fortnite and the rally fear
7926.narrative: Horizon Zero Dawn obliterated Fortnite after rally fear and casual recognition had made the matchup look more uncertain on paper than it really was. The writeup treats the rout as another sign that GameFAQs' remaining voters strongly reject casualbait.

7927.headline: Resident Evil 2 opens with a huge statement
7927.narrative: Resident Evil 2 crushed Danganronpa 2 and immediately looked much stronger than Mass Effect 2 had in the same division. The writeup treats the result as confirmation that the remake's acclaim translated into major contest strength.

7928.headline: DOOM crushes one of the bracket's weakest games
7928.narrative: DOOM demolished INSIDE and looked far stronger than many had expected from a modern shooter. The writeup later concludes that INSIDE was simply one of the weakest games in the bracket rather than a meaningful strength test.

7929.headline: Awakening wins but badly hurts its deep-run case
7929.narrative: Fire Emblem: Awakening beat Deus Ex but failed to look strong enough for the deeper run many bracketmakers wanted. The writeup treats the result as a clear warning after simultaneous games in the division posted much stronger performances.

7930.headline: Bloodborne crushes Call of Duty's fading reputation
7930.narrative: Bloodborne crushed Black Ops while the writeup marvels at how completely Call of Duty's old contest relevance had vanished. The result also exposed casual bracketmakers who still gave the famous shooter too much credit.

7931.headline: Smash Ultimate opens with a fighting-game rout
7931.narrative: Smash Ultimate annihilated Tekken 7 and looked every bit like the division's overwhelming favorite. Much of the writeup uses the result to celebrate Smash's dominance over traditional fighting-game expectations.

7932.headline: A Link Between Worlds beats Bayonetta without SFF
7932.narrative: A Link Between Worlds comfortably beat Bayonetta despite the latter's Nintendo and Smash associations. The writeup explicitly says the match did not look like SFF and instead treats both games as legitimate within their natural strength.

7933.headline: Spider-Man gives licensed games a major statement
7933.narrative: Marvel's Spider-Man demolished Dead Space 2 and gave a licensed superhero game an unusually strong contest showing. The writeup uses the result to argue that high-quality licensed games can possess real GameFAQs strength.

7934.headline: Minecraft crushes Dota amid an eligibility complaint
7934.narrative: Minecraft crushed Dota 2 despite the writeup's complaint that Minecraft should not have been eligible under the contest's release-year rules. Dota never received the rally some feared and is treated as another example of rallybait collapsing naturally.

7935.headline: Octopath topples Undertale without a rally
7935.narrative: Octopath Traveler upset defending champion Undertale after the outside rally that defined 2015 never materialized. The writeup treats Undertale's relatively respectable loss as evidence that it retained a real fanbase even after its rally era ended.

7936.headline: Shovel Knight advances while Undertale steals the attention
7936.narrative: Shovel Knight beat Dragon's Dogma comfortably, though the writeup considers the performance merely solid rather than evidence of the huge indie strength some had expected. Undertale's simultaneous loss overshadowed most discussion of the match.

7937.headline: Devil May Cry 5 finally redeems the series
7937.narrative: Devil May Cry 5 beat Tropical Freeze in a debated matchup and gave the series long-awaited redemption after years of weak game-contest results. The writeup treats the win as a major correction to Devil May Cry's poor historical reputation.

7938.headline: Odyssey buries Mortal Kombat under heavy SFF
7938.narrative: Super Mario Odyssey produced an enormous rout that immediately made people reconsider whether Smash Ultimate was the obvious divisional favorite. Mortal Kombat's collapse was so severe that the writeup treats it as one of the strangest results of the round.
7938.anomaly_note: The writeup says Mortal Kombat 11 was buried under layers of SFF against Super Mario Odyssey, making its already poor showing even harder to interpret naturally.

7939.headline: GTA V wins but cannot escape anti-GTA voting
7939.narrative: Grand Theft Auto V beat Baba Is You but was briefly embarrassed by Board 8 anti-GTA voting at the start. The writeup treats the result as another example of GTA's unusual inability to produce clean blowouts even against extremely weak opposition.

7940.headline: Cuphead opens strongly and fuels early upset hype
7940.narrative: Cuphead beat XCOM 2 comfortably and strengthened the early-contest belief that some indie games had real GameFAQs strength. Its fast start also helped create early hype for a possible upset of Grand Theft Auto V.

7941.headline: Persona 4 Golden immediately looks dangerous
7941.narrative: Persona 4 Golden crushed FTL and immediately looked like a serious threat to escape a crowded division. The writeup treats Golden as functioning essentially like the original Persona 4 despite its Vita-only status.

7942.headline: Red Dead Redemption sets up a major Persona showdown
7942.narrative: Red Dead Redemption routed Ghost Trick and produced almost the same kind of opening statement as Persona 4 Golden. That set up their coming second-round match as one of the bracket's clearest tossups.

7943.headline: Xenoblade SFFs Splatoon and seizes the spotlight
7943.narrative: Xenoblade Chronicles crushed Splatoon 2 and instantly became a serious divisional contender. Even allowing for heavy Nintendo overlap, the writeup treats the performance as one of the round's biggest statements.
7943.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Xenoblade Chronicles versus Splatoon 2 an SFF beatdown and says Splatoon was especially vulnerable to being suppressed by a stronger Nintendo favorite.

7944.headline: Overwatch wins the battle of unpopular games
7944.narrative: Overwatch beat Death Stranding in a matchup the writeup frames as a battle between two widely disliked games. The result is treated as more a failure by Death Stranding than a meaningful endorsement of Overwatch.

7945.headline: Ori shocks Dragon Age in a major first-round upset
7945.narrative: Ori and the Blind Forest upset Dragon Age: Inquisition after taking control early and never truly surrendering it. The writeup credits Dragon Age's decline and Ori's recent sequel and Switch exposure as major background factors.

7946.headline: Three Houses wins but raises immediate warning signs
7946.narrative: Fire Emblem: Three Houses won comfortably but looked much weaker than expected next to Xenoblade Chronicles. The writeup treats Smash-related anti-voting and Fire Emblem's familiar tendency to underperform as serious warning signs.

7947.headline: The Witcher 3 SFFs Odyssey and looks elite
7947.narrative: The Witcher 3 obliterated Assassin's Creed Odyssey and immediately looked transformed from its 2015 form. The writeup treats the result as a championship-level statement even if some of the margin came from overlap.
7947.anomaly_note: Ctes explicitly says The Witcher 3 held the SFF hammer over Assassin's Creed Odyssey because of their overlapping open-world appeal and that the effect hit hard.

7948.headline: Mass Effect 3 gets its redemption over StarCraft II
7948.narrative: Mass Effect 3 beat StarCraft II much more decisively than their franchises' older matchup suggested. The writeup treats the result as redemption for Mass Effect 3 and another sign of Blizzard's declining contest strength.

7949.headline: Stardew Valley crushes Destiny and leads the indie field
7949.narrative: Stardew Valley demolished Destiny and emerged as one of the strongest-looking indie games of the opening round. The writeup still cautions that Destiny's extreme unpopularity may have exaggerated the performance.

7950.headline: Galaxy 2 delivers a legendary first-round blowout
7950.narrative: Super Mario Galaxy 2 produced one of the contest's most extreme first-round blowouts against Return of the Obra Dinn. The writeup also criticizes the seeding that placed both games far from where their strength suggested they belonged.

7951.headline: New Vegas cruises and eases Bethesda concerns
7951.narrative: Fallout: New Vegas crushed The Stanley Parable in a routine first-round mismatch. The writeup treats the win as modest reassurance that Fallout had not suffered as much from Bethesda backlash as some feared.

7952.headline: Dark Souls III continues the Souls resurgence
7952.narrative: Dark Souls III handled Dishonored without difficulty and continued the broader pattern of Souls games outperforming expectations. The writeup uses the result mainly to strengthen confidence in the franchise as a whole.

7953.headline: Nioh humiliates the consensus in a major upset
7953.narrative: Nioh upset The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth after nearly every prediction group favored Isaac. The writeup treats the result as another warning that the contest's 2017-era Souls-style games were much stronger than expected.

7954.headline: God of War opens with a heavyweight rout
7954.narrative: God of War annihilated The Talos Principle and looked every bit like a serious heavyweight. The writeup notes that The Witcher 3's simultaneous performance still kept God of War's division path looking difficult.

7955.headline: Persona 5 crushes Heavy Rain and looks fully mainstream
7955.narrative: Persona 5 crushed Heavy Rain and reinforced how completely the Persona series had entered the GameFAQs mainstream. The writeup treats Persona 5 as one of the bracket's easiest games to trust in the early rounds.

7956.headline: Black Flag wins a low-tier fodder duel
7956.narrative: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag beat Civilization V in a matchup the writeup considers a low-tier 8/9 contest. The winner is treated as merely earning the right to face a much stronger Persona 5.

7957.headline: Sonic Mania wins and immediately looks vulnerable
7957.narrative: Sonic Mania beat Ys VIII but performed badly enough to inspire real second-round upset talk around Super Meat Boy. The writeup treats the weak showing as a significant warning despite the comfortable win.

7958.headline: Super Meat Boy validates the guru nomination
7958.narrative: Super Meat Boy crushed Slay the Spire and gave Board 8's guru nomination a rare clean contest win. Combined with Sonic Mania's weak showing, the result fueled hopes for a much bigger upset next round.

7959.headline: Portal 2 wins without showing its later strength
7959.narrative: Portal 2 handled Tomb Raider in a routine first-round match without producing the kind of statement its supporters wanted. The writeup still treats Portal 2 as the most likely divisional finalist entering Round Two.

7960.headline: Kingdom Hearts III wins but badly underperforms
7960.narrative: Kingdom Hearts III beat Disco Elysium comfortably but looked weak compared with Portal 2 and Red Dead Redemption 2. The writeup treats the result as a serious underperformance for a major franchise entry.

7961.headline: New Leaf finally gives Animal Crossing a clean win
7961.narrative: Animal Crossing: New Leaf beat Street Fighter V after years of weak Animal Crossing contest history. The writeup sees the win as evidence that the series had become more relevant, while Street Fighter V's poor reputation made the matchup easier.

7962.headline: Red Dead Redemption 2 cruises through weak opposition
7962.narrative: Red Dead Redemption 2 demolished Dying Light in a completely routine top-seed-style matchup. The writeup treats the blowout mainly as a necessary first test before much stronger opposition arrived.

7963.headline: Dark Souls opens with a massive statement
7963.narrative: Dark Souls obliterated Hotline Miami and immediately confirmed the writeup's belief that the franchise had gained major respect over the decade. The performance pushed Dark Souls into serious divisional-title consideration.

7964.headline: Rocket League wins the first real tossup
7964.narrative: Rocket League narrowly beat Dragon Ball FighterZ in one of the opening round's first genuinely uncertain matches. The writeup remembers the matchup mainly for finally providing close-match drama after a long run of blowouts.

7965.headline: Yakuza 0 finally converts Board 8 enthusiasm into a win
7965.narrative: Yakuza 0 beat The Witness and gave the long-promoted Board 8 franchise a straightforward contest win. The writeup treats the result as validation of Yakuza's growing visibility more than proof of major strength.

7966.headline: Metal Gear Solid V wins an oddly themed matchup
7966.narrative: Metal Gear Solid V beat Dead Cells in a matchup whose pairing the writeup considers deliberately ironic because both revolve around missing or phantom body parts. The result itself did little to repair Metal Gear's declining reputation.

7967.headline: Arkham City wins but leaves the door open
7967.narrative: Batman: Arkham City beat Xenoblade Chronicles 2, but the margin was close enough to create concern about Batman's deeper prospects. The writeup also treats Xenoblade 2 as a respectable loss for a relatively niche JRPG.

7968.headline: BioShock Infinite wins without looking strong
7968.narrative: BioShock Infinite doubled Terraria but still looked weak because Terraria was later treated as one of the bracket's poorest games. The writeup sees the result as another sign that BioShock's peak had passed.

7969.headline: Diablo III overwhelms a Board 8 niche favorite
7969.narrative: Diablo III crushed Virtue's Last Reward despite an absurdly anti-Blizzard Board 8 opening vote. The writeup treats the result more as evidence of VLR's extreme niche weakness than as a Blizzard rebound.

7970.headline: The Last of Us wins but trails Dark Souls
7970.narrative: The Last of Us routed Crusader Kings II but failed to match the strongest statements from the division. The writeup treats the result as a warning for its planned showdown with Dark Souls.

7971.headline: Skyrim wins big and still scares its supporters
7971.narrative: Skyrim crushed Subnautica but looked weak in the opening board vote compared with The Witcher 3 and Dark Souls. The writeup treats that early weakness as a major warning for a game many had picked to reach the final.

7972.headline: Journey survives a battle near the bottom
7972.narrative: Journey beat Fate / Grand Order in a matchup the writeup expected to identify one of the weakest Round Two entrants. The result reflects GameFAQs' limited interest in mobile gacha games more than meaningful Journey strength.

7973.headline: Final Fantasy XIV turns respect into contest strength
7973.narrative: Final Fantasy XIV beat Crypt of the NecroDancer and looked better than many expected from an MMO on GameFAQs. The writeup treats the result as evidence that the game's strong modern reputation had translated into real contest value.

7974.headline: Mario Kart 8 punishes another Uncharted high seed
7974.narrative: Mario Kart 8 upset Uncharted 4 and continued Uncharted's history of collapsing as a high seed. The writeup treats the result as proof that Mario Kart's Switch-era success had erased much of its old Wii U weakness.

7975.headline: Pokémon HGSS opens with an elite-level rout
7975.narrative: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver obliterated Night in the Woods and immediately looked like a true proxy for the older Pokémon Gold and Silver games. The result put Skyrim on notice for a possible later matchup.

7976.headline: Celeste survives Rayman in the Round One thriller
7976.narrative: Celeste and Rayman Legends stayed extremely close for nearly the entire match before Celeste escaped with the win. The writeup celebrates it as the best match of an otherwise blowout-heavy opening round.

7977.headline: Divinity advances through one of the weakest matchups
7977.narrative: Divinity: Original Sin II beat Hearthstone in a matchup the writeup expected to produce one of the weakest surviving games. Hearthstone's anti-Blizzard baggage and poor historical strength made the outcome straightforward.

7978.headline: NieR Automata SFFs Bayonetta 2 in a brutal draw
7978.narrative: NieR: Automata crushed Bayonetta 2 and looked excellent entering the next round. The writeup later treats heavy overlap between the two action-game fanbases as the best explanation for how lopsided the result became.
7978.anomaly_note: Ctes says the most likely explanation is that NieR: Automata SFFed Bayonetta 2 because of their overlapping Platinum-style action audience, and explicitly says he believes the SFF explanation most.

7979.headline: Breath of the Wild looks completely untouchable
7979.narrative: Breath of the Wild demolished Halo: Reach and joined the rare group of games producing enormous blowouts in consecutive rounds. The writeup treats the performance as confirmation that even a hypothetical late rally might not be enough to stop Zelda.

7980.headline: Final Fantasy XV barely avoids an indie embarrassment
7980.narrative: Final Fantasy XV survived Hollow Knight in a matchup that came far closer to embarrassment than a mainline Final Fantasy game should have allowed. The writeup treats the win as further evidence of FFXV's weak standing on the site.

7981.headline: Monster Hunter crushes Sekiro and the Souls sweep
7981.narrative: Monster Hunter: World beat Sekiro far more comfortably than expected and ended the writeup's hope that every Souls-like game would overperform. The result is framed as a major disappointment for Sekiro and a strong statement for Monster Hunter.

7982.headline: Dragon Quest XI proves its strength is real
7982.narrative: Dragon Quest XI demolished Bastion and proved its first-round rout was not merely a fanbase-overlap fluke. The writeup treats it as by far the strongest Dragon Quest contest showing to date.

7983.headline: Mass Effect 2 answers its critics with a rout
7983.narrative: Mass Effect 2 crushed Fallout 4 more decisively than expected and repaired the concern created by its first-round performance. The writeup notes that people floated SFF as an explanation, but does not settle on it.

7984.headline: Horizon beats Borderlands with a rally-spillover tailwind
7984.narrative: Horizon Zero Dawn upset Borderlands 2 and never looked back after seizing control early. The Bloodborne rally in the neighboring match added a small extra boost to an already convincing Horizon win.
7984.anomaly_note: The writeup says the simultaneous Bloodborne rally boosted Horizon Zero Dawn further after it had already taken control of Borderlands 2.

7985.headline: Resident Evil 2 beats a rally-boosted DOOM
7985.narrative: Resident Evil 2 beat DOOM in a debated matchup and confirmed that DOOM's first-round destruction of INSIDE had overstated its strength. Rally spillover helped DOOM somewhat but never threatened the result.
7985.anomaly_note: The writeup says DOOM was performing worse before the simultaneous Bloodborne rallies arrived and boosted it against Resident Evil 2.

7986.headline: Bloodborne rallies hard after already taking control
7986.narrative: Bloodborne beat Fire Emblem: Awakening and then pulled away sharply once its subreddit rally gained traction. The match established Bloodborne as both naturally strong and capable of meaningful outside mobilization.
7986.anomaly_note: The writeup says Bloodborne fans organized subreddit rally threads that materially increased its margin over Fire Emblem: Awakening, turning a closer natural win into a much larger one.

7987.headline: Smash Ultimate SFFs A Link Between Worlds
7987.narrative: Smash Ultimate crushed A Link Between Worlds in a badly drawn same-audience matchup. The writeup treats the loss as unusually harsh for a Zelda game but heavily distorted by Nintendo overlap.
7987.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Smash Ultimate versus A Link Between Worlds a standard SFF match and says the Zelda game was likely suppressed heavily by the stronger Nintendo title.

7988.headline: Spider-Man beats Minecraft despite rally spillover
7988.narrative: Marvel's Spider-Man beat Minecraft and validated the experts who had trusted its natural strength over casual recognition and rally fear. Simultaneous rally traffic helped Minecraft somewhat but did not change the outcome.
7988.anomaly_note: The writeup says rallying in the simultaneous Octopath Traveler versus Shovel Knight match shifted support toward Minecraft and reduced Spider-Man's percentage during this poll.

7989.headline: A developer rally swings the Octopath-Shovel Knight classic
7989.narrative: Octopath Traveler and Shovel Knight traded momentum for nearly the entire day before outside support became decisive late. After Octopath's pinned subreddit rally gained control, an official Shovel Knight developer push reversed the match and stole the finish.
7989.anomaly_note: The writeup describes sustained two-sided subreddit rallying and says Yacht Club Games' late official Twitter push decisively swung the finish toward Shovel Knight.

7990.headline: Odyssey crushes Devil May Cry and keeps gaining hype
7990.narrative: Super Mario Odyssey demolished Devil May Cry 5 and continued to look stronger than Smash Ultimate through the early rounds. The writeup treats the result as another major boost to Odyssey's divisional hype.

7991.headline: GTA V crushes the Cuphead upset hype
7991.narrative: Grand Theft Auto V quickly erased the much-hyped Cuphead upset scenario and controlled the match throughout. The writeup treats GTA V as clearly stronger than the rest of its historically weak contest franchise.

7992.headline: Persona 4 Golden rallies past Red Dead Redemption
7992.narrative: Persona 4 Golden led from the start but repeatedly needed outside support to repel Red Dead Redemption's pushes. The final score was close even though Red Dead never actually took the lead.
7992.anomaly_note: The writeup says Persona 4 Golden received repeated Reddit and Board 8 rally support, plus some rally spillover, and argues that the outside help likely made the difference in its narrow win.

7993.headline: Xenoblade crushes Overwatch and seizes the division
7993.narrative: Xenoblade Chronicles destroyed Overwatch and proved its first-round blowout was not merely a favorable same-fanbase matchup. The result established Xenoblade as the new favorite to win the division.

7994.headline: Three Houses wins but loses its favorite status
7994.narrative: Fire Emblem: Three Houses beat Ori but again looked much weaker than expected. Combined with Xenoblade's simultaneous dominance, the result badly damaged Three Houses' status as the presumed division favorite.

7995.headline: Witcher 3 SFFs Mass Effect 3 into oblivion
7995.narrative: The Witcher 3 obliterated Mass Effect 3 and looked increasingly untouchable in the lower half of the bracket. The writeup treats the scale of the rout as partly fanbase suppression and partly genuine elite strength.
7995.anomaly_note: The writeup says The Witcher 3 suppressed Mass Effect 3 through what became known as Western SFF, with their overlapping Western RPG audience making the blowout even larger.

7996.headline: Galaxy 2 wins despite Stardew rally spillover
7996.narrative: Super Mario Galaxy 2 still won comfortably despite rally spillover helping Stardew Valley. The writeup treats both games as respectable while acknowledging that Galaxy 2's next Witcher matchup looked grim.
7996.anomaly_note: The writeup says rally traffic from the simultaneous match disproportionately boosted Stardew Valley and reduced Super Mario Galaxy 2's final margin.

7997.headline: New Vegas wins a two-sided rally battle
7997.narrative: Fallout: New Vegas beat Dark Souls III in a debated matchup where both sides attracted outside support. The stronger New Vegas rally helped preserve a result that still broadly matched pre-match expectations.
7997.anomaly_note: The writeup says both Dark Souls III and Fallout: New Vegas received organized rally support, with the New Vegas subreddit push ultimately proving much stronger.

7998.headline: God of War crushes a partially SFFed Nioh
7998.narrative: God of War demolished Nioh and continued to look strong enough for a deep run. The writeup sees some fanbase overlap in the rout but still considers God of War's underlying performance impressive.
7998.anomaly_note: The writeup says Nioh was probably suppressed to some extent by God of War because both games appealed to overlapping PlayStation action audiences.

7999.headline: Persona 5 crushes Black Flag and looks mainstream
7999.narrative: Persona 5 demolished Assassin's Creed IV and reinforced the series' emergence as a mainstream GameFAQs force. The result also made Witcher 3's earlier Assassin's Creed rout look less uniquely informative.

8000.headline: Sonic Mania SFFs Super Meat Boy in a rout
8000.narrative: Sonic Mania unexpectedly routed Super Meat Boy in what had been treated as a close matchup. The writeup attributes part of the blowout to overlapping platformer support.
8000.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Sonic Mania versus Super Meat Boy an SFF match, arguing that the two platformers share enough audience for Sonic to suppress the indie game.

8001.headline: Portal 2 crushes Kingdom Hearts III
8001.narrative: Portal 2 demolished Kingdom Hearts III and ended one of the more popular second-round upset picks. The writeup treats Kingdom Hearts III's disappointing reception as a major reason the series failed to retain its old strength.

8002.headline: Red Dead Redemption 2 handles Animal Crossing
8002.narrative: Red Dead Redemption 2 comfortably beat Animal Crossing: New Leaf despite New Horizons hype giving the older Animal Crossing entry a theoretical boost. The match confirmed that RDR2 remained respectable even on a site hostile to Rockstar.

8003.headline: Dark Souls crushes Rocket League and looks dangerous
8003.narrative: Dark Souls obliterated Rocket League and moved from strong contender to serious semifinal threat. The writeup treats the result as another clear sign that Souls had gained enormous respect since the prior games contest.

8004.headline: Metal Gear Solid V wins while Yakuza earns respect
8004.narrative: Metal Gear Solid V beat Yakuza 0 but looked weak enough to reinforce the franchise's decline. Yakuza's respectable showing also validated that its first-round success was not entirely opponent-driven.

8005.headline: Arkham City rebounds against BioShock Infinite
8005.narrative: Batman: Arkham City handled BioShock Infinite more comfortably than its shaky first round suggested. The writeup treats the result as a partial rebound for Batman and another sign of BioShock's decline.

8006.headline: The Last of Us wins but loses ground to Dark Souls
8006.narrative: The Last of Us beat Diablo III easily but still underperformed enough to damage its status as a likely division winner. The writeup focuses heavily on Diablo and Blizzard's damaged reputation while looking ahead to Dark Souls.

8007.headline: Skyrim wins big and still looks vulnerable
8007.narrative: Skyrim routed Journey but looked weak compared with Witcher 3's earlier results. The match became the first major reason to doubt Skyrim's presumed path to the final.

8008.headline: Mario Kart 8 beats Final Fantasy XIV cleanly
8008.narrative: Mario Kart 8 comfortably eliminated Final Fantasy XIV and continued rehabilitating its reputation after the Wii U era. The result also weakened the idea that Final Fantasy XIV's modern acclaim would translate into contest strength.

8009.headline: Pokémon HGSS crushes Rayman and keeps rising
8009.narrative: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver crushed Rayman Legends and continued looking like a viable proxy for the much older Gold and Silver. The writeup treats the remake's legitimacy as increasingly hard to dispute.

8010.headline: NieR wins while Divinity rallies down the margin
8010.narrative: NieR: Automata won comfortably while Divinity rallied hard enough to distort the final margin and later extrapolated standings. The push was visible but never made the match competitive.
8010.anomaly_note: The writeup says Divinity: Original Sin II mounted a significant Reddit rally after the opening and reduced the size of NieR: Automata's natural blowout, though it never threatened the winner.

8011.headline: Breath of the Wild obliterates Final Fantasy XV
8011.narrative: Breath of the Wild destroyed Final Fantasy XV and completed three straight overwhelming wins. The writeup considers the result historically dominant while treating possible fanbase overlap as too uncertain to explain much.

8012.headline: Dragon Quest XI survives Monster Hunter's rally
8012.narrative: Dragon Quest XI survived a spirited Monster Hunter rally and confirmed that its surprising contest strength was genuine. Monster Hunter still exited with more respect than expected.
8012.anomaly_note: The writeup says Monster Hunter: World mounted a meaningful rally that repeatedly cut into Dragon Quest XI's lead and reduced the final margin without seriously threatening the result.

8013.headline: Mass Effect 2 wins despite Bloodborne rally spillover
8013.narrative: Mass Effect 2 beat Horizon Zero Dawn despite rally spillover boosting Horizon. The underlying result kept Mass Effect favored for the division while also validating Horizon as stronger than expected.
8013.anomaly_note: The writeup says spillover from the simultaneous Bloodborne rally significantly favored Horizon Zero Dawn and lowered Mass Effect 2's final percentage.

8014.headline: Resident Evil 2 survives Bloodborne's rally
8014.narrative: Resident Evil 2 survived Bloodborne in the contest's defining close match after a major rally was curtailed midway through the poll. The writeup treats the moderation decision as the central reason Bloodborne failed to complete the upset.
8014.anomaly_note: The writeup says Bloodborne received a major subreddit rally that nearly swung the match, and that the moderators' decision to disallow rally threads midway through the poll was the decisive factor in Resident Evil 2 surviving.

8015.headline: Smash wins while Odyssey keeps looking stronger
8015.narrative: Smash Ultimate crushed Spider-Man in a predictable divisional semifinal, but once again looked less dominant than Super Mario Odyssey. The comparison further fueled upset talk for their coming head-to-head match.

8016.headline: Odyssey crushes Shovel Knight and raises Smash doubts
8016.narrative: Super Mario Odyssey demolished Shovel Knight and produced a third straight performance that looked stronger than Smash Ultimate's. The writeup notes the conspicuous absence of the developer rally that had saved Shovel Knight previously.

8017.headline: Persona 4 Golden beats GTA V without drama
8017.narrative: Persona 4 Golden beat Grand Theft Auto V from wire to wire and completed another bracket-busting win without current-match rally assistance. The result established Persona 4 Golden as the contest's most surprising divisional finalist.

8018.headline: Xenoblade crushes a partially SFFed Three Houses
8018.narrative: Xenoblade Chronicles crushed Fire Emblem: Three Houses and completed the collapse of the pre-contest division favorite. The writeup sees some same-audience suppression but puts more emphasis on anti-voting and Xenoblade's genuine rise.
8018.anomaly_note: The writeup says Three Houses was probably SFFed to some extent by Xenoblade Chronicles, although anti-Fire-Emblem voting and general overestimation are treated as larger factors.

8019.headline: Witcher 3 beats Galaxy 2 and keeps rolling
8019.narrative: The Witcher 3 beat Super Mario Galaxy 2 after a briefly entertaining opening and again looked stronger than expected. Galaxy 2 still performed well enough to confirm that its earlier blowouts were not purely weak-opponent artifacts.

8020.headline: God of War beats New Vegas and meets the buzzsaw
8020.narrative: God of War beat Fallout: New Vegas in a match that was never seriously in doubt, though New Vegas remained respectable. The result sent God of War into the division final with little hope of stopping Witcher 3.

8021.headline: Persona 5 obliterates Sonic Mania
8021.narrative: Persona 5 annihilated Sonic Mania and continued to look like the clear class of its division. The writeup treats Sonic's run as mostly bracket-driven while emphasizing Persona's modern mainstream strength.

8022.headline: Portal 2 quietly ends Red Dead Redemption 2
8022.narrative: Portal 2 beat Red Dead Redemption 2 in a closer-looking divisional semifinal that remained under control for most of the day. The result validated Portal 2's hidden strength and ended the author's overconfidence in newer games.

8023.headline: Dark Souls widens the gap on Metal Gear Solid V
8023.narrative: Dark Souls repeated its 2015 win over Metal Gear Solid V with a much larger margin. The writeup treats the widening gap as a clean combination of Souls rising and Metal Gear declining.

8024.headline: The Last of Us advances with another warning
8024.narrative: The Last of Us beat Batman: Arkham City but again failed to look strong enough to threaten Dark Souls. The result left its popular pre-contest division-win pick effectively doomed.

8025.headline: Skyrim wins but becomes an upset target
8025.narrative: Skyrim beat Mario Kart 8 but looked weak enough to become a serious target for later upset speculation. The writeup treats Mario Kart's prior SFF history as irrelevant to this current matchup.

8026.headline: Pokémon survives NieR's rally efforts
8026.narrative: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver survived an initially close NieR: Automata challenge and pulled away once the early rally pressure faded. The result closed Round Three with Pokémon still looking surprisingly legitimate.
8026.anomaly_note: The writeup says NieR: Automata supporters had active rally efforts during the match, including the jokingly described hentai rallies, though those pushes never became large enough to overturn Pokémon.

8027.headline: Breath of the Wild wins while Dragon Quest earns respect
8027.narrative: Breath of the Wild comfortably beat Dragon Quest XI but finally fell well short of its earlier overwhelming percentages. The writeup treats the result as evidence that Dragon Quest XI was much stronger than the bracket had initially assumed.

8028.headline: Mass Effect 2 edges Resident Evil 2
8028.narrative: Mass Effect 2 narrowly beat Resident Evil 2 in one of the most debated Round Four matches. The result validated Mass Effect as the natural division winner while ending Resident Evil 2's bandwagon.

8029.headline: Smash reverse-SFFs Odyssey and restores the hierarchy
8029.narrative: Smash Ultimate beat Super Mario Odyssey despite Odyssey looking stronger in every prior round. The writeup treats the result as a hierarchy-driven same-fanbase matchup, with reverse SFF offered as the main explanation for the reversal.
8029.anomaly_note: Ulti explicitly argues that Smash Ultimate reverse-SFFed Super Mario Odyssey, while the broader writeup also treats Nintendo hierarchy and same-fanbase effects as central to why Smash won more comfortably than expected.

8030.headline: Xenoblade survives Persona 4 Golden's late rallies
8030.narrative: Xenoblade Chronicles survived Persona 4 Golden in the last truly great close match of the contest. Persona's rallies repeatedly cut the lead, and without the registered-user weighting Persona would have narrowly won.
8030.anomaly_note: The writeup says Persona 4 Golden received repeated and increasingly intense rally support throughout the match, culminating in a late push that nearly overturned Xenoblade's lead.

8031.headline: Witcher 3 SFFs God of War and looks unstoppable
8031.narrative: The Witcher 3 crushed God of War far more severely than expected and looked completely secure on its path to the final. The writeup attributes part of the rout to overlapping Western audiences while still crediting Witcher's genuine strength.
8031.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly says some form of SFF occurred between The Witcher 3 and God of War because of their overlapping Western open-world audience, while warning that the effect was probably overestimated.

8032.headline: Persona 5 crushes Portal 2 with a small rally boost
8032.narrative: Persona 5 crushed Portal 2 after the opening minutes and won the division comfortably. A continuing Persona rally thread added a small boost but was not necessary to the result.
8032.anomaly_note: The writeup says the Persona subreddit maintained a rally thread and later redirected it toward Persona 5, giving Persona a small current-match boost even though the effect was not large.

8033.headline: Dark Souls wins inside a massive Last of Us rant
8033.narrative: The writeup is dominated by a lengthy discussion of The Last of Us Part II leaks and broader cultural arguments; the match itself is summarized as Dark Souls comfortably beating a badly damaged Last of Us.

8034.headline: Skyrim finally delivers its redemption match
8034.narrative: Skyrim decisively beat Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver and finally delivered the strong performance its supporters had been waiting for. The result restored confidence that Skyrim was still a legitimate late-round game.

8035.headline: Breath of the Wild keeps doubling everything
8035.narrative: Breath of the Wild doubled Mass Effect 2 in the quarterfinals and maintained one of the most dominant game-contest runs ever. The writeup treats Dragon Quest XI's prior resistance as newly impressive in hindsight.

8036.headline: Smash ends Xenoblade's surprise run comfortably
8036.narrative: Smash Ultimate comfortably ended Xenoblade's surprise run and advanced to the semifinal. Although some observers called the result SFF, the writeup explicitly questions whether meaningful suppression occurred and emphasizes Xenoblade's bandwagon instead.

8037.headline: Witcher 3 absorbs Persona 5's rally and wins
8037.narrative: The Witcher 3 beat Persona 5 after an entertaining opening and confirmed that even a major Persona push was not enough to threaten it. The result sent Witcher into the semifinal looking almost untouchable.
8037.anomaly_note: The writeup says Persona 5 rallied heavily from the opening and received roughly hundreds of outside votes, though The Witcher 3 repeatedly absorbed the pushes and pulled away.

8038.headline: Skyrim outlasts Dark Souls in the last close quarterfinal
8038.narrative: Skyrim and Dark Souls stayed nearly even for the opening hours before Skyrim's stronger morning vote finally created separation. The writeup treats it as the last genuinely competitive match of the contest and a strong final showing for Dark Souls.

8039.headline: Breath of the Wild SFFs Smash in the semifinal
8039.narrative: Breath of the Wild demolished Smash Ultimate in a semifinal and continued its run of overwhelming late-round victories. Even accounting for heavy Nintendo SFF, the writeup treats the performance as extraordinary.
8039.anomaly_note: The writeup explicitly calls Breath of the Wild versus Smash Ultimate a bad case of SFF, with Zelda's place atop the Nintendo hierarchy suppressing Smash.

8040.headline: Witcher 3 beats Skyrim and completes its pre-final rise
8040.narrative: The Witcher 3 beat Skyrim comfortably in the semifinal after spending the entire contest steadily overturning pre-contest expectations. The writeup attributes Witcher's rise to several reinforcing factors, including Netflix exposure, broader respect, Switch availability and Bethesda fatigue, while treating possible SFF as only speculative.

8041.headline: Breath of the Wild wins despite a heavy Witcher rally
8041.narrative: Breath of the Wild completed its dominant championship run, but Witcher 3's rally made the final substantially more respectable than the opening suggested. The writeup treats Witcher as the contest's breakout star even in defeat.
8041.anomaly_note: The writeup says Witcher 3 fans rallied heavily throughout the final and materially cut Breath of the Wild's natural margin, even though the rally never put the winner in danger.

8090.headline: Breath of the Wild routs Majora's Mask in the bonus
8090.narrative: Breath of the Wild crushed Majora's Mask in the post-contest bonus between the winners of two Game of the Decade contests. The writeup is split on whether the same-series matchup involved meaningful SFF, so the cause is left unresolved rather than tagged.
